title: Very rigid cover; good quality; partially works on earlier Stylo phone
text: I ordered this for my LG G Stylo phone, but it was designed for a Stylo 2, which is apparently just slightly different.  It does fit my phone, but it partially covers the camera flash and completely covers the laser detection auto focus. I believe it also covers the headphone jack. All the other holes line up okay (microphone, charging port, speaker and hole for the stylus).  All the front openings are available because this is a one-sided case.  If you don't use the camera that much or the headphone jack (which I don't), you could make it work.  It is very rigid, so it seems as if it would be very durable and long lasting.  Because it is a completely rigid case, it was a little difficult to slip the phone into it and I may have cracked the back cover of the phone (the battery cover).  It's possible that it was already cracked from dropping the phone a few times, but I know I made several of the cracks worse putting it in the case and then removing the case.  When I first removed the case, it pulled the back off the phone, in fact.  Possibly the fit might not be quite as tight on a Stylo 2, but if it was not a good firm fit, the case would not stay in place.  My suggestion - once you have it in the case, don't remove it, unless you have to in order to get to the battery or memory card inside your phone.  The only thing that I really didn't like is that this is a one sided case that covers only the back, ends and side of the phone but not the front.  My current case has a cover, to cover the front of the phone as well, so it protects it much better.  My attempts to fit this case to a phone that it wasn't quite designed for should not impact your decision to buy this case.  All I would say is to just be careful inserting it into the case, so as not to flex the phone at all, which might crack the back phone cover (the battery cover) as it did mine.  I wasn't keen on the pink color, but you can order this in other colors.

title: Charges New iPad Very Fast (Needs Lightning to USB-C Cable)
text:
This ESR USB-C 18W FAST WALL CHARGER WITH PD (UL Certified, with Foldable Prong) charges my new iPad Air (3rd Gen) very fast--much, much faster than the Apple 12W USB Charger that came with it.

PD means “Power Delivery”. USB PD is a new power standard that can be used across multiple devices, so that you don’t need a lot of different adapters. PD increases power levels--up to 100W--so that devices charge faster. PD determines how much power each device needs, and ensures that each device is NOT overcharged. This ESR USB charger delivers 18W of power.

PD chargers have USB-C ports, so you will need a cable with a USB-C plug (rather than the familiar flat USB plug) to connect your iPad, cellphone, etc. My iPad uses a lightning cable, so I ordered this [[ASIN:B07CMN7DCX Apple Lightning to USB-C cable]]. It’s a genuine Apple cable that arrives new in a sealed Apple box, so I know it’s safe to use with the iPad.

Until I got the settings on the new iPad adjusted to eliminate battery-draining default features, I was actually having to curtail my iPad use. The iPad was discharging rapidly, and the recharging with the ordinary USB adapter was taking forever. This 18W PD adapter solved the problem completely. The iPad recharges quickly even when it’s connected to my home wireless network and I’m using it.

title: Solid Basic Phone Case
text:
It has been a while since I have had an Otterbox phone case. I recently upgraded my phone and wanted a basic clear case for it, and I chose this one. So far I am happy with it.

This is a basic, no-frills case for the iPhone 13. As mentioned I chose the clear case and it is very much that - it is not frosted or opaque like another case I have but is absolutely clear.

The case is designed for bumper shocks more than anything and it delivers. It has a thick, semi-pliable bumper guard as well as a fair amount of thickness on the back so your phone is well protected. It does a good job with medium height drops and fumbles and it keeps the phone for getting scratched up when jammed in a pocket of briefcase.

The button covers work well and the phone is as operable as if I put no case on it at all. I have had no issues with unresponsive buttons related to this case. The speaker, microphone and lightning ports all line up nicely on the bottom as well and the case does not interfere with any of these. Finally, the case comes to the perimeter of the screen but does not actually touch the screen so it does not interfere with screen covers - I major issue I have seen with a few cheap cases in the past.

I am pleased with this case and expect to get years of service from it. It provides good protection for the phone and it does not interfere with the phone's operation at all.

title: Works Well
text:
I have worked with a number of power banks like this one, and all of them are similar in concept and basic function though they vary in capacity, number of ports, included accessories like carabiners and other features. This is one of the larger-capacity packs with which I have worked and so far I have not had any issues with it. It appears to be a solid workhorse.

At the heart of any of these battery packs is a set of rechargeable batteries, which is where these things get their weight. Generally speaking, the heavier the power bank the more batteries and more capacity the bank possesses. This one is no exception to that. At a capacity of 25,000 mA, this is a bit of a brute and has some heft to it. That said, it is slightly smaller and lighter than most of the higher-capacity units I have used.

It’s a handsome fellow and looks quite a bit like a smart phone.

There are two output ports for charging USB devices. One of them is rated for 5V/1A and the other is at 5V/2.1A. This does not mean that when you plug in a tablet or phone that it will steadily output a full 1A or 2.1A. Putting a USB power meter on the ports when charging my phone on the 1A port, the power fluctuates, especially if I am actually doing things on my phone at the time. When “at rest”, my phone typically draws about 0.5A, but when I open an app or open a web page in the browser, it spikes and will pull quite a bit more but then it settles again.

I have not drained this pack completely yet so I am not sure how many charges I can get with it when it comes to my phone. My phone can be charged from dead to 100% on a pack that has a 2,500 mA capacity, so in theory this one should be capable of giving me 10 full charges between needing to be recharged itself. We’ll see. It does get my phone charged up relatively quickly, and it shows its own capacity while it is charging so I’ll know when it is getting low.

So far, I have no complaints with this battery pack and I am pleased with it. It looks nice, it has a very high capacity and it works as advertised.

title: Good Lens, Clip is Passable
text:
I have worked with a number of lenses for phones and I have seen some interesting variations. Some require a special case to work with a phone (and therefore are model-specific) while others use a special clip that clamps over the phone’s lens. This one falls into the latter design type and for what it is it’s very good, though there is room for a little improvement.

There are two main components to this lens. There is the clip to which the lens attaches, and there is the lens itself which is actually a pair of lenses. The clip is a solid and sturdy thing with a strong grip so I will not slip off the phone when in use, a problem I have seen with lenses of this type on occasion. The part that touches the back of the phone has a thin foam pad that provides grip, and the pad has a slight swivel action to it so in theory it will lay flat regardless of the phone’s shape. It works in that regard, even with the phone case on.

Now, that said, to get this lens to really work I have to take my phone out of its case. That’s inconvenient but not a deal breaker for me because my phone case is a simple slip-on case. For those using a more complex case it may prove to be more tedious. There are things that could have been done to make it fit regardless of the case.

The lens itself is a two-piece assembly, as many are. When assembled it is a wide-angle lens that enhances the field of view in the shot, especially when zoomed out. When only the base is used, it is a high-magnification macro lens that is great for taking clear pics of things that are very close. In both cases, I have found the images to come out with very little distortion and the images are clear and sharp. For the macro lens test I used my thumb as a test subject and I was able to get good ridge detail on my thumb print.

The lens includes a nice cloth bag that keeps it clean and protects it from scratches. It’s not much protection against crush damage when the lens is stored in a book bag but it’s certainly better than nothing and will keep the lens mostly pristine when on the go.

This is a good lens, let down by a basic clamp that could have been better. If you don’t mind taking your phone out of the case to use this lens, the lens will serve you well and you’ll be rewarded with solid, clear pics.

title: Easy to Apply, No Impact to Responsiveness
text:
I have an iPhone 6s and I have a bad tendency to break my screen protectors on said phone. I am loathe to replace them since they tend to be expensive at the store, and they’re not something I think to buy when I have one that is not broken. I was given an opportunity to test these screen protectors and they have proven to be worth their salt. These are much more affordable than those you buy at a store and they work just as well.

These come in a two-pack which is great news for this clumsy fellow. I have a very bad tendency to drop my phone and invariably the screen gets caught right on the edge and the cracks spider out, so having an extra one close by when I do break one again is a good thing. I presently have one of the two applied to my screen and so far it has held up for a couple of weeks. I have dropped my phone a couple of times but so far the screen protector has held.

Application is simple and easy. I am used to seeing alcohol wipes in the package with most protectors, but this package did not have one. Everything you need is in there, though. If you are careful and you follow the directions on the package, you end up with a screen protector that fits right and does not have bubbles. I got it right on the first try.

The screen protectors do not cover the curve which I have come to regard as a good thing. Screen protectors that wrap around the edges to the metal actually interfere with some phone cases or vice versa.

I do like the anti-fingerprint coating which does a decent job of keeping the screen more visible. I dislike a smudged screen so I like how this screen protector helps. It is not 100% fingerprint-proof but it does cut down the prints quite a lot.

So far it has not appreciably diminished sensitivity on the screen either. There is certainly some desensitizing that it brings but it is not enough for me to notice. The screen has remained responsive and clear.

I have nothing to criticize when it comes to these screen protectors. They go on easy, they fit right, they do not show every last fingerprint and they are substantially less expensive than what you buy in the stores.

Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no/minimal cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Tempered Glass Privacy Screen - Works Great
text:
Most people think of screen protection for a mobile phone as a glass or plastic cover that prevents the actual screen from shattering. That’s true, this is the most important aspect of screen protection. But, what about protecting the data displayed on the screen? I have seen privacy screens for laptop screens, but this is the first I have used with a mobile phone and it works exactly like the laptop screen protectors.

Similar to a regular screen protector, this is a thin sheet of glass that applies very smoothly and easily with no bubbles. It has fine screen coverage to the edge of the phone - this has been an issue on some other screen protectors I have used but not this one.

With this screen protector in place, the screen is definitely darker than usual and it might be helpful to adjust the screen brightness. It is a lot like looking at your screen through a pair of sunglasses. Turning the phone at a 45-degree angle makes the screen appear completely black as if the screen has been turned off - no light can be seen at all.

Before I put this protector on the phone I held it up to a light source and saw a repeating pattern of the light source itself, almost like I had held up a mirror to a mirror to get a replicated image. I think this protector works via polarized light and the repeating image is an effect of that - I have seen similar phenomena when wearing polarizing sunglasses.

If protecting the data on your phone screen is as important to you as protecting the screen itself, this is the screen protector you need. It works great, is easy to apply and is sufficient protection for you phone’s screen to prevent physical damage. Just make sure you have the right one for your model of phone.

title: Who designed this? I returned it.
text:
The listing name for this case includes the term, "Shock-Absorption Armor". Sorry, but nope. This case is made from rigid plastic which is too hard to provide much in the way of drop protection. Have you ever dropped your phone getting out of the car? I have, and the thought of dropping it in this case is terrifying. I returned it and purchased (yet another) Speck Presidio Grip case (3x the price), and my new phone is now protected properly in a one-piece case with a soft interior and a hard outer shell with rubber grip and corner bumpers. Most of the cases which meet this description are two separate pieces, and the Speck seems to be the only quality case which isn't (I have also tried Trident in the past, but the rubber in their case fell apart). A one-piece case is MUCH easier is you are taking it on and off all the time (see below).

Also, it should be noted that due to the hard material this case is constructed from, it is not flexible, and getting it off the phone is a nightmare. I do not know why case manufacturers don't seem to understand this model of phone (Z3) uses Moto Mods. If you use Mods (which I do, all the time), you have to remove the case to attach them. Getting this case off is hard and it even feels a bit like the phone is in danger of bending in the process (scary!). This is just not a well-designed product, and it is not appropriate for either drop protection or daily use with this phone if you use Moto Mods (I use multiple Qi charging + extended battery mods).

Also, this case provides no grip assistance and is actually quite slippery, as it is made from hard plastic. I simply cannot recommend this case. I returned it.

title: SECURE case for the Galaxy Note
text:
In the month I have had my new Galaxy Note, I have tried four cases and three different types of belt clips and ended up ticked off and aggravated each time. Until the Cellet Executive Case. This thing looks good and actually works! First the Note slides into the case from the top and it fits as it should. Then the flap of the case folds down over the top - preventing the phone from falling out if the case is upended.

Secondly the case snaps closed with an actual snap instead of a magnet on the bottom - securely holding your phone inside the case where it belongs. Third - the top flap is elevated just a bit so that when it's snapped closed the top part does not scratch your phone screen - even with something tucked into the packet of the flap. I still use a screen protector, but the spacing is a nice perk with this case. There is a tiny little loop on the outside edge of the case where you could attach a cord (like you would on a camera).

Fourth - the belt clip is built into the case rather than an after thought add on. It is also stitched on, so one can assume it should stay in place with regular use. Two full days of use and the belt clip has held my Note nicely in place on my hip while out at the barn working with the horses - the last two I tried both failed and broke within hours! The leather on the case is smooth and looks good - there is a light saddle tan color on the inside that contrasts very nicely with the black exterior. The cutouts for the camera, S-Pen, speaker and volume buttons are all placed correctly and do not interfer with normal use of the phone's features. My only complaint is that the power button cutout slightly overlaps the actual power button, so you have to push through a tiny sliver of leather - not a big deal at all in the general overview. Certainly not enough of a problem to warrant a star deduction.

On a humorous note - the first day using this case had my Mother laughing out loud. Apparently flipping the top back to use the phone reminded her of the old Tri-corders from the original Star Trek. Now...admittedly, I am a total Sci-Fi geek, so this does have a certain appeal. I am ordering a second one of these cases as a back up for the future. Definately worth every penny!

title: Cellphone arm moves too much; great idea, needs some improvement
text:
Not bad, but not the best.

First I will describe the product, then let you know how it can all go wrong.

Easy to put together. Comes with directions, don't really need them.

This is basically a lamp with a cellphone holder. The lamp is a ring with three settings: "white, warm yellow, warm yellow + white". You can adjust the brightness level for any of those modes. The lamp ring can be manipulated in a few different directions. The lamp gets it power from USB only. The cord of the lamp runs freely out from back of ring, and is approximately 65" long. There is a switch to turn it on (and adjust lamp mode and brightness) located about half way down the length (between 24"-27" from lamp ring). The switch has 4 settings. "Up" & "Down" switches to change brightness levels, an "on/off" switch, and a "mode" switch to change between (white), (warm yellow), (warm yellow + white).

The base of the stand has three sturdy legs that spread out fairly flat. When not in use, they can be arranged to be all folded tight together, and used supposedly as an awkward handle for self stick. The entire stand itself at full height is approximately 47". My measurements are not exact, and I have the lamp ring in full upright position. The stand can be adjusted just by turning the tubes/poles- they drop down some as they are loosened. You can collapse all of them to create a very short table top lamp, or they can all be extended to create medium-tall lamp.

This last part is actually what makes me kinda not like this unit. By adjusting one, it is way too easy to accidentally adjust another, so while you may want to make a section taller, but the whole thing collapses too short. You try to make it right again, and things move. All these parts do this. It is not a simple adjustment unless you get it just right, and don't move anything else. So that is annoying. Even by just moving the lamp ring, you can easily put enough pressure to loosen up one of the tubes, once again collapsing the pole and making it shorter. Same deal with the cellphone holder. There are too many moving parts and not designed to be sturdy enough to handle these adjustments without impacting the other. As a photographer and avid reviewer, I need to be able to make quick adjustments without much time or hassle. If you just need a light, or just need to adjust once in awhile--and have patience- then this will be fine for that use; pretty good really!

Ok, now the cellphone holder. I like the tension holder. It is solid on one end, and has a sliding tension bracket with silicone grip. Not bad. It holds my Google Pixel 3xl just fine (once I take it out of case). BUT the weight of it can pull the holder down, and while the holder itself seems to do a fine job, the spot where the holder attaches to the stand is not latched on enough to to securely hold the weight, or be able to handle adjustments, or tap it for pics, etc. See, the spot that holds the cellphone holder arm (rugged material, about 8") to the pole of the stand is a vice style clamp. However, the poles are smooth, and while the vice parts have some traction on each side, it is not enough to firmly hold the cellphone holder in place firmly; it drags it down some. I've tried it on the pole with widest diameter down to smallest- all of them make me question its ability to stay in place. I don't know about you, but this makes me queasy to trust it to keep my expensive cellphone safe from drops.

THAT, and if you try to make adjustment to that area, the whole thing can start collapsing on itself (see prior paragraph).

So yeh, I love the idea of this equipment. It is something I want and need in my life- but I get frustrated with it. I will continue to use it as intended as I still need to use something. If I come up with any ideas how to deal with some of the short comings, i will share my thoughts. I will say that the overall quality of every part seem good. I am impressed with that!

My reduction in rating is based primarily on the cellphone holder arm staying in place. Even with everything else perfectly adjusted, and behaving perfectly (I am generously considering user error), the arm of the cellphone holder dips significantly, and therefore impeded my ability to do my job/tasks.

title: Versatile Kit With Many Configurations Possible
text:
The Ring Light with Stand and Phone Holder was a really nice surprise. This is actually a 2 pack of gooseneck desk clamps that come with 2 swivel ball-jointed adapters, a small 6" ring light and a spring-loaded phone holder. The phone holder can accommodate a phone from 6.5cm (2 3/4") up to 10cm (4"). The gooseneck alone has a length of 58.5cm (23cm) from the surface of the desktop mount. The clamp opens to a maximum depth of 6cm (2 1/4"). This should fit most desktops. The ring light has 11 different brightness settings with 3 different color temperatures. I like that the control is on the cord because it helps prevent accidentally resetting while manipulating the position of the light. Each part has the standard 1/4" threading, so this can work with many different compatible components available from various sources. This is great because a reflector mount or clip can be used, different phone mounts, light weight cameras or different sizes of ring light besides what is included in the kit.

The allows for filming, photos and lighting from overhead of the table/desk top, instead of only from the side as you would have with tripods. It preserves your table top space. I really like this to take photos of some desktop projects I'm working on from an overhead perspective. It also is great for those with limited floor space or anyone that wishes to avoid having their fragile equipment on the floor (especially great for anyone with rowdy animals or crawling babies and toddlers). I can have the ring light setup on my desk and no fears of my dogs running into it or knocking something over.

On thing worth noting is that there is padding on the top side of the desk clamp. On the threaded underside, there is not padding. I've simply used a felt furniture pad on this to protect the underside of surfaces. I have a stash of these in my junk drawer. They're not at all expensive. You can find them in nearly any shop that sells basic home goods. It would have been nice if this was included.

I've compared the price point to similar offerings and concluded this is among the best values. This is especially true considering that these are 2 separate goosenecks with an adjustable, secure mount. I would highly recommend the Ring Light with Stand and Phone Holder for it's versatility and value.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful and will click the Helpful button below.

title: Not the Best Engineering, Not for Heavy Cameras
text:
Endurax Cell Phone Tripod 60" isn't sturdy enough for heavier cameras. A simple point-and-shoot or cell phone would probably work fine. It's stated on the box it will hold up to 6.6lbs, but I wouldn't recommend any more than 3lbs. The tension thumb screws lock into place with little nuts that will drop out of the head mount if you loosen too far, which is easy to do. If this happens in the grass, they would be easily lost. One of the tension thumb screws and nuts isn't pre-positioned, it's in a baggie and the instructions state how to place it. The other 2 tension thumb screws are already positioned, so I'm unsure why this is sent to customers without being fully assembled. The cell phone holder does extend to hold some of the wider phones, so that is nice. There is a remote included. I don't use those, so I cannot comment on that. The tension for the spread of the tripod legs isn't terribly secure, and without some counter weights, it could easily topple over. Usually, camera tripods have a hook to hold some counter weights, but this one does not. The legs are not terribly sturdy, so I certainly would not try a very heavy camera on this tripod.

However, if you are looking for a budget tripod for a light-weight camera, ring light or something else light-weight, this will do the job. It's not the worst tripod I have tested and reviewed, but it's far, far from the best. I wouldn't recommend this one because the nuts can fall out and be lost so easily, making it useless. If the nuts were securely placed, and there was a hook for counter weights, this would be a better value. If I do use this beyond testing, I'm adding some tape to cover the slots for the thumb screw nuts. I'm also not going to use this anywhere it may be accidentally bumped, or in wind because it's just going to topple over so easily. This would be better for very occasional indoor use.

The two nice points I can find is that a carrying/storage bag is included and the legs extend easily are are easy to adjust.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.

text:

Firstly, it fits my iPhone 11 perfectly - all buttons work, switches are easily accessible, cable ports free of obstruction and sound ports are unblocked.

The case is softer than many and while it withstood our minimal stress tests it will not provide a great deal of added protection.

The corners and surrounding edges are reinforced rubber - providing adequate protection if impacted there. As with many similar cases, Emerge utilizes a small air pocket area under each corner which provides a buffer in case of a direct corner impact.

The case stands .5mm above the LCD screen providing minimal protection if it was a flat face fall.

This case is truly crystal clear. While many of these cases have a hint of color this one is clear allowing the color of your phone to shine through.

As with all minimalist cases, it adds very little bulk or weight and will provide a minimal amount, yet necessary, added protection. This is not the case for a teenager or someone who is rough on their phone but it will work great for many people.

I have used a minimalist case for years without incident and look forward to using this one from Speck.

title: Not For Daily Use (Unless Near Water) But Handy To Have On Many Occasions
text:
My husband has a history of crazy damage to cell phones. He got a job near a lake and considering that he just accidentally shut his phone in the hood of his car (yep, it's toast) I wanted to be sure his phone has protection from water since he is working near a lake. As a contractor you have to be prepared for a variety of situations.

WHAT IS THIS CASE LIKE?
This case is a really big case. It will fit a larger phone and fits the Moto G7 Power fine and can probably go slightly wider too. The case has a back window in it so that the camera can take pictures- although why you would want to do that through plastic I don't understand- and the front is completely see through.

ELASTIC
There is an elastic band which holds the phone up against the front window. There is still some space however, so the plastic is not very tight against the whole surface.

ZIPPER
The zipper is definitely waterproof and is a silicone track. They say to lube it with zipper lube from time to time, but don't say what kind.

LANYARD
This comes with a lanyard which allows you to keep this around your neck for easy access. That is a really cool feature if you are camping, or doing outdoor activities. You can have access for quick photos, and still keep it where you can see it.

BELT LOOP
The belt loop on this allows for a maximum of a 1 inch belt. It is very tight.

DOES THIS FLOAT?
Yes, this does float. If you happen to drop it in the water, it will float for a time so you can find it.

WHAT IS THIS GOOD FOR?
This is good for those who work outdoors, are going to have to work in the rain for a long period of time, who are working near water, who are camping , doing outdoor activities, and anyone who needs to be sure their phone is protected from water damage.

WHO MIGHT NOT LIKE THIS?
My husband did not think this was convenient. It is usable through the plastic, but he felt like it was awkward. He is doing most of the work on a cottage and not in or close to the water, but he has to refill buckets of water since the water is not working in the cottage.

So, I would say if you are not going to be in danger of water submersion this might seem cumbersome to you.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you are working through water, heavy rains, around bodies of water, or are busy in outdoor activities like camping, etc, this phone case would probably be a great thing to have. Those activities are not phone centered, so just having the phone protected is a great asset. If you want to just have protection against water but use your phone constantly, this might seem cumbersome to you.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. This is a great idea. For camping and activities outdoors where you just want your phone handy, but not used constantly, this is a FIVE STARS item. If you are using your phone a lot and want it handy to be protected from rain, this will still work well, but you might find it a bit clumsy. FOUR stars is for that kind of use.

title: Not Perfect, But I Love This!
text:
The Jabra Freeway is one of the most handy little gadgets that I have used when it comes to bluetooth and cell phones. About the size of a half size of a paperback book, this speaker is really a handy little gizmo.

The set up is really easy as the instructions are audio and integrated in the unit. Each area of control on the unit is clearly marked and easy to access while driving. The volume button on the unit is easy to reach and easy to use. It is just sensitive enough so that it will work but not so easy that it is constantly being hit by mistake.

The phone button (looks like a receiver of a regular phone) is a little hard to see if you are looking for it, as it curves around back of the unit, but it is easy enough to find that you don't really have to look for it.

The voice commands are not always easy to use, however. I have tested this unit with two phones- both Samsung Rugby phones. When using the voice, you have to press the VOICE button on the unit, wait for it to tell you to "Say a Command" then say "Phone commands" then the Rugby says, "Say a Command" through the Freeway speaker and you have to tell it what to do. Sometimes I find that even though I am speaking clearly and saying exactly what needs to be said, the system gets messed up and I can not use the voice command again unless I reset the Jabra Unit, or sometimes I have to go back in and reset something on my phone.

For instance, I told the phone (via Jabra Freeway) to dial a number that I had been using with no problem before. Suddenly I was in some kind of research mode that I could not get out of. I am not sure what the problem is yet- if the phone is trying to override the speaker or what, but it is frustrating.

At that point, I have to shut the unit off and then turn it on again if I want to use voice commands on the Jabra Freeway unit.

When leaving the vehicle, the unit connection does shut off but the speaker still is technically on. It is best to turn it completely off at the end of the day, however, since it will stay charged longer.

Also, when it gets really hot (like 120 degrees in a sun baked car) or really cold, I would not recommend leaving this in the car- it is easy enough to remove and replace, however, so it is just a matter of making a habit of removing it from the car in extreme heat or cold.

Despite the frustration with having to reset on voice mode, if I just want to access the unit, I can easily press the buttons and use it that way until I turn the unit on and off again.

Sound quality is fantastic- people remark that they can not hear the wind hardly at all when my windows are open, and I can also hear very clearly when the volume is not up too high. In fact, sometimes I have to turn the volume down because people say I am talking too loud when I am barely speaking! This is a huge change from all of my ear pieces!

WHAT I LIKE
The voice commands are handy when they work.
Speaker works beautifully even with windows open
Controls are easy to access and clearly marked
Long talk time
Clear sound
Phone hooks up when entering car again
Will tell how much battery talk time is left when asked

WHAT I DON'T LIKE
Voice does not always work well
Sometimes have to reset phone when commands get mixed up
Runs phone down faster when leaving car and coming back through a day- looking for bluetooth connection- but the unit itself holds charge really well

Despite some limitations, I still absolutely love the Freeway and compared to the Blue Ant S4, it is much easier to use, and much more handy to have in the car. Compared to the Blue Ant S4, I find that the sound is similar, wind block is also similar, but the controls in the Blue Ant S4 frustrate me- they are hard to use and sometimes unresponsive. The Jabra Freeway is superior in that department. I like using it much better. And it definitely beats any of the Plantronics ear pieces I have tried to use in the car. I have gone through quite a few of them from the highest end to the most basic.

I will be using the Jabra Freeway from now on in the car as long as it performs well.

Update Sep18, 2007:
I've occasionally experienced some problems with this item in the time I've had it, thought this info might be useful if you're considering buying this.

One problem is an occasional "hang" when dialing -- you make a voice dial call, the phone says the name so you know it got the right number, but then nothing happens. Usually you give it a puzzled look after a few seconds, disconnect and try again, and everything works fine.

Sometimes however it's a real hang -- the phone's waiting for the device, the device is waiting for the phone (probably some piece of the bluetooth protocol got dropped on the floor), and you can't disconnect, you can't power the device down, nothing. You have to get your phone out and disconnect the device from the bluetooth menu, then recycle the power on the device, then you can proceed again. I haven't figured out why this happens, or a surefire way to prevent it. Doesn't happen a lot, but it shouldn't happen at all, right?

title: Reliable charger for most electronics, but has a ground loop buzz with analog audio
text:
Like the title says - it charges most electrical devices at a decent rate. It does not seem compatible with various proprietary fast charging standards, but it also doesn't charge things slowly, it puts out plenty of power to top off devices even during use.

It feels very sold - it has some heft in the hand, the materials are dense and smooth, there is a pleasing matte finish to it. I'd like it to seat a bit better/more tightly in the cigarette lighter socket, but that may be the socket and not the charger.

My major complaint is that the power on this unit is not isolated, which means it is capable of creating a ground loop with analog audio devices, thus putting out a hum. This is disappointed for a device of this kind, even if analog audio is considerably more rare these days than it used to be. I have a much less expensive USB DC-DC buck converter which I tied in elsewhere in the car, and that does not have any such issue. Indeed this is how I know the noise is from the Anker - the exact same setup on the buck converter, which is connected to the same socket, has no issue were as the Anker has noise where ever it is connected. This necessitates the use of an isolator somewhere else in my setup.

If you don't care about the noise, then there's no problem, this is a good car charger. If noise is a potential problem, I'd look elsewhere or prepare to do your own isolation.

title: Great Product for the Price
text:
I received my Ravelli tripod quickly and in perfect condition.

I have used the tripod many times, including in the middle of the night, in a foot of snow to take some long-exposure sky photos. It is very light, has metal legs with rubber feet and plastic components. It has so many different adjustment options that I'm able to set up the camera exactly how I want to.

There is a crank lever to allow the threaded center bar to go higher, a large swivel handle that goes up and down and side to side, a hinge type plate to do vertical or angled photos, and of course two levels of leg adjustments. Since there are a lot of adjustment knobs and levers you really have to be aware of what each one does. That way you don't accidentally add too much pressure to an adjuster when it doesn't do what you want it to and breaks. The product is all plastic, so I can see if handled roughly where this could happen. I haven't had any problems though. There are also two bubble gauges to make sure everything is set level.

The bag is handy and durable, but since it takes a bit of time to squeeze the tripod in and out of it, I usually do without it. The tripod has a handle on it which makes it easy to carry anyway.

I also always just leave the quick release plate attached to my DSLR. It makes for a quicker set-up. If I forget to check if the knob on the bottom of the plate is tight, the camera plate does slowly move downwards if I'm taking vertical photos. I use a Nikon D5100 with an 18-55mm lens and the tripod doesn't have any problem holding it that way... if it's tight. There is also a hook in the center of the tripod which can be used to hold weight for added stability, which a lot of the previous reviewers didn't mention. I haven't needed to use it though.

All in all I was happily surprised at the quality and design of the tripod for the price.

title: It's a suction cup, not a sticky gel pad
text:
Don't call it a "sticky gel pad" it's a suction cup! I misinterpreted this during the install and placed the second sticky gel between the suction cup and dash pad. It became a permanent mount that worked very well but when it came time to remove, it's unusable for the next car.

Very disappointed!!

*UPDATED*
iOttie replied almost immediately after writing my initial review. Taking her advice I sent iOttie Customer Service an email. The email reply wasn't as quick as the response I received here on Amazon. Approximately 5 days later I followed up with a second email expressing my disappointment and had expected a quicker reply based on what I had already experienced. This got the ball rolling where IIRC I sent two more emails. The first was answering some of their questions and confirming what I had already tried. While the next was simply an email giving them my mailing address. 5 days later I had received a replacement.

There were some product development changes from the first product received as compared to the second. The first contained separate sticky gel pads that the consumer was to place on the surfaces of the suction cup and on the dash mat. However, on the second product, both the suction cup and dash are already sticky. A much thinner sticky surface vs a separate, thicker gel pad.

I probably would have given this product a 4 Star rating initially. If I hadn't had any problems. Hard to get too excited over a phone holder. If I were to average out my experience, I'd probably give it a 4 Star rating. But I'm going to side with customer service on this one because it is what separates this from many other companies. 5 Stars!!

title: I like these cases; you may or may not.
text:
These *are* lightweight and not-amazing-quality cases whose faux-leather skin starts to flake off after a couple/few months' use, but the structural integrity, and so the functionality, of the cases lasts much longer and I'll probably continue to buy them as long as Reiko continues to make them, as they're of the form-factor I like - horizontal carry with full belt loops - and the magnetic closure makes them extremely easy and intuitive to use - I take my phone out of the case many times a day without even thinking about it; opening this case and pulling out the phone has long become a physical action my brain doesn't need to pay much attention to at all. Sometimes getting the phone back in is a little clunkier - the top flap can "close" into the inside of the case, requiring pulling out before the phone can be put in - and at other times, like when I'm driving, it can be hard to tell just *where* the flap's gotten to without examining the case by eye (which isn't practical while driving - which is why I've taken to usually leaving my phone on the center console, where I can see it at a glance, instead of in the case when I drive).

In short, this case has pluses and minuses, but for me the pluses way outweigh the minuses. Each person will have to make their own determination as to whether thats...*the case!* (har har har!!...sorry)...for them.

My wrists are small, so I have to size the bands down as small as possible, with the buckle nearly touching one of the connectors. So that means the buckle sits right on my wrist bone, and every time I move my wrist, the sides dig into my skin.

title: Big phone grip, limited adjustability
text:
As the name implies, the RhinoShield GRIPMAX is a BIG phone grip. I have a Note 20 Ultra, a big phone, and the grip leaves about ¾ of an inch between the camera and the bottom of the phone. So I would definitely check the size of your phone against this grip, or maybe use it on a tablet.

The GRIPMAX measures 3¾ inches tall and 2⅜ inches wide.

It folds flat, and it’s about ¼ of an inch thick. So it doesn’t stick out too far from the phone back, and doesn’t get caught on my pocket when I take my phone in and out.

I have the Geometric Wolf design, which looks to be printed on the grip. So it should hold up. I can actually feel the lines of the design, a nice little tactile bonus.

The GRIPMAX supports the weight of my phone in landscape or portrait orientation. The grip itself doesn’t rotate like a ring or popsocket, so I have to set my phone in either orientation.

I do wish the angle of the grip was adjustable. It’s either opened or closed, there’s no in-between.

title: Works for reading ebooks
text:
I use this Tik Tok Bluetooth Remote Control solely when reading ebooks. I like to read in bed, but it’s not always comfortable to hold my phone in such a way that I can turn the page. Sometimes I just want to prop my phone up and read without reaching for the screen every few seconds.

So that’s why this ring appealed to me. Put it on a finger and tap the buttons to turn the pages.

There aren’t any instructions for ebook reading. Sure, using the ring remote is pretty simple -- tap the buttons -- but at first I couldn’t get it to work with the Kindle app. The ring worked instantly with Moon+ Reader Pro; tap the back or forward button as needed. For the Kindle app, a tap did not work. I finally figured out that I have to long press the buttons to get a page turn in the Kindle app.

The ring is made from plastic that is really slippery. The ring is top heavy, so it constantly spins on my finger. I understand the ring band is open to fit a range of finger sizes, but I wish it had some texture or grip.

The charging case is proprietary. The ring goes inside the case, the case charges via USB-C. You cannot plug a cord directly into the ring itself.

title: Speck Products Presidio Grip Case for iPhone 8 Plus (Also fits 7 Plus and 6S/6 Plus), Black
text:
My mother recently switched to an iPhone 8 Plus after years with a normal 6, so she wanted a case that would help her get used to the bigger width of the phone. This is the third case we tried, and the one she liked the most because of all the grippy rubber that was part of the case.

This Speck case has a grippy back and sides, so she never felt like she was going to drop her phone. At the same time, she didn’t want a bulky case, and this one definitely isn’t. The profile is pretty slim, nothing like an Otterbox.

The case fits the iPhone 8 well, with button covers and cutouts, and it’s very easy to put on and off when she wants to try a different case.

title: Limited functionality, low quality band, and disproportionate price for what it offers
text:
I've worn watches since I was a teenager. Typically I prefer natural leather bands, as I have a skin condition where I develop contact dermatitis after prolonged contact with my own sweat. This watch has a silicon band, which does not absorb sweat and in fact seems to generate more sweat than other watch bands I have used in the past. This leaves me with rashes after several days, forcing me to switch wrists to deal with the rash. The band is also not sturdy, and has already broken twice, necessitating the purchase of a new band. Unfortunately a leather band is exhorbent in price from the manufacturer, so I was forced to replace with another silicon band.

The watch is pretty easy to use, but the flow app seems limited in several ways. A great example of this is monitoring my sleep. I have a non-24 hour sleep wake rhythm disorder so I do not sleep on a set schedule at a set time each night. The watch and flow app make me specify a time window when I normally sleep, but in reality this can quickly change from one day to the next. I could get 4 hours today, 12 tomorrow, 7 the next all at different sleep-wake times, depending on when my body clock wants rest. I can go for several days without sleep at all, or sleep 20 hours in one shot as well and the watch as well as the app do not seem designed to deal with this rapid or wild fluctuation. I have a higher resting heart rate than most people at around 100 bpm, which also confuses the watch making it think my cardio activity is elevated, when in reality it is resting. The flow link doesn't connect over wifi and requires a manual connection to sync, which I find inconvenient and outdated given bluetooth and wifi capabilities today. All in all, the watch is decent, but not worth several hundred dollars and in hindsight had I known all I do today about it, I would have went with something that offers better functionality and personalization.

title: Nicely built; very convenient form factor
text:
Normally I look for the maximum mAh when getting a powerbank since it gives me the ability to recharge multiple small devices, or even a couple large devices without running out of power. However, the large capacity ones are basically like carrying around a brick. This powerbank, while only offering 3000mAh, comes packaged as a very easy to take along format.

It's weighs only 2.5 ounces and is about 4.25 inches long and less than an inch thick. The case is plastic, but the quality is quite good, with nicely matched seams. All the edges are rounded so it feels comfortable to hold. The bottom edge is flat, and allows it to stand upright without toppling over.

Although it's small, it still has all the main features of a powerbank. It has one USB output (2.1A), a micro USB input for charging (with each port next to each other), and a 4 LED "gas gauge" that shows the charge level. On the end opposite the port it has an LED flashlight. Normally the flashlight feature is of minor use on a conventionally-shaped powerbank, but in this case it actually works very well as a flashlight. In fact, I could see people buying it mainly to use just for that. The flashlight lens is recessed and has a nicely designed surround.

It comes with two USB cables, both of which are stout and durable. It also comes with two lanyards: one that is long enough for neck use; another shorter one for (I imagine) wrist use. Since the powerbank is so small and light, wearing it on a lanyard is very feasible. The lanyard construction is just so-so, but decent enough for general use. It also comes with a user guide that is actually helpful and well-written. Don't see that much anymore!

Operation is fine - works just like any other powerbank. But, to be useful, a powerbank has to be carried along with you. The size makes that very easy to do, and the flashlight performance and design makes this even more useful to carry with you. Despite the fact that it has only a 3000mAh capacity, I would recommend this highly.
[Sample provided for review]

title: Sleek look; excellent quality construction; some constraints on what it can hold
text:
I was very impressed with the construction quality of this case. The leather is very smooth and supple. It has the feel of a high quality wallet. The stitching is even and tight. I could live without the embossed "V" logo at the base, but it's not too obtrusive.

The case fits the 5s very well, with no wriggling or rattle.

One of the benefits of the case is that it allows you to carry cash or credit cards in the pouch. Well in theory you could, but anything more than a single card makes the case bulge out and kills the sleek look. Plus, it's a tight fit to get anything in and out of the pouch.

You can also open the case and keep things in the midsection since it has a magnetic closure. Again, that's somewhat impractical - there is only one magnet at the upper corner, leaving the bottom corner unlatched. Slim, lightweight items (such as paper currency) stay put, but credit cards fell out when I gave it a shake test.

Still, it's well worth considering if you're looking for a nicely made, attractive leather case. Just don't expect it to serve as a pack mule - it can take a card or two, or perhaps a bill or two, but that's about it.
[Sample provided for review]

title: MUST HAVE for Sony A6400
text:
[[VIDEOID:391f52c189a28f6d0fe5cefb30022336]] This is absolutely the best all-around gimbal I have ever used. Does great with my Sony A6400 - all the features work when connected via the multi-cable. Phone mount holds my LG V60 in a case comfortably, too. Motors are surprisingly strong for such a lightweight device. A decent phone app to control things when not physically touching the gimbal rounds out the package.

The Pros:
Strength - Holds my mirrorless A6400, a Canon 200D/SL2 (though without added features), or a cell phone. Motors had zero issues, and everything stayed stable. I was concerned because the 200D is so much heavier with the kit lens, but it worked just fine.
Lightweight - I mean...It's really very light weight. Mixture of metal and plastic, but still feels very sturdy. I wasn't fatigued carrying it around with me.
Features - Can control many of the features on my Sony. It's comparable with other similar gimbals, but it has a few neat things such as the selfie mode and in inception mode. I especially like the selfie mode. Will be handy for vlogging.
Battery - About four hours of use and I'm at about 50% on the battery. This was a mixture of BT connection to phone, wired connection to camera, and general real world use. Shouldn't have any issues reaching about 8 hours per charge. Almost double the time I get from my heavier gimbal.
Speed - Following mode works very well. The reaction time from the gimbal is quicker than I expected. Will be nice to use this feature when moving around at my desk.
Balancing - Seriously only needs TINY adjustments to balance. I marked the perfect places for each camera with a different color paint pen. Phone is the hardest to balance simply because of the odd shape.

The Cons: (Minor nitpicks)
Tripod - I wish it was about an inch wider. Would provide substantially more stability. It works fine, but I feel like it might tip over when using it with my phone. With an actual camera attached, it is heavy enough that it doesn't move.
Cable Length - I kinda wish the cables were a few inches longer. The milti-cable for the A6400 is fine in normal use, and doesn't hinder mobility except in "inception" mode. This is where the couple extra inches would be handy. Otherwise the cables are long enough.

Final thoughts: This is an exceptional gimbal for the price. I have tried gimbals priced a hundred dollars higher that provide the same gimbal functionality but lack in the software department or camera control. This is my go-to gimbal. G6Max handles every camera I own, is really easy to use, and is light enough that I am comfortable taking it with me. I'm extremely impressed.

title: Nice Overall
text: I'm using mine with the iPhone 6. The box that it comes in has a handy ruler on the side so you can actually tell if the case is the correct size for your particular phone. This cell phone armband has several features that make it quite nice. First, it has two loops on the band that give it the ability to work on very small up to quite large arms. The loops are for the initial adjustment and the Velcro is what actually fastens the band. The actual phone case is separate from the band, held together by a clip, giving you the ability to remove the case from the band while the band is on the arm. The zipper pull and the armband both have reflectivity, which I really like since I do most of my exercise in the dark hours. Another feature that I really like is that the case is "weather resistant", meaning that the zipper is constructed out of a material that, I believe, would be quite effective keeping moisture out in the case of a light shower. However, the actual material of the case is neoprene and would let moisture penetrate, so it's definitely not for a major rainstorm. But even at that, I think the weather resistance is a benefit. The band is comfortable and relatively secure, but as with a lot of sport cases I've seen, needs something to secure the zipper to keep it from flopping.

This booster comes with an indoor antennae that is meant to be installed on the ceiling, an antennae to install outside high enough up to get a clear shot to the nearest tower and the actual booster itself that both antennae connect to via cables. This booster works well for us out here and I think it would be a good option for people living in the country like us, but be sure to check what band your service uses before you order it. text:
Since the S10 is still very new, it'll probably be a bit longer before we start seeing any tempered glass screen protectors that will still work with the fingerprint scanner. I picked this up since I have used IQ Shield for my Switch and its still looking good, and the screen protector on the S10 is complete garbage. Thankfully this screen protector meets my current needs. I think it'll do for most people, but its not perfect:

Pros:
-Cheap
-Works with fingerprint scanner
-More durable than the standard one the phone comes with
-Easy to apply

Cons:
-Isn't going to protect from a drop, just scratching (not really the fault of the screen protector, you'd need tempered glass for that)
-This is more just an issue with trying to apply any screen protector to the curved edges, but I CANNOT get the edges totally sealed against the glass. No matter how hard or long I pressed on the edges, there was still a very very very thin line along the edge where it wasn't sticking. Honestly, the only way I can see getting around this is if the cover was manufactured to already be curved or stronger adhesive (but then you have other issues with phone damage).
-Instructions need to be more clear. No specific times are noted just "when it dries" or "few hours". All-in-all, you can't really beat this protector for this price and IQ shield has already proven they can do a fine job on both my Switch and Charge 3, so I'd consider them reliable.

title: Good Screen Protector
text:
Some of the negative reviews here are a bit confusing. I'm writing this one primarily to set a few records straight.

First of all, these screen protectors are stickers. They're thin plastic. Their purpose is to add a layer of cheap material over your expensive glass screen in order to prevent scuffs, scratches, chips, etc. The reason you get six in the package is that these are not supposed to be durable! They're expendable and disposable. You use one until it wears out, then you use another.

Second, installation is an absolute breeze. I've used lots of these sorts of products for my devices over the years and this one had one of the easiest installations I've ever done. Anyone who is complaining that it took them four tries or whatever, didn't bother actually watching the installation video. The protector also wraps around the curvature of the Versa 2 just fine. Again, you need to watch the video and do it at the right time. I recommend watching both the watch video and the "curved device" video as you'll get tips in each.

Here's a quick run-down of how to properly install:
- First of all, you need a dust-free area. A good tip for this is to use your bathroom, immediately after a shower. The water vapor will drag a lot of the dust out of the air.
- Second, make sure your hands are clean and oil-free. See the shower tip.
- Next, use scissors and cut out one protector -- you'll be spraying it with a bunch of liquid and there's no reason to get the adjacent ones wet.
- Now spray the watch face with the included solution. One spray seems to be sufficient here.
- Now spray the fingers on both of your hands. Don't worry, the solution doesn't smell especially bad.
- Now spray the front of the protector.
- Now use your wet fingers and peel up the protector and liberally spray the back.
- Finally, put the protector in place on the watch. Slide it around a bit into position. Hold half of it in place with your thumb and squeegee the liquid out from the other half. The protector will shift a bit. Gently push it back into place. Then hold and squeegee again, in a different direction. (I alternate Up-Right-Down-Left when doing this so I get equal coverage.)
- Keep repeating the above step until the protector starts to stick to the watch. Then give it a couple of final swipes with the squeegee.
- The curved edges will not be in place at this point. That's okay! Put the watch down and walk away for 15 minutes.
- Now come back and using the microfiber cloth gently polish/press the protector, from the middle outward, all the way into the curved edges. They'll stick. Push them evenly around the face of the watch and all will be great.
- And finally, wait 8 hours. Come back and give the edges another little pass if you need to.

I'm deducting one star primarily for that 8 hour wait. I've never had to do that before. The installation instructions mention a hair dryer for quicker drying but they also mention simply doing this right before bed, and that seems to be an easier and perhaps better option.

Once in place, the screen protector is crystal clear and doesn't interfere in any way with using your watch. Which is really all you can ask for. I'd like these to be ever-so-slightly wider. They don't quite cover the entire glass face of the watch. (They're short by maybe 1mm.) That's fine from a usability perspective and you can barely see it but I think a bit more edge-to-edge coverage would help improve snag resistance. These sorts of protectors, for me, always seem to wear out at the side because a bit of lint or dirt gets under the edge and destroys adhesion, so having the protector right up against the metal would help.

Anyway, that's that. Easy install, great clarity, does what it's supposed to do. No real complaints except the 8 hour set time, but even that is not a very big deal. Good product.

title: Great adapter, with some tweaking
text:
I already wore a watch as a pendant, so when my husband gave me an Apple Watch series 4 (40mm), I wanted to do the same thing. This pendant adapter was exactly what I wanted for a couple of reasons:

1) The adapter pieces are made of high-quality metal, so I knew they wouldn't break or accidentally allow my watch to fall.
2) I wanted only the connector; I didn't want a case or any additional weight around my neck.
3) This adapter let me hang the watch upside down so that I could use it without having to turn the watch around to read it.

The first set I ordered had a problem: the loops were twisted (not parallel to the thin metal connector), so I couldn't slide that half into the bottom of the watch (hanging upside down). I requested an exchange, and received a proper replacement set.

The second time the loops were too close to the metal connector, so I very carefully squeezed the loops closer together so that there was more clearance between the slide and the loops. That worked! Now my watch sits securely around my neck. With a sufficiently long chain (30 inches), I can look down to read and interact with my watch.

Photo 1: Loops on the bottom of the watch
Photo 2: Shows the very tight clearance between loops and watch body
Photo 3: The angle at which I squeezed the loops
Photo 4: Exact placement of the pliers.

Do this only if the adapter doesn't slide into the watch groove easily! I hope you enjoy this set as much as I do.

title: Works as advertised but some trial and error may be required.
text:
It took me a while to figure it out, but apparently depending on your particular TV model, the connection sequence really matters. If you happen to have Vizio and you keep getting "No signal" on your TV, try the following connection sequence:
1. Turn on TV and set Input to whatever HDMI port you will be connecting your phone to.
2. Plug in Powered micro-USB cable into the female micro-USB socket on the side of the adapter.
3. Plug in the other end of the HDMI cable from your TV to the female HDMI socket on the adapter.
4. The very last step, after everything is connected, plug in the adapter into micro-USB socket on your phone.

The phone should instantly recognize the connection and display "HDMI Video Out Connected" on the notification bar. Once your phone is connected - you will see your phone's display being duplicated on the TV screen. You will be able to play games or watch movies streamed to your phone directly from Amazon or other services, if your TV does not have its own internet connection.

Just to be safe like working with computers, he used a piece of wood for grounding (by simply touching it) so that he wouldn't transfer any static discharge to the phone. Your expertise at playing operation will come in handy! Lol I'm charging it now but it worked immediately after installation. Not sure how long I should be charging it or how often I should do so. But I'm super excited about not having to keep it constantly plugged in for it to work. Being this early, I will give an update at a later date.

EDIT 11/20/14: After receiving a firestorm of bad reviews their first week of delivery due to having the wrong sized case in the box, this company's CEO must have messaged all the unhappy people to promise them they would do the right thing. The correct item was shipped the next possible business day. And as a good gesture for the inconvenience, they did not ask for the first case back.

PROS:
-Well made, stitching seems very strong.
-Easily fits 3 cards, but I still keep my cash separately.
-All the cut outs are spot on.
-I have not had any trouble controlling any of the buttons.
-Very thin around the edges of the case, so it does not make the phone seem too much bigger. Still fits in my car mount.
-Credit card stand slot is a nice feature.

POSSIBLE IMPROVEMENTS:
-When inserting a credit card into the stand slot, it sits at almost a 90 degree angle. It would be nice if the slot could be angled slightly so viewing could be at 75-80 degree angle
-Different color cases would be nice. I understand the leather needing to be black, but the rubber portion that protects the phone should come in different colors. I like red cases because it's easier to find the phone. A lot of furniture, wires, and other devices are dark in color. Having a brighter colored case makes it easier to find your phone.

Thanks again to this company for stepping up and correcting a small fiasco during this item's launch!!

title: This is not an iPhone so don't expect iPhone quality...BUT
text: The old saying, "You get what you pay for" may actually NOT apply here! The phone has great call quality for the price and is an excellent starter phone for teens who have a tendency to drop, lose, or otherwise abuse their phones. This would be easy enough to replace. No contracts is an additional plus. It is Wi-Fi ready right out of the box, and yes, it can make WiFi calls, too! There is a Goigle app that allows you to even get your own phone number and make as well as receive calls using just WiFi for peanuts a year...and it includes voice mail as well. The camera is not all that great in megapixel, but it will suffice for teen use, believe me. The screen is just about as bright as my iPhone 6s, but definitely not as vibrant, but again, this is a phone...you are not buying a movie player or camera. I have found that the battery longevity varies, truly depending upon what programs you install and if they are allowed to run "in the background." The fact that you can install up to 64 GB of memory beats an iPhone hands down. Finally, just remember, the more programs that you add to this phone, despite the additional memory, the faster the battery will drain! For the price, this phone cannot be beat!

title: Good phone protection with Poor screen touch recognition
text:
The case makes your phone seem solid and indestructible. I like the texturing and the slight rubberized feel to help make it feel like I have a great grip on this phone. The screen seems to be protected and completely visible. The clip fingers feel like they will hold on to a belt buckle without any issues.

The biggest problem is that the screens sensitivity is diminished by too much. I used to be able to lightly have my finger on the screen without any issues in movement. Now I have to press down and sometimes it still isn't recognizing my movements. I have tried to verify that the screen protector is on properly and regularly press down around the screen and on the screen protector to try to get better recognition. I also made sure that my old screen protector was off before putting on this case. For reference, I was using this screen protector as well as a couple of different supcase cases as are linked to below: [[ASIN:B01ACXSKAG Armorsuit MilitaryShield Anti-Bubble Ultra HD Case Friendly Screen Protector for Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge - Clear]]

The case really bulk up the phone to the point it looks twice the size it is when naked.
The belt clip doesn't feel as strong as the Supcase I used previously. [[ASIN:B01BLI4FWI Galaxy S7 Edge Case, SUPCASE Full-body Rugged Holster Case WITHOUT Screen Protector for Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge (2016 Release), Unicorn Beetle PRO Series - Retail Package(Black/Black)]]
This case blocks out the beauty of the phone itself (as do a lot of cases), I wanted to try a case that allowed most of the back to be seen, such as this one: [[ASIN:B01BLIBS0A Galaxy S7 Edge Case, SUPCASE Unicorn Beetle Series Premium Hybrid Protective Clear Case for Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge 2016 Release, Retail Package (Frost/Black)]]

All-in-all, I am disappointed by this case as I wanted to like it. The built-in screen protector really is a deal breaker on this case as I can't keep trying to check my notifications 5 times before it decides that it recognizes me touching up there, and not the bottom of the screen at the end of the movement.

title: Included template is a brilliant additon
text:
I purchased this case because both my girlfriend and another friend have it, and love it.

It fits perfectly. All necessary ports are clear. It went on easy and seems to provide a decent amount of protection. I've only had mine for a few weeks but my girlfriend has had hers for over a year and it hasn't yellowed at all.

I love the template that comes with it, that allows you to cut out and place your own pictures or designs inside the back of the case. This is brilliant for a clear case and one of the reasons I chose this over another case. I'm not a fan of the volume buttons on the 5x. They feel loose and kind of cheap. This case actually IMPROVES the feel of the volume buttons making them feel more substantial and providing more feedback when you press them. The case is slim and doesn't add much bulk to the phone, but GREATLY improves the feel in your had. The naked 5x felt too thin and like it could slip out of my hand at any moment. This case is smoth, and not sicky but sill provides great grip.

The only thing I would improve...the "feet" on the back are a little rough feeling. And still don't lift the phone enough for the camera to not touch the surface it's resting on, but that's minor and to be expected with a case this slim.

title: No Luck Using This One.
text:
I'm going to be one of the few dissenting opinions on this screen protector. Here is my little saga with the Armorsuit Shield -

When I got my brand new S7 edge I wanted it really protected. I have never used a screen protector on a phone before - I've also never paid so much for a phone before!! I had a case and the Armorsuit before I bought the phone!! I put the screen protector on just after getting the phone all set up and ready to go.

The application was really easy. I love wet application covers (used them for my fitbit) as they are so much more forgiving than the dry application. You can really take your time and get good alignment. This protector is great as far as the size and cut out spaces. It fits perfectly and leaves the tiniest of margins along the edge to prevent your case from lifting the corners.

That's where the love ends. After several days the screen still looked hazy. A slight rainbow (the plastic film) was always present on my screen and was particularly annoying when a lot of white was present on the screen (like when reading). Any tiny bubbles did disappear but it never got clear.

After about 2 weeks - YEP- the screen had lifted up and rolled back on itself. It was a mess! Lint and crud stuck to it. I removed the Armorsuit and tried to pick all the crap off, but a good bit remained and the smudges never really came out. I also noticed that my screen was not as responsive after putting the Armorshield back on again. I think messing up the adhesive reduced the sensitivity. It was a real pain - but something I didn't notice when the screen protector was first applied. I think this was from removing and replacing it. After a few days I just pulled it off. As far as this being "reusable", don't bank on it. If you take it off for any reason - stuff will stick to the back side and you'll never get it clean again.

To save my phone I do want to at least try another protector - but I'll be trying out another brand this time.

I ended up having to take my watch to a jeweler to get the band off without damaging my new Galaxy Watch 4 Classic which added a nice little service charge on top my bad experience. Now I am left a little perplexed because I have been rather happy with my other Ritche bands but I have little desire to risk trying any more. In fact I have set aside my other Ritche bands until I can talk to customer service and find out how in the world the little knob could break off or how to remove when it does. The jeweler used what looked like a dremel to cut the pin and he said he had never seen a band like this have the quick release break like this. So, I am back to using my Samsung bands for now. Just be aware of this issue. People should just be aware of the issue and this may be a one off as well as I haven't had any issues with my other bands. Maybe I will work up enough courage to try one of my other bands after I talk to support and if so I will post an update. But even if it is a one off issue the band is still shorter than all my other bands so this particular band still might be an issue for some people especially if you have larger wrists like myself.

If you continue to place the instruction sheet inside the case....make sure said instructions are visible and not obscured by the shoulder strap to make it easy to open the case. Regardless of the country of manufacture do the world a favor and have the instructions written of at least proofread by someone that actually is conversant with the language of your target market. Although stylish, inexpensive and ergonomically designed, the plastics that make up the two-piece (a soft inner sleeve and a hard, back-only half sleeve that slips over it) case unfortunately pick up a static charge each time the encased phone is slid in and out of the back pocket where I keep it. This results in the iPhone 5's glass screen being perpetually dusty, and in need of a wipe. I'm certain that it's the case that is the cause because I did a two day test, removing the case to see if the dust accumulation would go away. It did, but returned instantly when I put the case back on. Not a disaster, but not something that I am particularly happy with. I suppose I will eventually try another case when I get fed up with cleaning the screen all the time.

J.M. Tepper

I could've sent it back to them and gotten a replacement for $18.95(+ my cost of shipping) but I decided if I'm going to pay that, I'd rather order the Tech Armor for $14.95 or so. The Spigen was good, but it is a little thicker than the other ones. It's .4mm versus the Tech Armor and Skinomi which are .33mm.

The Tech Armor one was a bit disappointing, as the edges started chipping away after a few weeks' use. The chips lead to cracks, for anyone wondering why that matters. I dropped the device and cracked the screen recently. The screen cracked, but the Tech Armor did not (yay?). I cracked it while removing it off the screen which led me to go shopping for another tempered glass.

I ordered the Skinomi since the price is reasonable, and the specs look identical to every other tempered glass. When I got it, the packaging was nice, the installation was simple, as i had previously experienced with my other glasses. I couldn't find the raised home button it supposedly came with. Not important (to me, at least), because I had purchased a pack of 18 on eBay for like $5.

So far it is smooth and clear. The only drawback which is pretty important is the fit. It is about 1mm too narrow. When applying, one edge is all the way to the edge of the device, but it left a 1mm gap on the other side, which is annoying. I will update with my experience if it does start chipping at the edges like my Tech Armor did. I have added a photo to show the narrowness in the fit.

Update #1: I could not find an option to add a photo =(

title: Great, but just not for me.
text:
An iPhone case is such a personal and subjective purchase. Personally, I loved many things about this case, but the drawbacks led me to return it. Here is my list of Pros/Cons:

********************
PROS:

1. SNUG FIT - very securely hugs the iPhone with absolutely ZERO chance of the case falling off or iPhone falling out.
2. LOW PROFILE - I love how this phone adds almost zero bulk to the sleek design of the iPhone 6.
3. STYLE - The lines are clean and the logo is subtle.
4. PRICE - Absolutely the best value, coming in at almost half the cost of other cases.
********************
CONS:

a. TEXTURE - I personally did not like the texture of the material. It was grippy enough to hold, but it felt a little too rough for my comfort.
b. COLOR - I ordered the frost, which had a strange muting effect on the gold back. I think I would have preferred just a solid grey or white.

********************
NOTES:

i. Some have complained about the low height of the front of the case, fearing that it may not properly protect the screen. I did not see this as an issue, as it definitely keeps the screen off a flat surface.
ii. I ultimately chose to return this case because of the dull color of the frost and the actual texture of the case. If they made this in a smoother texture and a solid white or grey, I would have kept this case.

title: Love these! A must-have for big phones.
text:
I've been buying these for my boyfriend for ages. He got used to using it with the iPhone 6 Plus, and it definitely improved his grip on the phone. I love them for this purpose too, because I have small hands, and am constantly afraid that I'm going to drop my phone when I'm trying to tap icons across the screen with only one hand.

The adhesive is very strong - neither me nor my partner has ever had one unstick itself from our phone. This also means that you need to be careful putting it on the device - make sure that you have the placement exact, and if you're a little picky about things being perfectly straight (like myself), line it up with care. The elastic is high quality, and doesn't stretch out. I suppose this might depend on the user and how careful they are with it, but mine have always stayed in great shape even after a full year of constant use.

You can apply these directly to the phone, but we always use them with a case so our devices are protected. Make sure your phone case is grease-free and has a flat back before you put it on. I usually swab mine with a little rubbing alcohol on a cotton ball, and then use a dry one to soak up excess liquid before I stick it down. Press the love handle down firmly and hold for a few seconds, and voila! Perfect.

title: Product Has Numerous Issues
text:
This speakerphone has numerous issues.
(1) The speaker phone will randomly disconnect and immediately re-connect which is annoying while driving as it announces this process for everybody in the car to hear. e.g. "discon....connected". I have a Galaxy Note 5 and an iPhone 6S and this happens with either phone.
(2) Speakerphone does not always announce "Power On" or "Power Off" when changing the position of the power switch.
(3) If the speakerphone does not understand a voice command it will sometimes just not answer back. For example saying "Battery" should provide the battery status but 9 times out of 10 it wont understand me and just does nothing. It does not even respond with "please say again" or whatever the correct response is.
(4) Speech recognition is poor. Using the battery status example above I have to say "baaatteeerrryyyy" for it to understand the command which is very unnatural and also embarrassing if you have passengers in the vehicle with you.
When it is working, the speech is clear and callers say I sound fine. But it is more trouble than it is worth. Will review return process as this is not one of the cheaper options and I was expecting more from a name brand.
