title: Google Pixel 4a for the WIN!
text:
This phone was purchased after extensive research and positive first hand experience with the Pixel 3a. After several weeks of waiting for the new phone to ship after it was released, I am very pleased with the functionality of this new Pixel 4a.

One of the biggest selling points for this phone is the price. I didn’t want to finance another $800 phone from Verizon so I opted for an unlocked phone that I could purchase and connect to their network. This phone was a bargain at $349, but there is nothing cheap about this phone except for the price.

The Good: Besides winning on price, this phone was a breeze to set up. The SIM card easily inserted into the phone and it quickly connected to the Verizon network without issue. The set up instructions were easy to follow to get the phone up and running quickly. The Pixel 4a also transferred all data, apps, and pictures from my old Galaxy S7. It used a USB cable to connect and download everything. Even texts, voicemails, and everything else transferred over so I never felt lost. Google Chrome and Gmail are my primary browser and email so browsing history and saved passwords also transferred over. Apps needed to be logged into again and there were some forgotten password issues, but nothing that couldn't be fixed.

Once connected this phone operates smoothly and it is easy to navigate. It is a bit different than th 3a and other Android phone as there is no back button and everything is controlled through swipes. It takes some getting used to but works smoothly once you get it down. The camera is outstanding and surpasses any phone previously used. Another bonus with this phone is the battery life which ranks high on my list of important features. This battery lasts all day long even with regular use. The battery on the 3a is great and the battery on the 4a is awesome! It also charges very quickly with the provided charger and I estimate a full charge takes approximately one hour.

The Bad: The bad really isn’t all that bad when taken in proper context. There is a reason this phone is half the price of other models since it’s missing some luxury features. Apparently this phone isn’t waterproof, which comes as a surprise to me since I’ve never known any phone to be waterproof and am always careful with my phones around water. Wireless charging capability is also missing from this phone so you may miss that feature if wireless charging is your thing. It really isn't a big deal though since the battery lasts so long this phone is rarely on the charger anyway.

This phone does take a USC-C cable so it isn't compatible with the cables from older Android and Kindle devices, which use Micro USB cables. It comes with one USB-C cable but you may want to purchase another if you like extra ones around the house or in the car. Again, not a huge deal because of the battery life.

Summary: This is an outstanding phone and should work well for the vast majority of users. It operates and looks far more expensive than it really is, making me realize how much the phone companies are ripping us off selling overpriced phones. It wins in value, setup, camera, operating speed and battery life. Minor points are lost for missing some of the fancier features like wireless charging and being a different charging cable than most people already have, but those don’t weigh heavily on my opinion of this Google Pixel 4a so I am giving this a strong four stars.

title: Great case, great price.
text:
This fit my Google Pixel 3a like a glove and the phone is now we'll protected from all angles. This case has an appropriate raised edge so any drop won't crack or damage the screen. The power and volume buttons function properly and the ports are all fully accessable.

On that note, this won't provide much, if any, moisture protection like an OtterBox since the ports are all exposed so don't order this expecting your phone is all of a sudden waterproof.

This case grips well so it won't slide out of your hand. Also, the fingerprint reader and camera lens in the back are fully exposed so this case won't interfere with either of those functions.

My only negative remark is based on a prior experience with an identical Crave brand case. The hard outer shell can crack when dropped. In one respect it fully protected the phone so it did the job, but you may also find yourself needing to replace the case if you drop it in a hard surface, especially on the corner.

Overall this is a solid case and fits the Google Pixel 3a perfectly. It's also a bargain at under $12 so you're getting a great case at a great price.

title: Tempered Glass Protection!
text: I am one of those people who tend to drop their phone a lot. I leave it sit on the arm of the chair when I am sitting and invariably, it slips off and always crashes to the floor face down. Fact of life for me. So since my phone is an investment, I choose to always have a tempered glass screen protector on it. It has saved my actual phone screen more times than I care to count. Whether you are trying to protect your phone from cracks or chips from falling, or simply scratches and fingerprints from every day use, you should have a tempered glass screen protector. This protector pack is value for your money as it is a 2 pack and undoubtedly, I will end up going through both of them at some point! The screen protectors fit my screen well, I have an iphone 6 and did not receive protectors for the plus as some reviewers did. title: Recommended with reservations
text:
This is a pretty good little endoscope. I had gotten it as a "poor man's otoscope" (including my own ears) as well as peering into other difficult places where I can't get my head into. I have a Moto X Pure smartphone with Marshmallow Android. I couldn't get my OCR reader to pick up the code in the instructions, but I downloaded the first endoscope app I found (ScopeCam). At that point, I had no problem with using it in my smartphone. The LED light is a little weak, but I was able to see straight down to my ear drum. Having said that, if you are going to be looking behind a wall or some place dark, it is going to be lacking. As far as I can tell, there are only software settings to toggle it on/off (not brighter).

When I plugged the USB into Windows 10, it was recognized right away, but I needed to install the software from the mini-CD to get the viewer going. It was zipped in a RAR format, so you may have to google that if you haven't dealt with that before. Nothing hard about it. But I haven't used RAR in a few years and I'm sure it will confuse a lot of users. It would have been nice to have 2 folders--Android and PC. And then have the software already extracted in the PC folder. It's not like it took a lot of space. Also, the specs say that the endoscope has 1280*720 resolution in PC mode. ...my software was limited to 640*480. So the hardware may go up that high, but I was unable to test / verify it because of the software.

I received this product at a discount in exchange for a fair & honest review. This is not a bad endoscope. I'm not saying stay away from it. I'm just saying that your satisfaction will depend on usage. If it's a completely dark environment, you may be disappointed. But if you're trying to look between a wall, you'll likely be wanting a longer cable anyway. In other settings it works pretty well. It's nice to have my phone in one hand and have the endoscope in the other to peer behind something, especially without dragging 15' cable that some other brands have. My main recommendation to Verdy is to clean up the software-side of things.

title: unreliable performance
text: I really researched a new phone. My parameters were good battery life (check) and a good camera (big check) but I have been very disappointed with other functions.  As I got accustomed to the phone over the several months since I purchased it, I know that some glitches were my unfamiliarity with a different device.  However, by now, I pretty much know the phone and I have no explanation for the number of times that I have found out that the phone never rang or the text never notified me.  Or the phone was ringing but the screen wasn't showing a caller and I literally could not answer the call!!  My lesson has been to only buy from brick and mortar locations where I can return the faulty phone or seek the help of a real live human when needed. Santa will be getting a note from me for a new phone under the tree.

title: The Best Headset Available on the Market but Have the Right Expectations
text:
This headset is not perfectly perfect in every way but it is the best that you can buy.

This is the only headset in the Plantronics lineup listed as having "premium" quality sound. It is Plantronics' flagship headset. Plantronics is the industry leader in earpiece headsets. If you are looking for the highest-quality headset you can buy, look no more. You have come to the right page.

The primary complaint I've read about on the Plantronics customer service site is that after two years the battery will die a natural death due to old age. So do realize that this will not last forever. If your battery dies while the headset is under warranty, that's too soon and Plantronics will replace it. If your battery dies in less than 2 years but out of warranty, Plantronics is currently offering customers substantial discounts to buy replacements. (Save your receipt! Scan it if you're paperless. Or buy it from Amazon where they will keep a record for you.)

I just bought my second one - the first lasted about 4 years for me with light use. I did read that some can get extra life out of their battery by putting the headset into a ziploc and then into the freezer overnight... so if you're here for a replacement, you might try that first and buy a little more time. I got a few extra months out of mine by discarding the (optional accessory) case I was using to charge it and by charging it directly through the OEM cord that came with it (so save that too!).

WHAT YOU GET:
Packaging is Easy to Open: there is a large sticker sealing the opening to the smallish box closed. That is easily cut with a pair of scissors. Then pull out the cardboard wings that are tucked into slots on each side of the front of the box and open it up.
- Plantronics headset (battery is permanently installed)
- Proprietary charging cord with separate wall plug
- Two additional ear plugs -- larger and smaller than the one preinstalled on the headset
- Foam covers for the ear plugs, to use or not as you prefer
- Instruction Booklet
- Instructions on Firmware Update
- Safety Warnings
- Some stuff in another language

The cord is USB on the wall end and proprietary on the headset end (only matches the headset). That means that you can plug the cord into the computer to get firmware and software updates from Plantronics (which is the first thing that they recommend you do upon unpackaging your headset). The cord is short, just under 10" long (without the connectors).

It's easy to change the ear plugs in and out so that you can try different sizes. You just press in and turn to the left. To insert one, you press in and turn to the right. (All of this is in the instruction book.) I found that I could use the small or the medium. I'm a 5'7" woman who weighs more than she should but you wouldn't hate sitting next to me on a plane. The ear plug sits loosely just inside your ear. You may not even feel it. It's definitely not a snug fit and you will hear surrounding sounds in both ears. What keeps the headset in place is the rest of it, not the ear plug.

The boom mic is adjustable. I found it was directly pointed toward my mouth in it's lowest position.

The device has a call button on the round part, from which the boom extends. That's for taking and ending calls if you don't want to use voice commands, which also work. On the underside of the boom is another button that mutes calls among other things. There is a volume rocker on the upper back part of the largest part of the device -- the part that goes behind the ear. And below that is the on/off switch. At the bottom of the back is the charging connector -- just a bit of recessed coppery looking metal.

It reads "Plantronics" in very subtle small pale gray lettering at the bottom of the largest part of the device, on both sides. You can see where it is in the small shiny black part at the bottom of the picture.

If you have the right expectations (it's not a magic genie... It may only last for two years... A very few of them will be defective and will require replacement...), you will be delighted with your purchase. You will not find better sound quality anywhere else. If you are used to music headphones, the looser, more open feel of the headset in your ear (or barely touching the front of your ear), might take some adjustment.

I highly recommend this product and am confident that, if after reading this review you still want it, you will not be disappointed.

UPDATE: One feature I have come to really appreciate is the voice commands. Some parts of my house get spotty cell phone reception. So, when I'm wearing the headset (during work hours), I always leave my phone in a "good reception area" of the house. If a call comes in, I don't have to rush back to the headset to pick it up, I just say, "answer" and the headset picks up the call. If the caller is in my address book, the phone will announce who's calling. If I'm silent or say "decline," the call is not picked up.

title: LOVE! LOVE! LOVE IT!!
text: LOVE! LOVE! LOVE IT!! I'm not one who usually does a lot of reviews. The ones I do are usually quick and short. This one is longer, but I think will really be helpful to those on a quest for a DECENT phone case for their Zenfone2.  I'm Excited because after three weeks of searching I have FINALLY found a case that lives up to the description. I pray this review helps someone who is searching for a DECENT, FUNCTIONAL and PROTECTIVE case for the Asus ZenFone2. I went thru FOUR different cases that were cheap plastic, slippery and NOT shock absorbent even though they claimed they were. FUNCTIONALITY: All of the buttons and ports line up perfectly. This one works perfectly when turning the phone on and off!!!! HALLELUJAH!! One of the other cases I tried didn't work at all in that regard. As many of you Zenfone2 owners know, it's a GREAT PHONE, however a design flaw is that the on/off button is not the easiest to operate. Locating the button at the top of the phone instead of the side was a smart move by Asus, however the button is very small and kind of recessed so some if the case manufacturers did a poor job of designing their cases to actually function with the on/off button. This case actually makes it EASIER to turn the phone on and off!!  MATERIALS & SHOCK ABSORBANCY: I wanted and needed the soft rubber, shock absorbent, nice grip "Tire like" material and all I could find were sad limitations made of cheap hard plastic or plastic covered cardboard like wallet cases that were slippery and not shock absorbent. This case is the type that can be used two ways. Use the rubber shock absorbent, slim layer by itself or attach the hard shell. The shell has a texturized back which is a plus.  I have four stars instead of five because the only thing I find not perfect about this case is that although it is not super slippery like the others. The sides of the shell layer could use a little strip of some type of texture for gripping like the back. I will fix that by attaching some little Velcro Brand Grippers sold at Wal-Mart and craft stores. Hope this review saves someone the pains of searching for a DECENT, FUNCTIONAL, SHOCK ABSORBENT Phone Case!

title: Overall good case with some issues.
text: The reason I chose to purchase this case specifically even though it's manufactured by a company that I've never heard of is because this was the only case for the Samsung Galaxy s23+ that includes a built-in screen protector and a holster. The case fits the phone well, and is sturdy, although not as sturdy as Otterbox or Supcase or Unicorn Beetle. I noticed in the reviews some people complaining about issues with fingerprint scanning through the built-in screen protector. I have not had this issue and fingerprint scanning works great. You must make sure that there is no dirt or air between the screen and the inside of the screen protector. Make sure to properly train the fingerprint in. Lastly, you need to press your finger FIRMLY for it to be read. I rarely have a misread and it works 99.9% of the time. My only complaint is that the way this case is engineered, when you try to slide the phone into the holster, the outside rubber housing of the case snags on the holster and starts to come off. This is a pretty major issue if you ask me, and needs to be addressed. For this reason alone I would not repurchase this case. For now, I will stick with this case until something better comes along.

title: Don't waste your money . . . and don't make the same mistake I did . . .
text:
When this case was not available from Amazon (from Davis Case), I ordered it on the Davis Case website. I wish I hadn't. While the leather and construction are very good, that's the only good thing I can say about it. The overall design SUCKS.

First, if you actually need to put just one card in every slot, you WILL NOT be able to close the case and keep it closed with the "magnetic" strap. Apparently, no one ever tested the design with actual credit cards in the pockets. If you also need to carry some cash or store some receipts as well, forget it.

Second, one of the best features of the Note 9 is the ability to use a wireless charger. With this case, that's an impossibility for two reasons. the magnet that hold the "detachable" phone enclosure to the case completely prevents the phone from charging, attached to the case or not.

If the first flaw doesn't bother you, and you don't use a rapid charger, then I suppose you might like this case. But I hated it and threw it in the trash. What was my mistake . . . I couldn't return it because I had already cut the closure strap off before I discovered the charging flaw.

title: A true and honest review
text:
I want to make a very clear comparison between this case and another case I purchased earlier this year from another Amazon vendor and made by Tucch. In two months I have dropped my iPhone in the Tucch case on two separate occasions - the first time the top left corner and the back of the hard plastic case broke, the 2nd time the top right side broke, as did my iPhone screen. So I've managed to destroy the protective Tucch case and lost $179.99 to Apple for the phone repair.

Thus, the reason why I ordered this particular case. This case arrived on time and appears constructed very well. The leather and stitching are really nice. The actual case inside is NOT hard plastic, it's rubber. It completely surrounds the phone on all 4 sides vs. covering only the corners like other cases. This seems to be a much better design, but only time will tell. History says I'll drop my phone soon enough to fully test it out.

I currently have (3) credit cards, drivers license, and (2) gift cards in the card slots and in the space behind the card slots. So it holds plenty. The foldable stand function is quite a nice surprise, although not why I bought the case. But cool enough that I may just use it.

Overall, I recommend this case. It's a keeper.

title: A great set of ballpoints for everyday use with styli for occasional use
text:
This review is for the 12 pack of ballpoint/stylus combo pens. Originally because of the iPad mentioned in the description and because this listing also has the other kinds of tablet pencils that you can use for artwork on your tablet, I thought these were stylus’s with very narrow ends for precision work. What I saw as the tapered end was actually the ballpoint part of the pen- so that was a bit confusing for someone watching a show, while skimming on Amazon for something to help with my Nonogram/sodoku games on my cell phone and something that I could also use as art pencil on my tablet.

However, I am quite happy with this really numerous set of pens/stylus’s. There are plenty to share with family. It states 6 colors but there are only 2 colors with 6 pens in each color. The pens are either silver or black. Both write in black ink as shown in the seller’s photos. The pens write well and it’s always nice to have a pen that can be turned around as a stylus in a pinch.

To summarize:
Pros
1. You get 12 of them!
2. You have a pen right there with the stylus. Multitool devices are handy.
3. The pens and stylus’s do work.
4. On a tablet, the stylus was good for signing documents or any type of large writing. It glides smoothly along the glass.
5. Can use this in stores for touch screens or number pads during pandemic
6. The rubber spherical pad is a lot nicer than my 10 year old stylus that had more of a sponge type end.

Cons
1. You get 12 of them...(maybe about 8 too many?)
2. When you use the stylus for longer periods, the clip for the pen part (like the clip if you wanted to attach this to your shirt pocket) gets in the way of a natural stylus grip. I had indents on my finger from the clip when trying to assess how well the stylus works.
3. The stylus itself while described in the details as ultra-sensitive touch and accurate writing didn’t quite live up to my hopes. On the iPhone 11 Pro Max phone it was only marginally better than my finger at nonogram games. It often would hit a square next to the one I was trying to put a mark in. Which was the top reason I had desired a stylus. It had a hard time nearer the edge of the screen to register as well.

title: All in one pack for new phone
text:
Having a case, screen protector, and camera protector all in one kit is very convenient and cost effective.
The kit included two tempered glass screen protectors, two camera protectors, two sets of wipes, two sets of stickers, and one case. What it did not include was any instructions on how to install the screen protector or camera protectors. While I've installed plenty of these in the past, I still like having instructions as each brand is a little different and sometimes there's tips that help to ensure a perfect install. This kit also did not include any kind of installation tray to make it easier to install the screen, it just included stickers. I had a few trays that came with protectors for an S22, unfortunately as the S23 is slightly different in size it would not fit in those trays. Installation of the screen protector was easy, but not as easy as others. Not wanting to get any dust on the protector I set it up with the stickers prior to removing the protective film. However the stickers popped off while I was removing the film and messed up the alignment so I had to remove it and try again only to find a speck of dust had snuck in, so I had to remove it, remove the speck and try again.
On the plastic sheet the camera protectors come on it does indicate which is the top and bottom so you can install it the right direction. As the cameras are symmetrical, I'm not exactly sure if there's any difference between the top and bottom, but I did make sure to install it in the orientation indicated.
Keep in mind that this is a tempered glass protector which will interfere with the on-screen fingerprint reader. If you plan on using the on-screen fingerprint reader you'll have more success with a plastic screen protector rather than glass.
The case fits well and allows full operation of all buttons.

title: Not as advertised - beware
text: This item is not tempered glass, it's plastic or very cheap glass at best. There seems to be 2-3 "tempered glass" screen protectors for the Note 8 for sale on Amazon, they are repackaged into slightly different packaging and sold as tempered glass. They are all cheap and chip within a few days, and have horrible adhesive, usually only on the edges. Because the adhesive is only on the edge, they also are not very sensitive to touch. I've been buying glass screen protectors for years for all the previous Note devices and never had problems like this. I've had to send back now counting six screen protectors in a couple months, and of the six, only 3 of them were unique products, even if they came in slightly different packaging or were from different buyers. Some of them have good ratings, too, and I'm not sure how they pulled it off... maybe fake? This is definitely a real review, do not waste your money on this if you want a screen protector that will do a good job and last.

title: Nice for the Price!
text:
Well, well. This is a perfect example of a product that I didn't know I needed until I got it. I've been using a clamp style vent mounted phone holder for about 8 months. Perfectly fine, but it requires a bit of time and strategy to get the phone secured into it. And both hands. But the opportunity to own this came up and I thought I'd give it a shot. I'm glad I did.

First, simply sitting the phone onto the magnetic connector instead of fighting with a spring is VERY nice. One less thing to bother with in the morning. The mount comes packaged with a 1.75 x 2.75 inch metal plate, the magnetic button to place on the vent and extra adhesive pads. I use a thick Otterbox Defender case because I'm really good at dropping phones. I first tried inserting the plate inside the plastic inner case which did not work, as the case was too thick to allow the magnetic connection. I attached the plate to the outside of the plastic (but beneath the rubber outer case) and that worked fine. The connection to the magnet is quite strong. I drive a short, very bumpy section of dirt road several times a day and the phone stays securely attached to the mount, and the mount stays in the vent. The metal plate is very thin and light and added almost no weight to my already heavy case.

I've seen a few questions related to damage to the cars vent from using this. The actual connection is four steel pins which are covered in thick rubber. All car vents are different, but in my case I don't see how this could do any damage. One thing to keep in mind is that the connector has two ways of connecting. One direction is for thin vent blades, the other direction is for thicker blades. Make sure you look closely at which will be a better fit for your particular situation before using! I would also imagine the usefulness of this product would depend on the dashboard layout of your particular vehicle. I would prefer the phone to be sitting a bit more vertical than my car allows, but I'm not going to vote down the product because of this.

Overall the ALBK Magnetic Phone Holder seems to be a well made, clever little device that gets the job done and doesn't cost a fortune doing it.

Docked one star because the item was shipped in a small pillow pack envelope and the packaging was fairly severely crushed on receipt. The item was fine but I believe it wouldn't have taken much more rough handling in transit to have damaged the unit itself.

I was provided this product at a discounted price for review but if I had hated it, you'd know it!

I've tried 7 different glass screen protectors for my 5T. All of them had various issues: bubbles, rainbow effect in middle, dot pattern, edges not sticking, cutting off sides of screen with black bars

Some other pros: No rainbow effect, no bubbles, applied very easily, touch sensitivity is great since only 0.2mm thick.

The only negative that comes to mind is when looking at the phone from the side you see the light refract off the edges of the screen protector since it doesn't cover the full screen, treating your eyes to a colorful rainbow. title: 5 Star To 1 Star In Eight Hours
text:
I really wanted to like this booster, but it quit working after 8 hours of use so I sent it back. Amazon's return policy and performance was outstanding. Amazon gets 5 stars, but the booster only gets one.

I'm one of those guys who usually don't read the instructions, but in this case, I downloaded the manual and read it closely before I even ordered the booster. There are some specific conditions that need to be met and I wanted to ensure that the physical layout of my installation met those requirements. (It did) Because I had seen some critical reviews I decided to do a temporary installation before drilling holes and running cables. I ran the RG-6 cable through open windows instead of drilling holes through the walls. I mounted the Yagi antenna on a temporary 12 foot mast for aiming purposes. I moved the booster/antenna unit around in the house for best location testing purposes. I carefully aimed the Yagi antenna at the nearest Verizon Cell tower and fired up the system and it worked just fine. So far, so good. The cell tower was 14 miles away from my cabin in sparsely populated Northern Wisconsin and I was quite impressed. The before-booster one bar cell signal was -115 dbm signal strength inside the cabin. After-booster installation gave me a hugely improved -96 dbm signal strength inside the cabin which was a great improvement and gave me four bars on the phone. For reference, the cell tower signal strength outside of the cabin and before booster installation was between -112 to -102 dbm. (When you are dealing with signal strength readings in dbm the least negative reading is better. -1 dbm is about the best you can get. I used an app called "Network Cell Info Lite" to get signal measurements.) I tried the booster in several locations to give the best coverage in the cabin and sure enough, the best location had 30 feet of separation between the Yagi antenna and the inside antenna and the Yagi pointing away from the inside antenna. The indicator lights worked as described in the manual. I was a happy camper and was making plans to do the permanent installation on the next day. After watching a couple of hours of TV I decided to turn off the booster before going to bed.

When I put my hand on the booster to turn it off it was HOT. There were no indicator lights illuminating except the power light. All of the Cellular band indicator lights were dark. I determined that I would trouble shoot it in the morning. The first thing I did was to tighten the cable connections as stated in the trouble shooting guide. I turned the booster on and got only the power light again. I loosened and re-tightened the cable connection and got the same result. I wiggled the connection and got some cellular band indicator lights but ended up with dark indicator lights again shortly thereafter and an illuminated power light. Thinking the supplied RG-6 cable might be bad, I swapped out the supplied RG-6 cable with 50 feet of RG-6 cable that I use with my satellite TV dish. No improvement. The verified known good RG-6 cable gave the same results as the supplied RG-6 cable. Obviously something was wrong inside the booster itself and I decided to return it.

When the booster worked it was 5 star quality. Unfortunately, the system failed after about 8 hours of on and off use. I need to get much more than 8 hours of service out of a $366 purchase so it gets a 1 star rating.

title: Buy Another Brand...Quality Control Issues Mean these are Useless.
text:
Frankly, this is the first Tempered Glass I've ever received that didn't "just work" out of the box. My G6 phone case came with some tempered glass that wasn't very thick or high quality, so I bought this to put on my and my wife's phone.

The first screen I put on my phone had an upper left area by the front facing camera that just absolutely would not stick...it hung off like it did not have any sticky tack on it at all. The second I put on my wife's and there were a few bubbles that reduced over the next 24 hours to be tiny, but are still there. The third that I now use has issues all around the corners of the screen where the screen protector simply won't go down.

Just so you are aware I've used tempered glass now for 6 different phones, clean, use microfiber, and take off all dust, and never once had issues like this. It's really disappointing because now I don't have any extra and will have to buy a new tempered glass since the first one was useless and the phones look like crud with the other two we used. Sad...just sad. I have absolutely no idea how these get such high ranking with such terrible quality control.

title: Read this before you buy...
text:
I've owned this product for 6 months now. Everyone reviewing this will tell you how great it is and how good the quality is, and they're right. Here's my input:
-the buttons on the side of the phone are not pronounced in any way, so with 3 buttons on the left side, theres no clear touch definition between them. This will affect you when trying to turn the volume up and down or taking a screenshot, especially at night. It's annoying, but not a deal breaker for me, just doesnt make it 5 stars.

The best advice I have: if you end up buying this, put only enough cards in there to where the magnet will close without popping open. Use it like that for a week and work in the leather with a little mink oil or leather conditioner (think baseball glove). Then add a card or two every week and it'll get to where you can add several. Currently, I have 6 cards and 2 business cards and could put a little more, but when I started, I could only put 2 cards in it.

It's an awesome case, I love the design. If the side buttons had just a little more thickness to them (on the operating side), it'd be a 5 star product. I'd love to see color variations too, (brown and black, blue and brown, red and black).

Eventually the two bottom ports simply decided to "not work" entirely which is completely stupid because I rarely ever used those ports to begin with. don't buy this device...get a cheaper hub with more slots, or a 3.0 hub with more features.

text:
I could have spent $10 elsewhere and gotten the same quality phone case.
First, I noticed the little UAG logo on the back wasn't straight. Looking at it closer I realized they are stickers. Metal stickers. The 'G' will not stay where it's supposed to be.
Then, I was having issues with my wireless charger. I couldn't figure out why it worked so well and then one day it just wouldn't get a solid connection. It was suggested that the metal on my UAG was interfering. I took my case off and tried the charger again. Instant connection with no issues.
But, before I could do that... When I took my UAG case off, the 5 little silicone pieces stayed on my phone. They slipped right out if the case.

title: Edges don't stay down...but you get 2
text:
to start off, i'm gonna just tell you that i'm really, really good at putting these things on. provided that i'm in the right environment and the screen protector is accurately cut, i can get screen protectors on perfectly and without any dust underneath. if i do get dust underneath, i'm usually able to get them all out with some scotch tape. if i just end up failing, i peel it off, throw it away, and start with a new one. ok, wanted to get that outta the way so that everyone knows what kind of crazy person this review is coming from.

Pros: glass seems to be of good quality, but of course i'm not going to purposely put it through any stress tests...but so far so good. the cut is excellent! i know some people have gripes about a screen protector not going all the way to the edge, but with the iphone 6, that's just not really possible. i've tried the glass screen protectors that go all the way to the edge and, although it looked great at first, the edge of the protector is just dangling enough over the curve of the screen to start collecting dust. So in regards to the cut, this one is perfect.

Cons: with consideration to the fact that this protector doesn't extend to the curves of the iphone's screen, it SHOULD sit completely flat. however, it doesn't. you can clearly see where the adhesive has not completely adhered to the iphone's screen. this is only true on the long sides of the screen and the bottom corners. between 1-3mm of the protector is clearly not sticking to the screen. so, this kinda sucks. the fact that this package comes with 2 protectors is kinda nice. i'm a little tempted to peel this off and try the second one, but i'll sit tight for now.

so far, i'm not really liking this screen protector, but it's only been on my phone for about 10 minutes. in some cases, the screen "settles" on the phone over some time, but in my experience, i'm a little pessimistic about this happening. if it does happen i'll come back and adjust my review. but if not, then this is my assessment of this product.

hope this helps everyone!

title: DO NOT BUY! Horribly flawed
text:
I would give this product NEGATIVE STARS if I could. I would like to say I did purchase this product from a different retailer but it is the same product.
I used to have an "otter" case and LOVED it. It is EXTREMELYsturdy as I am fairly rough with my phone. However it is not water proof which is something I was looking for after I got water on my phone.
So naturally I purchased this case with good reviews.
However, my phone case fell apart after two months! I had my otter box for a year and it went thru Hell before I needed a new one.

I would like to say:

1) It is NOT water proof. there is a small rubber piece on the inside of the case that can easily dislodge (if the case is opened and then closed again) and cause the entire phone to leak water into it. Even after "testing" the phone for water leaking and closing the case securely, it leaked water every time.
2) Cheaply made. The soft plastic is very cheap. Much more flimsy then the otter box. The front plastic screen has come away from the rest of the phone because it is held on by a cheap glue. This causes water to enter through an entirely different place now.
3) Horrible screen design! The screen does not lie flush to the phone so it causes mistakes all the time when texting and you have to press hard also.
4) The sound on speaker is horrible because the phone is not snug enough in the case so there is an annoying echo sound.
5) It is bulky and ugly also.
6) If you want to wear earbuds you have to screw in and attach and extra piece that is stiff/inflexible and unappealing in order to use any cord device. If you lose the piece you're screwed. Otherwise you must get a Bluetooth device to listen to music or talk on the phone.

Skip this case. Find an alternative.

title: I'm recommending this to everyone I know
text: I'm happy and impressed. I was able to install the screen protector fast and easily. The screen it's self is solid and real tempered glass. It's really hard to find a tempered glass screen protector that will stick to the phone and work with the finger sensor on the Galaxy S10 Plus but I've found it. The screen protector comes with a little uv light and liquid adhesive. I made sure all of the dust was off of the screen before pouring the adhesive in the middle of the screen. Then carefully placed the screen on top of it. I let all of the liquid move to the edges of the screen. I made sure there were no bubbles. title: Manage your expectations and you'll be fine with this phone
text:
I needed an inexpensive WiFi phone, and thought this one would fit the bill. I didn't need a high-powered smartphone, like my Samsung SIII Mini. I was pleased that the phone started the update process as soon as I set it up, and in short order it was running Android 5.0.2. The best word I can use to describe this phone is "adequate." Sound quality on a WiFi call is adequate. The screen is adequate in quality, and a good size without being too large. I noticed some brightness fluctuation occasionally, which might have been caused by power fluctuation from the battery, but had no trouble reading EPub files with Aldiko. With WiFi and Bluetooth both on, the battery dropped by 50% in a couple of hours. With both off, and the screen sleeping, the battery dropped by 70% in 2 days. The included earbuds were downright crap. Listening to music with my Audiotechnica monitor headphones, sound was better but still not very good. I suspect it's the DAC. Video: don't even try. Playing an MP4 file with VLC, there was so much stuttering that it was unwatchable. General apps ran relatively smoothly, but this isn't a gaming machine. I tried 2 different pinball apps, and one ran smoothly while the other one dragged. (But why would anyone play pinball on a 5-inch screen anyway?)

Want an inexpensive phone for basic use? This is a pretty good deal at less than $100. If you expect it to run like a high-end Samsung or LG, you'll be sorely disappointed, but if you take it for what it is, you'll be content.

title: More convenient than I had expected!
text:
First of all, customer service was quick to reply and very helpful. That's usually the #1 measure of a good product or company.

Second, this band works great and was quite surprising. When I got it I didn't think much of the ability to quickly twist off the phone. But, as I've used this a few times now, I'm beginning to see how incredibly convenient this simple feature is. This feature comes with a caveat, however. With this cool feature comes some extra height to the coupling section of the band. This has not yet been an issue at all. it's not "floppy". I don't run, so I can't say it "wouldn't" flop... But, during my mediocre workouts, it's never been an issue.

I didn't realize it at first, but the ability to quickly remove my phone and reattach it has been incredible. It's such a small and simple feature and I think it's THE reason I love this band so much. My original assumption was that I would put my music on and not think about my phone until I was done with my workout. But, now that I HAVE this feature, I find myself frequently twisting it off, changing up my music, and slapping it back on. It's INCREDIBLY convenient! When my wife texts me during a workout; twist-off, reply, twist on. When I want to switch playlists; twist-off, switch lists, twist on. When I want to switch to a podcast; twist-off, switch app, twist on.

I had no idea how much I would use and enjoy this simple feature. I definitely recommend this product!

title: Great phone case: offers protection with limited bulk
text:
This is a great case!! I'm very impressed. It offers wonderful protection AND is cute!! I love the design and it's not bulky, so it keeps the sleek profile of my iphone 6 that drew me to the phone in the first place.

I love using double layered armored cases, and I've seen ones at the retail store that go for around 30 dollars. So when I saw that Caseguru was offering the same concept for nearly half the price, I was wondering what was sacrificed. The answer is nothing. Caseguru offers a high quality case that is at a budget compared to it's competitors.

Having two layers for a case makes a great way to absorb shock and scratches. The inner layer is a rubbery like bumper that fits perfectly and allows easy access for the buttons. The outer Rose Gold layer can be snapped on and provides structural support and scratch resistance. The sum of its parts allows for serious fortifications and you can drop your phone without having to worry about compromising it.

Cables and screen protectors will work as usual. You can fit your charging cable and the speakers are not obstructed. You also do not have to worry about the screen protector being inhibited. Just remember that just like any other armored case, you have to make sure it fits your arm bands and charging docks.

The only thing the case doesn't protect is the back Apple logo is open. That means it can still be scratched by loose change. However, all the other cases have left the Apple Logo exposed and I cannot fault this case for that. Instead I use a spare screen protector to protect the logo. I honestly don't mind the apple logo being exposed because I think that's part of the apple design I love...just a simple apple logo on the back.

As a sidenote, I just want to note that even with a Rose Gold Armor shield plate, the black bumper doesn't make the phone look very feminine. I will not hold it against this case, but just note that having a Rose Gold Phone with a Rose Gold case will not look too graceful. But, I don't really care about the femininity of my phone case. I want it to offer great protection, add limited bulk, and be something I can easily spot.

title: Seriously--buy this.  The BEST and most practical waterproof phone case out there!
text:
What a great invention this case is!! I cannot recommend this highly enough. Especially if you have an active lifestyle or are exposed to the elements at all. I purchased this for a beach vacation because I wanted to be able to get great shots in and under the water. I'm always jealous of people who have the waterproof pouches, but I wanted something that fit tighter like this actual case does. The waterproof pouches are okay, but the pictures do not turn out as clearly and the phone isn't as easy to handle, especially pressing the buttons through the pouch, if that makes sense...

I have a few other iPhone 6 waterproof cases I have used and none were quite like this. I went with the rose gold color that I've been so obsessed with lately. My iphone is also the rose gold color so I loved that I could make it match. I also love that there were so many different color options, which I've never seen before with any other waterproof cases.

At first glance this case wasn't as bulky as my other cases. I was nervous that it would leak water actually, because I'm so used to the heavy duty waterproof vaults that they sell as waterproof cases. The case also feels lightweight, which is awesome for travel and for getting those action shots on the go. It came in a nice box that has a magnetic closure and in the box was a white microfiber cloth, a wrist strap, a headphone jack extension cord, and the case itself. It has 2 parts, one rose gold bottom piece that has a metal material around the sides of the phone and more of a plastic material on the back and it has a front piece which has a clear part that covers the screen and has black around the edges.

As suggested and HIGHLY recommended (because there are cases out there that say they are waterproof that aren't, or the occasional defective product) you test this case underwater before inserting your phone to make sure it's air tight. I made sure the case was closed tight and put it under running water. I then submerged the case into a bowl that was full of water. After both of these tests there wasn't a single drop of water inside of the case so I felt more confident with it's ability to block out the water.

This case isn't ridiculously hard to remove from my phone like all of the other waterproof cases I have had in the past which is why I was surprised it is so effective at keeping water out. There is a slight divot type thing at the bottom left corner of the case, which I like because it helps me get traction to be able to put the case on and take it off again. The metal rose gold piece has a ridge/groove along the top of it and the top piece, which is kind of like a rubber, will wrap around it tightly which will keep the water from touching your phone.

Another thing that i love about this waterproof case was how easily accessible all of the buttons are to push, unlike those waterproof pouches on the market. Usually with waterproof cases you have to push harder on the buttons or they just become un-functional, which is annoying. The finger id sign-in on the home button is easily still usable, but if you want to mute or un-mute the sound, you will need to do so before securing the waterproof case, or else you'll have to remove the case, flip that little switch and then reinstall the case.

Also, with some waterproof cases the clear touch screen cover makes the phone's touch screen not want to pick up what you are tapping on as easily. But this screen didn't change the touch sensitivity at all, my phone easily still picked up on what I was typing or tapping on, and I even have a glass screen protector already on my phone as well. Even though the case covering the edges of my touch screen rise up to help protect the screen of my phone from damages, the case doesn't get in my way when trying to use my phone or type a message. The case also feels sturdy like it would protect my phone in case I dropped it. I'm thinking I may just use it as my daily case, since I tend to be pretty tough on my equipment and move around a lot.

One thing is that my headphone cord won't fit into my phone with this case on, but honestly, that's hardly an issue for me,. It also makes sense, because if you have access to the headphone jack, then the case can't be air/water tight. I can plug that into my headphone jack and then plug my headphones into that. The music then comes through as clear as usual. The wrist strap feels very comfortable and is just plain black with HESGI written in white on it. I chose not to use the wrist strap except when I am swimming and using this with active water sports and activities. There are 2 holes on the bottom right corner of the case which is where it would tie around.

The box says Hesgi: The Best Waterproof Case, and I don't disagree at all. This is definitely my favorite waterproof case. I feel that it is worth the current list price of $39.99.

I hope I provided enough information in my review for you to determine if this case is the right one for you and serves your needs. I personally cannot say enough good things about it. title: Smooth surface sheet = Returning to that good ol Intuos 4/5 feel
text:
Exactly what the title says. It's been the better part of a year since I upgraded to this new tablet and replacement texture sheet, so this is more of a long-term review.

Before writing this review, I went ahead and compared the surfaces of my old Intuos 4 & 5 with the current Intuos Pro with the smooth sheet thrown on it. As far as "tooth" goes, there is no real discernable difference between the unworn texture in the corners of my old Intuos 4 & 5 and the Intuos Pro smooth sheet. This includes nib wear on the current Pro Pen 2. Nib wear on the smooth sheet has turned out to be basically identical to the Intuos 4 & 5. Which is surprising, considering the Pro Pen 2 uses a nib roughly half the diameter of the old Grip Pen, for some reason. Usually thinner material = quicker wear, so I'm not really sure how that's turned out to be the same as well.

One thing I've noticed is that the current Intuos Pro sheets have a bit more of a "rubbery" quality in terms of drag feel. Almost like a layer of hard rubber compound rather than a sheet of hard plastic. It's a subtle difference in feel, but it's there.

I've heard that Wacom ditched the slicker, hard plastic material of previous generations for a harder-wearing rubber-based compound on the sheets for their current iterations of the Intuos Pro. If that's true, then it would certainly explain the subtle difference in feel. But this is unconfirmed rumor, so take it for what you will.
But if that is indeed the case, it would certainly explain a lot. This new material they're using for the texture sheets has proven extremely resilient. After 6-8 months of almost daily use, my smooth texture sheet looks like the older Intuos4/5 after a month-ish of semi-intensive use. The smooth texture sheet just has a bit of subtle scuffing near the center after all of this. Also, I'm still using my original nib, which hasn't worn noticeably since the initial session with the default medium sheet. So I don't see myself needing to buy replacements for either in a very long time.

Basically, Wacom has struck an interesting balance with the materials used for the smooth sheet and the narrower nibs: drastically increased durability, enough drag to not feel like you're slicking around on glass, but not enough texture/grip to wear your narrower nibs prematurely. (Assuming you're using the smooth surface)
I just wish Wacom would start treating these smooth sheets as their included defaults instead of the medium textured ones, considering this is by far the only real gripe I've heard anyone bringing up against the current Intuos Pro line at all.

title: "Superman: A Messianic, Christian Perspective"
text:
Since others can do a much better job relating the story, I will give my take on the film only from a singular perspective--the Christian messianic take on Superman as 'savior'.

First off, I enjoyed the movie. As one who remembers the original Lois Lane and Jimmy Olsen from the TV series, it was nice to see them again in cameo roles.

The special effects rock--literally. The quakes, shakes, (near) crashes will pound you, and these were well-done. I will not discuss the plot involving Lois, Clark, Lois's husband and son, etc. Other reviewers can do that. But suffice it to say, this is a great story.

The film--over 2.5 hours long--is two movies. The first half is the typical (and nicely done) Superman fare. Unlike many, I did not feel the opening sequences lagged. They tied up loose ends, provided retrospection and the acting (all the way through) was great.

My only disappointment was the made-to-happen `bonding' between Lois's husband and Clark Kent. Not disappointing because it happened, but because it didn't. It came close at times, but never really materialized. What a shame.

The second half of the film was Messianic--to the point of going `over the top' in some instances. This is not a complaint. It would be hard to believe however, that all of this was unintentional. Even the names of the main characters contain the moniker 'El', which is a Hebraism for 'God'. Initially, like Christ, Superman comes to the world unrecognized, unappreciated, and rejected (Lois's "Why the World Doesn't Need Superman" wins a Pulitzer Prize).

In short, there are crystals (belonging to the destroyed world of Superman's father), which are stolen by the villain Lex Luther. He seeks to create his own 'world' by propagating these crystals in the sea, but he underestimates the proclivity with which the crystals grow. These ever-growing masses even fuse with the kryptonite Luther uses to encase them as they are 'planted'.

Superman must save the world from the rapidly growing crystals. But to do so, he must succumb to the power of the deadly kryptonite. He must face the enemy in order to defeat it. In short, we see the hero suffering, dying, departing to the 'underworld', rising from the dead in glory, and finally ascending into the heavens. The messianic overtones (or undertones) are as obvious as the twice-repeated "...the father becomes the son; the son becomes the father", and the father's words "They (humanity) only need the light to guide them. I sent you, my only son.". Christ, of course, is the 'Light of the world'. One can hardly miss the father to son: "...you will never be alone", much as Christ claimed co-eternity with His Father.

For those seeking theology in the film, it is not easy to miss the crystals as 'sin'. As Satan perverted that which was meant for good from the Father's world, so Luther steals the crystals. Both the crystals and Satan's deception in Eden involve that which was to make one 'wise'. Too, as evil lurked in that first garden with Adam and Eve, and confronted Christ in Gethsemane, His garden place of solitude, so the evil Lex Luther stole the crystals from Superman's place of solitude.

The prevalence and permeation of sin in the world is the pictured in the crystals' growth which becomes virtually out of control. And embedded within is the deadly kryptonite--the sting of sin--death. Superman, in seeking to be the savior, is seemingly defeated by Luther (Satan) and the cruel mistreatment at the villain's hand is reminiscent of Christ's torture by the Romans, and in a similar vein, the torture of Aslan by the White Witch in The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe.

At last, Superman is stabbed by Luther with one of the deadly crystals, and, like Christ, "tastes the sting of death and sin", though He is innocent. There is a descent into the deep 'abyss' of the sea, (although this is not the final death scene) reminding one of Christ's descent into the belly of the earth. But Superman will eventually return and rid the planet of this evil by lifting the entire thorny-appearing, dark crystal 'world' skyward (Christ being `lifted up' and bearing the sin of the world), and separating it forever from the earth he loves.

In the end, the empty hospital room where Superman dies screams 'empty tomb!'. Like Christ, even his clothing lies neatly folded beside him. But the hero gloriously ascends from death into the clouds after reminding those who would miss him: "I'm always around", much as Christ's "I am with you always".

I won't give away the scenes and plot twists that made this film enjoyable, but it's impossible to miss the messianic overtones.

I tried a few cases before, but this one is by far the best among what I tried so far, in terms of touch sensitivity. This is the first time when I feel like I can use Apple Watch as if there is no protective cover. The only think I wish it were different is that I wish the edge of the screen not as sharp (not too sharp but not round either) and mimic the round form of the original touch screen. We'll see if it is scratch resistant, or how well the case protects my watch (I have been using less the a week so far), but so far I love it.

I have been using this product for about a week, and I am moderately happy so far. I used to use all-silicone transparent or white cases since my iPhone is always white and want my iPhone to look white even with the case. But the problem with silicone is, it easily takes color of jeans or other colored materials. For example, I have to throw away my transparent or white silicone cases typically after 2-3 months, since it got so dirty (blue most of the time).

I decided to try this case because the back of the case of hard (mimicking the back of iPhone Xs), and thus it doesn't (at least easily) take color, while the side bumper is silicone so the phone is protected by occasional dropping (I trust soft cases more than hard cases).

The quality looks good. The back of the case actually looks like iPhone (wish apple mark is there, but I guess it is impossible legally...) The case is very secure (indeed it is hard to take iPhone out of the case), and seems sturdy. So my first impression is good. We'll see how long it lasts (without turning blue).

One complain is that I wish the silicone is painted with silver-ish color so the side silicone bumper doesn't take color easily. But maybe since it is on the side, it might not take color easily. We'll see.

The side buttons are super easy to press, which is often not true of "slim" cases.

title: With Adonit, it's always reaching for, but not quite achieving, perfection.
text:
I've been using Adonit styli since their very earliest models. I admit to mostly loving the company, even though the products sometimes frustrate me. Making the occasional "owie" better is absolutely top-notch customer support.

My favorite stylus remains one of the Adonit models that has a tiny disc at the tip. I'm an experienced user now and always carry a package of extra disc tips in my wallet when I use it. Just the price of using the tool, but it is a great tool.

I really wish Adonit would focus on making instruments for Android and Windows devices, which is what my phones, tablets and touch-screen computers are.

The Adonit Pixel is not universally compatible with all Apple devices, so be sure to check Adonit's compatibility list before ordering. Inj my case, only my iPad Mini 2 is compatible.

So far, I have used it as a straight stylus or pen and did not try any of the advanced drawing features. I draw almost nothing, but I am a heavy notetaker and styli that drag, lose contact or are otherwise flakey drive me nuts. I hate most rubber nubs, though Wacom makes or made some great rubber tipped styluses.

So for plain vanilla notetaking so far, how is this? Great. It is somewhat heft, which gives me better control. The tip is 1.9mm which also enhances control. Because of age-related arthritis, the buttons do me virtually no good, which is true of all other styluses as well.

On the whole, I like it as a notetaking tool, though I do have to overcome my comfort and familiarity with the older disc-tipped instruments. One of these days, I'll install a compatible drawing application and give it a try, though I doubt that any app will give me artistic talent.

Jerry

title: Edit: Needs a redesign. Image quality affected.
text:
***Update: I bought and returned 2 of these. With the first pack I noted that the flash was obstructed and unusable with the protector. I was willing to put up with that, but this glass cracks and scratches SO EASILY. I went through 3 protectors in a week through normal use. They would scratch with no apparent explanation. Against my better judgment I returned these and ordered another pack. The second pack had the same issues as the first - the wet wipes leave a cloudy, soapy residue, the soft cloth sheds dust, and the flash is unusable. However, this new pack also seemed to have a yellowish tint to the glass. My picture quality was slightly affected, which is simply unacceptable as I purchased this phone for the camera features. I really wanted to love this, and it makes me uneasy to have the lenses uncovered in a thin case. Unfortunately, I just haven't found a product that protects the cameras without affecting the picture quality.

Overall this lens cover was easy to install and does not seem to affect picture clarity. It also makes the surface of the camera lenses flat and therefore easier to wipe off. The box does not include instructions but every screen protector is more or less the same so it was easy to figure out. I didn’t like the isopropyl alcohol wipes these came with - I ended up using an ethyl alcohol wipe from a different kit. The 70% isopropyl alcohol wipes leave a soapy substance behind. The dry wipes leaves dust behind, which can be removed by the dust stickers. The kit does not come with a cloth lens cleaner.

I attached 2 photos - the clear one was taken with the LiDAR feature and the overexposed one was taken with the flash. The seller claims the flash operates normally - this is untrue. However, I don’t use flash so it’s not much of an issue for me. It is something to be aware of because the seller states that the flash works normally and it doesn’t.

title: Essential! Awesome protection, durability, style, and design all in an affordable package!
text:
When I first got my HTC One M8, I loved the feel of it - slender and smooth. So I didn't use a case. Big mistake! A case is a MUST for this phone. Without a case this dense phone has a low friction against surfaces so it slides and falls very easily (due to the brush metal case). The first time I dropped it, was a very bad day. Scratches and dents were all over the phone after a few months of use. The problem was that it always fell out of my pocket, especially with shorts. I even lost it in another country, but I won't get into that. I finally broke the internal speaker and made a small crack in the screen after dropping it and ended up having to pay over $200 to repair it, including the screen and entire back panel. That's why you NEED a case for this phone. At this point I got a new case, this one.

This case is a very sturdy and protective one that truly solves the slippage problem the phone has. I hardly ever drop it now! I also like that it has the matte black without any fanciness. It truly doesn't sacrifice the premium look of the phone, just makes it a little bigger in size. After having it for about 4 months now, I can see the compilation of scratches on the back panel of the case which would obviously be on the phone itself without the cover. I have also dropped it a few times but the case has definitely kept it from harm. That's because if you drop it on the corners, the entire case absorbs the shock due to its stiffness. So it also actually decreases the shock to the internal parts of the phone by dissipating the force. For people concerned with the size of the phone increasing because of a cover, yes this phone has a moderate to high amount of armor, but it fits snug, as if it were bonded to the phone and I've had no problems putting it into my pocket. I won't recommend it to minimalists though since there are slimmer cases on the market.

Things I don't like about the case are the dust compiling on the camera lens. It is pretty hard to clean with the case on and always seems to come back fast when you put it in pockets. I never really had big issues using the camera, but it does seem like the object focus is a little sluggish since I got the cover. I wouldn't count this as a serious problem at all though. I've also had trouble plugging certain things into the headphone jack and usb port so I think a little more plugging room would solve this problem. The buttons on the phone work pretty good, not as good as on the phone itself, but good. The buttons don't usually press while in the pocket which is pretty important.

So overall this phone case deserves a 5 star rating because the value you get for a case that's under $20. It does exactly what it needs to do to keep your phone safe and some may argue that it enhances the appearance of the already premium HTC One M8. Therefore, you really can't go wrong with this case, unless you are looking for minimal or maximal armor.

I've used the handlebar mount a lot more than the saddle mount. The handlebar mount is very sturdy. I don't know how people are breaking these unless they got a defective unit or something. Picture quality is pretty good. Videos look nice and stable when I'm using the mount. You can definitely tell the difference between this and when I'm holding the GoPro in my hand. The videos are way more stable in the mount. I have a Session, so it's very easy to switch between having the camera in the mount vs taking it out to shoot by hand.

I don't have anything against the saddle mount. It seems very sturdy, as well. I just tend to ride with a saddle bag most of the time. Besides, the front-facing videos seem a lot more interesting to me. The saddle mount would be great if you have 2 cameras. That way you would get a different point of view from time to time and you wouldn't have to waste time moving the camera from front to back. Honestly, I'm just to lazy to use the saddle mount all that often.

title: Cheap material and very difficult to get on and off
text:
I bought this case after seeing all the 5-star reviews and after receiving the case, I'm wondering if any of them actually purchased and used the case. First thing I noticed was the rubber shell material. It was stiff with sharp edges and felt cheap. From the pictures I was expecting a ridged texture on the back. The material is actually just the stiff rubber with glossy stripes along the back.

Next was the outer plastic frame that fits along the edge of the phone. The material felt again, very cheap.

Finally there was the matter of actually getting the case onto the phone. As I stated before, the rubber shell is very stiff. This made it very difficult to squeeze the phone in. Three out of four corners were no problem, but that last corner wouldn't budge without excessive force, and even then it would roll in on itself. The flimsy outer frame was even more difficult to fit over the shell and it has these little tabs on the back that are supposed to slide into slots in the rubber shell to keep it in place, but they just got in the way. This outer frame also required excessive force to slip the fourth corner into place, and it felt like either the flimsy frame or the phone itself was going to break.

I give this case two stars because once the case is on the phone and aligned properly, the power and volume buttons felt good to the touch and responded well. The case will probably be able to protect your phone from drops but don't expect to be able to slip it on and off with ease. I was going to keep the case since I got it with an 80% off deal, until I found out the hole in the case for the audio port is too small for the 3.5mm audio cord that I use. It is a very common cord, but it seems that only something the size of the Samsung ear buds that came with the phone will actually fit.

This is the first phone screen I have changed. Following the instructions on YouTube made it easy. Note: Heat was definitely needed to separate the touch screen from the LCD frame. A plastic guitar pick or separator tool is useful to avoid scratching the LCD.
Also note this unit already has the adhesive applied around the edges so no additional tape is needed. Make sure you get the correct screen for your phone, The S5830 uses a different screen from the S5830i.
Work carefully in a clean space and don't forget to remove the protective film from the new screen (it was obvious due to the extra pull tabs on this unit).

title: Excellent quality!
text: I just finished installing this strap to my 2nd Samsung Gear S3.  As soon as I opened the package I was VERY impressed by the high quality of leather used in its construction. The leather measures 1/8th inch thick- nothing cheap or flimsy here. The glossy black leather pairs nicely with the S3 making it look very dressy. Installation can be done without tools since the springs are built into both connecting ends of the strap, just like the OEM rubber strap. Highly recommend!

text: This is a an excellent screen protector. Installation is very simple and straightforward. Also, the quality of the screen protector is top notch. The only reason I knocked off 1 star is because of the fact that the screen protector does not seem to be quite 100 percent transparent. Zagg shields are 100 percent transparent and you cannot tell there is a shield on with the naked eye. Though minuscule, this particular case is not quite up to the 100 percent transparency that Zag provides. However Zagg also charges a premium for their shields. title: If the angle of the phone doesn't work for you, invert the mount.  But beware...
text:
I first tried the installation based on the visual instructions on the package. Although that gave me good access to the radio and other in-car entertainment and dashboard controls, it put the phone screen facing up towards the roof and a bit tough to see the screen.

I then flipped the mount upside down... the photos accompanying this review shows the inverted CD slot position with an iPhone 6 in a 2016 Honda CR-V. Note it covers access to the volume knob and other main audio controls.

I don't often reach for the dashboard controls while driving so this wasn't a problem for me (I control the volume and other audio controls from the steering wheel). The only times having the mount in this position cause a problem is when setting/changing some car entertainment/dashboard functions (clock, setting radio station, etc.) but I do that very infrequently, with the SUV stopped and I take the phone out so I can reach around for the controls.

So if this isn't a deal breaker for you, it's a good mount. However, if you often fiddle with the dashboard controls and the CD mount makes it difficult for you to access the controls, you may want to consider a different CD mount.

EDIT: Added photos with the CD mount in the advertised position (note better access to dashboard controls but angle of phone is different)

title: Too good to be true
text:
The package these arrived in shows heavy garage tools (hammer, large wrench...) being stuck to a wall. There's also an image of these pads holding a cell phone to a car's dashboard. From the "super strength" advertised, I thought this would work well to hold down sun screens (netting) in my car. The screens I use hang down vertically from the car's metal frame--not against the window itself. This means they flap around annoyingly as you drive. From the advertisement of this "Glue pad," this should have been a very simple task: attach pads to car doors & attach screens to pads. Boom! But it didn't work that way. The screens just don't stick to the pads. I have to reattach the screens every few minutes. Why even bother, then?

I used these pads in a cool car (no stick), a warm car (no stick), during the day (no stick), at night (no stick). I don't need gel pad around my house. I need them in my car. And for that, they just don't work. I certainly wouldn't trust my heavier mobile phone to these pads stuck to my car's dashboard. On the positive side, I was able to remove the pad without any residue left on my car's doors so I can send them back to Amazon. Good thing I didn't first try the much more expensive rolls of tape (same material) since I'd have had to cut them to fit my needs, probably voiding the return.

title: MiFi certified, works reliably

Have you tried various chargers and cables for your Apple devices only to find they don't work or fail very quickly? You can find much cheaper (per unit) deals on these chargers & cables, but this MiFi certified just works. I've tried it on my Ipad, Iphone and various small USB-recharged electronics that use micro-USB connectors. This charger charges them all. And for the price, I'm satisfied. I was going to buy a larger desktop unit to charge up to 11 USB devices at once but this small travel unit is far more economical and works for most of my needs. The cable seems very sturdy. My only regret is that the charger comes with only ONE cable--and it's just 3-feet long. Other chargers give you two cables and they're 6-feet or longer. But, this was the best deal on a MiFi certified unit I can trust to work with all my Apple devices.

I'll update my review if this unit fails...

title: Should Have Gotten the Samsung
text:
I was so excited to be getting a replacement phone for my LG Volt. I was THIS close to getting a Samsung, but this sounded like such an amazing deal-- a huge 5.5 inch screen, 13 megapixel camera, and 8 gigs of onboard memory for only $89. Plus I'd always been envious of my husband's (older gen) Desire because the BlinkFeed feature looked so cool. So, I got this phone instead of the S3/4's I'd been looking at. I have to say, I am sort of regretting it, though the price softened the blow.

First off, the screen is big and I love it. Despite it's size, it feels nice in my hand and isn't too heavy. The camera isn't what I'd hoped for, but I didn't care for the one on the Volt either. The flash blows out picture quality too much. I wind up using my old Samsung tablet without flash to snap most pics, and the quality's much better.

The Blink Feed I couldn't wait to have got replaced almost immediately. It drained battery power too fast, plus there wasn't as much customization as I would have liked.

My biggest problem with this phone, which annoyed me enough that I ALMOST sent it back, was the memory. The phone claims to have 8 gigs on board, twice as much as my LG Volt. Don't believe this for a second. I had the Volt for a year and loaded it up with apps, live wallpapers, etc, and was still occasionally adding near the end. I never once got the "insufficient memory" warning. The first WEEK I had the Desire, it did a system update. BAM, next thing I know, I'm getting the dreaded message--and I hadn't even loaded all the apps from my previous phone. I rolled back all updates, still no go. Next I stripped off apps, the custom launcher I'd replaced Blink Feed with, etc. Nope. Finally, by doing a factory reset, going through each app, moving what was allowed to the SD, emptying caches, etc., I was finally able to free up 1 1/2 gigs. Mind you, I don't have a million apps. Just the usual social media, a small launcher/lock screen, a couple wallpapers, a 3rd party text app, my receipt/rebate apps, a workout app, and a couple small word games. I did some research and found out that these HTC's are notorious resource hogs. What the phone has to load in just to run leaves you with almost nothing. I suppose I could root it and free up more space, but I've never done that with my phones. And seriously, I should be able to load basic things on a brand new, 8 gig phone.

So, if you're looking for a cheap smartphone with a large display to use as an actual phone and maybe do a couple other things, this is a steal! If you love to load up apps and want a great camera, keep looking.
