title: The Fine Print
text:
This product works as advertised if you use a later generation tablet or cell phone. It did not work with an IPad 1 but it did work with an IPad 3 and with a Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 7 inch model. It also worked well with my Samsung Galaxy Note II cell phone. There are 5 stations available in my area that are accessible with the Dyle box. All of them gave a crystal clear picture most of the time no matter what part of the metro area I tested them except for one station that worked 80% of the time. (I live in suburban Cincinnati)

You are probably thinking why did this guy give the thing 3 stars if it worked as well as he said it did? I'll tell you what they are not telling you based on my personal experience. Dyle TV does not have broadcasting rights to rebroadcast NFL football. I tried to watch 3 different games the weekend that I had it. All of them were blacked out. One channel broadcasted their alternative weather channel during the game. The other channel had a static banner up the entire game stating that Dyle TV did not have rebroadcasting rights. One channel did broadcast pregame highlights but the picture became very pixelated every time they showed game highlights. I also heard on my local news station that the Dyle TV service is currently free but they (Dyle) reserve the rights to charge for the service in the future. Perhaps someone from Dyle can comment on this.

I would guess that the native resolution of Dyle TV is something around 640 x 360 pixels. This means that the signal is less than high definition which would have to be at least 1280 X 720 to be 720p. There is a picture resize tool in their application which allows you to view channels in their native resolution. The native resolution on some channels yielded a picture that was about 1/8 the size of my cell phone which is tiny. I would expect that the thing would be able to rebroadcast in high definition on a phone or tablet that has the capability to replay a signal in 1080p.

I'm not trying to badmouth or bash this product. It does work and it is watchable. The picture stayed almost perfectly synced with the sound all the time. It works as advertised. My deal breakers were the lack of high definition and no NFL rebroadcast on Sundays which were enough for me to send it back. It is also too expensive in my opinion. I can buy a RCA DPTM70R 7-Inch 60Hz TV right here on Amazon for $15 less than this unit and have a 7 inch TV that will get all the broadcast NFL games in my area and I don't have to worry about the battery on my phone running down. I will also get many more channels with the RCA TV vs. Dyle. The RCA will receive all of the broadcast stations in my area. (44 channels) The Dyle unit only gets 5. From what I understand, my area has more Dyle stations than most so you should check to see what you are going to get before you buy this. Don't assume you will get all of the stations in your area because you won't.

Also beware that the audiovox unit is about the size of half a pack of cigarettes if you would cut it in half top to bottom. I would think that it would be very easy to loose. I would suggest to Audiovox that they put some sort of thingy on the box so you can attach it to a lanyard or a key ring so you don't loose the thing.

title: Wonderful!
text:
I've only had this for two months, but my experiences with it have been nothing but positive. I've haven't used it every day, since I certainly don't need a GPS for my daily travel from and to my workplace, but still, I've used it numerous times with zero issues.

I've driven my motorcycle at a maximum speed of 90 km/h (55 mph) over roads so bumpy you'd swear you're in an earthquake, and I've never had any displacement issues. Some people complain about the phone flying off the grip, or the grip uncontrollably rotating the phone, and I have suffered neither. The phone hasn't even moved enough to touch a button, even though due to the size and design of my phone one of the holder's arms sits right between the "On" and "Volume Up" buttons, milimeters from each.

My phone is a Motorola Moto G 2nd Gen with a Fosmon STURDY case. Granted, there's a chance the case's material is better at holding its grip against the rubber arms of the holder than the phone's material, but I doubt they're much different. My opinion? Those negative reviews stem from either older versions for the holder which have then been improved or, most likely, from user error, either by using the holder improperly or not using the correct model for their phone size.

So far so great. Some negative reviews gave me reservations at first, but these have been completely dissipated.

title: Mechanically it rocks- has serious limitations for charging your phone.
text: Let me start by saying that mechanically, the product rocks. While it's all plastic, it's built solid. I have it stuck to a vertical surface and coming off at a crazy angle with a hefty Samsung Galaxy Note 5 that puts a lot of stress on the suction cup holder but still it stays. But let's not oversell the wireless charging function. If you think you're going to pop your phone into the bracket and then cruise down the road using Google Maps, playing music, etc., think again. If your phone screen is off, no GPS and not talking on the phone or playing music, the phone will charge and pretty quickly, I might add. But if you leave the screen on or use the GPS, there's simply not enough juice to charge the phone. So wherever the battery is, is where it will stay if you leave the screen lit or use the GPS. And if you use the GPS AND leave the screen lit as I do, the charger will not be able to keep up and the battery will continue to drain. I doubt this is a design defect of this product, but rather just the nature of wireless charging. I think it's really designed for nighttime use when the phone isn't being used at all.

Mine lasted for over a year before breaking, which I am happy with since I really put it through a lot. It never fell off the phone due to drops, felt great in the hand due to the chamfered edges, and felt good against my face since the ridge around the outside edge is low.

It ended up breaking at the bottom due partially to my heavy use, and partially to a design flaw. I am always having to stick 1/8" stereo jacks into it to test audio, and those jacks are sometimes too fat for the case, so the case was forced open slightly, but a wider opening for the headphone jack would have prevented this. Over time, the tabs that snap the two haves of the case together failed, and the thin bottom edge of the case broke in half. I have replaced it with a Magpul Executive Field Case which I actually like much better.

title: Early purchase impressions
text:
Just received this portable charger. First impression is - it's heavier weight and larger dimensions (length, thickness, not necessarily width) than I anticipated. I wouldn't carry (nor would it fit) in a mens pants pocket - it would have to be in a backpack or separate shoulder-like carry pouch. I think it's too big for any of my fanny packs. Is it portable? Yes, but not that compact. I bought it mostly for its usb-c port (since my Apple snuck that in on my ipad pro and none of my other power packs are compatible) and that it's rated to recharge it about 3 cycles (well suited for a long intercontinental air flight or multiple days without a wall outlet) plus a little power remaining for my iphone 6s plus. I used my ipad pro charger (18w) as it's usb-c and this power pack comes naked (no power adapter/cords). Arrived with 1-2 out of 4 battery led lights lit, and a full top-off took about 8-9 hours which fits right in to about what I read on-line. Probably from ground zero I'd plan 11 hours.

What I need to figure out now is how it fits into my 'travel light' approach as that's why I have an ipad pro for remote work while mobile rather than a laptop pc brick. I will probably have to leave this unit in the car due to its weight and size, ready for a charge but not within arm's reach unless I'm on a road trip. Will it fit into my thin shoulder ipad pro accessories pocket? Yes, horizontally not vertically. But its far heavier and thicker than the tablet it's to server, sort of like a sumo wrestler protector for an acrobat. Hmm, so this sucker better charge when it's called on or the brick it is will be downgraded from 4 to 1 star in no time flat.

This is a '30' model, the next lower is '20' but its dimensions are about the same (but weight about 0.5 lbs more) so I decided to gamble on its capacity as the size differential wasn't substantial between the models but about double the rated charge capacity. So I went for it.

More later.

title: 2nd SIM FAIL (Was: Nice Dual Sim Phone for Price)
text:
(Update 6/12/17, ~6 months ownership)
FAIL: One of the primary reasons for getting this phone is the dual sim capability. Unfortunately the phone won't support LTE with both sim slots at the same time. When one is set LTE, then the other is set to 2G. Well, with H2O Wireless (and probably ATT), 2G is no longer supported, so the 2nd sim slot is useless. You may as well be carrying a single SIM phone. That said, I have both sims in the phone and switch between the two of them which is about a 2-3 minute task. It's just too bad that both SIMs can't be active simultaneously as intended.
---
My wife bought this phone for me for Xmas '16 (Amazon Prime, seller unknown). I had some trepidation because of the reviews that indicate others were receiving single SIM phones, but the one I received has two SIM slots and although I haven't tested the second slot yet, Android reports the existence of the second slot (besides the slot is uncovered and has contacts).
It's a little disappointing that the phone doesn't have a compass sensor. I'll have to back to carrying a compass when traveling. Also at least one panorama-camera app requires the compass sensor.
Some specs indicate a quad core processor and other specs indicate an octo core processor. Android/apps reports 8 cores but cores 5-8 always seem to be sleeping/blank - bummer.
Otherwise, with the ability to take a 128Gb micro SD memory card, kicks ass on my old S3... And the fact that the S7 battery isn't (easy to) replaceable, was a deal breaker.
Oh, and I wish the phone had 32Gb for installed apps. After getting the phone config'd with all my apps, including corp-ware to read email, I'm down to 4.81GB.

title: Easy Setup but needs to be reset daily
text:
I bought the new updated black one at AT&T for 120, which is better than the 300+ price on Amazon. It is really easy to install: just plug in the small black device to your ethernet port on your internet modem (minimum requirement is 1.5mbps download speed and 526kps upload speed; mine is 5mbps download and 1.5mbps upload and it works flawlessly), plug in power, and put it near a window, then go online to activate the device by putting in your phone number (to receive a text message with a pin number to register your device), then put in your address, then put in the phone numbers that you want connected to the device (up to 12 devices can be listed, but only 4 people can talk simultaneously), wait up to 90 minutes for the device to connect to AT&T server (the AT&T Microcell website shows your progress and will text you when everything is ready), and then your phone should say "AT&T M-Cell" instead of the regular "AT&T" (this is how you know you are connected to the Microcell). The range is really good (I live in a 700 square foot apartment, and my modem is on one side of the apartment; I can get 5-bars (-68 dBm) on my iPhone 5S all around my apartment.

Pros: setup should take only 3-5 minutes to read all of the directions and setup everything. The box and device are really small (6 inches x 2 inches x 6 inches). Only $120 for the new black one (the pictured one here on Amazon is the old white version) at AT&T store (only big AT&T stores carry it, so you should call the store to see if they sell it; I just went to the closest retail store but they didn't have it). I used to have the Wilson DT 4G Signal Booster, but it didn't work most of the time because my signal was weak to begin with (best was 2-bars [114 dBm] at one small area in my apartment); also, you would need to mount the device on the roof or pole outside of your apartment for best results. With the Microcell, you just need to make sure your phone can get a GPS signal (that is why the device needs to be near the window). Call quality is similar to what I would get in an area with good cell signal. Texting works just as well. Like other reviews say, you can get this device free at an AT&T store; all you have to do is go to the store and tell them your address; an employee will pull up a map on their iPAD to check if that address is a "dead zone"; if your address is located in that dead zone, then then will just go get you a microcell for free (if you are on a family plan, then you still need to change your primary address to the "dead zone" address); be sure to return the microcell if you decide to change your primary address out to a normal cell signal area or else they will charge you for it later on.

Cons: I've had this device for a week; and everyday, I had to unplug the power and plug it back in (even though the lights on the device say everything is okay). It sucks because my cellphone would disconnect in the middle of the night, so I would miss anyone who called me when I sleep. After you power back on the device, it still takes like 3 minutes to be able to operate correctly.

EDIT: so now I've had the product now for 2 weeks. I have just discovered why my microcell should be on the window platform instead of on the ground. Apparently, my microcell kept losing the GPS signal when I had on the ground of where my window was located, and then once I put it in between my blinds and window, it has been working perfectly for 3 days straight without unplugging and plugging it back it. Since I lost connection to the M-Cell, I started to move my microcell around the apartment; and once I went to the window, my cell phone suddenly connected to M-Cell (which means to your microcell). I guess the microcell depends on the location to get a good GPS fix even though your microcell shows a light that the GPS is working. So to conclude: if you need to keep on unplugging/plugging in your microcell for your cell phone daily to connect to it, then I would first suggest you move around your microcell around your place with a cell phone in your hand until you connect to M-Cell.

title: not stable + cheaply made
text:
This combo car dock mount for Android (micro USB) phones has been pretty good over the past couple days. I actually used it for my Nexus 6P (which has a 5.7" display, dimensions of 159.3 x 77.8 x 7.3 mm, and weighs at 178 g) in my 2004 Acura TL. The Nexus 6P has a USB-C port, and fortunately, this mount has the ability to unscrew the base and remove its micro USB cable, then install your own cable on the base. I had my own USB-C to USB-A cable which fits fine with this mount. One thing to note is that you are only able to have it place at the center bottom - this can conflict some other phones since others have their charging ports someplace else, but luckily, most phones today have it in the center bottom anyway.

For those who want me to cut to the chase:
This mount is not worth the money. For over thirty five bucks, i expected a more high quality and stable mount, but i did not get that kind of experience. Suction cup isn't so strong, in the vent-mounting mode: the mount will slide off as you tilt your phone, so that mode is pretty much useless. In "mini-mount" mode (which is having the mount placed anywhere you like using the adhesive base) it performs its best, but your too limited on where to place it in a vehicle, plus the adhesive will weaken overtime in the vehicle with hot days. In order to keep the phone tucked in the mount, you have to have the phone plugged in at all times - which causes a hassle. Plus if you're a person like me - i don't always like to have my phone charging when it doesn't need to be.

Vent mode:
The mount itself snaps in the vent clip's base. Make sure you have the screw in between the two parts, so you can screw it on the mount after snapping it together. The vent clip is easy to clip on. You are able to rotate the mount in this mode. Unfortunately, The vent clip is not stable. I don't have to try to rotate the mount, and the mount will just fall down, then as i tilt it, the clip just slips off the vent - making it useless and dangerous to have installed in this mode. I do not recommend this feature. My phone's weight is not even that heavy compared to other new phones today.

Suction cup mode:
In this mode, you can install the mount on a base that can be placed pretty much anywhere - even on glass with its bottom suction cup. In my case, i have it on my wooden drawer. You are able to lock it so, the bottom won't move too much. In the description, it says that it sticks on anything. At first, it did seem like it could hold its own, but after multiple tilts with my phone mounted, the suction cup popped right off my wooden drawer. Even with the lock on, it doesn't stay stable on my drawer. It may stick better on glass, but considering its quality in vent mode, i highly doubt that it will stay stable on glass. Plus, it can be dangerous.

Mini-mount mode:
I found that this mode is the most stable. You snap your mount into the base - which has an adhesive back that you can place anywhere. I recommend to not have it on rubber that is in the vehicle as the adhesive will melt the easiest on hot days - making the base slip right off. I couldn't find the perfect spot to place the adhesive, but i did attached an image within the review just for show. Rotating the mount with my phone inside was really good. The adhesive is pretty strong. Of course i did not leave it in that mode because it just looks so unsafe while driving, so i removed it after i took the pictures. Other vehicles are different, so you will probably find a better spot other than mine - which is at the bottom corner of my radio. I don't know how it will hold up in the long run, but there is a chance for the adhesive to melt in hot days, so i still would not recommend it overall. It's just less likely to fall off when placed on material (eg. plastic) other than rubber - considering the hot days.

PROS:
- Versatile
- Ability to replace the charging cable

CONS:
- Feels cheap
- Vent mode / not at all stable
- Suction cup / not stable after multiple rotates
- Mini-mount / adhesive will melt overtime when in vehicle
- Always have to have charger plugged in to keep phone stable in mount
- Dangerous because of its poor quality

I ended up not continuing to use this product. My intentions were to mainly use this in my vehicle, but it is just very unsafe. For the price, I can easily say that this is not a good product. I won't say that it is completely useless - it does have different functions, so others can find their own ways to work things out, especially when other vehicles are different. I received this product at a discounted rate in exchange for an honest review.

title: Not Clear, and Discolors Terribly
text:
I bought this case exactly two months ago. Right after I ordered the case, the owner noted on XDA that he would opt for the Black case instead because it was higher quality material. I should have cancelled and re-ordered, but I didn't.

So, let me start out with what I like about the case, cuz there are some good things for the 10 bux I paid:

1) It's a cheap TPU case that does what it's supposed to do - protect the phone.

2) The included screen protector is decent.

But, now for the bad:

1) The case is NOT clear. It's frosted, and that was a huge disappointment that wasn't immediately obvious at the time of purchase. I'm surprised they haven't changed the description yet.

2) The case discolors TERRIBLY. I've had it for two weeks, and the device is ALWAYS on a clean surface or in my backpack pockets, yet the case is a mustard yellow, trending towards orange. I've washed it once with mild soap to no avail. Granted, I live in a desert area, but this case is essentially UGLY after a mere 2 months.

3) The case feels cheap, and it loosens up over time, allowing more fine particulate matter into the back to create abrasion marks (tiny scratches). I have only had the case off 4 times total in those 2 months, and it's never been in direct sunlight or conditions over 100F, yet it's loose and sloppy to the point of the left and right sides peeling away when you merely hold it.

4) The button cutout hole positioning is OK, for the most part, but makes it hard to get a normal headphone plug ALL the way into the jack. Every pair of headphones and earbuds I have, from the stock Samsung ones, to Panasonic, Beats, Etymotic Research, JBuds, etc. all exhibit this exact same issue, and it causes the TPU case to stretch at that location. Generally not good.

5) The Diztronic owner recommended NOT buying this one on XDA-Developers. He says the black shiny case is a better material.

In short, this is the first case I've purchased for any phone. My past HTC Titan, HTC Mogul, and Samsung Galaxy were always fine without cases, probably because they cost me nothing from Sprint. However, switching to AT&T meant paying some bucks up front for a Galaxy S3, and I figured I'd protect it with a case. Well, this Diztronic Clear TPU case does protect it, but it sure ain't sexy doing it, and it feels like it won't last for more than a couple more months. That and the discoloration are clear reasons to avoid this not-so-clear case.

Update 09-17-12:

Diztronic gladly replaced this badly discolored and loose clear case with the [[ASIN:B0089FA27E Diztronic High Gloss Black Flexible TPU Case & Screen Protector for Samsung Galaxy S III [Diztronic Retail Packaging]]] under warranty. Shipping from north to south across the middle of the country took exactly 1 day. They fulfilled my warranty request on Saturday, and I have the replacement product on my Galaxy S3 today! Great customer service and no complaints with that at all!

However, as to the "clear" product which this review refers to, there's a pretty good reason why it's $2 less than the other versions of the product. My clear case has discoloration spots that are clearly where my fingers sit when I hold the phone, and I'm not a smoker or coffee drinker... I think it's just not a good quality of TPU or something that causes all this discoloration. I would opt for a different colored case. White or clear probably isn't the best choice for long-term sexiness of the phone.

title: So far so good
text:
So, I've had this for about an hour now and this is all based on that initial experience. Will update if anything goes awry later, but... Setup was seamless! Just log into your google account from your old and new phone, then follow the prompts. It'll take a while for OS updates and your apps to download and install, but it does that all in the background. Came with about half a battery, so I was able to get going immediately. Honestly, with the cases off, it's maybe 30% thicker than my old Galaxy S8 with a cracked screen, which isn't a problem at all. I LOVE the color of the back. I've seen a few complaints about the included case, and well... Mine is fine! It's probably not the case I'd get, as I'd prefer something sleeker and may be buying a new one, but this one is thick, fits snugly, and it seems like it will provide outstanding protection for this phone. So far it's running quickly, I've been logging back into all of my accounts. There are probably a few utilities that aren't great or that I'll miss from my Galaxy, but the beauty of Android is that ALL of that is customizable. There are tons of alternative calling, messaging, firewall, antivirus, camera, gallery, and file manager apps on the market, which I'll be exploring in the coming weeks as I use this more, but stock Android is also very usable without tons of customization. I'll miss the NFC and Qi wireless charging that this phone doesn't have, but for a ~$100 temporary/backup phone, those aren't completely necessary.

Update: I ended up needing the NFC for my blood glucose meter, so I had to replace the phone, but I'm still using it daily. It's a great device to carry around while I'm working on projects and listening to music. Since my SIM is in my main phone, this one is basically an iPod touch. I've used it for the past 4 days straight on WIFI with Bluetooth turned on, listening to music and the battery is only now at 59%. It's a slow charge, but also lasts FOREVER on a charge! Gives me the opportunity to work on projects without distractions from my regular phone constantly buzzing to tell me about something that I "might" want to know about. Works well using Youtube and Twitter and connects to all of my stuff really reliably. It's also very lightweight and I love that the headphone jack is on top.

title: Very clear and feature rich - A significant improvement over the M50
text:
I bought the Plantronics Voyager Legend Bluetooth Headset hoping it would improve my comprehensibility particularly while driving. In the five months prior I had been using the Plantronics M50, but had received numerous complaints of poor voice quality even though I could hear my counterparts very well. They often stated that it sounded like I was talking in a wind storm. After connecting the device to my iPhone 5, which it does very quickly. I placed a few test calls, which went well. A few weeks after getting the headset I talked with a coworker in California for the entire length of my commute, at the end of my call I asked him if he had any issues understanding me, and he said he did not. While this device is about twice the cost of the M50, if you are going to be talking while driving or moving about, I would recommend the Legend over the M50.

I also like the voice commands that are built in, the auto answer feature, when you put it on your ear, the fact that can be worn on either ear, and the battery status announcement.

I should note that this device like many Bluetooth devices is very sensitive to interference, particularly from your own body. I notice it will cut out occasionally if it is on the other side of my body. (The water in our bodies is particularly good at blocking signal.) However, with that said it does have pretty good range and I have left my phone in the car and can get 30-50' away without dropping.

I paired this purchase with the Wilson Electronics - Sleek 4G-V - Verizon 4G Cell Phone Signal Booster. Together they make great pair for safe, reliable, frustration free conversations while driving.

title: Good Product BUT USB output is NOT 3.0A (combined) but rather 2.1A (combined)
text:
I recently contacted Amazon and its supplier, (T-Bar) about the return of the Targus Plug-N-Power Charging Station (T-Bar actually shipped a handYman version) because of the shipped version only having a 2.1A (combined) USB output -- versus the Targus advertised 3A output. I was disappointed and asked for a return.
Since that time, I have learned that Targus does not actually meet their 3A output spec; it is also a 2.1A output. And, I can find no similar product which does so.
Consequently I will be keeping and using the handYman unit that was delivered.
NOTES:
1) The Amazon description should be highlighted to state that the Targus unit offers ONLY a 2.1A USB combined output.
2) Although the handYman unit delivered is (I believe) identical, L-T Bar should ship the quoted product OR at least inquire prior to sending a substitute item.
3) The furnished unit will (slowly) charge both an iPad3 and a iPhone5 simultaneously. Charging only one at a time would result in a faster charge.
4) Plugs conveniently into existing 120VAC 2-socket outlets.

Additional Note: L-T Bar (the vendor) contcted me on Jan 7, 2013 to request that I remove their rating of two-stars as a vendor, saying that they shipped a Targus unit. I declined as the product received from them is boldly labeled handYman. The packaging states "handYman Smart POWER, Model No. S9P 332 NIWG, Made in China. I strongly feel that a vendor SHOULD NOT send substitute product without first contacting the purchaser!

title: Works pretty well.
text:
Purchased for use with a Galaxy 4 on the AT&T network while in my RV. Went from about -115db with just the phone to averaging -85db with the Sleek 4G and a 22" trucker/RV antenna mounted to the ladder on my RV. Didn't try the smaller included antenna, just the larger one. This is getting a 4G signal in a remote area, it hasn't boosted it to the LTE network, but it should if there is a signal present. The signal is consistent and almost no dropouts, although it does drop from time to time. Still, in this same spot, I would normally only get a spotty 3G connection.

I would like to see it boost reception to LTE, but very possible the LTE signal isn't directed into this remote area, surrounded by mountains in a valley.

Of Note: Galaxy 4 mounted in an Otterbox Defender case, fits well and snug with the largest clamps in the outer slots. Much bigger than this and you may need to see if they make wider clamps.

title: I love this phone!
text: For the price this is a great value and great middle ground to us as a transition from BB10 to Android on Blackberry which is a reality we're all going to have to face.  As of yesterday I was still using a Passport and while it did all I needed I was really struggling with having such a dated phone.  My options were to go to a flip or come to terms with modern times and I chose the latter.  I'm a Blackberry loyalist and have to say this is much better than the Passport, the build quality of the PP was better overall but I find the K1 to be a better experience.  I have an ATT sim card in one slot and TracFone in slot 2 and both work fine.  I also updated everything to Oreo without any troubles.  There are two versions of this BBB100-7 though, you can open the dialer and type *#837837# to find out if you have PRD-63764-001 (Indian marker) or 002 (Indonesian market) and it's my understanding the 002 version is the one that's struggled with updates.  I bought on an auction site from an Indian seller in part to make sure I got the Indian version.  I think that's all I can say for now.  I will add the keys are a little mushy (more like a 9900 than the Passport) and the Key2 addresses many issues of the Key1 but with it currently being 2x the price I don't think it's worth it so I bought the Key1 as a backup in advance of the Key2 I've yet to buy.  The Key2 LE is an option but feels more like a compromise with the BBB100-7 as an option over the BBB100-1.  Lastly, I don't use WiFi calling or VOLTE so I can't comment on those.

While I am an Amazon junkie, I got this phone through my carrier. There are actually four or five U8800 models. Presumably, this is the U8800-51. There is little difference in Android phones. They are all the same Chinese schlock. A couple of things you should know:

There are phones being sold with four different versions of Android; <2.2, 2.2 ("Froyo"), 2.3 ("Gingerbread") and 4.0 ("Ice Cream Sandwich"). This phone runs on Froyo which will run 99% of Google apps. One downside to this phone is that it is probably cannot be upgraded to Gingerbread. For the VAST number of users that will be irrelevant.

If you want access to the Google apps market (most of which is free), browse, use email - great. This is also a good media player (audio and video). Oh and it actually makes and receives phone calls too. I am a cord cutter and this is terrific communicator. It plays very well with my bluetooth headset and has a good speaker as well. The camera is good - not great. While it is 5 megapixel, the lens is very wide angle. The digital zoom erodes picture quality. However, unlike many phone in this range it DOES have a flash.

One other thing that you should know is that Huawei (sounds like a Hawaiian disease) expects you to get technical support from your carrier. Their US tech support is awful.

title: I like it, but long term, only suction on window worked.
text:
This functions just as described. The only thing about the product is that I really wish there was a way to tilt down at the base. I drive a 2014 Ford Escape and there isn't much of a choice as to where to put this. It's on the windshield or right in front of the CD player on top of the dash. I will never use the CD player, but if I do, I can detach the arm from the secured disc to put a CD in.

As far as I can tell, all Qi chargers cause the phone to feel warm to the touch. If the screen is on and you are using the Qi at the same time, it will get warmer, faster. If driving with the screen off, it doesn't get so warm.

I'm using this with a Google Nexus 6 and the fit is perfect. The Qi charges nicely. I play the game Ingress, which means you tend to drive with the screen on, like a navigation app. I've used this during game play and it keeps up with the charge.

I specifically got this for my Nexus 6, but before it arrived, I used it with a Motorola Razr HD and it still fit. If I wanted to charge it while it was in the holder, I had to adjust it up from the rim where the phone sets because of where the charge slot is on the side, but the fact that this grips the phone very well without having to add stress to the side grips, it worked perfectly when.

It also comes with little tabs to route the cable around. They have a glue backing, and I used mine plus a few that came with my husband's charger. Some of the glue backing did not stick to a particular type of material on one part of my console, so I used craft glue dots to secure without any problems. Those little tabs are AWESOME and help you route the cable out of the way, completely.

Again, I just took one star off because it doesn't bend at the base. I could see why, as this might create an imbalance in the suction... but the mount where the phone sits tilts well. The benefit of it bending at the base would make it less visible to other divers and put it closer to me.

Overall, I would recommend this product!

****** EDITED 1/25/2015
After a few months, the tab that attached to my dash area for the suction cup to attach to slowly decayed, and the glue was of no use for the backing. It is now mounted to my windshield and I really don't like where it is, but I'm dealing with it. I like the options for charging, and it fits my huge phone, so I'm keeping it and not looking elsewhere. However, I really wish all the glue backing to all of the pieces had been worth it. NONE of them have survived since I posted this review.

title: Nice heavy duty skewers
text:
I received these as a promotion about a month ago. I finally got a chance to open them up and use them a few times in the last week or so.

As per usual with Fresher products BBQ accessories, it was packaged very nicely, making you feel confident you are getting a quality product out of the gate. These skewers were a bit larger than I expected, which was a nice surprise. I like the large oak handles and stainless heavy duty skewers.

After using them twice with a variety of meats and veggies on them, I've decided I like them a lot and will continue to use them. I must say i'm used to using your standard wood sticks you can buy and bulk. Those work for large groups, but what I like about these is they are a flat stainless skewer, which results in the food on them doesn't spin very easily when you are rotating them around the grill. Had a piece or two still move a little but nothing like the bargain sticks. I think if they made these a 16th of an inch wider it would remedy any movement at all.

On a side note, while the oak handles are nice, be sure to not place them directly on your grill so they don't burn. I left a little room near the handles so I could still close the lid on my pellet smoker.

All in all great product, probably going to buy a 2nd set just to have for larger groups.

title: Tech Armor makes great ballistic screen protectors. You should have one.
text:
Good stuff. I have purchased many of these Tech Armor screen protectors. I have 4 at the moment; 2 on LG G3 devices, 1 on an LG G4 and one on my new iPhone 6S which is what this review is about:

They do the trick, protecting the screen from drops and direct hits, and from scratches. A really smooth/slick surface that is very sensitive, just like the original iPhone screen surface. I have seen these protect the screen on several occasions (I am an IT Director and used these for execs and IT personnel.)

The only issue I have with the latest one, the iPhone 6S screen protector, is it's not a full screen protection because the screen is curved around the edges. So, at the edge of the screen protector, there seems to be a small gap where the screen protector does not touch. I am not sure if this is "by design" or because of the curved screen. I don't like this gap and would prefer it to be be secure 100% around the screen. See attached pics for examples of this. Also, I would highly suggest you purchase a decent, heavy duty case such as the inexpensive, TechArmor iPhone 6s case [[ASIN:B00MF8U0RS Apple iPhone 6 Case, Tech Armor Apple iPhone 6S / iPhone 6 (4.7-inch) Air Space Grey/Clear FlexProtect Perfect Fit Case]] It adds protection for the parts of the screen, not covered by this screen protector.

There is an edge to edge version of this ballistic glass screen protector from Tech Armor. [[ASIN:B00OY5T5SA iPhone 6S Screen Protector, Tech Armor HYBRID Edge to Edge Glass (.2mm) Apple iPhone 6S / iPhone 6 (4.7-inch) Screen Protector (Wht) [1]]]

title: Handy little power supply (6700 mAH)
text:
This is a nice little power supply, some details about it.
* Box includes power supply and USB to USB micro cord to recharge it.
* No powerbrick. You either need your own power brick (I suppose it's assumed we all have a number of these kicking around) or need to hook it up to a laptop to recharge it.
* Easy to use. Plug it in and hit the button and start charging. Hit the button when nothing is connected and 1 of 4 LEDs will light up to give an approximate charge level.
* Design is quite nice though I suppose it help to generally like the Duracell battery design.
* Charging my iPhone 8 from about 25% charge used about 1 led light on the power supply. The box says you should be able to get about 2 charges to pre-iPhone x out of it. This seems reasonable from my quick test.
* Heat. I didn't notice any excess heat when charging the supply (I get quite a bit when charging a different brand)
* Airline carry-on compliant.
* No supply to phone connection built in or cable included. I get that many power supplies don't include USB micro or C or lightning cables but I have one that has this and it is VERY handy.

All in all, a nice looking, easy to use 6700 mAH external power supply.

title: Great product, great service..
text:
So about two weeks ago I went on a road trip with my best friend and I saw that she had this car phone mount. I liked it because of how it looked and because the material is silicone. I knew it would look awesome in my car.

I got the package within 2 days so it was super fast shipping!

I couldn't wait to install it in my car so I decided to do it as soon as I got it. I was so sad when the mount didn’t hold my phone tightly. I wanted to know why so I clicked "sold by" - "ask a question" to contact Vanmass customer service. They responded quick!. I got two guide pictures, a video, and suggestions.

The instruction they provided were:
After placing the mobile phone, grasp the back place of the clamp arms (as shown in the red circle in the first picture) and press them tightly towards the center. Until you can't hear the sound of the pressing sound. This allows the clamp arms to play their maximum role-- well fix and protect the phone.

That turned out to be my issue.. the grasp place I put before is the front place of the clamp arm (like the blue circle in the second picture). So actually, I didn't make the clamp arms tight. Thanks to the Vanmass service team for helping me out. Now it's stable to use and the phone isn't loose. It also provides the safest guarantee for our phones. A must have companion on our road trips!

This is a high quality car phone mount and I loved that the seller was able to help me out quickly. Thanks, Vanmass!

title: So many bubbles, can't remove them all...not even when I try so hard it cracks the glass...
text:
Phone: iPhone SE 2020 (2nd generation)

OK, so I'm not a complete newb with glass protectors. I've put them on my old Samsung A01 and on the company's two mobile phones. Little to no problem.

Now I try Mr. Shieldz on my iPhone SE. Yes, I watched the how-to video first.

Attempt #1
Clean the screen carefully. Being very careful, I place the glass on the phone. No problem, placed correctly. BUT...bubbles. Lots of bubbles. Lots and lots and lots of tiny bubbles, plus a few big bubbles. Lots of the tiny bubbles don't go away, and even some of the large bubbles are giving me trouble. I press harder. They still don't go away. I press harder. I crack the glass. A big crack on the edge of the glass.

Dispose of first glass shield. Warn myself to "go easy" on the next one.

Attempt #2
Clean the screen carefully. Being very careful, I place the glass on the phone. Slightly off this time, but still good enough for the phone to function correctly. BUT...still bubbles. Lots of bubbles. Lots and lots and lots of tiny bubbles, plus a few big bubbles. Lots of the tiny bubbles don't go away, and even some of the large bubbles are giving me trouble. I press harder. The tiny bubbles still don't go away. I press harder. I crack the glass. A minor crack...again on the edge.

OK, so:
I can NOT remove the bubbles that form under the shield, not even when I press so hard that I crack the glass on the edge that I am pushing toward. (Note: both attempts, in the middle of the long side of the glass at the edge.) The bubbles remain stubbornly in place. NEARLY TWO DOZEN bubbles remain under the glass.

I won't be buying this brand again for my iPhone SE. Maybe this brand works on other phones, but not on this phone.

title: Pure Garbage
text:
I do not know what video recorder these other folks have gotten, but the one I received is total trash and I am returning it. Let me give you a few of the highlights.
Batteries: one was dead on arrival, the other holds its charge for about 20 minutes.
Image quality: If this is a 2.7 K 42 MP image then I am a moose and we all know moose don’t know how to type. And yeah, I did try every setting offered on the camera just in case they accidentally had the high quality and low quality settings reversed. The image quality here is extremely poor and it is full of JPG artifacts. The image is constantly bouncing and moving more than a bad signal from 1980s rabbit ears on a TV.
White balance: suuuuuuure. Overcompensates so much in one direction or the other that I was either orange or blue. No middle ground.
Auto focus: it is auto focused in one place and one place alone. Don’t move too far away from or closer than that area.
Microphone: don’t even bother. It will just frustrate you more.
The only positive it gets from me is that it is easy to navigate and understand the menus. That, however, is not worth all the downside.
Bottom line, this video camera is total garbage and I see on deeper investigation that I should have done before that this company built up their reviews with a different product. Shady. Don’t waste your money or effort with this. My 16 year old digital video camera takes better footage.

title: Weight counts
text:
Just received today. Specs say 7oz, but actual weight is 10.6oz. Otoh, it does have USB-C, it's bidirectional and PD. The alternative is to velcro the lightest 10k mAhr bank (5.5oz) to a 2oz Lixada solar panel with the advantage of being able to monitor the half-Amp power generation and disadvantage of fiddly connectors. For hikers, the decision usually comes down to weight.

Dizaul makes a nice panel, but it's too heavy to make it into the pack. The panel advertises 0.23A (vs 0.5A Lixada) solar panel. One would think designers could put a half-size panel in for half the weight? Instead, it weighs almost triple? Maybe the wireless charger adds the weight? Not sure who's (inefficiently) wireless charging, when they need a portable battery, but maybe that's a big market?

Dizaul seems like a company on top of technology? First to USB-C, clean waterproof design and it all seems to work properly? Maybe on the next design-cycle make the smaller battery-banks ultralight? Dump the wireless, add a tiny bidirectional current meter (2g, see "Gearmo" meter) for solar and an extra mounting hole to prevent swinging (Lixada has many mounting holes)?

Gave five-stars, because Dizaul's ahead of others, but it's really 4.55 due to its weight. Next time, after others catch-up, rating may go down? Unless Dizaul 3.0 weighs 6oz? 6oz is six-stars.

text:
I was asked by the company to review this band and was given the product. My opinions are not in any way influenced by the company and are solely mine.

This watch band is a great band for the price. The magnet is strong, it fits my wrist well, it's light weight, and it looks quite nice. The reason I only gave it 4 stars is for two reasons.

1) It does pinch my arm hair. I have another milanese band from a different company and it has never pulled my arm hair. It also had a tiny link that must have been loose or something, but it snagged one of my shirts, which was kind of irritating because it was new and kind of expensive (for what I normally pay for clothes).

2) The buttons on the frame don't quite contact the buttons on the actual watch in the same way that the frame that comes with the watch does. I find myself having to push the button in harder and push a few times before it is responsive.

Would I buy this again? Yes. I think it is a nice band for the price.

One thing to note is that I did not have a chance to workout with it to test the magnet during a P90x3 workout, but it is stronger than my other milanese band and I think it would hold up very well during a workout.

title: Recommended especially to those who require excellent protection without the bulk
text:
I was very impressed by the quality of this case. I have had a number of iPhone cases and this is one of the better ones.
This is a two piece case consisting of a TPU (soft silicone) cover with a tougher plastic outer bumper. At first I was a little puzzled by how this case was supposed to be put on the phone but I soon realized that you have to pull the TPU away from the bumper - I chose to do so where the volume buttons insert into the plastic bumper. Then you place the phone into the TPU cover and slide the bumper on. It is not difficult once you have tried once or twice. It is a very protective case adding a layer around the front and sides of the phone to protect it from bumps. The lip (the amount that the case protrudes above the glass at the edges) was much more than you usually get with most cases (1.2mm where most are 1mm or in many cases, less). This is a good thing if you're prone to dropping your phone. Check out other reviews for casesI have made in the past and you'll see this has been a sore point for me. Not with this phone! In fact the only downside to this case is that the protection that it affords adds a little heft to the size of the phone especially compared to a TPU one piece case but....those cases would not protect the phone as much as this one does.
It's also worth noting that the back of the phone has a very slight pattern on the back made up of raised dots. Looks carefully at the photos and you'll see them. I think it looks good and no doubt helps to protect the phone further acting as a shock absorbing layer. It is possible these will attract dust/dirt if you're constantly removing the case although it is easily cleaned if that happens. The case is made in Korea.

title: A good protector for your phone
text:
On seeing the pictures of the Caseology Parallax case, I was really excited about it. I have been a fan of the color blue all along and hence my iphone is blue. But the green appeared to be different and I wanted to try it out. On seeing the physical product, I wasn't as thrilled as I thought I would be.

The case is made of 2 different material - a soft rubber TPU and a hard PC plastic. The case feels safe but only time will tell if it will hold up good. Now the good and the bad,

Pros
+ The case feels sturdy and fits snug on the phone
+ Design is unique
+ Very nice colour on the soft TPU, but a matte finish on the plastic would've been better imo
+ The cutouts on it are accurate

Cons
- The case feels slippery
- The buttons are stiff and take some effort to press
- It does not provide anywhere on the page that it is Magsafe compatible. That causes a lot of confusion amongst people when they want to work with Magsafe

I'd recommend this one. This is a strict 4.25 to 4.5 out of a 5.

After few month, I am never going back to cradle mounts or mounts that you can’t position your phone perfectly for — especially considering the price difference is less than $10 usually. The only con is that I can’t buy these in bulk for less than $5 each to attach to other things. I have other magnets but this combo of thin 3M VHB adhesive and the ring mount beats most other things I have tried.

title: Doesn't really work with the iPad Air 2
text: I'm a university student and I was interested in using my iPad Air 2 for note-taking. After researching a number of different styluses, this one seemed like it would be the best option for me. The stylus itself is a nice weight and feels comfortable to hold, but the cap on top covering the charging port tore off after I gently pushed it back to charge the pen. You also twist the pen to turn it on, and while I write it really likes to twist itself back off, which is incredibly frustrating. As for the pen's writing capabilities, it's not every accurate or consistent. Sometimes it's very sensitive and a light tap will register, while other times you must press hard to get a response. It disconnects very easily, and quite regularly. I tried using it with Goodnotes 4 and Bamboo Paper, however neither of them work with the pen very well. This is an incredibly frustrating stylus to work with and I would not recommend for anyone using an iPad Air 2.

title: All of the Quality & Features of More Expensive Brand Models
text:
This Mariety Phone Mount For Car is a replacement for my older phone mount of the same design. The old one was deteriorating from heavy use. This is a solid car mount with many ways to mount your phone for visibility and access. The stickey/suction mount base holds the unit firmly on a fine pebbled plastic dashboard surface. After mounting it, I had to reposition it slightly and it took quite an effort to release the grip.

The unit holds my Pixel 7 Pro easily and firmly. The gripping jaws firmly hold the phone by pinching the jaws/arms together firmly. It releases the phone just as easily by pressing a mechanical release arm on the lower right side of the cradle. The release is positioned so that the phone will not be released inadvertently while adjusting the phone angle.

This phone cradle is completely mechanical. It does not require power to use. It does not (and does not claim) to wirelessly charge your phone. It has adequate space between the support feet at the base of the phone to insert the charging cord into the base of the phone.

The phone cradle can be rotated to display the phone in portrait or landscape views. The phone mount also comes with a air vent louver mounting bracket, which worked well, but did not position my phone conveniently in my vehicle, so I haven't stress tested it on rough roads.

A good, basic automotive phone mount at a very reasonable price.

title: So far, so good
text:
I just installed the 5s screen to my daughter's phone, which had been cracked for over a month. Out of warranty, Apple was charging us about $269, our Sprint insurance was a $200 deductible fee, the mall kiosk repair guys around $150...
I settled on Icracked based on word of mouth reviews on Reddit and other sites and saw that it had the least trifling Amazon reviews.
I've replaced 3 iphone 5c screens before (just screen swaps), so I was pretty familiar with the inside of the phone and its delicate cables.

The whole process took me 2 hours b/c the phone had been missing screws (I used some from a leftover 5c) and I was frozen on a couple steps.
The kit is great, but use some scotch tape to stick your screws on in chronological order of removal, as they WILL get lost if you don't. I also found it helpful to use the foam cushion that shipped with the phone as a protective surface to lay the screen on when working with the back part. When you're done and ready to close the phone be careful to seat the screen in without forcing it! I found that using the flat side of the black "spudger" was a good tool to help press the inner metal sides of the new screen into the housing. The instructions are pretty clear, but not the booklet's photos. I went online to ifixit for clear pics.
I see no wash-out or lines. It looks like the real deal! Fingers crossed!!!

title: BEST IN MARKET - u Get what u pay for - strong suction cup, magnets and charger
text:
I tried several different types of phone holders for my Samsung Galaxy S8+ (Beast). They either failed by falling off wherever I had them suction cup mounted (suction cup failure) or the mechanical pressure clamps that held the phone itself vertically failed, broken plastic from stress, clamping ability failure. I had one that actually fell apart - maybe due to size and weight of phone or maybe due to poor craftsmanship - none of these device also CHARGED phone wirelessly.

Now the Scosche is not the least expensive option - it is in the high priced category and I usually don't go there unless there is a reason - well after much research and reviews - I decided to give this a try - first one I bought locally so I could touch and inspect it physically before I laid out that much cash for a phone holder / charger. But when you see and hold this product u can see the quality in build and materials - weight, build structure, operation and components / materials used and the perfection in build tolerances, fit and finish is perfect to my eyes.

Lots of metal in the right places for strength, durability and quality. OK how does it perform- we own two one for wife and me. For the first time I used the suction cup mount on dashboard (with other brands I used windshield cause of better adhesion). This product had a very wide, sticky and strong suction cup with lock so I tried the more difficult to stick dashboard surface - after cleaning as per detailed instructions. It came off once during the extreme heat wave of 95+ heat and 90%+ humidity that last almost 2 weeks straight - to be expected in those temp extremes with car windows closed parked in sun in driveway for a few days without driving and A/C.
After re-sticking and driving on all kinds of road surfaces (smooth highway to pot hole ridden stop/go bumper to bumper Jersey shore traffic adhesion was flawless.

Charging and magnetic holder - my only complaint is that Scosche could have provided double the number of metal plates (2 sets of each size/type instead of just 1) first because of need and second because of price paid - these plates are not expensive item to manufacture and it is difficult finding after market plates that fit and work with this unit. Why u say? Because I bought new cover for S8+ (Otterbox Strata wallet style cover - see separate review for it) - this is a strong, thick leather wallet style cover also very high quality but it is also much thicker/denser than old plain plastic snap on cover/protector. I was concerned that wireless charging thru this material and magnetic strength thru the same - would be an issue especially with the location (small area) on Samsung phones for wireless charging - the base charger has only about 1/8-3/16" play up/down & side/side - phone must be aligned correctly for charging to begin - add (or subtract) to that the addition of rectangular shaped metal plates one on top and one on bottom and the placement of the camera and finger print reader on back of phone and u have to be very careful where u place metal plates (U really can't remove them once they are set in place and adhesive sets - again why an extra set should be supplied since u don't mount these plates to the actual phone - u mount to cover either inside between phone and cover if cover is thin enough or outside on back of cover like in my case with the Otterbox Strata.

Did magnets hold phone vertically and securely and after alignment - did the phone charge wirelessly consistently? Yes on both accounts - magnets are excellent - superior strength = phone has never fallen off charger/holder due to magnet slippage - only once when the suction cup failed not the magnets - as far as charging - through this very thick Otterbox cover - yes - as well as my inside desktop wireless charger that is not being bounced around in a car and is extra slippery on surface so phone moves if u blow on it too hard. I would say that once aligned properly (not a lot of wiggle room for alignment) and Samsung phone beeps to let u know its charging (really can't see charging BLUE LED on Scosche - its covered by the huge S8+ size) - Don't recommend trying to align phone while driving - too distracting and in my case I can't reach that far without removing seatbelt. In my case navigation is not thru cell its separate car system with larger screen - but if I had to use phone screen, I would probably not use Otterbox cover cause of front cover on Otterbox - would have to be folded back over back cover and that would be too thick for magnets and charging - so I would use old plastic cover for phone with open front while driving (old metal plates still there) and use Otterbox when I leave car - changing covers is literally a snap.

So testing the Scosche in the worst possible case I can think of - thick leather Otterbox cover/protector, with Samsung very sensitive small wireless charging area on back of phone - this is a worst case test and the Scosche passed with flying colors - it also accepts my dual output high current car 12 Volt fast charging adapter (cigarette lighter adapter) - this is higher current and faster charging than most regular cigarette lighter to usb converters and newer car built in USB charge ports - u want the highest your phone can handle - in my case 2 amp. Product comes with 12 Volt car adapter that is also high current for fast charging (2 Amps) and different bases for different mounting options - it is a complete package also has stick on wire holders to route USB wire from back of magnetic holder/charger to power source whether you plug directly into USB plug or use the included 12 volt cigarette outlet converter to USB.
HIGHLY RECOMMENDED BEST PRODUCT OF THIS TYPE AVAILABLE ANYWHERE - PRICE IS FAIR CONSIDERING RELIABLITY AND BUILD and it holds and charges phone - at same time.

Chris

title: Great value, great product, good installation instructions
text: I highly recommend these screen protectors. I purchased my new iPhone at a local store and the store was selling screen protectors, $50 for one tempered glass screen protector. I couldn’t make myself do that and had a feeling I could find something of similar quality a lot cheaper. Fortunately, Amazon came through for me once again. However, the instructional video and instructions provided with the screen protectors explained the procedure quite well and I was able to install mine for the first time with no problems. I have had mine for over a month now, it’s working exactly as my old screen protector on my previous phone which I had for over six years and dropped many times. title: ITMBET Holds Charge Well and Compares Favorably to the Original Alcatel
text:
The ITMBET TLi013C1 battery for my Alcatel Go Flip 3 flip phone held its charge well and compares favorably to the original Alcatel. It was received at 62% charge as measured on the Go Flip 3 phone.

The original TLi013C1 battery performed the best of all. Of three replacements that I bought on Amazon, I returned two of them because they failed to hold a charge (see my other reviews). One lost 27% percent of its charge in 3 days without using the flip phone at all.

Both the original Alcatel and ITMBET batteries held their charge at 100% after being fully charged, removed from the phone for 3 days, reinserted into the phone, and measuring the battery strength.

For the discharge rate of both batteries when the phone was not used at all, the results were similar enough for me to decide to keep the ITMBET battery.

Original Alcatel TLi013C1 discharge rate when phone was not used:
0 hours @ 100% charge
48 hours @ 87% charge
54 hours @ 85% charge

ITMBET TLi013C1 discharge rate when phone was not used:
0 hours @ 100% charge
48 hours @ 82% charge
54 hours @ 78% charge

By comparison to a battery that I returned on Amazon.
WayPro TLi013C1 discharge rate when phone was not used:
0 hours @ 100% charge
24 hours @ 81% charge
37 hours @ 73% charge

BOTTOM LINE: The ITMBET TLi013C1 held its charge almost as well as the original Alcatel TLi013C1.

title: Slim, light weight, nice
text:
I often forget to charge my phone and it usually tend to die at the most crucial moment. This Portable Charger Wireless Power Bank is a great solution to my problem. It is not bigger than my iPhone XR and because it is wireless I don't need the cords. But I can still use the cords for other phones, if any of my friends will be in immediate need of extra life for their phones.
Now about the performance of this Portable Charger Wireless Power Bank. It took >20% of bank power to give my phone >15% battery life. And it charged 50% of my phone's battery in more than an hour (wireless), - not perfectly fast. And it takes forever to charge the bank itself via computer. Better to plug it in adapter, but the cord is so short - just about 11 inches! - you have to keep it close to outlet.
Though the battery bank has kind of rubber covering, the phone won't stay on it while driving the car, for example. It should be lay flat on stable surface to do the job. The phone holder is not a necessity for the charger, and it doesn't charge the phone when it is in the holder.
It has the button to turn the power on, but to turn it off you have to wait. It turns off itself, sometimes while my phone is laying on it, waiting to be charged, and SURPRISE! - the bank turned itself off and the charging process was interrupted.
On stand by the bank holds the charge good - only 1-3% per day.

title: Well-Priced, Waterproof, And Does The Job, But Tight Retaining Loop
text:
My husband has been looking for waterproof and warm-weather appropriate watch bands to replace some of his leather ones for the season. While he likes his leather watch straps, he finds that they get uncomfortable during the sweaty spring/summer months. I suggested that he try out this Silicone Smart Watch Band. After replacing one of his leather watch straps with this one and wearing it for a while, he debated between giving this band 3 or 4 stars. Ultimately, he settled on 4 because the watch band is currently so well priced on Amazon. He said that if the price rises substantially, however, he'd have to reconsider his appraisal.

On the positive side, the band fits his 22mm sport watch perfectly between the lugs. Also, he noticed that the lug end of the band has a slight curvature versus a completely straight end. This slight curve hugs the shape of his watch's round case a bit, and definitely looks better than if it were totally flat across the lug end. Also, the band comes with quick release spring bars, which are very convenient when replacing watch straps. The band is basic black and goes well with many of his watches. While the band does not have the softest silicone material that he's had on a watch band, it is decent and fairly comfortable. He also likes the look and feel of the solid, brushed metal buckle.

The negatives he found were in regard to how smoothly, or rather not smoothly, the band goes onto the wrist. The first issue is that the band tends to catch on the sides of the buckle as it's going through. The second issue is that the retaining loop is tight, and very snug when trying to pass the the end of the watch band through. My husband is hoping that with more use, the band will wear in and the loop will loosen up. However, these issues can be inconvenient and annoying, and detract from the watch band's positive aspects. Overall though, the band does the job, is waterproof, and very affordable, so my husband can overlook the difficulty encountered when putting it on.

title: Easy way to fix a wrong purchased cable!
text:
I bought a couple high end usb cables and thought they were for micro-usb (I didn't read the entire description). Since I liked the cables and hate returning things, I searched around and found these adapters.
They are FEMALE type C input to MALE micro-usb output. They are used to change a type C charging cord into a micro-usb charging cord.
The reason I am explaining in detail is that it took me forever to find these adapters. Almost all of the ones commonly found were female micro-usb to male type C (used to upgrade old chargi g cords to the new type C connector. This was the ONLY one I could find that reversed the type C connector back to a micro-usb.
They connect tightly and work perfectly!

title: Not a Rift, but an incredible deal.
text:
I've never been a gamer until I tried this - it had me hooked. It was much more comfortable than Google Cardboard and so much cheaper than devices that require high-end phones.

Pros
The "3D" spacialized sound works so well. Some apps suggest headphones but I think the built-in sound may be better.
I didn't get dizzy/sick at all, which I got from the Playstation VR, Google Cardboard, and from many 1st person xbox shooters.
Battery life Is great but I don't have much to compare it to.
The straps felt pretty comfortable on my head, and adjusted easily.
The controller is easy to calibrate, it only takes about 2 seconds and never seemed to lose callibration.
After the initial setup, I never needed my phone. Everything is doable in the Oculus Go's UI.
There's a lot of games, media viewers, web browsers, 360 videos, and more.
Even if you only use this to watch movies, it's still cheaper than buying a huge TV.

Cons
Resolution was good for the price, but could be better
Some light may be visible by the nose, but its better than the nose area being too tight
Only 1 controller

If you've used the Oculus Rift, this isn't as good. You can't move around in the game by moving IRL, the resolution is lower, and the controllers aren't nearly as advanced. Having said that, I would rather have 10 Oculus Go's than 1 Oculus Rift, and that is cheaper than the full Rift Setup.

The 32gb version was enough for plenty of games, however I went with the 64gb version. There will be more games over time and they'll be growing in size. It's also nice to be able to load a bunch of movies & games on it for travel. I plan to buy a few as gifts to family and friends.

title: ridiculously good for the price
text: I can't believe you get TWO 20,000mAh power banks for this price.  Spouse and I game a LOT (Pokemon, Wizards Unite, Ingress, usually all three simultaneously), with 3 phones between us, sometimes for hours on end (what can I say? we've been married 26 years and this is our latest hobby 😂), so we rely heavily on power banks and never carry anything less than 10,000, though 20,000 is preferred. These units are great - two wide USB ports on each so a single power bank can support two phones, and, honestly, you never run out of battery. I recently took both of these camping, and they kept the phones for 5 people charged for 3 days. Granted, I was the only person using their phone super-frequently, but I was super impressed regardless - 3 days is a long time and most battery packs would have run out after just a day or so.  The downside is that these are a bit heavy. They aren't bulky like battery packs used to be, and they're probably smaller and thicker than your current phone (depending on model), but rather dense/heavy. So this isn't a small palm-sized charger like some people prefer, but still perfect for slipping into a back pocket or coat pocket. And honestly usually you'd pay $40-$70 for a single such unit. I can't believe these cost just $30 for two (as of today's prices on Amazon). You're not going to find a better deal than this for serious power needs.

title: I've had three smart phones (i-phone 3gs
text:
I've had three smart phones (i-phone 3gs, Nexus 4 and now this) and this is my favorite. The camera is fantastic and takes beautiful pictures. Unlike the i-phone, I can use it with any Android-compatible accessories and don't have to sell
my firstborn to Apple everytime I need a new cord, and unlike the Nexus it's fairly user-friendly. My only complaints are:

1) short battery life
2) the phone is big, which is great for watching Netflix but it doesn't fit in my universal car phone holder and it's a bit uncomfortable to type on one-handed
3) no quick way to mute the ringer; the volume control affects different types of sounds depending on what you're doing with the phone at the time you use it

UPDATE: It's been 6 months since I first reviewed this phone. While I am still happy with it, I have discovered a couple more problems:

1) In the past couple of weeks I have developed "smart phone thumb," i.e. pain at the base of my right thumb. I never had this with either of my previous smartphones, which were smaller than this one.

2) Twice the phone has crashed and I have been unable to restart it using the button- there seemed to be a disconnect between the button on the back of the phone and the phone itself. Both times I had to take the battery out of the phone to get it to start again.

3) There is something weird with the port in this phone that connects to the power cord. I have already been through 3 android-compatible cords. They plug in fine at the beginning, but after a few uses the connection between the cord and the phone becomes loose, to the point where the phone does not charge, even when it is plugged in.

Installation was a breeze - you twist the elevated stand for the Apple Watch and you can place your Apple Watch charger inside (only the Original one would work). I'd recommend picking one up from Amazon along with a longer USB-C cable since the one that is provided is a bit short - about 3 ft. I am using a 5V/2amp one and it was charging my iPhone, Airpods & Apple Watch fairly decently, but I'd still recommend a QC3 one.

title: Motorola EX119 Changing Language Back to English
text:
I decided to write this review because my phone has English and Thai and one day it switched into Thai Language (squiggly scripting text) and I had to go to a Thai Restaurant to find an interpreter. So to help others out here is how to get to the language screen to switch back to English.

1. Click on Settings (Gear Icon main menu screen)

2. Click on Number Three (3 on left side) = Phone settings

3. Click on Number Three (3 on left side) = Language

4. Next Screen Toggle English which is the top line

5. Hit Save, the check mark button, and you should be back in English mode

On my side, put a little sticky note on the battery so not to forget, better than trips to find an interpretor! Otherwise Great Phone!

title: Fancy!
text: This dash car charger is much fancier than I realized when I purchased it.  It is made of a pretty heavy plastic and the joints have a locking mechanism on them that makes it very stable.  It was easy to install.  I just cleaned the dash with a little alcohol and let it air dry for about a minute, and then stuck the adhesive disk on the dash.  It said to wait 15 minutes, but I waited 24 hours to be sure it was good and stuck.  I plugged it into the fast-charging port in my car and stuck my phone in it and it automatically closed to grip my phone.  I was so surprised by that.  I thought I had to squeeze the sides to make it close, but, nope, it sensed my phone was there and did the gripping all on its own.  I was impressed.  My phone was on 14% battery life and I was actually talking on the phone and mapping us somewhere at the same time.  20 minutes later, I was surprised to see that even though I had been using my phone the entire time, I still had a charge up to 21%.  After I stopped talking on the phone and stopped using the map, my phone charged up to 27% in just 5 more minutes.  So, if you use the right charging plug, this thing will charge your phone up really fast.  It never wavered or looked like it was about to drop my phone at any time.  To remove the phone, just press and hold one or both buttons on the sides and the grips automatically release at a slow, measured pace.  It was very smooth, and very bougee feeling, lol.  I was hoping that the arm of it, at the suction cup part, would swivel so I could rotate it between facing the passenger seat, and facing the driver's side, but you do have to release the suction cup and re-suction it down to the plate to move it.  That makes sense, though, because otherwise the phone could swing around wildly on bumpy or curvy roads.  I live in Central Florida and it gets really hot here, so I'm concerned about the heat melting the glue that holds down the plate on the dash, but I will have to wait a few more months before I can find out if that is an issue.  Otherwise, I am very happy with my purchase.  This is the best car charger I have found so far.

title: GREAT phone - too bad I didn't buy it from someone else...
text:
The problem I have is not with this amazing phone, but with the vendor who sold it to me. My old phone was getting to a point where I was really tempted to just throw it against a wall, so I needed a replacement fast. I didn't want to settle for whatever I could get first - that's how I ended up with the phone I've been using for the past year.
I always wanted this phone. I wanted it before it hit the street. When it was brand new three years ago, its retail price was over $600. I was expecting to pay about a ⅓ of that now. I was really surprised to find it for just over $100!
A lot of vendors are still moving this model. All LG phone are pretty great and really easy to use, but this phone was ahead of its time when it came out, and is still competitive with most new phones being released today. It was the first phone to have more than one camera lens. The sound (especially with wired headphones) is really something else, and you just have to see the pictures and videos to appreciate them, but let me just tell you, they don't even have a bunch of settings (although there is a "manual photo mode" that you kind of have to know what you're doing with a camera to understand how to use it). Basically anybody could put it on auto and take a really good picture without even trying. And the video has a stabilizer to make sure your recordings don't look like the Blair Witch Project. There are audio enhancers to make video sound a lot better too.
This model comes out of the box new with Android 7.0, but is upgradable to 9.0, so you could really have this phone for a few years and not feel like you're missing out not trading in after a year, even two (maybe three!).
Now, here are the reasons I'm giving a 2 star review:

1. I paid the vendor for expedited shipping and didn't get my phone for almost a week. Amazon gave me a credit for the $9 I paid for expedited delivery that I didn't get. At that rate, I should've gotten the phone in two days - not 6.
2. My phone didn't have anyone else's information saved on it, but it was filled with the previous users stupid apps and games. I don't like that. It's a red flag that other problems will be overlooked, and they were.
3. I can't hear or be heard on phone calls without using speakerphone or a headset. I'll have to take it to a repair place at my expense now, because I definitely DO NOT trust this vendor to replace my phone with a better working phone in the same model, and also don't want to be without my new phone for who knows how long.
All that aside, its still probably my favorite phone I've ever used, and in all honesty, I typically use a headset for calls anyway. I just would have liked to *know what I'm getting into* to begin with. But I doubt they even knew. I don't think they fully test what they're selling, and if they think they do, that's so much worse.
I'm a very discriminating consumer, but I review items I buy fairly. The review always accurately reflects my experience with my purchase. I don't like having negative things to say. I'd much rather not have to say them - but I also would really prefer to spare other consumers from a similar experience. I won't buy from these people again. I'd strongly advise others not to either.

(The case in photos was purchased separately, but also on Amazon - and it's a really great case!)

title: Pro: Does a great job, Cons: short AC cable and flimsy stand
text:
This Ring light comes complete with 10.2” light, stand, and phone attachment.

Pros: the stand is fully height adjustable and has a series of easy quick-lock clips. There is also a fully adjustable phone holder which can be rotated 360° and moves in all directions which makes dialing in your frame effortless.

The light is the main event here and because of its large size, (10.2”) it gives off a wide, diffuse light. It is adjustable to three hues - cool, neutral and warm. Best of all, the intensity is fully adjustable with a dimmer that is not incremental but completely smooth. We found it easy to get the precise light level we were looking for in order to complement my partner’s face for her online business videos. It really improved the quality of her videos and made them instantly look far more professional than her previous work.

Cons: the AC cable is shorter than I would've hoped, limited placement unless one attaches it to an AC extension cord. No big deal but it deserves mention.

Also, the stand is a bit flimsy. It seems to be constructed from aluminum. As such it’s very light, and could potentially be knocked over quite easily. Just be mindful of this when in use.

I feel the pros far outweigh the the cons. At this price point, you certainly get a lot of bang for your buck. We’ve tried a couple other low priced units and feel this is currently one of the best ones at this price. Four well deserved stars.
