The other really annoying thing is that there are a plethora of words the phone refuses to put into text, unless you type every letter and click the check mark. Every time.
It will not put these words into the phone's dictionary for you, either. This includes words like "sucks" (and any derivatives of), sexy, butt, and things like that. Really? Trying to say the heat has sucked the life out of you is naughty? Saying your butt hurts from sitting on it is too? I seriously don't need my phone censoring words for me. I'm an adult.
Also, I STILL haven't figured out how to use my own sounds for notifications. So my phone sounds like everyone else's around me. We never know who's phone is getting a text message so we all have to check our stupid phones.

The main "plus" to this phone is that the battery lasts longer than most.

title: I'm so glad I tried these!
text: I received my screen protectors through the mail and immediately began the process to install one on my phone. They were packed in a heavy zip lock style back inside of a small bubble envelope, well protected. I removed the product and examined to make sure that all of the promised content was present and accounted for, and it was. I read the directions first, just to make sure there wasn't anything special for these that I haven't dealt with before. The one thing I noticed with the instructions was that they described the installation of the protectors I'm used to installing. Normally, my protectors are sandwiched between two protective film layers. These only had one protective side. I'm assuming that this is due to them having the anti-glare surface on one side, not a big deal. I placed the protector on my phone to do a test fit. I noticed that this product was actually much smaller than the ones I had put on the phone previously. I found out that i absolutely love the size difference. So many protectors are cut to the exact size of the front of my phone, all the way to the bezel. title: Sturdy and secure case. Great quality, as expected from Spigen!
text:
I used a Rugged Armor case for my Note 5 for 5 years, and I absolutely loved it! It fit well over my screen protector, and even after a good amount of drops, my phone doesn't have any cracks at all. I recently upgraded and decided to go back to Spigen because of my experience with my previous phone.

Needless to say, the Rugged Armor case is a classic. The design looks just like my old case, although the buttons panels are connected by some thin bridges. No problems there yet, although I could envision it collecting dust and possibly having a larger chance of snapping. Otherwise, it's a sleek design that hugs the phone and feels great in my hand. The case is fairly flexible, so it's easy to put on and peel off. However, it's just thick enough that it feels strong and protective. It's durable enough that it protects against normal wear and tear. The buttons feel very great--there's a nice, dulled click and tactile feedback with just enough resistance that it is addicting to press the buttons! The edges are raised above the edge of the phone, so I have no concerns about the screen or camera being damaged when I place the phone down, even on uneven surfaces.

The case also supports wireless charging and fits the phone very nicely. I tried a couple of the knockoffs that you can find on Amazon, but those either feel clumsy or awkward or do not align with the buttons or ports cleanly.

The only downside to this case is that it is not transparent, so it covers the color of the phone. With the Samsung S20 FE, one of the nicest features is the color. I ended up going with the Spigen Ultra Hybrid, but the Rugged Armor case is so nice that I couldn't help but leave a 5-star review for it too.

title: Did not last more than a week - way to many issues to be a long term iWatch protector - CANNOT GET WET with iWatch 3!
text:
I would not recommend this to anyone unless they do not use their iwatch under normal conditions as it does not hold up:

Pros:
- Screen matches into the iWatch very well where unless you are really looking, most would not be able to tell the watch has a screen protector.
- Glass screen protector that looks pretty well on the face (I also list this as a con - see below) that is probably better than flexible screen protectors.
- Easy to put on without bubbles.

Cons:
- Glass screen protector is not crystal clear like a amFirm iphone glass protector that I think does not take aware the iPhone clarity at all. I would rate this one about 90% of clear, where you do loose the OLED crystal clear sharpnes of the screen when installed (you do get used to it but shame to lose anything from the nice OLED screen.
- Sensitivity is lost. Pushing on an icon seems to be pretty good as one is pressing down. I found swiping does have frequent misses where you have to double swipe to get the screen to scroll in about 10-20% of the swipes.
- Corners of the glass protector that wrap around the watch are evidently very fragile. I did not have mine installed more than a week and the glass fractured and broke and I never recall hitting the watch on anything.
- THIS IS A BIG ONE FOR ME - I have a water proof iWatch 3 and my install was bubble free. First time I took a shower with the installed screen protector, about 80% of the screen was separated with a large bubble/water underneath that did not try out. Description did not say anything about not getting your iWatch 3 wet.
- Package describes getting the dust removal tape and wet/dry wipes. My wet wipe was bone dry and no dust removal tape. Contacted the seller, they blame Amazon (even though Amazon just ships out the pre-packaged item so they only shipped what was given to them). Seller to promptly send me out another - same result. No dust removal tape.

title: From a Z1 Copact user
text:
I've owned a Z1 Compact and it was my favorite phone. However, it wasn't as "water resistant" as advertised and I ended up messing it up pretty bad. Now I am trying my luck with Z3 Compact but keeping it on land. Same great size, nearly identical to the Moto X (2013) and original Compact. It fits in your hand well, super light, and a surprising amount of screen on such a small frame. To top it off, it has a bigger battery than many 5"+ phones. The gross fingerprint issue found on the Z1 has been solved, but its still made of glass all over so I will be getting a screen protector and case. I think the rim has also changed from metal to plastic but overall has a much better look so I don't mind. Port covers have been cleaned up going from 3 to 2. Camera is excellent as you'd expect from an Xperia.

One HUGE drawback and the reason for the -1 start – Its riddled with Vodefone junkware in addition to Sony's gaudy candy shell icon themed apps. 'adb shell pm block ...' is your new friend to clean up the waste that cannot be uninstalled or disabled. It also seems to be lacking the Sony notes app that was found on the Z1, its silly, but I really liked it and its a shame to see Keep replace it. Users should not have to strip out or replace core system components but it seems like this device is particular crufty out of the box. The hardware is why I bought it though and if you are the slightest bit curious you can fix all of its shortcomings which are all software related as far as I can tell.

title: Sleek looks, lots of power, and THREE top-mounted ports make this a winner
text:
I'm a sucker for power banks. We can never have enough back-up power for our ever-expanding collection of wireless devices, and this one is my new favorite.

It sports a hefty capacity in a sleek design. It has a soft-touch plastic exterior that almost feels like smooth rubber. Not tacky (so it won't stick in your pocket), but not so slippery that you feel like it'll slide out of your hand. The view screen is large and clear enough to see at a glance. The flashlight isn't going to blow you away, but might come in handy when you need a bit of light in a dark room. The block is slightly taller and slightly skinnier than other 20k banks I have, but appears smaller and sleeker at a glance. I was surprised to find it was almost the same size when I put them next to each other. It will fit easily in a pant pocket, but might be too heavy for some tastes. A small backpack pocket or purse might be a more comfortable place for on the go charging.

And speaking of pockets, what pushes this charger to the top of my collection and makes it my new go-to for a day out is that all three ports are top-mounted. Side-mounted ports make for awkward cord positioning in a pants' pocket or skinny bag, whereas ports on top allow the cords to exit the pocket un-kinked. Having the input port (to charge the power bank) also function as a rapid-charge output port is a huge plus. Using the cord that came with my Google Pixel 6, I was able to rapid-charge my phone as quickly as plugging it in to the wall charger I normally use.

In limited multi-device testing, the charger was able to charge three devices at the same time, including rapid-charging via the USB-C port while standard charging the devices plugged into the two USB ports.

In single-use charging, the bank was able to bring an aging iPhone XR from roughly 20% to full in about 2 hours while using the phone steadily at the same time, and brought the power bank from 85% to about 55%. Standard charge speeds were a bit faster when the phone wasn't in use, obviously, but generally speaking if I'm using a portable charger on the go, it'll be to keep a phone alive and charged while in use, and this one is more than up to the task. It should be able to provide multiple full charges to phones before needing to be charged itself. The charger never felt warm to the touch while in use, though all tests were done inside in the air conditioning.

The charger arrived neatly packed and had 85% charge right out of the box. IMPORTANT NOTE: Don't overlook the included charging cable and carrying pouch! They are tucked into the rolled ends of the cardboard sleeve that the charger ships in. I almost overlooked them...don't accidentally throw them out!

Bottom line: This checks all the boxes for what a portable charger should offer. Convenient size for carrying, plenty of backup power, able to charge a phone while using it, and enough ports to keep several devices going at once. The top-mount positioning is a huge plus!

title: Very bulky but quite surdy
text:
I had my Fold 2 naked for a month before this got here and I have really enjoyed how slim and compact it is. My phone fits in my pocket without a problem and doesn't feel overly boxy. This case removes all of the sleek lines and replaces them with jarring edges and corners. Most annoyingly this case adds about 1/5th of an inch / half a centimeter to the width of the phone. That may not sound like a lot but that is roughly the same thickness as the unfolded phone already, which means that it adds about another 50% of thickness to what is already the thickest phone on the market (when folded). Additionally, the protector around the bezel on the front screen is so thick that I can't even pull down the app try from the top anymore. My finger can't swipe over the top edge to pull down the notifications or system tray.
I will say that this thing feels very sturdy and I am not nearly as worried as I have been for the past month about it getting damaged. This thing is like one step down from an Otter Box. It doesn't actually have screen protectors on the case as there are already some pre installed by Samsung on the phone itself but it does a great job of protecting the outsides, the corners, and most notably, the hinge as I have found few other cases that cases that actually cover the hinge.
In the end, this is too much case for me. Too big, more protection than I probably need for my lifestyle and the added thickness and inability to swipe down from the top on the outside screen are a deal breaker for me.
My Spigen Thin Fit case is already on the way.

title: Best case for accident-prone individuals, everyday use
text: The first case I received was not waterproof, so I exchanged through Amazon. I wish lifeproof's warranty were a bit better, you shouldn't have to pay for shipping and handling to replace a brand new case that you never used if it came from the manufacturer defective. It's supposed to be waterproof from the get-go. My other complaint is that my screen is often activated by the side of my face when I am talking on the phone using this case. I think this has to do with the offset created by the bumper around the screen, but it's a small price to pay to protect my screen from shattering. I love that I am able to touch the actual screen of my phone while having it fully protected from water and dust. I bake a lot, so my phone gets coated in flour and splashed by liquid, but this case has not leaked yet! I test is periodically using the dummy phone included just to ensure it is still waterproof. Unfortunately, my case just got a crack in the thin piece of plastic between the screen and the home button, so i have to deal with lifeproof to get a new one as it has been less than 6 months...so the case isn't really lifeproof, but since it's relatively cheap for this model and it's only a few bucks to redeem the warranty, I don't mind. It's better than the fre case I had previously, as the home button covers always wore out after a few months as well, and they reduced touchscreen sensitivity.

title: You get what you pay for…
text:
Pros:

- For the price of about $20 you get a knock off Gameboy that fits in your pocket. (Affordable)

- Has a good selection of games to play.

- Is made from hard plastic that would most likely withstand small drops. The screen may not survive though.

- Has decent sound quality.

- Looks cool.

- It doesn’t take very long to charge.

- It’s very portable so it’s great for long car rides.

- The buttons for the actual phone part of the case are very clicky and respond properly to touch.

Cons:

- The screen cuts off some of the text in game. So in order to see it you have to turn your phone to the side to see under the black rim.

- The buttons have a decent amount of input lag. Sometimes they don’t respond at all so they may need to be pushed down twice.

- The rubber buttons tend to get stuck under the plastic case after pushing them down.

- The screen is very poor quality and hurts my eyes to look at after using for a little while. Mainly this is an issue on the menu screen. Once your in game the quality seems to improve slightly. It could just be the way they setup the menu in terms of brightness and color choices.

- The controls can be a bit confusing. But once you figure it out it gets a lot better.

- The case really won’t protect your phone very much, so be sure to not use this as your day to day case.

- There are spelling errors. One such example is that they called Tetris, “Tetrisa”.

title: Too bulky, too intrusive. Top of the line protection but too much to be truly useful.
text:
There's so much to like about this case I hate to be this critical of it.

But, cases have gotten increasingly better lately and starting with the Note 8 and then the Galaxy S9, things got great. If you look at the higher end Note 8 cases, everything works well and they even have that Marquee scrolling of the time. The s9 cases have the transparent flap with open access to the buttons that allow you to look into it even when the case was closed.

I tried this case. The fit is excellent in terms of not being too tight, not being too lose and keeping open access to the back. Well, not so much on the last one, the fingerprint reader has been a headache since I tried this case. The side buttons are a total pain too. Instead of just feeling for them and changing my volume or invoking Bixby, I have to often play around with them. It bugs me, it'll bug you too.

This case offers high levels of protection, I think you'd survive just about any drop with it. I dare say it almost provides more than you need. The see through plastic case doesn't put much heft on the front and top, but adds a notable amount on the back and sides.

The reason I can't use this a lot though is that I end up taking 5 or six seconds trying to get the fingerprint to work, even after I've adapted to the new fit. The volume buttons have the same issue. If you drop your phone alot and need a lot of protection, this will work but for me, the tradeoff wasn't worth it.

title: As long as you fit the profile, this is a great device.
text:
I like this and I think it's beneficial but it has very specific use cases. As the description states, you need to have a provider that allows use of a booster. That's a big deal but I have T-Mobile so it was not a problem for me. The next big issue is that you need to have a fair amount of range to set the device up. I tried using it constrained in my home office and I wasn't able to get anything of significance. When I separated the components into other rooms, it started to work much better. lastly, you MUST have connectivity to begin with. If you have 1 bar for instance, this will give you a benefit. If you're in a dead zone, you'll stay in a dead zone. Each of these are major factors b/c chances are, you may be looking into one of these b/c you have these problems to begin with.

I've already set up a booster before and got a pretty decent benefit so I knew what I was doing. I was able to swap out my old one with this one and had everything in place already (the only difference is where I had to place the components but i did my homework already. Setup can be a little daunting if you're not handy although any semi-competent handy man can get this set up for your pretty easily and cheaply.

I noticed other people mentioning that you needed a lot of cable. I found that to be the case as well. In my case, it's about 15-20 meters. Since I had it set up before, I was already prepared although I had to get a longer cable b/c my components weren't that far apart before.

So what was the end result? The low zones in my house, which would waver between 1-2 bars, went to full speed or right under it (I can't say for sure but during some bad storms it seems to decrease a little, but I don't know if that's related to the receiver or the original connection.

If you have the space, have some connectivity and have dead or bad zones in your house, this will definitely do the trick. I bought one before and was willing to pay for this one (although in full disclosure I got it through Vines) so yes, I think it's worth it.

title: Don't buy if for Nexus 7 w/case
text:
I received this as a gift. For $50 bones, it needs to charge through tablet cases. I can't get it to work with the Moku Slim Fit ([[ASIN:B008FLYROG MoKo Slim fit Google Android Tablet]] From what I've seen it only works with the Poetic Slimline case (some reported that didn't even work for them) and, conveniently, the official Google case. It's more of a hassle to take it out of the case then it is to use this charger. I don't really want to get a new case just to use this, and it seems it won't charge then.

The only thing Google says about this product on their website is that "Important: If you have a case on your Nexus device, you may need to remove it to charge your device." [...] So at least they tell you. However, this fact is actually omitted on the paper copy of the Wireless Charger quick start guide included in the box.

If you use your Nexus 7 caseless it works wonderfully. No problem finding this sweet spot, magnet works well, seems to charge quickly, and is quiet. However I don't have any other Qi capable devices, so I'll probably sell it.

title: Nice secure phone mount for your bike to make your ride more enjoyable!
text:
I had the opportunity to test out these headphones for the seller.

Easy to install – 3 – see comments below
Quality of material – 5
Versatility - 5
Security features – 3
Sturdiness – 5

What I liked:
• I was able to mount my iPhone on my handlebars to use my phone and listen to music.
• Also, allowed me to use a free bike app and eliminate the cost of buying a bike computer which more than offset the cost of the phone mount.
• Full phone access
• Looks well-made and visually appealing.
• Mounts easily to my bike handle bars with the claw grip and big enough to mount on my frame.
• Additional phone mounting rubber bands included since eventually the rubber bands will break.
• Price competitive to other brands
• Seller offers a metal version of the product for heavy duty use for ~$5 more.
• Seller’s refund or replacement policy

What I don’t like:
• Hard to mount my iPhone 11 into the phone holder especially the rubber banding of the 4 corners. Would be a real pain if you had to remove the phone numerous times on your ride. I do have a case on my phone so probably part of the problem.
• I doubt I would use this mount on a motor cycle. I just see the claw loosing up and a $700+ phone being damaged and even lost on the highway. I’m using it on a bike so same thing could happen but not driving at high speeds and on a freeway. I would think for motorcycle use you would want something more fail proof.

Room for Improvement:
• Rubber band mounting system
• Fail safe for motorcycle usage by use of more secure mounting of phone mount to motorcycle and phone to phone mount.

title: Thin / Best For Smaller-Sized 'Loads'
text:
I received a free item to review. The entire collection of bags out of the box gave off quite a strong offgassing of lavender scent, which bothered us (although our dog was quite intrigued). I ended up storing all but the current roll in the garage.

The bags are smaller than supermarket plastic bags we use and, at first, were a little tricky to open. Once you get the knack they're comparable to thin kitchen garbage container bags. However, thin plastic means you'll be feeling more of what your dog leaves on the ground than you do when scrunching up a heavier bag. The design makes them easy enough to tie and seal without having any 'aroma' escape.

I like the oversized capsule dispenser if you're going on a road trip, otherwise, like garbage bags, it feels natural for us to just tear a bag off the roll as needed.

The bottom line is the bags do the job without any fear of breaking and the 640 count should last us well over a year.

text:
After reading the reviews on the 1st generation model, I found this to be much heavier duty than I expected. It looks and feels like it would last through commercial use. I was expecting something cheap. I used it to cut a new SIM card to MicroSIM size and it worked in my iPhone 4. One reviewer said that it only cut half way through, and I think I know why. It is cutting a square, so as it cuts the first part, it snaps and sounds like it is done, but you have to push down until it cuts all the way. It will snap a second time. Once this is done, the SIM will eject out the bottom and land on the table with a nice clean cut all the way around.

One note. The SIM was a tight fit in the SIM carrier, so I had to make sure it was perfectly flush in the carrier before it would slide into the phone. Once inserted, it worked perfectly.

The only reason I needed this item was that my AT&T contract was over and I had AT&T unlock my iPhone 4. This allowed me to use my AARP discount at Consumer Cellular and keep my iPhone. I plan to purchase a Nokia Lumia 920 soon and this SIM will work in it as well.

title: shows off the design of the iphone
text:
It took me hours to finally pick a cover for my new Verizon white Iphone! There are THOUSANDS to choose from. I had seen the metallic looking ones and thought they looked cool and sleek, but then reviewers said the color chips off. Otter boxes are just too bulky. I wanted something that was hard, but not hard plastic that could break or came in two pieces. I didn't want silicone or anything that would catch fur/hair/lint or obstruct from a quick insert into my pocket. I guess what I really wanted was a cover that would protect from drops, but not add bulk to my phone, and yet have a nice design that showed off the design of the phone.

This case fits the bill! It is a clear firm rubber, that is very transparent. The lip that comes up over the top of the phone gives a great amount of protection to the front. The circular design on the back is nice. It is not paint, it is actually carved on the inside of the cover. It has openings for the volume, mute and on/off switch. I like that personally. I have heard other cases can push down on the buttons if they are snug. This avoids that issue. This rubber will not end up stretchy like some of the silicone cases.

The screen protector was a joke. The little plastic piece they send along for removing bubbles actually scratched it all up. Do yourself a favor and get a Zagg. They can be pricey, but they are indestructible, don't cause glare and resist smudging. Sign up for their mailing list and you'll end up with a 50% off coupon at some point. I am not even basing my rating on this dinky after-thought of a screen protector. It is solely based on the case only. LOVE IT!

title: Enjoy wireless convenience for both your iPhone and Apple Watch!
text: This is a dual charger for any iPhone that uses wireless charging, as well as a magnetic charger for the Apple Watch. Setup is easy; you really just unbox it and the charger and then plug it in. The wireless charger works well. It charges very fast and I noticed it even works through an OtterBox Defender case! The Apple Watch charger works as expected, plus it allows you to position the watch to be used in Alarm mode (laying it on the side). I have had no issues with the charger. This is a more “premium” charger and so it costs more. I believe it does work better than other wireless chargers that I have tried. The one that I had before would not work through an OtterBox case at all. This charger also comes in white or black, which is an added plus. It is a bit pricey, but I believe what you get in terms of the improvement in charging speed as well as the design of the charger is worth it. I have not heard any high pitched noise while using the charger but others have. I would recommend this if you are serious about wireless charging/charing your Apple Watch. It works well, and is a nice addition to any peripheral connection for wireless charging phones.

title: I am in love!
text:
For ruggedized cases, my go-to has always been the Otterbox series. I have heard of Lifeproof but I did not try it because Otterbox was meeting my needs. While I always appreciate the complete protection of the Defender case, the sheer bulk of the case combined with the large size of my iPhone 7 Plus made it very hard to use. I tried an Otterbox Symmetry case, which fits much better, but then it leaves the front part of the phone exposed.

I decided to give this Lifeproof case a try and I am glad I did. This case provides the protection I like in a minimal form factor, so it is not bulky at all! This case also adds waterproofing to the equation, but since the iPhone 7 Plus is designed to be a bit waterproof, that may or may not be a big deal. The case is a little challenging to get open because it seals so tightly, but it is well worth the trouble. It comes with the case, some stickers, and a cleaning cloth. I was able to get the iPhone in the case and sealed without too much issue. The case completely encloses the iPhone, and usually I don't like that because then the touch responsiveness on the display takes a hit. But with this case, whatever they use to cover the screen does not interfere with the display nearly as much as the built-in screen protector on the Otterbox Defender does.

There are instructions on how to test the case if you plan on exposing it to water. I don't but it is nice they included those instructions. The only potential issue I can see with this case is that when you put it on, the switch that covers the mute switch actually changes the direction that you flip it in in order to turn on the vibration or ringer. So you have to press the switch backward to turn the mute off, and forward to enable the mute function.

This is officially my new favorite case for my iPhone! I highly recommend it.

text:
Easy install and looks great. The main reason for this is to protect my expensive Apple Watch from the abuses of daily life and this case does a great job.

I really enjoy how it makes the screen flatter without affecting the touch sensitivity or functions of the watch itself. After about a month so far, the screen adhesion seems spot on and has not lifted at all.
At this point, I've not tested for water intrusion but I usually avoid water with my electronics even if the have a submersion rating.

My only gripe is with the cover for the digital crown. The case does a fine job protecting the crown, however it is as wide as the crown and has no beveling on the edge and makes using the crown almost impossible.

Beyond that gripe, the case provides great protection and looks good on the wrist without adding too much weight or bulk. It is a great case for protecting your watch and should be considered.

title: It also slides apart whenever it feels like it, but your phone won't fall out b/c ...
text:
So this case is actually only 3800 mah. There is a typo in the description.

The case works, and recharges my phone quickly, so it solved the problem it was meant for. However, it created several other dilemmas.
The case offers absolutely zero protections from front or side drops. It only covers the back, bottom, and corners.
The top of the case slides apart from the bottom in order to put your phone. It also slides apart whenever it feels like it, but your phone won't fall out b/c the case is hooked into your micro usb port.
Since it adds a few millimeters to the width of your phone only from the back, it makes it awkward to hit your volume buttons. You have to contort your thumb weirdly to pivot from the edge and its just awkward.

Over all the case serves its purpose of keeping your phone alive, but note the cons. It;s a good bit problematic for $30.

title: Very Nice Premium Screen Protector!!
text:
This is a really nice screen protector. It arrived in a package that closes and seals. Enclosed in the package was the screen protector in a protective cover, instructions to put it on, a wet and dry wipe to clean your phones screen, a dust absorber (if you don't know what this is, because I hadn't seen it before, it is like a sticker. Once you clean your screen you dab this sticker over your screen and it will pick up any of those pesky little pieces of dust that sometimes leave a little bubble under your protector - these are awesome!!), this also included a guide sticker - it's the first time I've seen this. You can put it on your phone so that you are laying the protector in the correct spot the first time.

Putting it on: I love these new screen protectors that are glass because they are thicker than those old flimsy protectors. Remember the old protectors where you have 2 tabs and it says to pull one piece off, put the screen protector on, and then pull the second tab off? Well on the glass protectors, because they are thicker, there is only one tab to pull off before you put it on your phone.

Because it's thicker, when you put it on (if you cleaned your screen properly and removed dust particles), it goes right on and you just watch the air moving out from under the protector. You may have to rub a little with your finger to get a couple air bubbles out but you may not have to. It's finally a screen saver that anyone can put on!!!

This screen protector is anti-scratching, and anti-shattering. I have not dropped my phone yet (I drop my phone alot!), so I can't verify that, but it certainly seems like a high quality screen protector that I feel confident will protect my phone.

title: Misses the mark on too many important must-haves
text:
I'm rating this as 2-stars mainly because the volume is inconsistent for some things like spoken navigation directions, the current price, and difference in functionality based on what "mode" you decide to use (I'll explain that in more detail later).
I recently rated the Supertooth HD as a near-perfect 5-star bluetooth device and used 14 main criteria. I will paste that list here and describe how the Minikit+ stacks up:

==============My 14 Most Important Criteria Items============
#1. It should have caller-id that speaks the name of the caller
----------
The Parrot Minikit+ has two modes. Mode 1 means it will use its own personal voice-recognition feature. This is great if your phone does not have voice-dial built-in, but most phones these days like Android, iPhone/Siri, Blackberry and Windows Phone all have built-in voice-dial.

Mode 2 means it will only use your phone's voice-recognition system.

Great, so which Mode do you choose and why is this such a big deal?
Well Mode 1 (use the Parrot's voice-recognition system) allows for spoken-name caller ID, and its voice-dial seems to be very accurate and quick to use. However, there's no way to activate your phone's native voice-dial (the Green/Call button will only use the Parrot's voice-recognition system), so if your phone supports Voice To Text Messaging, then there's not a way to dictate a text message, etc.

So what about Mode 2 (use your phone's native voice-dial)? Mode 2 means that when you press the Green/Call button, it immediately activates your phone's native voice-dial. So if your phone or its apps support voice-to-text or reading email aloud or opening an app, then you can do this as you normally would. The only down-side I've discovered is that you do not get spoken-name caller-id, because the Parrot uses its phonebook to do the caller-id. Well, why can't you have both??

In order to switch modes (not well documented) you have to hold down the Red and Center button to turn off automatic phonebook synchronization. Well unfortunately, you can't switch the functionality of the Green/Call button unless you clear the Parrot's memory (hold down red and green button). If you clear the memory, you lose the phonebook, which is what the Parrot used for caller-id. Rock and a hard place. I suppose if your phone supports "Bluetooth contacts object-push" you *might* be able to have both, but my Windows Phone does not support that.

#2. It should automatically turn on/off as you are away from the car
---------
Yes! The Minikit+ does an excellent job of turning off when your phone is away from the car and then auto-sensing to turn itself back on (ie. has a vibration sensor) when you get back in. I was very happy with this feature.

#3. It should have ample volume while driving at highway speeds
----------
This is inconsistent. When I was testing this on my couch, I thought the highest volume was fine. When I went on a test-drive, the spoken directions routed through this bluetooth speakerphone were simply not loud enough, even at max volume. Compared to the Supertooth HD's max volume, the Minikit+ really pales in comparison.

#4. You should only have to press a single and easily accessible button to answer or place a call
----------
This is poorly designed. You have to press the small Green/Call button to answer instead of the large center button. (Actually it does have *Voice-Answer* but you can only Answer or Reject, versus Answer, Reject and Ignore. [The difference between Reject and Ignore is that Reject sends the call immediately to voicemail, whereas Ignore just silences the ringing, but it rings the standard number of times before it goes to voicemail, so it seems like you genuinely missed the call, versus rejecting it.])

I missed a couple of calls because I was saying "accept", then "Accept", then "ACCEPT!!" and the Minikit+ wouldn't pick up the call. I finally turned off Voice-Answer.

Ending the call also fails, in that you have to press the small Red/Hang-up button, versus the large center button. If you accidentally press the center button, you will either engage the DTMF tones or the volume control. If you accidentally press the Green button again, you will go to 'Discrete' mode which means the speakerphone routes the audio to your phone. This was pretty frustrating, especially while you are driving and do not want to take your eyes off the road to see what button to press!

#5. It should make use of your phone's built-in voice recognition system (if your phone has this)
----------
This is very poorly documented, please see my answer to #1 about the 2 different Modes above. My discoveries are not in the quick-start guide nor on Parrot's website PDF user manual.

#6. It should be easy to pair and auto-download your phone's contacts
----------
I give them a B- on this one, practically every other bluetooth speakerphone device out there does this automatically when you turn it on for the first time, the Minikit+ does work, but you have to read the manual to know what button to press to make it go into pairing mode. Read #1 above, it cannot automatically download your phone's contacts AND use your phone's native voice-dial at the same time, unless your phone supports Bluetooth object-push, which my phone does not.

#7. It should reconnect easily when you are in the car
---------
Yes, this it does.

#8. Callers should be able to hear you clearly at highway speeds
----------
Callers can hear me, but again, the volume is inconsistent and simply not as loud as other devices I've used.

#9. The charging port should not be obstructed when the device is installed on a sunvisor
----------
Yes, the charging port is on the side of the device.

#10. It should have a long battery life
----------
Unknown at this time, haven't used it for that long; I will update this review the first time I need to charge it.

#11. It should be reliable whether it is -40 degrees in Fargo or the internal car temperature reaches 140 degrees in Texas
---------
This is unknown at this time, temperatures have been mild. [Update 2-5-2013: See Comment #1 below, thanks Joe! --- This device is not reliable in temperatures below freezing. At 15degrees F, a fully charged battery will deplete itself.]

#12. It should have good documentation or manufacturer's website and support
---------
Yes they have good documentation and support on their website, but they need better differentiating names! Be careful when buying in that the Minkit+, Minikit Slim, Minikit Smart are 3 different models. In fact sometimes you only see "Minikit" advertised so you might not be getting what you're expecting. When I tried to update the Firmware, their software updater is not updated to even show the Minikit+ as of this writing. (The "plus" is the newest Minikit model)

#13. It should be usable whether the sun visor is flipped down or up
---------
I give them kudos for this one. They provide a sunvisor band that allows you to mount the device with the sun visor flipped up or down very quickly. The sunvisor band has "pockets" that allow you to easily clip the device to the band, versus the sunvisor. Simple, yet clever thinking.

#14. It should be reasonably priced
---------
For cheaper, the Motorola T325 beats this hands down. For a little more, the Supertooth HD is still my car bluetooth speakerphone 5-star product of choice.

Additional Information
---------------------------
I do want to mention one really cool feature on the Minikit+ that I haven't seen on any other bluetooth device - the center control knob sends out DTMF tones. When you call something and it says "Press 1 to continue" without reaching for your phone, how do you press "1" from your bluetooth speakerphone?? Well, the Parrot Minikit+ has the answer. You press the control knob and it announces "0" or "1" or "star" or "hash" etc as you rotate the dial. So if you need to press 1 to continue, you spin the dial until it says "1" and you press the button and it sends the DTMF tone for 1. This is also pretty slick for voicemail, like pressing "Pound" to go to the next voicemail or pressing "7" to delete the current message. I wish more manufacturers would add a slick option like that.

In Summary
===========
I really wanted this device to knock 'em out of the park, but it fails my criteria list in #1 (if you want to use your phone's native voice-recognition), #3, #4, #5, and #8. For the same price (as of this writing), the Supertooth HD is the way to go.

Update - 12-22-2011: I did try the TextFriendly.net 6 month trial and even imported my contacts, however, everytime I call the Nationwide USA phone number, it answers and plays music and then says, "service not available at this time."

title: Provides needed extra screen protection
text:
I prefer the extra screen protection afforded by a second shatter-resistant layer of glass. Have just installed on new iPhone 6S (yes, I know I'm not avant-garde when it comes to latest iPhones), but I had to replace an iPhone 5S which I managed to abuse enough to pop the screen out of the case. But in five years of abuse the Tech Armor Ballistic Glass screen protector did its job very well.
My biggest concern during installation on the 5S and now on the 6S was could I position the glass protector properly? I shouldn't have worried because with only a little care (after watching the Tech Armor instructional video) I was able to position the protective glass straight and with no entrapped dust, dirt or bubbles.
I feel it is actually easier to install the Tech Armor glass because it is rigid and easier to hold during install than a flexible film protector which seems to flop around too much and is trickier to position properly. It is also more difficult to scratch the glass compared to softer film protectors and easier to keep clean during use.
I've never found the touch screen properties of the iPhone to change at all because of the extra layer of glass and it seems that outdoor screen glare is reduced, but without darkening the screen in low ambient light situations.
After five years of experience with the Tech Armor glass on my previous phone I am a firm believer because it showed no scratches or blemishes looking just the same as when installed originally.
I've tried protective films on my phones and iPods, but they just don't hold up as well and need to be periodically replaced because they come loose, or they develop scratches and bubbles besides being more difficult to position properly during installation.
Tech Armor provides two glass shields in case you need a backup, but I've never needed to use the backup glass.

title: Far exceeded my expectations! Except for 1 thing.
text:
When I ordered this case, I took a gamble since there were no reviews on it. I think I paid $6.25 a week ago. As of today 3/25/13, it's even cheaper, less than $5.00.

The order originally said 2-4 weeks for delivery. No big deal. It came in less than a week, which was awesome. Thanks Amazon Prime!

Ok, so on to the review....

I ordered the black. It comes as 2 pieces. A rubber piece and a hard case piece. The hard case piece separates. It fits the phone very nicely. Then you add the silicone on top of it to keep it all together.

The volume, power, headphone and other ports are covered by the silicone. The ports open are the camera, speaker and mic. The power button and volume rocker on the silicone don't protrude obnoxiously. They are fairly flush, but you can still feel a small bump to know that you are on the button. The silicone buttons are very responsive. I did not have to overly keep pushing or push hard to get my phone to respond.

The back of the phone even comes with a kickstand. It does take a little finger nail action to dig it out. This is good because that means the kickstand won't just flop out randomly. The kickstand itself has a brace. It was well thought out.

My last phone had the $50 Otter Box. What I liked about the otter box was that it had a protective shield on the screen as part of the case. But it was really big and bulky. This case does not offer the option of the protective screen. It also doesn't cost $50! Like the Otter Box, this new case does add to quite a bit of thickness. You are afterall adding 2 layers of plastic, top and bottom and 2 layers of silicone, top and bottom. So don't complain that it adds thickness because I'm already telling you IT DOES.

I have also had just a plastic case that snaps together on my last phone when I finally gave up on the Otter Box. Which, by the way, the kickstand broke off on the case! On the cheap $3 case from ebay, when the phone would hit the floor at times, the plastic case would break apart. In some ways that was good, because it cushioned the fall of the phone. The shock mostly dissipated into the break apart case. With this new case, if it hits the floor, the plastic will not break apart as now the silicone is holding it together. So whether this is good or bad, I can't really comment. I'm guessing the rubber from the silicone will take the brunt of the force. I'm not a physics major, but it would be interesting to find out wouldn't it? I'm not dropping my phone to find out...haa haa. Not dropping the phone in the first place would be ideal, but accidents do happen.

Ok, on to the negative.....

My usb charger was too thick to push into the power port. I had to use a different charger where the plastic on the plug was thinner. But not all chargers will fit into the port because the plastic part of the case is a really tight fit. This is the only reason I didn't give it 5 stars.

Still, the black plastic portions are slick and should provide some friction when you hold it. *** Not a fan.  I had a very similar case (but not by the same manufacturer that I'm aware of) on my Galaxy S3 which has served me very well, and was hoping this one would be as good.  Unfortunately the materials are not as ergonomically designed as my old case.  The plastic belt clip holder is very smooth plastic, and the black plastic portion that slips over the silicone case is also slippery, smooth plastic.  This gives it very little grip in your hand, and I can literally tilt the holder upside down and my phone begins to slide out. Two very gentle shakes and it comes completely out of the holder. My old case had a thin rubber coating on the plastics that provided a much better feel and provided enough friction to keep the phone in the holder, but not so much that it was difficult to remove. Not sure what I can do to improve the grip of the plastic on the phone itself, other than maybe rough it up with some fine grit sandpaper. title: My use case is unique
text:
EDIT August 2021:

I've noticed that the battery indicator is grossly inaccurate. The phone will be completely juiced out despite reflecting 50% or more just prior. This has happened multiple times despite complete charging. It still lasts days on airplane mode, but this inaccuracy makes it not trustworthy.

PROBLEM

Every website and tons of other services are now requiring MFA - 6 digit codes to supplement your password to log in. I don't like how many are doing it, and I don't like clogging up my email with them nor do I want that garbage on my phone. I don't do text messages.

So what I needed was basically a "thing" to do the Authenticator for all services in one interface that didn't require any connection to anything else, but was portable enough to carry around.

This fits the bill. I will note a few issues.

To do Google Play, you do have to add an account. I was hesitant to do this because this is coded to think it's in India somewhere, and I wasn't sure about privacy or security. So I downloaded the APK separately for Google Authenticator (which requires no Google account). Since this has a camera, you can scan the QR code for any such service and add to the list. Works a treat.

Now rather than taking up to a minute to fumble around to get the code, it's a few seconds at most. Exactly what I wanted.

The browser on this is some garbage - it wants all sorts of privacy breaching permissions just to open, so it's sketchy as all get-out. I suggest if you're going to use this for an actual phone/device, don't use the built-in browser, download Edge or Chrome or Firefox Mobile and use those, then disable the built in browser.

In my case, I don't even need WiFi much less cell signal (I can always use it as a backup with my Google Voice account if needed, but I already have plenty of devices for that), so with data off the battery life is stellar, lasting multiple days even with the screen left on.

The main complaint I have is the touchscreen. It's a bit under-sensitive, not responding to swipes and taps like I'd expect. This could be the screen protector, I'm not sure. I'm not comfortable removing it at this time; if that changes I'll update the review, but it should work regardless of screen protector.

title: Tried a few others and this is the best one.
text:
I tried a few others from Amazon that had good ratings, but they had major flaws that annoyed me. Below is a list of what I liked that the others didn’t do very well.

Adhesive is more of a silicone coating and not a glue. In the other screen protectors I tried, they all used an adhesive that looses its tackiness if you have to reposition the protector. You have to make sure you lay it down perfectly or it will start coming loose. You can reposition the Jbao and it will still attach perfectly. Also, this silicone coating covers the whole screen, which also prevents the rainbow effect that protectors get when they only have adhesive on the edge.

I really like that the Jbao screen protector was smaller that the others I tried. They were so perfectly sized that if you were not 100% on all the edges, it would create a slight lip that would catch and pull the screen up if you used a protective case. The Jbao cover enough screen to protect it, yet allow any case to be used. Other reviewers have said this is a negative, but you can clearly see that the manufacturer intended it to fit this way.

The clarity is fantastic and looks like it does not have a screen protector installed. One of the others I tried had a checker or dot like pattern in the coating. Other protectors would show a hue or a shimmering efect when the phone was at an angle. The Jbao is near perfect.

The only negative that I have is the edge has a few tiny flaws, but they do not affect the screen viewing at all. Hard to explain, but it is so minor that I am not removing a star.

Basically, the Jbao Direct Xiaomi Mi A2/Mi 6X Screen Protector has met all my needs and I will be buying another pack just to have on hand.

title: Versatile and attractive but the cutouts for ports is obstructive
text:
I bought this for my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 and it fits the phone fine, as a protective case.

It's also very attractive and made with high quality materials.

There are few things that I find to be major drawbacks, but which I solved on my own.

1. The cutouts in the case for the headphone jack and power cord are obstructive. They're too small so when you plug your headphones or power cord in the plastic is in the way and will not allow full contact.

Solution: Using a cardboard knife I cut larger holes. For the power cutout I actually must merged it with the other cutouts. This did not damage the integrity of the case. It still holds the phone firmly.

2. A handstrap: This case is handy as a kind of wallet. While it can't be packed with cash it can hold your ID and some credit cards. When I go grocery shopping I write my grocery list as an S Note. Then I just bring in my phone in this case and I have my list, my ID, and my form of payment all in one convenient place. However, it's not convenient to keep setting the phone down. And handstrap would be handy.

Solution: So, what I did was punch a hole in the part of the leather of the case that holds the phone (not the spine) and put in a lanyard I had at home. This worked passably, but one designed by Moss Greg would probably be more attractive and functional.

3. Clasp - there is no clasp to keep the case closed. I thought I would actually prefer no clasp because I don't like the extra bulk a clasp adds. But, now it flops open all the time and I worry I might lose stuff I have in it. Also, I have seen cases where clasps were very sleep and added only insignificant thickness.

Solution: None so far.

Don't get me wrong. This is a very nice case and my favorite, so far. But it needs some improvement.

title: Waste O' Money for me
text:
When I saw this headset and its associated reviews, I immediately threw $150 at it and had it overnighted. (Thank you, Amazon Prime!) I've used it for 3 days now, I'm on and off my phone all day every day for about 18 hours (work). So... I hate it.

I have used multiple bluetooths over the years, because I can't drive and talk on the phone without wrecking my car, and I'm in my car all day for my job. I have used several Plantronics, some I liked, some I loved. My cat ate many of them because plantronics apparently makes a tasty device. I have used an inexpensive Samsung and a moderately expensive Motorola model too. I have liked most, loved some and hated none until now. My most important requirements are clear conversation, noise reduction and talk time. Every single one of the afore-mentioned bluetooths were better than this one. I forgot to verify my requirements, in my excitement to get this highly rated BT.

This thing lasted just exactly 3.5 hours before repeatedly beeping its death knell in my ear. This caused me to go look up the model and see that I had in fact inadvertently bought a bluetooth with a ridiculously short battery life. In this day and age, who makes bluetooths that die so fast? This is supposed to be a bluetooth to listen to music, answer your phone, whatever.. but apparently you can only do it for about 4 hours and then it's toast. Personally, I do not care how great the music sounds (it wasn't that great), if the battery drops dead in 4 hours, it's useless to me.

Just picked up a Plantronics M50. It does everything I need and lasts 11 hours. In fact, I think it lasted longer than 11 hours. The sound quality is perfect for calls and it's not bad at all for music, though I have headphones if I need music.

So if you're shopping for a bluetooth to make and receive phone calls, and you'd like it to last all day, this is not your bluetooth. I'm giving this Bose BT 2 stars because it paired fast and it was comfortable.

title: Great for amateur use, but CANNOT be used for artists!
text:
This has 70% of the functionality of the real Apple Pencil 2 at 1/3 of the price. I am surprised how good this is. I own the Genuine Apple Pencil 2 for my iPad Pro 12.9 and got this for my wife’s iPad 11 and functionally is most of the way there with a few small items missing (see below).

The good: The pencil looks and feels just like the Genuine Apple Pencil 2 but with an extra LED on the top. It even comes with a box that looks similar to the Apple Pencil. It comes with additional two replacement tips whereas the Apple Pencil doesn’t include any.

It charges on the iPad magnetically and it even shows the battery percentage when you swipe to the left. I noticed is that it is missing the notification when you attach it to the iPad thought but that seems like a minor issue. The only identifiable physical difference is the LED ring on the other end of the pencil that tells you when it is charging, low, or full. This serves as the missing on-screen indicator on the iPad.

The sensitivity, functionality, and speed seems on par with the Apple Pencil 2. I haven’t compared head to head to see the levels of sensitivity or speed but if you really can’t tell a difference then that is telling. There is even tilt sensor which is helpful. Tilt sensor is good for brushes to give you wider side strokes rather than just the point.

The bad: There are a few notable features from the Apple Pencil that is missing. One is the tap sensor. On the genuine Apple Pencil 2 you can tap on the pencil with your index finger and change to the eraser. It serves as an extra button to customize. There is no tap functionality on this pencil.

The second MAJOR issue is the lack of pressure sensitivity. Pressure sensitivity lets you press harder down on the pencil for thicker or thinner lines. This is a huge issue if you are a professional visual artist or even an amateur artist who wants to sketch. Many artists have switched to the iPad and Apple Pencil 2 form Wacom and other industry standard drawing tablets because the sensitivity is so good. Without pressure sensitivity you cant make light lines and heavy lines and have to constantly switch via software. At first I thought maybe it was an incompatibility with the Notes app, but I checked online and it lists tilt sensitivity but not pressure as a feature. I am not surprised because for the price pressure sensitivity is likely too much to ask for. This is a MAJOR issue for professionals.

I am generally very surprised by the quality of this third party pencil. It really is a great third party replacement. However the lack of pressure makes it useless for artists or professionals. This is a good pencil for taking notes, drawing for fun, maybe for a student. Please be aware of the limitations before you buy,

title: Locks in place and sturdy
text:
I've tried many phone holders, from those that has a big suction cup that you attach to your windshield, another to your dashboard, another that just slides over one of the vent ribs (with no hook), and one that takes up one of the cupholders. All of them were disappointments. The suction cup one would melt during the summer and leave a trail of sticky melted adhesive on the windshield, the dashboard one would never stick properly to the dashboard, the one that just slides over a vent rib would fall out from the vent when weighted with the phone, and the cupholder one would take up a cupholder space.

This magnetic holder is legit.

The holder has a metal hook that extends or retracts as you turn the piece that contains the hook. If you twist it counter-clockwise, the hook extends out, while the clockwise direction shortens the hook. So, extend the hook out, insert it into the vent to latch onto a vent fin, then tighten the hook for a solid hold.

Now when I first tried placing my iPhone 13 Pro with a clear plastic protector case on top of the holder, the phone immediately fell off. The phone did not have a strong magnetic attraction to the holder.

I noticed inside the box that there are two plates, a round one and a rectangular one. I took my phone out of the case and placed the rectangular plate in the middle of the case, and sandwiched the plate between the plastic phone case and my phone. I then tried placing the back of the phone to the holder and it held with a strong magnetic grip.

This is the first holder that I've used that works for me.

My only main concern is the vent fin and how it'll hold up with the phone's weight and with the bumps and bouncing of everyday driving in the long run. I'm sure the fin will be the first to break/crack before the holder does. Time will tell.

In the meantime, it's the first holder that I've used that holds my phone well and has a sturdy and firm grip in the vent.

title: Perfect dual 'hidey hole' for smartphone and credit cards!
text:
This has turned out to be a perfect solution for the protection of my smartphone. I love its features...the gorgeous color combination, the non-slip texture, the perfect fit around the phone, the card slots (I double them up and get 5 or 6 in them), the pretty shape of the tongue holding the cover down and the firm magnet inside. I replace my batteries often (get a Samsung Galaxie...you never run out of 'gas') and it's so easy to slip them in and out. I have been using it for 6 months now and the fit stays secure no matter how often I remove the cover to replace batteries. One of the biggest benefits of such a wallet for me is that I can clip a stylus down the spine and I can lay the phone down any side up and have it well protected. I purchased a second one of these in case something happens to the first one but so far so good. I purchased several more for my nieces and nephews in Australia, all made to fit their Androids and Iphones. They were thrilled with them.

Just a very personal suggestion next time you are making any changes, I would love the front slot to be clear plastic for a drivers licence or a photo. But honestly the wallet has not suffered injury from all that I stuff into it. I have stopped taking a purse with me when I duck into a shop! Taking a photo with the cover opened is a bit of a challenge but you get used to it!

You have a winner, Karen and Jennifer!

title: Perfect.
text:
Sharp looking (I got blue,) minimal design, completely encases my S9 phone. Has all the needed holes in the right places for charging cable, speaker, and earbuds. The thin black bezel (rubber bumper) that runs around the edge has tactile "buttons" to activate the phone's buttons right beneath (volume, Bixby, power). Sensitivity of both buttons and screen is excellent. I see no need for a different (eg. glass) screen protector.

You fit the phone into the front screen protector frame first. Then you fit those into the back of the case. The back is black rubber with a colored insert (in my case blue). It has a built-in bezel that surrounds the phone and curves up and slightly over. The screen protector frame snaps into the bezel and you're good to go. The black rubber bezel makes it easy to hold the phone without slipping out of you hands.
My only objection was that it was danged hard to initially pull the screen protector frame out of the back case. The rubber bezel is that tight, but it also means it is that secure. This case will not come apart unless you really work at it. It was packaged carefully with thin film over the screen protector (which I didn't remove until I had everything assembled). I'm impressed Very well designed. Highly recommend.

title: Terrible product, but probably best available option.
text:
I am a gadget nerd and am almost OCD about scratches on my electronics. I try to keep all my equipment in pristine condition to protect their resale value, functionality, and aesthetic quality. I ordered several kinds of screen protectors to try, and essentially hate them all.

I tried the ZAGG invisible shield, and not only was it a hassle to put on (and I am relatively good at applying Zagg skins because I've used them several times in the past, and applied several to this specific phone as well). The liquid solution is a hassle to use without getting it in the cracks/openings of the device, it is hard to keep your fingers wet to avoid fingerprints on the adhesive side of the skin, bubbles and dust are impossible to avoid, and even when I had gotten rid of all bubbles/dust, the skin later develops the 'orange peel' effect, where the skin is bubbly and dimply like the skin of an orange. It impairs clarity of the screen and is an overall pain. It also accumulates tons of smear marks from your fingers swiping the touch screen. However, it is impossible to scratch.

That is in stark contrast to the Seidio Screen Protector. Although application is somewhat more straight forward, it is a dust/lint MAGNET, and fingerprints are permanent. Dust can be removed with a piece of tape, but while you're removing one dust particle, ten others will float over and stick to other parts of the skin. If you do somehow manage to lay down the skin without dust and align it corectly, you only have about a days worth of use before scratches start to accumulate. It is somewhat resistant to smaller scratches, but if you put your phone in a purse, backpack, basically anything other than a velvet plush case, expect it to have some deep gouges before too long. It also never completely adheres around the top speaker and the optical track ball. There are bubbles around those areas where it reffused to stick, and I returned 2 packs of screen protectors for this reason. None of them stuck around these areas and eventually I gave up.

In the end, its the lesser of several evils. I haven't found a screen protector that I am happy with yet, but this one seems to be doing the job of keeping my real screen from being demolished. However, I would probably prefer the Zagg invisible shield if I could do everything over again, simply because you can't scratch it and they guarantee their product. However, its $20 where as the Seidio 2 pack was like $14 or something? It's pretty arbitrary...they are all frustrating.

Hope this helps. Good luck!

title: Great case with a couple of issues, I still am giving it 5 stars!
text:
I bought this case a year ago, and after getting a properly attached steel plate for my magnetic car holder, I pretty much loved it. But first, the bad:

- The door for the lightning port was too stiff and harmed my lightning cable. My solution was to cut it off, and my XR is generally water resistant, and it is not that important.

- After a year of use the kickstand broke. Frankly, that is no too bad, with as much as use the kickstand. One of the little tabs broke, and the kickstand and the ability to attach to the phone to the magnetic mount was compromised. The top of the kickstand is where the magnetic plate is, so I had to purchase a new case. So I bought a new Unicorn Pro case!

The second case was much easier to attach a new magnetic plate! The plate I used previously, required heavy duty double backed tape. With the second case, the adhesive on the plate was all that was needed to properly stick on the plate to the top of the kickstand. Further, the Lightning port flap was not as stiff, and works great.

Of course, the new kickstand is very stiff, and I popped the kickstand off the track! I contacted Supcase, and they are replacing the case, no questions asked! Great service. The lesson here is when disengaging the kickstand, press the underneath the middle of the top of the stand up, so it is easy to disengage. That will prevent the top of the stand from popping out.

title: If only the magnets were stronger…
text:
I’ve been excited to get my hands on this battery pack. It’s pretty much the only model to date that offers MagSafe connectivity on BOTH sides — on one side to charge your iPhone, on the other to charge the battery. Plus, of course, MagSafe isn’t limited to charging, you can also use a variety of other accessories with MagSafe! But there’s a few issues I can’t help but notice.

1. The magnets are too weak on the iPhone side of this battery. (They’re plenty strong on the otter box logo side of the battery, though)
2. The iPhone side of this battery doesn’t have a grippy texture like silicone does, for example, so it takes very little sheer force to remove.
3. The Magnets on the logo side of the battery are lower down than those on the iPhone side — this means that accessories like a wallet will not be properly aligned if you connect them to the battery, though a ring holder or pop socket will work just fine.
4. This probably won’t fit an iPhone 14 Pro when those come out, because it’s really close to the camera bump on the 13 Pro.

I love the concept of this battery so much, though, that I’ve just ordered some magnets and an adhesive sheet of silicone so I can make the necessary design changes myself in order to make this battery better. If my mods are successful, I’ll probably update this review to show just how much better this battery could be. Just a couple design tweaks would make this the best battery pack on the market right now, and at it’s current price, it’s already a close contender.

title: Make this great phone better by updating to Android 2.2.2
text:
This is a great, inexpensive GSM phone for AT&T's GoPhone Prepaid Service. The screen resolution is very good. The battery life is excellent. Unlike many early model Android phones, the processor is sufficient to ensure a snappy experience. Bluetooth connectivity works perfectly. The phone can also be used on AT&T's postpaid service (or on AT&T MVNOs), so it is a relatively cheap replacement if you lose your phone. Although Otterbox makes no case specifically for this phone, the Otterbox Commuter for the LG Optimus fits and works perfectly. In addition, the phone can be rooted with Gingerbreak 1.2.

I have only two gripes. First, the included speakerphone is way too quiet to use it while driving or in any kind of noise. You can solve this by connecting with a bluetooth headset or bluetooth speakerphone.

The second is that the phone ships with Android 2.2.1, which has some bugs. Among other things, I had trouble getting all my contacts to sync. Some would sync, and others wouldn't. I knew that LG and AT&T had release a version 2.2.2, but (like many others) I couldn't seem to get it to download.

Here's the secret:

You must have an activated AT&T SIM card (or a SIM card from an AT&T MVNO) in order for the update to work. Don't try to update before you install and activate a SIM Card. Once you have an AT&T SIM Card activated and installed in the phone, wait until you receive a text message giving you the phone number. Then wait 10-15 more minutes.

You might also want to turn on Wifi, as this will make the download go faster. However, even with Wifi on, the phone must have an active SIM Card installed. This is because, before downloading the update, the phone does some kind of check over AT&T's network (probably to download a pointer to the location of the download file). It does so even if you have Wifi enabled. That's why you need an activated SIM Card. The card need not have any $$ on it. It just needs to be active and have a telephone number assigned to it.

Then navigate to:

Settings > About Phone > Software Update > Update Now

If you don't have an active SIM card when you do this, you'll either get a message saying that no update is available, or the phone will just sit there saying that it is checking for an update forever. When you cancel and try again, you'll be told to wait 24 hours.

You can bypass the "wait 24 hours message" either by factory resetting the phone, or by going to Settings > Applications > Manage Applications > Running > com.lge.omadmclient and selecting "clear data." Then go back to the Update Now screen above. You'll get an error message. Go back to update now a second time and you should be able to attempt the update again.

The update to Android 2.2.2 cured the syncing problems that I had and I found that the phones runs even faster and better than before.

title: "Stuck on you".......Awesome product!
text:
I've never written a review before good or bad. Koomus products are awesome! I had a Kenu air vent cell phone holder. It was okay at best until one and then two of the rubber pieces on the prongs that keeps it slipping out of the air vent came off making the holder useless. Then I tried the Koomus air vent holder and it worked perfectly. It has a different designed piece to keep it securely into the air vent and won't move until I decide to pull it out of the vent. Best damn vent mount I've ever used.

Now I drive for Lyft and have to constantly take my phone out of the cradle and then put it back in. So I took a look at the Koomus Pro Dashboard-M Universal Magnetic mount. This is what I had wanted all along. It is awesome. It is everything that Koomus says it is. If you read the instructions, the mount will be fitted to your dashboard or windshield like it's supposed to. The magnet (it comes with 2 although you'll really only need one) holds the phone in place and won't move until you're ready to take it off the holder. Then it just comes off easily with one hand. It's so much easier than having to use both hands to spread apart the spring loaded holders and remove your phone from the mount.

Here is the best part that truly makes this product so great. I moved to Las Vegas the first week of July 2016. It truly is hotter than hell here with temps in the high 90's and into the 100's nearly every day. I've had several dash mounts in the past and somehow they've always managed to lose contact with the dash and fall off with my expensive phone still attached to it. This Koomus mount hasn't yet shown any signs of starting to lose it's grip on the dash even with the excessive heat. I drive at ease knowing that my phone will stay where I put it for the duration of my drive.

title: Amazon reviews seem totally random
text:
I buy a lot of stuff thru Amazon, and almost always base buying decisions largely on product reviews. Unfortunately, the reviews have gotten SO random as to be of little use. Whether Amazon or the vendors are responsible for aggragating reviews for obviously different products I dont know, but in the case of this case <g>, I bought a Temdan heavy shockproof case for a galaxy s22 ultra.
My case came with 2 what seem to be glass screen protectors; I have to assume they don't have a lot of faith in their effectiveness. Happily, only one has been needed so far, and their video was essential for installing it.
On my phone, once the fingerprints were updated they worked as tho the screen protector was not there at all.
At least one of the beauty shots of the product I ordered seem to show a 2 piece case, with a hard cover clipping over the back. Mine did not have that clip on, nor did it seem to need it.
This is a hard case, not rubberized like some heavy duty cases, also not bulky like some heavy duty cases. For better or worse, the phone will slide on a table as one excellent video shows; if you don't want a "slidey" case, put the phone face down so the surround definitely stops any tendency for the phone to slide while still keeping the screen off the surface.
The sides of my case have a slightly textured surface to improve grip, but not nearly what a rubberized case such as Otterbox provides. On the flip side, this case is much easier to "pocket" than an Otterbox.
The ports are uncovered, the "pencil" easily accessible, and even without using the supplied camera lens covers the lenses are well recessed from the surface so should be out of harm's way. I had a heavier case on this phone previously which required careful placement for wireless chargers to work; this case seems to be easier to place for wireless charging.
This case is not an Otterbox; I have had several Otterboxes on various phones over the years and truly love them. But the s22 ultra was just too huge to add the bulk of a case with Otterbox protection. This Temdan case looks to offer basic protection at a basic price. YMMV.

title: Good, inexpensive dual charger
text:
I've used a bunch of different USB car chargers. The really inexpensive ones don't seem to last. I was using a very compact one that I really liked but it finally gave up the ghost. I settled on these because the reviews were good and the price (less than $10 per pair) was very reasonable.

I like that the knurled portion of the body is made from aluminum. I also like that one of the USB ports charges at 2.4A vs. 1A. My phone is older and the battery life depletes quickly, so the fast-charging port really helps.

The blue LED is nice, but not very bright. Not a big deal for me but it might be for someone else. I usually keep 2 cables plugged into the charger at all times so I never need to find the ports in low light.

I only needed 1 charger but having an extra is nice. I always have a replacement/loaner available without having to wait for another delivery or buying an overpriced one at the local brick-and-mortar store.

Unless I find something better, this will be my go-to USB car charger.

title: Great Car Charger!
text:
This is a pretty damn fine car charger.

The magnet is strong - shaking that thing didn't move the phone even a little. For reference, I'm sporting an iPhone 12 Pro Max with Apple's original silicon magsafe case. Without the case, it's just as strong, but the slicker surface of the iPhone itself made rotating the device a bit smoother. I don't know if that will translate to some unintentional rotation when I hit those washboard roads in the mountains - we'll see.

Charging is pretty quick - about what you'd expect from a magsafe charger running on the 20W Apple adapter. I have a 3.0 charger in the car so it should provide plenty of power, even while navigating.

Speaking of - I run an app called 'Strut' while driving a lot - it's a mapping app that makes a game out of 'lighting up' map tiles and seeing who can open up the most territory. Needless to say, running a gps app can really run down your battery while heating everything up. The fan seems to really move plenty of air, right at the back of the phone. This should allow it to dissipate heat, although it doesn't cool the air. Still, moving ambient air over the phone will help. As I have this placed in front of the vent, it's even better.

The blue glow isn't really visible once the phone is attached, but it's nice to see right where to set your phone when it's dark.

If I have to plug in the phone to use Car Play, my phone will automatically switch to the lightening port for charging. It's nice to have the two options as I rarely need Car Play just for my daily commute. I had one of those 'one-hand' type holders, but always found it awkward to reach around the side of the steering wheel and squeeze the thing, then 'catch' the phone as it fell forward. The magnet is strong, but prying the phone upward allows me to remove it easily with one hand.

One minor quibble - and since it's the car, not the device's fault - the space between the vertical vent vanes is too narrow to really fit the clamp. It causes the vanes to bulge outward a bit. Because I can't push it fully in to set it, the phone tends to shake a bit. But I found that the other device has the same size ball mount - so I used the articulating arm of the other holder with the HaloLock charger and it's perfect!

The vent mount piece of this now holds the 'one-hand' clamping device for passengers.

No car mount will ever fit every model of car, so that's a minor issue and easily compensated for.

I can't wait to bounce along some back roads and really put the magnet to the test!
