title: Truly, an amazing value.
text:
This is a review of the woednx 20mm Smart Watch Band 2-pack, in wine-red and blue, with an ASIN of B0B7RFCP8V.

Short version (TL;DR) - Negatives: Color choice. Positives: Comfortable. Secure. Don’t stink. Great Value.

Long version …

Frankly, these are great bands. I’m actually surprised by how nice they are, given the insanely low price. Anyway, let’s get to the details …

Negatives:

* Color Choices - a very minor negative, but something of a make-or-break regarding sales, I suspect. Really, it’d be nice if they offered more color choices. As-is, these are great for people with widely varied outfit color palettes, or couples, but, for those with a more narrow color range, the existing choices are pretty limiting. This is meant more as feedback to the seller than anything else and is, again, really a minor issue in my opinion.

Positives:

* Comfortable - I’ve been wearing one of these bands on my watch for a few days straight (sleeping with the watch on, too) and it’s very comfortable. The silicone is at a Goldilocks stiffness - it’s not too floppy, nor too hard. Also, I don’t think I understand why, but it seems like the scalloping on the inside of the band may be making things less clammy.

* Secure - these appear to have good attachment pins in them, as well as enough material around the pin that I’m perfectly satisfied it’s not at risk of tearing out. What’s really interesting is that these bands go beyond that. The double-loop setup they use to hold the strap tail does wonders in preventing it from getting caught on things, which definitely plays a role in ensuring the health of your watch. I’ve been using this with one snugged down toward the clasp and the other roughly centered between the last hole and the end of the tail, and it keeps everything flat and flush. Beyond that, these bands even have a little safety notch for the pins’ release levers. Once secured, you can rotate the pins so that the little levers can’t get tugged by moving on your arm, etc… As unlikely as that might be to happen in the first place, I love that this feature is there.

* Don’t Stink - this may be a more important note than you expect, but these don’t stink. Another silicone watch band I got around the same time, which happens to be about an order of magnitude more expensive, smells horrible. It’s been outgassing for about a week, and I still don’t want to put it on my wrist.

* Value - to recap, you’re getting not one, but two quite good watch bands for a few dollars. This is a ridiculous good value proposition.

In summary, if you have a watch that these’ll fit and like one of the color combinations being offered, stop thinking and buy them. This is one of the best values of any kind that I’ve run across on Amazon. Seriously.

title: Really cool phone if you give it a chance; another jump in tech for Google
text:
Professional reviews for phones are usually the best resource. However, that said, I think I should offer another perspective that isn't nearly as negative. In general, I think the reviewers were too harsh. Some of them even had me on the brink of canceling my order. Glad I didn't.

I have the 64GB XL.

Battery life - I am not seeing much difference from my Pixel 3. The horrible battery life mentioned in some reviews is not my experience. I consider myself an average smartphone user. I'm not a 16 year old on social media all day and I don't play games. I use it all day at work (email, text, in car for music, reading some blogs with videos, the occasional call) and a little at night. When I get home, I have over 50% left. I keep the always-on display on, I use motion sense, all the connection methods are on. The key here is that I don't see a big difference from my past phones.

Also - you have to give the Android OS time to use its adaptive battery function to manage various aspects of the phone. It learns your usage patterns and adjusts. This results in better battery life. I saw many reviews where the author didn't give it time.

HD Calling on AT&T - I bought this unlocked model on Amazon and when I swapped my SIM out, HD calling works normally. There might be an issue with corporate accounts but search the web and look at what some people did to circumvent it. This is an AT&T issue, not Google's.

Motion Sense - no, it doesn't have a lot of active functionality yet, only track skipping and alarm snoozing (which is AWESOME). What many reviews fail to highlight enough is that it augments the face unlock feature by bringing your phone to attention when you reach for it. It also allows you to turn off the always-on display then have it wake only when you are near the phone.

New assistant - pretty cool. Many of the basic requests are now handled on the phone, not requiring contact with Google servers. It really speeds things up.

As of Nov 1, it does have little things that I hope Google works out. Face Unlock needs to be updated to prevent unlocks when your eyes are closed. It would be nice if Smooth Display (90Hz) worked more often - although, I think the display is awesome as is, it can only get better. Google is planning to fix those. More apps need to support face unlock and that's a total wildcard; depends on the app. LastPass supports it so that's sort of a gateway to your other apps.

*UPDATE 11/19/19** Smooth Display (90Hz) has been corrected with the November security update. An already beautiful screen is even better now! Also - LastPass now supports Face Unlock.

Finally, you can't deny this is an expensive phone. I got it for, basically, $100 off and that brought it closer to an acceptable price for me. But - it's a personal decision. You'll have to weigh the value and decide if it works for you.

If you are considering this phone, I'll be honest, also consider the Pixel 3XL (or Pixel 3). Many of the new features on the 4 will make it to the 3. If you don't need to be on the cutting edge or the extra camera features, the 3/3XL is a great phone! However, you won't be disappointed by the 4XL. After a week of getting used to face unlock and the gestures, I really like this phone.

title: Great solution for seldom-used car to keep battery charged without hassle
text:
My Ford couldn't be hooked to a cigarette lighter-powered solar trickle charger because the lighter isn't powered unless the ignition switch is on.

This ODB II port connected solar charger was the perfect solution for me, after I tried to kludge a solution.

The results of the "kludge" make an interesting cautionary tale so here's how I came to the conclusion ODB would be better:
A few months ago I destroyed another solar panel by attempting to use the included straight-to-battery cables because I discovered I couldn't use the lighter connector. When attaching the power cables I got them backwards (positive going to negative and vice-versa) The impressive inch long deep burn scar in the plastic on the dash above the instrument panel and instant vaporization of the wire and insulation made it clear just how dangerous direct wiring to the battery can be if done wrong! Fortunately I was the only idiot near the car and I was clear of the wire that burnt to nothing in a flash - Lucky the dashboard was the only thing hurt in that foolish mistake!

I am a STICKLER for screen protectors and I DO NOT want them obscuring my display and this one just flat out gets in the way along the edges. Looking from any angle other than straight on has you looking through the edge of the protector and it blurs what is on the display. The bubbles and haloing just flat out irritate when you expect clarity.

The protector was 1.5 - 2 mm smaller than the face of the watch, leaving quite a visible unprotected ring on this watch. I think they need to re-market this for the SM-R720 models as their displays are actually smaller than the the SM-R730 (which is what I have). So BE WARNED, it won't fit the 3G/4G larger versions of the watch.

I have bought many Spigen products and been happy with most of them. Lately though quality seems to be slipping. This and my last purchase from them were faulty out of the box. If you sell something that says CLEAR make sure it is please :(

The idea that this protector is oleo-phobic or doesn't pick up smudges is a joke. Every finger touch was visible when I lifted my finger up.

I would have left this one star but I didn't give them a chance to make it right, I just returned it.

title: I like it for a clean slim fit but I think the protection is going to be proportional to the added size.
text:
[[ASIN:B010MWG3HO Galaxy Note 5 Case, Spigen® [Ultra Hybrid] AIR CUSHION [Crystal Clear] Clear back panel + TPU bumper for Galaxy Note 5 (2015) - Crystal Clear (SGP11684)]]

I have a thicker, heavy case for my Note 5 that does a great job of protecting it. One thing I realized is that I picked this particular color because I loved it and then I slapped it inside a case and hid it. Further the added bulk make it even larger.

Enter the Spigen hybrid clear case. It has soft TPU bumpers around the border and the back is poly carbonate plastic. I think the corner protection is pretty good but the rear protection I see failing if the impact is with a small enough object.

The cases fit is GREAT. Snug all around and the openings for chargers/headphones and microphones/speakers are also great. The camera is recessed int he opening in the rear to keep it from touching if you lay the phone on its back.

The case also is a fingerprint MAGNET. So is the phone though so whats the difference?

I did see one reviewer suggest his was yellowing after just a couple of days. I know TPU will pick up colors and the thing will most likely discolor with age and sunlight exposure but for $12 I expect to easily get a years worth out of it.

Bottom line if you want to feel like you are actually holding your device and seeing its clean lines and color then go for it! The protection isn't going to be otter-boxworthy but way better than going commando but it looks like you are going commando ;)

title: I've tried Droid, Pixel, iPhone, and now this
text:
I've had this phone for about two months now. To save time, yes, I would buy it again for what I paid ($179). Now for the details.

It is not a top-end phone but it doesn't claim to be. The outside is a little cheap feeling and the screen isn't incredibly sensitive. For example, I can play a game and press slightly away from buttons on the touchscreen and still activate them by pressing hard. The display is a decent resolution but again, not top-end. The RAM is also not top-end, so while there is a decent amount, it doesn't process quite as fast as I expected. For some reason it vibrates a lot for no reason that I can tell.

That being said, for the price you cannot beat what this phone does deliver. The processor is efficient and handles installing and downloading much quicker than I anticipated. Online gaming is certainly possible on low settings. Storage is not a problem and the phone is easily capable of being a work phone (i.e. dropbox, drive, docs, etc.). The 'gestures' for turning on the flashlight and camera are genius. I cannot tell you how many people have been interested in my phone just because of the karate-chop motion to turn on the flashlight. I do not have Alexa set-up for much of anything in my house, but this phone looks like it would take care of that well. The speakers... this might be the most impressive feature of the phone. I'm an audiophile and the idea of using smartphone speakers for music listening to me is horrendous. These are powerful and have decent clarity. The final positive is the battery. At least for now, it will charge quickly (like 30 mins quickly) and hold that charge easily two days if I am not playing any games or streaming video for a long time. I would say I've been able to get around six-eight hours of streaming on one charge, no problem.

Moto may have won me back as a customer with this phone. They are smart to undercut the competition by manufacturing a mid-level phone at an entry-level price. iPhone's are notorious for "software update" issues that make old models function poorly. The Google Pixel just got flagged for the same reason, since all the motherboards are mysteriously dying after exactly two years (mine did!). Until I see a reason to confidently spend that much on a phone again, I'm sticking with these.

title: BEST CLEAR Case with the BEST protection!!!!
text:
In the past, I've tried clear cases because like most people looking for this type of case, you want to enjoy the beauty of the phone and not have it covered up . The clear cases in the past were either all TPU which often yellowed over time. Or they were a combination of TPU around the sides and a polycarbonate for the back. The polycarbonate would scratch. Spigen had this version for the iPhone X and I bought it. It only lasted a few months before I tossed it. Lint/dirt kept on getting behind the polycarbonate. And it was very difficult to remove the case. After a few times, the polycarbonate started to separate from the TPU and that was the end of it.

I was skeptical of the quartz version which replaces the polycarbonate back with tempered glass. The bumper portion is still TPU. I've had this for several months and I'm pretty impressed. I toss it around and have had it in my pocket both back and front. The tempered glass back is nice, easy to clean. No scratches, pristine. Overall, I don't see alot of lint getting in. The only thing to note is that having a smooth glass front and back will make this phone slippery! Then again the iPhone 11's new matte glass back was also slippery.

There's a nice raised lip around the camera and around the screen, such that when you place your phone on a flat surface they do not make contact. I do use a tempered glass screen protector. With this I lose the benefit of the raised lip around the screen. With the screen protector everything sits flush. Not a big deal since I don't know if there's a point to protect the screen protector.

I don't know how the case will do if I ever drop it. I'm counting on the protection though. I used to use Spigen tough armor cases, which are built like tanks and are worry-free. They're just ugly and I'm tired of the way they look. So I'm taking a bit of risk here.

So far so good. I'm pretty impressed.

title: Greatly improves our showers, but has some drawbacks
text:
We've had this in our shower for the past few months and it's really improved the quality of our showers. We like to listen to music or YouTube videos while we shower, but before using this, we either
A) left our phones outside the shower, in the sink or on the counter, which made the sound hard to hear unless we turned it up super loud, which could disturb others in the house, or...
B) brought our phones into the shower which could risk getting water in the charging port, and you couldn't really use the touch screen while in the shower

This little apparatus has mostly solved the downsides of our various approaches by providing a secure, safe way to bring our phones into the shower. It adhered easily to the tile wall in our shower and is extremely secure - it's never fallen off the ball joint attachment. Now, we can even watch YouTube videos, and use the touchscreen cover to skip YouTube ads, skip songs, or change playlists, all while showering! You can even rotate 360 degrees to switch from portrait to landscape or vice versa, and tilt the device to view it from a different angle. It's wide and thick enough to fit my Pixel 7 Pro, without requiring that I remove its hefty case. The same goes for my partner's Samsung Galaxy Note 10, also with a case.

And our phones stay dry the whole time!

The one con that's worth noting has been echoed by other buyers here: The audio gets muffled a bit when putting your phone in here so I often need to turn the audio up to compensate - and the sound quality isn't so great when listening to detailed or fast conversations. But I don't know who goes into the shower expecting to do so.

That being said.. coming from iphone you will have to adjust how things work as iphone is made for those who.. well.. don't want to take the time to understand what their phones can REALLY do! iphone is an app machine and while droid gives you the same options there is so much more you can do with it and explore.

Also the charging port at the bottom others seem to hate it is fine, its a snap in place and as long as you get use to it, it is the LEAST of things to worry about.

The Android market is huge now, my friends iphones sucks next to my phone, and I couldn't be happier. Get this phone, you will not regret it.. if you do then get the One X..

title: Pretty but not all that sticky.
text:
I usually use a metal ring to help hold my phone, being notorious for my clumsiness. But it seems like everyone loves popsockets, so I decided to try it. Being a space geek, I got the blue nebula version, with plans to get the Moon style later if I liked them enough to get multiple tops.

I ordered a smooth plastic pink case to match the top, cleaned it as directed, and, ahem, popped the Popsocket on.

My first impression were a bit meh. It was pretty, and I could hold on to it, but it was just...okay. My grip on it didn't feel overly secure, and I wasn't sure it'd really help me not drop the phone. It wound up working fine - I was able to keep ahold of it most of the time - but it never felt as secure as having a ring. It also put the phone at a shallower angle than I prefer, but again, that's a personal thing.

At that point I'd have given it 4 stars, since my issues with it felt like personal preferences more than any fault of the PS.

What made it go from said 4 stars down to 3 was the fact that it started coming unstuck not even four months after I put it on. My rings, at a quarter the price, usually last *at least* a year, and I'm not particularly hard on them. It lasted for another six weeks or so, then came off totally at the most inopportune moments it could find.

In short, they're pretty and I really wish it would have worked as they have several fun space styles. That said, I wouldn't get another one. For the price, I would expect the adhesive to be far stickier and last longer than six months.

title: Excellent but with a few tweaks....
text:
I've had the Ulefone Armor 7 for about a week as of this review (Jan 2020). I'm coming from the Samsung S7 edge and previously from all Samsung Galaxy phones. I went with this phone for a few reasons. First it had more memory (RAM & ROM), larger battery, and big (but not too big) screen. Secondly the price is half what a flagship Samsung would cost and still not have similar specs.

I will tell you that this phone does NOT work with Sprint. I checked that the radios Sprint uses are installed on the phone prior to purchase but Sprint could not get it to activate. I switched to TMobile and had it working in minutes.

Initial impression is the phone is well built with modern unbranded Android 9. The only real issues I've encountered are mostly trivial except for one; maybe two depending on your opinion. First, as others have also reported, the USB C cable falls out extremely easily. Thank goodness there is wireless charging. Also thank goodness for the large battery. I'm a heavy phone user. My S7 edge went from 100% to 45% by 11am. The second issue is no cases. I know the phone is rugged but does that mean it has to be all scratched up. I found protectionfilms24 DOT com online. They make laser cut protection for the front, back, and camera lens. No available cases almost made me purchase a different phone.

A lot of my tried and true apps do not work on Android 9. So I'm spending a long time interviewing new candidates. Luckily my replacement launcher (Go) works and brought over all my settings.

Personally I would love the specs of this phone with a smaller screen. The 5.5" screen on my s7 edge was perfect size. Looking at the other phones offered by ulefone that have smaller screens also have less specs.

I'll report back if I find any reason to bore you some more

UPDATE: I just found this case on the ulefone website. ulefone DOT com/armor-7-multifunctional-protective-case-p0112.html Funny thing is I could not search for it

UPDATE 2/25/2020: The reason the USB C cable does not stay put very well is because of the protective rugged housing. ulefone did not leave enough space for a normal USB C cable to reach into the connector. ulefone did provide in the shipping box several connectors that are longer that work just fine.

I also have, as others have reported, an issue with the lack of touch responsiveness. Happens to me about 4-5 days. A simple restart fixes the issue.

UPDATE 7/25/20: I found that the lack of touch screen response happens when the keyboard is active. Particularly the use of emoticons. The good news is that if I rotate the phone horizontal and then vertical the screen becomes responsive without the need for a restart. I'm not sure if that is an Android, Google keyboard, or phone issue.

I also have, as others have reported, the issue with phone calls not ringing very loud even though volume is maxed. Speaker is not great.

I have also sent ulefone several emails which have not been answered.

UPDATE 3/26/2020: I have found that there are "long tip" or "extended tip" cables for rugged phones. They have a 10mm connector verses the normal 8mm connector.

UPDATE 7/25/20: For a rugged phone that assumably is going to work in construction and or other loud areas the max volume on the speaker is poor.

On a positive note. I have received 3 OTA updates.

Another awkward issue is the placement of the assignable function button. It is so low that I have a problem with the vehicle phone holder. The button falls directly inside the grips, which triggers the button.

1/10/2021 - The camera is very difficult to capture close up images. I tend to have to take a far shot and hope I can see what I need with zoom. Very disappointing.

text:
If you're in the market for a very minimalist type of case then this thin fit case by Spigen may be right up your ally. Featuring a very minimalist design indeed, you'll notice right off the bat that this thing is super light to hold. It adds very little weight to the already fairly light Note 4. You have full access to all of your buttons, including your heart rate sensor which works great with this case. Some other cases that offer more protection for your phone actually have made the heart rate sensor difficult to use, so I'm happy it works good in this case. The edges of the case are slightly raised which offers a little bit of protection in case your phone falls and lands on the display, but it is very little protection if any. I would highly recommend using a screen protector along with this case. The top and bottom of the phone are almost fully exposed, so if you do end up dropping it and it lands on either of those then it will most likely cause a little bit of damage.

This case feels good in the hands, and I didn't find it felt like it would be easier to lose grip of it in my hands. I did receive this to test out and provide feedback on but my review is honest. title: Is it OK to cut the metal part to make it a nano sim card? - NO
text:
This cutter appears to be able to cut a regular and micro sim card to a nano sim card.
However, when I placed a regular sim card, it will cut the metal part of the regular sim card.
I bought this pre-paid cheap Samsung phone from T-Mobile that uses a regular sim card to be used on iPhone5.

This product will do exactly that - it will cut part of the metal of the regular sim card.

to cut it to the nano sim card's size. Therefore, I cannot use this product to cut a regular sim card to a nano size and have a working sim card.
Did I buy something that I cannot use - YES.

title: Pop it out, pop it in, you're done.
text:
It really doesn't get any easier, and that is a fact. No instructions were included and for $[...] shipped to my door--- you CANNOT complain nor did I ever expect any. Truthfully, I still do not know how they shipped it to me so fast for the price, kudos. So a simple search on the internet and you will find dozens of videos of how to do it, and after watching 10-seconds I realized that it was easy as 1-2-3. In short: pop the chrome ring off with a small screwdriver, turn phone upside down and let trackball fall out, install new one with the tabs side to side, install new chrome ring with the missing prongs towards the top. Total time: 30-seconds.

As far as performance when compared to a good working OEM unit--- it is equal which, again, is all that you can ask for. The only real difference that I see is that the ball has a SMALL imperfection in the color ONLY--- again, $[...], no complaints as unlike the stock one that has definitely seen better days.... it resurrected a phone that otherwise was perfect and was only marred by a bad trackball (and previously an ailing battery). Plus, it beats taking a perfectly good phone to the local store and having them want to give you a refurbished unit that had who-knows-what wrong with it before.

Recommendation? If your trackball is at all not 100%, it is worth it hands down. So far I have spent $12 on repairs for my Blackberry-- one battery ($9) and this trackball ($3) which took it from needing to replace the phone to bringing it back to life.

The only thing that I did find out on another Blackberry was that when you push the ball down to select, it worked sometimes. This is something completely different than the trackball itself--- but rather the small circuit board that sits below the trackball. I repaired that one with a new board for less than $15 that I found on Amazon. So for the cursor to move around the screen--- that is the trackball, to select by pushing the ball---- that is the circuit board!

Am I writing this review to say how bad the case is? Absolutely not! As I mentioned, I am extremely rough on tools, cases, etc. To have a case that lasted me this long is nothing short of amazing. Much like luggage is designed to protect its contents, this case is designed to protect my phone. And my phone, thanks to this case, looks as good as it does the day I got it. I am absolutely happy to spend a mere $30 on a case that will continue to function well and protect my phone for another couple years.

Photo is of the brand new case as compared to the one I've used/abused/beat on for the last two years. It has held up extremely well!

title: Leather take of Apple’s design!
text:
Thought I would check this band out. There are tremendous amount of third party Alpine Loops, and they’re typically the nylon style, which is an attempt of mimicking Apple’s design.

This band at first look is that way, however, once you look at it closely, you’ll realize it’s different! The material is made of leather, and from what I can tell, appears to be genuine leather.

It is smooth to the touch, and let’s just say the comfort against the skin totally blows nylon and silicone bands out of the water. I have all 3 of Apple’s ultra bands, and for reference, I felt the Trail Loop was the most comfortable. But this band feels even better! Just off of the comfort variable alone I can recommend this.

The color is not the same orange as Apple’s orange. If I were to compare it to something, I’d say it’s closer to Hermes orange. Looks more classy than the orange that’s just screaming for attention.

The construction feels very good, but I am not sure how resistant or safe it would be to expose it to water — which could potentially mean that this is more of a dressy band instead of an active band.

Lastly, it might be because the loop is new, but tightening and loosening the band requires a little more effort, because the leather makes it tighter to move it back and forth. As long as it holds up, this shouldn’t be an issue however.

Very nice band, and I am thinking to get other colors!

title: Nice looking, but dead or defective on arrival
text:
# Initial impressions:
The product arrived in a nice looking box. It was easy to unpack and assemble.
The charger and adapter look to be good quality. There a nice rubber feet on the bottom to reduce slipping, and there is a rubber pad on the charger for the phone to sit on. The charger appears sturdy and well designed.
I was surprised that the included adapter was micro-USB, not USB-C, but it really doesn't matter.

# Mismatched Instructions:
When I plugged the charger in, the front LED turned red. Based on the included instructions, this indicates that it is charging, but I had not yet placed my phone on the charger. Later the light turned blue and then purple. These colors are not mentioned in the product instructions, so I don't know what they mean.
The instructions appear to be for a slightly different model, because they show an LED on the side of the charger, and only mention red and green LED status colors. But this charger has the LED on the front, and apparently uses red, blue, and purple status indicator colors.
The instructions also mention a "button" to press, but there is no button on this charger.

# Nonfunctional charger -- defective or damaged.
When I place my phone on the charger, nothing happens. The charger LED color does not change (remains purple) and the phone does not detect any charging. The adapter is firmly plugged in on both ends, so I don't think it is a connection issue. I have charged this phone successfully using a charger from another company, so I am sure that the phone supports Qi wireless charging.
The charger also outputs a faint electronic "whining" sound, so perhaps the charger is simply damaged or defective.

# No technical support
What I would really like to do is contact technical support for the device to ask what the LED colors mean and to determine if (A) the product is defective or (B) the product is simply not Qi compliant or (C) the product doesn't support my phone (which it should because any Qi-compliant charger should work). But unfortunately, there does not seem to be any product support.
Amazon does not list any support URL or phone number for Lamzien, and I cannot find a Lamzien support website or any information about one in the instructions that came with the product.

# Overall review
I would really like to give this product a good rating because it looks nice and has an excellent price. However, the product simply does not work. It includes the wrong instructions in the package, and there is apparently no technical support. So I have to give it the lowest rating.
If I am able to get some technical support or determine the problem on my own, I will update this review.

title: Good screen coverage and edge fit but mediocre instructions and adhesion over fingerprint scanner.
text:
Getting the protector on the phone was pretty simple and easy to line up by using the camera. It comes with two protectors and one protector for the cameras on the back of the phone. It is easy to lift of the protector without it cracking if you need to adjust after installation. The touch sensitivity is good. Side note: if you use the S-View Flip cover it will NOT work with this screen protector (to be fair I haven't found any screen protector that this case works with so more of an issue with the case not the protector).
Issues with the fingerprint scanner: It is difficult to get smooth adhesion over the fingerprint scanner. It always seems to pull up and create a smudged appearance when your screen is off (see picture). After installation I had to hold down the protector over the fingerprint scanner with great force several times to finally get the phone to recognize a fingerprint (the instructions state you only need to hold down for two seconds after wiping side to side several times). I also had to reenter my fingerprint scans. After installation you will have to push harder than normal to get it to recognize your fingerprint.
Issues with instructions: Their instructions are poorly written, using incorrect grammar, slang abbreviations, misspelling, confusing sentences, and the section about where to find "touch sensitivity" is incorrect for the type of phone the screen protector is for. The instructions DO NOT include any pictures, which makes it hard if you are a visual learner or if there is a language barrier.
Overall it is cheap option that provides decent functionality but some effort to get the fingerprint scanner to work.

Since I did not drain it I was able to allow a friend to recharge. She like it so much she is buying one. What sold me was the built in cables. I had little room in my purse to carry things and not having a cable was a benefit.
For me this unit is not for day to day use. I think if it was the built in cables might be a downside because they are likely to be the first thing to break. I am not saying they are poorly made, quite the opposite. They seem quite durable. But the cables bend and get pulled so I think they would wear out long before the battery.
I did a lot of research before buying this unit, and some chargers work quicker and hold more energy. That is why I bought this model. My friends were all impressed with this unit. At lunch I was able to fully recharge from 30%. My friend was not even close to this with her charger.

text:
This is an inexpensive phone, I paid $19.99 for it on sale, and it came with $30 worth of minutes with Net10. Couldn't beat the deal, and I had read fairly good reviews about the call clarity and battery life which were my main concerns, so I bought it. I am not UNhappy with it, but will probably upgrade when I see a good deal on a better phone.

PRO:
- Great reception
- Great call clarity
- GREAT battery life
- Easy to use

CON:
- Keys are small
- Keys are so sensitive I inadvertenly dial a call just by putting the phone in my purse. Must make it a habit to lock keys EVERY time I'm done, which is a pain.
- Ear piece is actually at the top of the phone, so you have to hold it slightly below your ear to hear. Works OK, just a little awkward to get used to.

I do like Net10 service. I am not a heavy phone user, perhaps 30 min/week, I do not want to 'surf' from my phone, or take pics. So the Nokia 1600 with Net10 is perfect and cheap for a basic user like me.

Their customer service leaves something to be desired, but only because it takes time to clearly understand each other and get the issue resolved. They put you on hold to talk to their 'manager', repeat things, etc. But they are courteous and DO get the job done ... just allow a little extra time and only call when you are feeling calm and patient.

title: Very impressive early experience at a very modest price point.
text: Early days yet (owned it for two weeks) but initial reaction is very favorable. I was expecting compromises in quality and performance at this very modest price point but I see none thus far. I've previously owned various models of iPhone (4, 5 & 6) and this is my first foray into the world of Android. This device compares very favorably to the iPhones I've owned, at about 1/3 of the price of current iPhone models. I had zero problems activating this phone with T-Mobile. I love the fact I am free to join and quit any mainstream US carrier with this phone. Call audio quality is excellent but I wish the speakerphone volume could be made louder. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity is simple and effective. Connectivity with my in-car Ford Sync system was seamless - I can make/receive audio calls completely hands-free using my contacts list and I can send/receive texts hands-free also but Sync limits me to about 20 "canned" text responses. I think the "adaptive brightness" feature needs some work - it's often too dark for my tastes. Battery consumption is excellent - I can usually go about two days on a single charge (with "Battery Saver" turned OFF) - and the "Turbo power" feature will recharge the device by about 40% in an astonishing 15 minutes and completely recharge a fully discharged battery in about 1 hr 35 mins. As a bit of a DSLR camera snob, I appreciate the "Professional" mode of this phone's camera which allows you some measure of control of Exposure compensation, White Balance, ISO, shutter speed, and focus etc. Ultimately however, it's still just a smartphone with very modest optics and a semi-clever imaging processor - so the final photos/videos are OK but not epic. OK for a quick snapshot/video if you don't have any better camera available. I wasn't very pleased with the frustrating and clumsy Android/Windows 10 contacts/calendar synchronization  - there's no iTunes to bail you out, you're on your own to figure it out (try the "My Phone Explorer" app in the Google Play store). However, that's a criticism of the Android operating system and so it's not fair to burden the phone itself with these issues. Overall, I'm very impressed with this phone - especially at this price point.

title: Better after using for a while
text:
UPDATE: I originally gave this three stars for those sharp buttons, but after using it for a month or so, I'm bumping it to 4. You acclimate quickly to the very prominent buttons and truth be told they haven't snapped on pockets again (the day I got it, it snagged and I expected it to be the norm, but I guess that was a fluke). I can even say at night when I have to reach over to adjust the volume for my airpods, I can definitely find and feel the volume buttons more easily in the dark than I could with my previous case. I've also dropped the phone a time or two and so far the case has protected it, though the drops weren't from really high and not onto concrete.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: I was really not expecting the buttons on this case to be so sharp—not sharp enough to cut skin, of course, but just very rigid, right-angled, and easy to catch on a back pocket both going in and coming out. They stick straight out from the phone case a full 1/16 inch. That's pretty far in phone-case-side terms. It’s not a comfortable feel. That said, you don’t have to fumble in the dark for a button… you know EXACTLY where it is. You can definitely find the buttons with gloves on, but if it's a knitted-type glove, the yarn might actually catch on the buttons.

On the plus side, the buttons integrate well with the actual phone controls and the case overall is a solid, tight fit. Only time will tell if it loosens up later but for now it seems like a well-fitted case. Case edges are also a bit on the rough side but not nearly as bad as the buttons and they actually help with grip. Seems like a good bit of “height” around the screen area and the material around the case feels robust enough to protect from average drops.

I’m torn about whether this should only be three stars but man… I really don’t like these hard buttons.

I use the extra features on the phone, such as swipe from very top for notifications and swipe from very bottom for alarms and flashlight so I feel that swiping over the protector edge interferes every time. title: UPDATED - Changed my rating from 2 stars to 4
text:
I got one of these when I bought my S7 Edge from Verizon, not realizing it was a Zagg protector (the Verizon box doesn't have the Zagg name on the front). Had I known, I would have declined and got a screen protector somewhere else as I've had experience with Zagg screen protectors in the past. They may work great to protect helicopter blades, but I don't care for them on a HD phone screen.

I will say that after less than 24 hours, all the bubbles were gone, but I spent time rubbing them all out. Not sure they would disappear on their own. There are 2 reasons I don't care for the Zagg protectors - they feel of them (almost rubbery) and they are not clear. You definitely can tell there's a protector on your screen. Makes your HD screen look crappy. Like a soft piece of wood after you write on it with a ball point pen. Subtle, yet noticeable impressions. Rub your finger nail on it and you'll have very noticeable mark.

I feel somewhat duped by Verizon, but I should have looked more closely at what I was buying. Do not recommend this screen protector.

<<<<<<<<UPDATED 7/27/16>>>>>>>>>
I'm changing my review from 2 stars to 4. I've had this screen protector on my device for a few months now and while I don't prefer these type of screen protectors, I'm realizing that protecting a curved screen isn't as easy as a flat one. This screen protector has not peeled back anywhere like so many others seem to have issues with. It works perfectly with my Caseology Envoy Series case (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B019PBJ6WM/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o06_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1). There are not many glowing reviews of any of the S7 Edge screen protectors so I feel I was too harsh on my first review. Since the TPU material is softer, it will show indentations and they really don't "heal", fortunately, you do not really notice them when looking directly at the screen. TPU material is not smooth like glass or some of the other screen protectors, but does do a good job in protecting screens. I'm satisfied enough with this screen protector to not want to change it or purchase a tempered glass one, but may in the future.

title: So happy it feels like a phone screen...not plastic!
text:
This is my first glass screen protector. I have tried plastic film and hated them. I could never get them on properly and always had air bubbles in them. The touch screen does not respond the way it should with a plastic film. I always ended up taking them off, there is nothing like the feel of the real phone screen. I just love it without a protector EXCEPT I recently dropped my phone in the garage and the screen shattered 😳 so after I got my screen replaced I knew I needed some protection. I decided to try the glass protector. I am so happy I did! What I like best about this screen protector is that it is very responsive. The screen responds exactly the way it does without a cover which is the most important feature to me. You can't tell that there is anything on the screen at all. I can't speak to its protection value as I fortunately have not dropped my phone again! But I will be sure to update the review if there is any change in that (hopefully not!). The packaging is great, however are are no real instructions included in the package. There are 2 wipes, one is marked 1. Wet, the other 2. Dry. So it was easy enough to figure out what to do. I used the wet wipe, then the dry wipe. It also comes with a sticker which says dust absorber. I didn't use that because it didn't appear that there was any dust left on the phone after the 2 wipes. There are also stickers to use as guides but I didn't use those either, I wasn't sure what to do with them. The glass protector has a tab that says to remove before applying. Once you take that off you have exposed the sticky side of the protector. I simply aligned that as best I could on the phone being sure the home button and sound opening were not covered. It went on very easily and smoothly, no air bubbles! I then put on the clear plastic phone case. I like the case, it has a thin profile and is very light so it does not distract from the beauty of the phone. It wraps around the sides of the phone nicely and is raised slightly higher than the face of the phone which I believe will help with protection.
What could be a negative is that the screen protector does not go all the way to the edge of the phone and does not meet the edge of the case so there is a slight gap of unprotected screen. That is the reason I am not giving it 5 stars. I don't know if it's a design flaw or if that's the way glass screen protectors are made. But other than that I am completely satisfied with this and very glad I got it. Now I don't need to worry that my keys are going to scratch my screen when my phone is in my purse. I received this product at a reduced price for my honest and unbiased review.

text:
Benson Reviewed Safe accessory for Google Nexus 5X!

There are major problems with 3rd party USB C charging wires and adaptors for Google Nexus 5X, 6P and other phones which used the fast charging technology.

Fast charging uses 3A throughput with damages equipment, melts plastics, and catches on firs. 3rd party no-name manufacturures can not be trusted as some of them did not follow the proper spec.

Google Engineer Benson Leung has tested, reviewd, and listed these as safe to use with Google Nexus 5X and 6P.

I researched this matter for 2 days.

These have a resistor which tells the phone and the old charger to switch to "Slow Charging" Mode. That will take longer, but it is the only safe way to use older chargers with new phones that have fast charging technology.

If you want fast charging and you want best bang for the buck devices (rather than very expensive brand names) stick with Anker.

title: Very-good minimal case
text:
This is my favorite case so far. I call it a "minimal" case. It is good for getting a good grip on the slippery phone. There is not much protection from dropping.

I had bad luck with the screen protector -- just kept getting dust underneath, and it looked bad, so now I use it without the screen protector. Maybe I will buy some other protectors and try my luck again.

I got a free Apple "bumper" case, but none of my non-Apple headphone plugs or multipin adapters will go through the case holes (such as the iGo car power adapter), as they are slightly bigger than the openings. On this case the holes are big enough, and the case is thin enough, that all my non-Apple plugs fit so far.

They could have cut an opening on the back for the Apple logo, for appearance sake, as Elago did on its series of cases for the iPhone 3G.

Be careful putting it on and taking it off. The buttons and silence switch can catch on the case openings, and I don't think you want to apply much sideways force to them. Just bending the sides slightly when putting it on or taking it off takes care of this. I find this a little tricky and I don't think this is a case you want to be putting on and taking off a lot.

After several weeks I now see bit of the rubbery/textured-paint coating rubbing off on the edges where I put the phone face down on a surface, showing the black plastic underneath. It is not easy to see and functionally I do not think it is significant.

When using the phone for turn-by-turn navigation in a car, it warms up quite a bit. I am a little concerned about the case -- any case -- insulating the phone and reducing air cooling. But, this case is thin and that concern will be less on this case than most others, I expect. Regarding this, the Apple bumper is nice as it is open on the back.

title: Almost a great phone
text: Butter smooth refresh rate, really good camera, although the selfie camera could be a little better. It is supposed to be a 5G phone, but on the AT&T network you cannot get anything more than 4G LTE! it is a US model which is nice. There are positives and negatives to the fact that it used to be a T-Mobile phone. I do get the Google feed and I also get T-Mobile television and some other feeds from T-Mobile but you cannot delete any of the T-Mobile software. For whatever reason the OnePlus 9 pro 5G is not compatible with AT&T's 5G Network. So you will have a 5G phone, that only runs 4G LTE if you use AT& T. I was on T-Mobile and loved it while I was in San Antonio Texas, but in Palm Coast Florida there are too many dead spots so I'm forced to use Cricket to get continuous service. That being said I don't get to experience the amazing benefits of 5G. It would be a better phone if it had an IR blaster, a headphone jack, even better if it had a quad DAC and definitely expandable storage. I've experienced a few glitches where on certain websites on Chrome, it would not allow me to do any of the functions on the website. It would say that I needed to Grant permissions which were already granted to Chrome. I deleted my Chrome app even though it was pre-installed on the phone so it wouldn't completely delete and then I re-updated chrome in the Google play store. That seemed to have fix the issue. That being said overall I'm very happy with the OnePlus 9Pro. I miss smart select from my Samsung Galaxy Note 9. Because it's nice to be able to take a screenshot of text and select the text as text, to go and put into an email or a message or whatever you need to use it for. Overall I'd say I give the OnePlus 9 Pro mobile phone a solid 9. I'm scared to update to Android 12 because I see that the color science on Android 12 update changes the camera and decreases the quality of the photos. it's interesting how that happened just before the launch of the OnePlus 10 pro. I think the cameras on this phone are really good. Are they perfect no. They're not like a Pixel or an iphone as far a consistent color science. but they are damn close. Honestly the video is better than most phones the pictures are really good. I wouldn't say they're the best but they're good. I highly recommend using the pro mode as pictures are far better with it. I also highly recommend using the wide-angle lens or the main shooter has these two take better pictures the third lens is a bit of a waste. OnePlus + 9 pro has a wide angle lens that is second to none, as there is no distortion at the edges. I would say it is far better, than the one on the OnePlus 10 pro as it doesn't give you that fish eye effect. Unless fisheye effect distortion is something you like. If that's the case this isn't the phone for you. But it is an excellent camera system. In fact I'd say it probably gives you the best shots in pro mode. I do see that there is some color shift when you switch between lenses. But overall I'd say it's a 95% solution. If they did better software upgrades as far as the camera I think it would be better but I'd say that overall I give the phone between an 85 and 95% solution. Don't get less than 256 gigs, as it doesn't have expandable storage which is disappointing. But I'd say the software experience is pretty good it's close to straight Google software and the enhancements overall are good. Like I said, I wish I could do OCR with my screenshots instead of just taking screenshots, like I did on my Samsung Galaxy Note 9 using smart select. But even Samsung isn't the same phone company anymore. They took away the headphone jack they took away expandable storage now they've even taken away the charger in the box. I was a consistent Samsung Galaxy Note user once they got rid of the note they got rid of expandable storage and they got rid of the charger in the box I would no longer Buy Samsung. And all of the reviewers focused solely on the cameras and so companies are no longer giving the great features like IR blasters and really cool things that adds so much to the phone I'm not really a wireless charging guy I don't really need that feature. And since I have a plate on the back of my phone I can't reverse charge with the case on cuz that's how I mount it to my dashboard. Since Samsung has taken this direction I will not buy their products anymore . That's why I left Samsung as after the Samsung Galaxy Note 9 I feel Samsung went in the wrong direction chasing apples customers instead of taking care of their customer base and expanding. I will say that the charger from OnePlus is amazing. although it didn't come included and Amazon renewed phone you get a charger, but not the OnePlus charger. It actually came with the Samsung charger. In a brown  cardboard plain box. Not the original packaging. And not a renewed box like I've gotten in other renewed cell phones I bought. I was able to buy a OnePlus fast charger on Amazon and it is quite fast. Make sure you get the USB c to USB c not the USB 3.0 to USB c. As that is the one from the OnePlus 8 and it is 45 Watts not 65 watts. With a 65 watt fast charger it charges really fast, in about 30 minutes from 0%. This Amazon renewed product did come with a charger. In fact it came with a Samsung charger, which isn't bad and in fact I don't use fast charging all the time, as I think using the fast charging all the time will decrease your battery life . I only use fast charging when it's an emergency. But I'm not disappointed in my purchase. I don't think that this is $1,000 phone but I think it's a really good phone between $600 and $700 it's a great phone. Overall I'm happy with the phone. The alert slider is a great thing every cellphone should have it. The $120 HZ 1440 screen is amazing quad HD AMOLED. Like I said I'm holding off and upgrading to Android 12 because I feel that it's not something I need although the android-12 features are amazing I do not like what Android 12 update for OnePlus 9 pro does to the camera. Another issue is that you can't use the side bar because it doesn't detect your finger dragging to the left or even to the right for that matter. Another issue that I found was that it wouldn't recognize my face , the camera is covered with the plastic film and if it even had a smudge on it it was enough for it to not know who you are. It does keep the phone protected I will say that but a lot of features become unusable.. You can't do the split screen with the sidebar, you can't use the facial recognition, it's very hard to drag menus downward and and it says it's waterproof but if you try to put something in the audio Jack the protective Covering disappears and there goes that. Also trying to open the little doors at the bottom for the charger and the stylus was was also painful if you have problems with your hands. Honestly, I regret buying this case and I wish that I had listened to the reviews more. Please please do not bother with this case trust me when I tell you it's a Royal pain in the neck.

title: Great bluetooth headset
text:
I bought this to remain hands free when I purchased my new Jeep that didn't come Bluetooth equipped.
PROS:
-Works great - great sound quality, easy to answer phone calls
-Stays in your ear- Stays in my ear perfectly without needing anything to go over my ear (even when the Jeep as no top or doors). Also comes with various ear pieces to find your perfect fit. As someone with small ear canals, I really appreciated this.
-Holds a charge- I use this for about 30 minutes a day most days and it lasts weeks on one charge. I believe you get about 8 hours of talk time per charge but I've found this to be longer than 8 hours
-Compact - you can't beat the size. It's easy to toss in a cupholder or your purse
-Connects to phone easily- It connected right away and I've never needed to reconnect
-Replaces headphones in a pinch- I've used in place of headphones to listen to music or a podcast when I've lost my headphones.

CONS:
-Volume levels- there are only 3 volume levels available. I wish it were more like the smaller increments that you can do on your phone. At times the medium level is too quiet but the loudest level is definitely loud. It's annoying but not a deal breaker.

Overall this is a great headset at a fantastic price. Would definitely recommend.

title: I like it
text:
I chose this phone because I wanted an easy-to-use, basic phone without a mp3 player and all that.

I haven't experienced any of the problems that the other people here have. I experienced the echo problem with another phone, but it was a problem with the network at that location, not the phone. Re the inside screen not turning off in power-save mode, I just tried it and it does turn off when I close the phone, just as it is supposed to. In fact I can see the screen go on when it hits a certain angle when opening. I think that person had a bad switch in the hinge.

So.

The good:

It is small, or at least small enough. It doesn't feel bulky in the pocket like my old Sanyo did.

The black shiny finish is part of the case and won't scratch off, unlike the silver paint on so many other phones.

It sounds fine, but not as good as my old Sanyo. Sometimes I could wish it went louder.

Reception is fine. I drive all over Denver and I have never had a dropped call.

It has speakerphone. It doesn't have a separate speaker on the outside, it just turns up the volume on the earpiece speaker. So I thought it would sound terrible, but it turns out it works okay.

It looks cool, or at least the high-schoolers I teach tell me so.

It is cheap. I got it for $29 when I renewed my plan.

The bad:

There is no silence button. When I attend a meeting or go to a movie, I have to open it up and hit the volume down button about 8 times. A single button that just turned off all the sound would be much better.

The keypad is a little difficult to use. It feels nearly like a flat surface, with very slight grooves to distinguish one button from another. Further, the buttons are not arranged in straight rows; the middle buttons, i.e., the 2, the 5, the 8, and the 0, are dropped slightly. These two things mean it is basically impossible to use the phone without looking. That isn't unique to this phone, of course. What I usually do is put a tiny drop of super glue on at least the "talk" and "end" buttons, so I can feel them and press them without looking.

When you go to the contact list and hit the first letter of the name you want, there is a delay before the screen shows you the names. It isn't a long delay, but it is there.

The voice command capability is versatile, but it means you have to tell it what you want to do, i.e., you have to say "Voice dial." That is the only voice command I would ever want it to do, but you have to tell it that every time. Also it doesn't work very well. I believe the software for that is not actually in the phone. It is either something like a java applet downloaded to phone on the fly, or it is done centrally on some server. The good thing about that is you don't have to (and you cannot) train the phone to recognize your particular voice. The bad thing is that the voice recognition doesn't work very well, especially with unusual names, of which I have lots.

The top and bottom feel nearly identical, so it is easy to open it upside down. If this problem keeps bugging me, I may file some notches on one side of the case, or do something else to let me feel which side is up.

title: Beware: Crashed 9 weeks in
text:
Less than 3 months after receiving this phone it is crashing. Data turning on and off, rebooting itself...tried resetting internet connections, new SIM card, and finally did a factory reset. Nothing worked, the hardware itself was bad. After spending 3-4 days with Sony tech people telling me to do troubleshooting I had already done, I finally get told to email them all my info including IMEI and they will send a return authorization for repair. Not even a replacement phone, a repair.
I emailed the requested info. Received nothing for several more days. Called in because the chat feature (which supposedly is open 9-8pm) never works, and no one responds to emails (I emailed multiple times). I was told I would receive the return authorization within the next day; auto email followup said within 48 hours. Three days later, still nothing. I had to call in again, and the guy said I would receive it within 3 hours. Still nothing. Next day, I call in again. This time I get angry, and another guy actually sends me the Fedex shipping label within an hour. So now I go to Fedex where I have to pay for my own box, and discover they only have shipping loss coverage for up to $100; the form says I can add extra to that, but Fedex says "no, that would have to be applied at the time the shipping label was created." So apparently if my new $600 phone gets lost or damaged in the mail, I'll just be out $500. And the real kicker is that I probably won't have it back for two weeks.
While the phone itself is lovely (beautiful screen) and it has good sound quality, I would advise people to steer clear of it. The camera is good as well, but really only for close-ups. The zoom is not good. Not at all worth the hassle and weeks without use of a new phone.

Update: I sent my device off to Sony for repair, and they sent it back in exactly the same condition. It doesn't work. They refuse to replace the phone. When I asked to speak to a supervisor, they hung up on me.

title: ... black otterbox commuter case for my Galaxy s3 and liked it enough
text: I had a lime green and black otterbox commuter case for my Galaxy s3 and liked it enough. It felt a little slippery in the hand but I liked the colors so it wasn't a big deal. One day I forgot my wallet and phone on the roof of my car. When I sped up to 45mph on a 2 lane road, I heard a clunk on the roof and watched in terror as my wallet and phone bounced across the pavement behind me, cards and receipts exploding everywhere. My phone bounced at least 3 times before landing face down on the asphalt and before I could pull over and get to it, 3 cares (one was a full size pickup) drove directly over the back of the phone. I thought for sure it was destroyed. To my utter shock and amazement, there wasn't a single scratch on the screen. Some tire scuffs and abrasions on the plastic case but the phone itself was completely untouched. And this isn't the defender series, this is only commuter. It only advertises to protect from small drops and bumps. Needless to say, I became an Otterbox fan for life. When I traded my s3 in for an S6 however, I was disappointed at the lack of color options and had to go with another case brand (Spigen Slim Armor in Mint, beautifully designed case!) which was very nice and aesthetic, but it didn't feel as secure as the Otterbox. Fast forward to today, I now have a Galaxy s7 with a mint and black Otterbox commuter and it's so nice being able to set my phone down and not feel like I'm scratching up the glass backing or the slightly protruded camera. I feel like I could throw my phone at the ground and it would still be just fine. The commuter series is a great case for protection without making the phone look bulky and ugly. Well worth the money!

title: Brilliant design!
text: This is the coolest addition to my camping gear I have gotten in a long time. This device is a solar charger that is about as big as a smartphone (just a little thicker). It has three solar panels that you unfold and place in direct sunlight. The cells charge the attached battery. You can tell how much the charge is by a series of blue LEDs on the battery pack. It charges up quite fast in strong light. There are two ports at the end that you use to charge–two USB output ports (for charging devices) and a micro USB input port (for charging the battery directly from a plugin). This is a great backup system. I was recently at Canyon de Chelly on an expensive tour and my phone battery died. You can use this to quickly charge up your system on the fly while you are still using your camera in the field. There is a built-in flashlight as well which has an SOS signal flasher and a more strobe-like flashing sequence. Overall this is the perfect system for camping and traveling for its portability, lightness, and ease of use. I like the fact that it has a battery so you can charge during the day and still use it as a backup power source at night. Brilliant design!

text:
Ive tried the 5 inch version of this family of phones and thought it was decent but I think the phone is pretty much more responsive and better in this 4.7 inch iteration of it. The camera responds faster as does the screen and it looks way more vibrant. Perhaps the smaller size does the processor better. Only con is the HDR of the camera produces grainy images while everything else looks as good as other phones in the 5MP range.

Phone feels pretty solid all around and in a really lovely color its fantastic. I love its weight and feel too as it doesnt even feel like what one would expect of the cost. In terms of the feature set, once I had all my favorite Google Apps going like Hulu, Crunchyroll, Youtube, Gmail, and Google Chrome beta it felt like it was my main phone. I could easily see myself using this as much as my main phone due to how it feels and how compact it is.

Charges to full power in only an hour on the usb connection and even faster plugged in, rivaling other phones or even better them in terms of time to charge when on usb to pc.

Definitely consider this phone if you are truly in the market for saving costs and have say T-Mobile (I have T-mobile and this works fine in my area with 3G+ more).

title: Great Smartphone from Tmo.
text:
Excellent phone from T-Mobile fully tacking advantage of their 4G LTE network. Today it received the Android 4.4.4 update as well offering faster speeds, fixing a few key glitches that the out of the box product had in some settings, and giving it a nicer refresh and make over in terms of the settings menu (different sounds, different organization), and a ps4 os sounding boot up screen before loading the T-mobile opening screen.

It is waterproof as Ive got it wet numerous times and saw no decreased phone performance. Without a screen protector the visuals look great. Photos look fantastic too, however Id definitely take advantage of uploading them to the google photos app as simply sharing them via the phone and then to say twitter or something they come out looking really compressed and trashy, going the goold photos album way uploads them (via drive) in their full native quality with no compression.

Video looks great on it though it seems some apps you need to actually hold the screen a bit far from you for it to look high definition and non grainy. Ive not experienced this phenomenon on the youtube apps, and perhaps its something software based via the apps specific (hulu for example, crunchyroll too).

All in all it is well worth the money and is a great phone for connectivity apps, and video watching. Sound is pretty loud as well though I typically connect it to one of many bluetooth speakers to play from.

Recharge time via ac adapter on wall is about 30minutes to full battery, on usb to a computer it takes many hours. Being fully connected on the network as well as not lowering brightness the phone last just about the entire day and more without a charge, so its much better than phones of the past.

title: Great metal mount for only $8
text:
These are very nice for mounting small cameras or bullet-shaped IR lights. Mount appears to be all aluminum due to light weight, lack of magnetic attraction, and shiny silver visible beneath paint. Also includes a soft black pad to prevent scratching the thing you're mounting. The part with the black pad can be completely unscrewed and flipped 180 degrees, which will move the center of the oval-shaped mounting hole in the black pad out 3.7cm (1.45") farther from the base and allow you to mount a larger item. Mount feels strong enough to take something fairly heavy. It comes with three wood screws for the base, drywall anchors, and one screw that fits a standard tripod mount hole in the device being mounted.

Comes with hex wrench for adjusting three different screws that let you rotate on three axis. All metal seems thick enough that I don't expect any problems with bending or loosening of the 3 screws. Screws go directly into the metal of the mount and if they strip the mount, there is no way to add a nut on the other side in 2 of the 3 cases. So be careful about cross-threading and don't over tighten the screws.

White paint does not seem thick enough to be powder coating. Metal is still visible in speckles in many areas. Paint is thinnest inside of the base of the mount so caulking above the mount is recommended to prevent water penetration outdoors. If the metal is truly aluminum it should self-protect itself for many years where the paint allows water through.

Concerns
I like this tripod but have a few concerns.

The ball joint, tightening washer, and thread bolt are all one solid plastic piece. The threaded area is short, so you may not get a full, sturdy connection to the phone holder or camera. (See photos)
My concern is through time, the threads will strip out or possibly break off.

text:
Wow! This is the easiest screen protector system I've ever use. So let me give you a summary of how it works. First you have the screen protector that you place over the phone after cleaning the glass. Then you put two clear rubber bands over the protector to set the screen protector in place.
After you set the screen protector the kit comes with two adhesive strips which taped to the side of the phone. You then remove the rubber bands and pull the protector to the right of the phone screen. Then you remove the protective strip from from the backside of the screen protector and place it on the phone screen. You then use the credit card like applicator to remove the bubbles from the screen and remove the top layer protector.
The instructions are easy to read with illustrations. Top scores for a great product and an easy way to apply the screen protector.

title: Unusable
text:
I have applied a screen protector on every hand-held electronic device I've owned and never once struggled with air bubbles. I've never once had to use more than one protector during application. Until now. I bought this screen protector because it claimed that it had anti-scratch self-healing protection. My previous screen protector was suffering from some minor blemishes and I wanted a clean look that would last. These not only have to be applied with a liquid solution (micellar water) that creates an absolute ton of air bubbles, but the material is rubbery and stretches when any kind of pressure is put on it. This comes with a rubber squeegee to pull the liquid from one side of the protector to the other.

- Attempt 1 - I attempted to apply the first protector, which immediately stuck to my phone in an awkward position because not enough liquid was applied (it sprays on...). My phone was very clean, so the screen was hydrophobic and would not allow the liquid to pool when sprayed. It instead created a bunch of small water droplets all over the screen. There was no way to salvage the protector at this point as the adhesive had been ruined.

- Attempt 2 - I tried again with a second protector, but this time poured a large concentration of the liquid into the center of the phone screen. I then held the protector above the phone so that it would make contact with the liquid center first and then pull the liquid along the surface. This seemed to work well except for a few tiny air bubbles at the bottom of the screen where there wasn't enough solution. Mostly a success... or so I thought. I took the squeegee and attempted to pull the solution toward the bottom of the screen, removing the air bubbles in the process. The squeegee is rubber and the protector is also rubbery, so there was a lot of resistance. I managed to get all but one air bubble out, and while I was sliding the squeegee across the top of the screen, it caught the protector in such a way that it gripped the surface and actually stretched the area it was touching, creating permanent large bubbles where the protector could no longer make contact with the phone screen.

- Attempt 3 - My last screen protector. I repeated my steps with attempt #2, but this time I used all of the remaining liquid in hopes that the air bubbles wouldn't be created this time and I wouldn't have to use the squeegee except to remove excess moisture. It seemed to work ok. The screen protector was positioned properly on my phone, and it looked like this time it was going to work. Then it came time to dry... Per Step 7 of the instructions included in this package, "Use your palms to hold down the edges for a few minutes at a time. If the edges still do not stick, wait a few more minutes and try again." ...what? Step 8 - "Allow a few hours for the protector to set and cure completely." At any point within a few hours, this screen protector may begin to peel away from the phone and has to be pressed back into place or else it won't stick properly. The screen is curved. How was this ever supposed to work?

This protector did not work for me. If you think you can manage it, it's a rather cheap experiment and a self-healing screen protector sounds great. After all, I may just not understand something fundamental in applying these. Some other reviewers have had great success with it. I won't be asking for a refund for that reason. Regardless, I won't be buying this again.

Even with both of these it’s less bulky than similar options I’ve owned. Plus, the outer edges of the face are shaped so they will make contact with the floor before the screen hits if you drop it.

My only complaint is that the hard rubber case fits over the power switch, which is added protection, but it’s hard to press the button all the way down. I have to focus and use extra force to get it to depress. I’m hoping it will soften a bit with use.

title: Tech Armor does a great job
text: Awesome "glass" protector so far. If I ever drop my phone and have to truly test this I hope I can make this a five star rating. With so many out there, how do you know which to choose?  I have a 5S and this fit perfectly. Not a bit smaller like some, which I thought would be helpful with the case question, but not really a problem.  I've purchased Tech Armor before and went with my gut. I do not have one spec of dust, no bubbles or any issues. Their application video was nothing new, I went with a different method learned online.  Use the "hinge" method - place the protector with the good side down (temporary plastic still in place) and place exactly where you want it. Then cut a dust strip in half and create "hinges" on one side. Fold it back, give the cleaned screen a final swipe then peel the protective layer. Fold it back over gently, press and smooth. Works every time. Once smoothed, gently remove the dust strips while holding down the protector. I did have an odd "bubble" in the middle that I thought was the glass adhesive but as I carefully smoothed it I was able to move the bubble to the edge. Gone!  The glass is perfect! Barely a fingerprint can be seen, and it wipes clean so easily! The fingerprint sensor works perfectly. Don't use the provided "home" buttons with your 5S. The whole package was impressive and so is this protector. Wish I had done this before wasting money on a regular screen protector. Feel much more confident in the protection of my phone now.

text:
The screen protector installed really easily and has a perfect fit! I was shocked that on my first attempt there were absolutely no bubbles and you can barely even tell the screen protector is there.

Install procedure: Install the screen protector in the bathroom (I have heard there is less lint/dust in the air there). Take the screen cloth (provided) and wipe the screen for a good 30 seconds. Even if the screen looks clean, keep wiping to make sure there is absolutely no oil or dust on the screen. Then take the dust remover sticker (provided) and use it to pick up any possible particles on every inch of the screen. This is a little bit of a pain, but only takes a minute to do the whole screen. Now remove the film on the cover and install it carefully in place. I used this procedure and it installed perfectly in about 5 minutes total.

Finally, the seller provided excellent customer service too. My original protector was damaged, but after a few quick emails the same day, they shipped me out a new one. I received the new one in perfect condition just 3 days later. Excellent all around!

title: Metal section on back does not stick well enough to any magnetic dash mount
text:
My Moto G7 works great in this case, love the looks and protection it offers.

An important function of my phone is the ability to stick to my magnetic dash mount.
This case does not do that - the connection is weak, so small vibrations will make the phone move around and fall off.

The metal disk on the back looks like it would works but it does not.
Tried it in 3 different magnetic mounts I have access to - all had the same problem

My theory is that most dash mounts rely on a larger surface area of metal on the phone case to connect to. The metal plate that came with my latest mount (Scosche) is almost 4 square inches while the metal disk on this phone is only about one square inch.

Currently looking for a small magnet to glue to my dash mount that would be slightly more focused on the small area of my phone metal disk see if it would hold better - hack some glue and we are good to go. If I can't find anything, I may have to go with a different case that either has a larger chunk of metal or a thinner case so I can use the metal plate that came with my mount. Not as much protection but will work with my dash mount.

text:
I randomly found this looking for charging accessories for my family's growing list of electronic devices. These usually go for 20 bucks before any discounts. I have ordered three, but only 1 has arrived yet. I live in Hawaii and Amazon shipping takes a little longer to get to the islands. Anyways, this device has already powered my Dell Latitude 5510 and will easily charge my Moto G100 and Pixel 6A. There was mention of more heat by other commenters, and I have observed that but should be expected from a smaller GAN device with a higher output that standard chargers.

EDIT: I just ordered the 67W single port version while the price was 8.99 before tax. These prices are great compared to the next best reviewed charger with similar specs. As of 11-02-2022, most of the items are unavailable. I ordered three of the dual port 65W chargers and one single port 67W charger. good to have on hand to charge all the devices I have at home with a family of 5.

EDIT (11-25-2022): I bought some more for family. Price dropped even more, not even made I paid what I paid earlier in the year. This is a great deal. I just had a first gen anker charger have a port go bad, so I decided I needed more of the GAN chargers to slowly replace my hardware. Nothing lasts forever. The PD usb c port will charge the new 9th gen ipad, which I also got on sale, at the max charging wattage of 30w. I don't know why the stock ipad charger is only 20w. Also, i'm typing this review on my work laptop while it is plugged into the 67w single-port charger.

Update 12-12-2022 I checked back and noticed two new products, the 20W and a 33W charger. I already own a dual 20W (40W total GAN charger) from another brand, apparently it was a non-labelled anker copy. Therefore, I passed on the 20W but purchased the 33W charger. This will be helpful for my kids 8th and 9th generation iPads that can utilize up to 30W chargers. Will update once received, currently slated for January 2023 delivery on Oahu.
