title: Loving it so far
text:
I was waiting for the Pixel 5 which came out the same time. The 5 was $100 more ($699) than Amazon's price of S20 FE of $599 at release (*S20 FE now $699) with the 5 using processing power of a few generations back with smaller battery capacity - this was a no brainer choice and Google over priced their flagship (I understand their camera is generally good and updates faster/ui cleaner - but that's not making up for everything else especially considering competition from this phone and OnePlus among others).

It's still brand new so time will tell a lot more but the phone is snappy and my wifi & cell signal are faster than my Honor View 10 that's being replaced. I use T-mobile and not in a 5G area yet (but one is close by I'll be able to test). I attached a pic of my speed test info on cell network. The bottom 2 similar results are default with 5G enabled in the cellular settings and the top (fastest) results is with the second option of 4G LTE/3/2 enabled. I thankfully read a post to disable 5G if not in network for one. My old phone would only get 25 download on average so the S20 FE has blown that away even at its worst.

I took a photo in an average edge lit room of some colored items and a pic in a very low light room (any light coming in is from a room at least 10ft away). I'm blown away by the low light pic - I can't explain how well lit the pic is compared to what my eyes perceive.

The first day I spent my time uninstalling and disabling whatever I could that was pre-installed by Samsung and tweaked shortcuts & and new to me (Samsung specific) features I wanted. I used the recommended Smart Switch to transfer files from my old phone (namely apps, selected pics, and texts & call records) and I used my saved backup from my launcher (Nova) to bring back the app/screen organization I had customized on my old phone. Now I get to enjoy.

It does charge fast and no problems connecting to 2 different Bluetooth headsets.

*Update* I realized my original download speed pic was clipped wrong (showed a 2G wifi download speed instead of LTE) so I removed the old and uploaded correct pic (speed increase still stands).

I placed prices in as they've changed since I purchased.

You can choose to bring your screen refresh to 60 to help extend battery (defaults at 120 - I recommend scrolling feeds and testing both out in other scenarios to see if it's worth it for you). As always, to extend battery on any phone, control background apps and their access, lower your screen brightness when able and keep GPS, wifi, Bluetooth off when not needed. If your phone has bad reception in an area you spend a prolonged period of time in and you don't need to call/text, put your phone in airplane mode and turn wifi on after (if wifi available/needed).

title: Worst, Most Expensive Phone We've Ever Owned
text:
This "smart" phone does nothing without Internet. All that my wife wanted was a phone that would keep her calendar and events. I decided to buy her something a little better and purchase an Android. She cannot store calendar events on this phone because it requires Internet. No problem, we took it to wi-fi. The phone connects to the wi-fi network, but told us we needed a "data plan" to connect to Internet (btw, we are able to connect to Internet on our laptops over the same wi-fi network). So, I relented and paid for a data connection. After doing so the phone told us we needed wi-fi. It became apparent that the phone would not connect to Internet no matter what we did.

So, I having been a software engineer for over 20 years, figured there must be something wrong with current firmware. Sure enough, I found reports all over the web about people having problem with this model connecting and that the firmware should be upgraded. Samsung has a software called "Kies" that you download on to your computer and manage firmware, media, software etc on the phone. So, I downloaded the 70MB software from Samsung over our 3G network, 45 minutes. I ran the software (takes about 90 seconds to start), to be greeted by a prompt saying I needed to upgrade the software. I was a bit frustrated that Samsung didn't keep their site up to date, costing me another 45 minute, 70MB download.

So we got the new software which did confirm that the phone required a firmware update. Great! I thought. Now we're getting somewhere. Kies downloaded the firmware and crashed while leaving a topmost window on my desktop. Alt+Ctrl+Esc was the only way to remove that.

So the phone doesn't work, Samsung's update software doesn't work and there are 238,000 page matches on Google if you search for "Samsung Kies Crash". I've searched through many of them and tried the suggestions without result.

If you have $120 to throw away, send it my way, but avoid this absolutely worthless phone!!!

text: I bought this case before the iPhone 6 even came out.  It looked good, had dual layer protection, was raised around the screen, basically had everything I was looking for.  Almost a year later, and I still like it!  It still looks amazing, and it has withstood a few drops here and there, and my phone is still in one piece.  I liked it so much that I told other people at work about it and they bought a few as well.  I take it apart every now and then, blow the dust out and reassemble.  I also use an iMagnet car mount in my car, and have installed a disc between the rubber and the hard shell, and it works great......so good that it has never fallen off the mount!  Let's face it, it's designed for protection, so it does add some "beefyness", but you have to expect that.  It adds very little bulk to the phone.  I have no problems with charging cords, or headphone cords, and I have used some non-standard headphones as well, and they have all worked.  I have also used this case in my pocket while I am cutting grass on a riding and a push mower.  For what you pay for this, it is an outstanding value.  If you are thinking about it, you should give the Obliq Orange case a try.

text:
So I've had Google Pixel phones for the last 6 years and I was very hesitant to switch over to Samsung because I wasn't sure if I would adapt to their user interface.

After the initial setup I adapted very easily to their new user interface it has a lot of great features even more so than Google so I was very happy about that.
For a folding phone this is an amazing deal I got the refurbished phone with no physical issues.
No appearance scratches and whatever it was received pretty well.
Only thing when I turned on the phone to set it up it like kept restarting over and over again and I really couldn't do anything.

Eventually it updated and everything was pretty smooth after that.

Within a couple weeks I got the Samsung UI 4.1.1 with the Windows taskbar which is amazing switching between apps multitasking...

Battery life has been amazing even though this phone is refurbished so it doesn't have the full capacity of the battery it's still performs pretty well I'm able to get 15 hours so I can get through a day easily.

The camera is not the best but still does the job so I really have nothing to complain about when it comes to this phone I'm pretty happy with it and I do plan on upgrading to the fold 5 when that comes out and I can use this phone as a trade-in and probably get more than I paid for it so that's great.

title: Covers light sensor on XT1045 Moto G 4G LTE
text: I installed this screen protector on a Moto G XT1045 4G LTE.  I found that the screen protector covers the  oval sensor next to the ear piece that turns the screen off during a phone call when the phone is held close to the head.  If the sensor is covered by the screen protector, the phone's logic assumes the phone is near the head and shuts off the screen.  I cut a small notch in the screen protector before removing either of the protective films.  The sensor works fine now but the protector has an uneven edge where I cut it.  I think there is some variability in the sensitivity of the sensor and ambient lighting conditions can vary widely.  In a well lit area maybe the sensor can be covered by the screen protector yet work properly.  The screen protector is easy to install following the directions to the letter.  When installed the protector has a bit of a tacky feel to it compared on an unprotected screen but it is easy to get used to.  At $6 for 3 protectors, it's just a fair value considering the sensor issue.  I would give 5 stars if it was properly cut at the factory.

title: Good overall but disappointing kickstand
text:
I've owned many cellphone cases in the past from several different vendors, including several from Spigen. While still a good case, I find it a little disappointing overall.

The case fits and protects the S8 very well. The internal TPU rubber layer feels well made and the hard plastic exoskeleton provides good structure. The curved edge of the screen is not obstructed by the case, but the extra case material on the sides makes it much easier to hold on to without accidentally interacting with the screen. The front of the case extends far enough past the screen to ensure you can safely set the phone face down on a surface without scratching things up. All the port cut outs are where expected and there's a good amount of room around the headphone jack to ensure they can be plugged in nicely. Another nice feature is that the case does not interfere with any of the wireless Qi chargers I've tried.

The downside is the kickstand. Compared to other cases I've used with a kickstand it feels very flimsy. While it does lock closed, when open there's no tension spring to hold it in place. It just kinda flops around. This means if you move the phone while the kickstand is out, it likely folds in and the phone ends up falling over. Further, the stand is only able to hold the phone up horizontally, unlike some other designs I've tried which can do both vertical and horizontal.

Overall I'll live with it, but the kickstand feels like a waste on an otherwise decent case.

title: Suits my purpose:  phone for my offspring that won't make me broke
text: It's fairly compact and svelte for an elcheapo $27.00 phone.  Triple minutes, you can find the minutes cards almost anywhere and, if you can't, you can purchase minutes online at the Tracfone website.  Clear, vibrant, sharp display screen.  Quick response to icons.  Exception:  Surfing on this is abysmal due to browser given and performance but that's perfect as I don't want my son wasting minutes surfing.  Has a slot for a MicroSD card.  They give you a 2GB MicroSD card as a freebie but I'd pump it up to at least 32GB if you want to turn this into an MP3 player.  I transferred my son's old T-Mobile phone number to this phone on a Saturday and the process was fairly straightforward.  They (Tracfone) ask a lot of nosy questions - really.  My address I can understand if there was loss or theft of the phone.  My email address - I said "no".  They had the nerve to ask for the last 4 of my SSN.  I said no way.  Things proceeded anyway.  Phone number was transferred within 4 hours.  You just power off and power back on and there ya go.  When they prompt for "activation" it's kind of a misnomer.  What they really meant in my case was "Add Airtime Minutes" which I did.  A $39.95 200 minute card became 600 minutes due to the Triple minutes.  This is what I wanted as, while I liked T-Mobile it is very difficult to get enough "talking" minutes from them under $50.00 a month.  Yeah they (T-Mobile) and Walmart sell a lesser known (semi-hidden!) $30.00 per month service but it didn't meet our needs.  This is my speed.  If you don't use your minutes you have (I think) 90 days before they expire.  On my personal tracfone, I can get through an entire year by buying maybe 3, 120 minute cards ($29.95) that get tripled to 360 minutes.  So...geez...for a years worth of mobile phone, I pay around $90-$100 dollars.  If web surfing is not your focus, then I can recommend this phone.  Can't beat it.

The silver ring that goes around the ball stood straight up, making it impossible to roll the ball so I had to use my old one. The tool they send with the kit only undoes the screws on the back of the phone, not the ones on the front that you have to take out to replace the trackball plate.
I may have just put it together awkwardly, but my X, C and 0 button are all connected. When I hit one button, it pushes all three. That might have been my mistake, I will find out tonight when I take it apart to take the screen cover off the back side of the screen. I didn't realize that there was a cover over it and it's driving me crazy. Also, there is sticky glue/tape around the frame of the screen so once you stick the face plate on it's hard to get it back up. It lifted my whole plasma screen up with it and almost ruined it.

title: Sticks well, but the screen becomes less crisp
text:
The installation requires some techniques. I watched the video very carefully before starting the process. To ensure the edge glue on tightly, I found that using the wedge came in the kit to scrape the edge from top to bottom multiple times over a few hours is easier than the palm technique recommended. So far it has been sticking well. With the phone case the edge would not be touched and lifted even when I use the task edge function very often. However, there are a few issues: the glue under the sheet is not the most even coating in the world. This microscopic unevenness causes the screen to be much less crisp. I can see the RGB of pixels all over the screen. I am seeing stripes for the areas where the glue is less even. Also, if you push too hard with the wedge trying to remove the bubbles, it makes indentations that would not go away. This is fortunately not visible when the screen is on.

If you are crazy about the crispness of the screen, don't buy this. If you are fine with small imperfections and are good at following instructions, this is something I think is worth trying. I wonder how easy is it to remove this and the glue from screen if the film needs to be replaced.

Update 7/26/2019: After using for 9 months, I finally couldn't take the horrible clarity and dents from this screen protector anymore. I decided to peel it off and buy another type of protector. Before I peeled it off, the edge of the protector still held very well. It was surprisingly easy to peel off with no residue. No struggle at all.

title: A definite winner for the iPhone 6!
text:
I've had this case now for a little over a week and I have to say I'm pleasantly surprised. I've been a loyal Otterbox drone for the past several years, dutifully getting a Commuter or Defender every year or two. However, I had a couple issues with two different cases with them (iPhone 5 and iPad) where the soft plastic was falling apart, so finally decided to break free and try something else......

I never heard of New Trent before, but that's part of the fun of Amazon!! This is a VERY high quality case. It fits well, offers great shock protection. It's a dual layer case, so you get the soft plastic that covers the sides and back of the phone, and the other layer is a harder plastic which is also on the sides and is the clear cover for the front. Looks great too - nice translucent look. Some cases on Amazon have great reviews and I was very tempted to get them, but they obscure the entire back of the phone. Call me superficial, but I like to see the Apple logo and the stylish back of the phone.

There's the added bonus of the different color cover that you can swap out. Jealous of your friend with the white iPhone? You can make yours look "just" like it.

Word of warning, the fingerprint scanner has a cover too. Just remember that, it's not just packaging material... I almost removed it when I opened the box! It works great too, haven't had any issues with my fingerprint scanning which was a concern of mine before since there's a barrier now between the sensor. There's two flip covers on the bottom for the headphone jack and charging port. Saves them from dust / misc buildup which is nice.

Highly recommended!!

title: Clear gel-like phone case that has wallet slot but not much phone protection
text:
This is a review for Kedoo's iPhone SE case with a wallet slot. The case is made from a thermoplastic polyurethane that really feels like a flexible gel-like substance, to me. It fits the phone really well, and the material allows the phone to have some of the best spaces for phone features like the volume and power buttons. There are even holes in the bottom of the phone case where the phone's audio comes out. Many other smartphone cases simply cover up the speakers and cause the audio to come out muffled.

As shown in the picture, the phone case also has a wallet slot so that you can put whatever card you may need to carry around with you. It's great for personal identification, a credit card, or even a Costco card if you frequently buy in bulk. This feature is a really nice addition to the standard phone case, especially for those of us that might forget ID cards or public transportation cards.

The one thing that I dislike about this case is that I don't feel it's very sturdy. Because of the flexibilty of the gel-like case, I don't think the case is going to do much to save my phone it takes a serious tumble from my hands or off a table. The description says that it provides protection from scratches and dents, and that may be true for the frame around the phone or its back. This case won't protect your phone from the internal system damage that results from the shock of a significant drop of the phone. I'll keep looking for a shockproof case that has the wallet slot feature. I like that component of this case, but don't think this one will serve me in every day usage.

text: I received my case today in good condition and like the other reviews I am satisfied for the most part. I would prefer Otter Box Defender case but there isn't one for Moto G4. The case is comprised of semi soft parts and hard plastic. The sides of the case have a rubbery texture that is rather hard not soft while the back and face plate are a very hard plastic. IT IS A BIG CASE so be forewarned. I have a tempered screen protector and it fit snugly in the case with no issues. Recommendation of you are interested in a cheap Otter Box knock off I recommend this case. Upon using this device now for a mere day and a half I have to change my rating.  This is a dual purpose case. It is meant for both the G4 and G4 Plus therefore it has a fingerprint button cutout to accommodate G4 plus. This allows a Lot of dust into the case on the standard G4. Further the cover for the plug port does not stay closed allowing debris and dust to enter port not to mention the is a protrusion on the cover that is very uncomfortable when holding phone one handed. title: Perfect fit, perfect and clarity
text:
This case is an excellent fit doesn’t add a lot of bulk. So far I haven’t had any yellowing issues with the case and my gold iphone continues to shine through just as it did on day one.

One minor detail that I’m happy about is that there is a tiny lip on the back of the case. Clear cases often get scratched over time on the back. This lip prevents the back of the case from directly touching the table or whatever flat surface it might be resting on so you shouldn’t have to worry about it sliding around and getting scuffed.

There is also a lip on the front so if you place the phone face down the screen won’t touch the table. This is also true if using a screen protector. With that in mind this case should be compatible with pretty much any screen protector.

Buttons are still easy to press, speaker cutouts are precise and the lighting port cutout allows for easy cable access although other than CarPlay. I use wireless charging which works fine with this case.

I do have the Apple wallet and while I’ve never tried the oem apple case. I can say that the magnet strength is on par with that of the phone without a case.

All in all I’m happy with this purchase

title: Great for switching devices
text:
So far I've used the nano to micro-sim adapter and nano to full size adapter.

For testing purposes. I've also tried the nano to micro sim adapter inside the micro to full size adapter. Confusing right? Well this part was just for testing for anyone who may have a micro sim wanting to go full size.

At any rate I've had zero issues using this in an iPhone 4S, OnePlus One, Alcatel basic phone, etc.. All different size sims.

While there isn't any adhesive. By design your sim snaps into this accessory. I've yet to experience any issues with it falling out.

For those who've had issues I'd bet it's one of two things in most situations. 1) They either made their own nano sim which was slightly too small so it doesn't snap in. These things are precise so if you cut your own nano sim the slightest bit off. It'd fit in the iPhone tray but you can have issues here. 2) Their phone has an awkward location for sim. In an alcatel I own. The full size sim slides in the device from under the battery. You of course need to slide the sim out rather then try to lift with your fingers and bend. if you bend of course it'll fall out.

Great adapter. Go for it.

I went to this phone which should work even if put in a fish bowl like on Youtube. No fishbowl tests, but life happens and things can get wet somehow. I've had it a month, still working. Battery life is okay, charge it once a day and don't leave any apps running that aren't needed. Use free wifi at all times. Battery life as others have noted is less than one wishes. (it does charge fast) A huge 3600amh battery is available for $90.

The sim card and the mini SD card go inside a nearly the same spot. A bit confusing and a small struggle to get them in with the battery. Look at the instructions closely, watch Youtube videos to get it right.

my S4mini dual would pick up a weak atnt signal in locations that the Sony does not at all, ... don't know why. Sony has same frequencies and 4glite. But the S4mini did a better job for me.
Camera is okay. Controls are a learning curve for me.
I like the physical keys on the S4mini for Back, Home etc, rather than the electronic image keys. That's me.
The waterproof/resistant feature is the major selling point given that the phone performs like other android phones by making phone calls and some internet activity. BUT this water repellency will go away as soon as the usb and/or headphone Jack covers break off. So I've purchased the charger and bluetooth headphones so that I don't keep messing with those covers and eventually break them off. (another $100) (By this time I've spent enough $ to justify buying a samsung Active... mmmm) But the Active is physically large in my pocket which I was trying to avoid. Tough to find the perfect phone.

The remote charger cradle runs $60 when other Sony Experia phones run half that or less. mmm not nice
I bought my charger from ebay and HK to save on cost. It's working great, still was $40.

The curve of the Sony is nice in the hand. It's lightweight and has bright clear colors. Volume and on/off on the same side is good, like it.
The phone is fine, still working after daily use of a month (it should be right?) and it's suppose to be water resistant.
I recommend it ... my logic is to avoid opening covers, and to use the charger and blue tooth.

title: Acevan to the rescue?
text:
My old battery would die at 15-55% and wouldn't charge to a full %100 most of the time.

I tried all of the tricks and apps to try to save my battery. I avoided major updates at some point, then tried them. I bought cheap replacement batteries from Ebay ($3-$5) and they did the same thing. Died at 35% and the batteries all drained to those percentages after 1-4hrs of use.
I thought there was something wrong with the hardware in my phone since none of these batteries were working, until I found a forum saying for sure that it is a battery problem, not a software or hardware issue in the phone itself.

I decided to try one more time before I gave up on my trusty Note 4. I decided to spend a bit (wow an extra $10 lol) more on a battery this time and came across this one. It had so many positive reviews. I also bought one for a similar price on Ebay as well, that supposedly was an original Samsung Note 4 battery and came with an external Samsung charger.

They both work wonderfully! I finally have a normal phone! Omg this is great. I spent over 1 yr with a crappy battery and wish I did this sooner.
Now my phone doesn't die for 12hrs of regular usage. If I'm online and browsing on it and listening to music, its still good for 5+ hrs before it needs a charge, which is fairly regular. If I had the internet and location off, I know this would last up to 2+days without needing a charge.

Overall I'm happy. I've had this product for almost 2 months now and so far I'm glad. I don't know how long it will last but I'm glad I can just take off the back of my phone and switch the battery when issues like this arise. I won't be switching from the note 4 yet.

title: Decent Gimbal with Some Quality Issues...
text:
I'll start by saying that the gimbal controls are all really solid. The app is also pretty decent, and it DOES do the job it's designed to do.

My problem is that the construction quality isn't made to last at all. The screw meant to tighten the main arm of the gimbal and keep it in its collapsed form doesn't really do anything on mine. The gimbal does stay extended during use, however, so I didn't think much of it. Then, just after the return period for this gimbal expired, the gimbal arm actually slid off the track entirely. Looking closer, I noticed the connection holding the arm on the track had been widening over time (shown in the picture here).

I was able to get the arm back on to the gimbal base, and the gimbal does still work despite having been in two pieces, but I wouldn't recommend someone who plans to use this regularly invest in it (I was using it to vlog a road trip, for example). I'm just waiting for mine to fully fail now, and I do wish I'd returned it when I first noticed the tightening screw doesn't work.

title: Great case for everyday use, enabled my phone to be undamaged in a drop.
text:
I can tell you this case has been drop tested by me. I was at Disney with my 6 day old IPhone7, having had this case for a total of 2 days, and tripped on a curb, dropping my phone to the concrete. I watched as it hit on a corner of the case, then bounced to land screen down on the pavement. Thankfully there were no rocks sticking up, and my phone and screen survived unscratched, still in new condition. Now the case did get 2 minor scratches on it, but because it's white and the plastic is not super hard I basically just rubbed it a bit and the scratches to the case became invisible.
I can now say for certain that this case will do the job and even protect your screen in a fall, as long as when it drops screen down you're lucky like I was and it's on a flat surface.
The case, has great shock protection, and is smooth enough to make removal from a pocket easy, but not slippery. It isn't a bulky case so won't add a lot of size to your phone. I would recommend this case to anyone looking for everyday phone protection.

Bottom line: excellent phone. Its display is bright, clear, and large. The front facing dual audio speakers are unbelievable. The WiFi connection is much improved over my last phone. And the best thing is you get Android updates. I got two when I first got the phone (which is normal to update the firmware initially) but I also just got another security update the other day. My other phones (and I'm not going to mention brands) rarely updated (if they updated at all). This phone has no bloatware so it is very fast. I had no issues pairing this phone to my car. Took only a minute or two to accomplish.
I was deciding between several new phones including OnePlus 3, ZTE Axon 7, the new Zenfone and about a half a dozen more. They are all probably good phones but so is this one and I know I will get firmware updates and get them quickly. Also, there are a zillion accessories available for the 6P.
Now to the size. I was concerned about a 5.7" display phone but it is no issue whatsoever for me. If you have very small hands, it might be but it is personal preference. The phone is tall and not that wide so it is easy to hold. The phone is not heavy at all. In fact, it was surprising light for me; not feather light but certainly not even a slight concern.
The Nexus 6P is a keeper!

title: Sharp edges / otherwise good.
text:
First off this case was made in such a way that it is practically fused with my phone. I don't think it will slide off the corners in my pocket like my old (Bodyglove) case did on my nexus 4. The buttons are significantly harder to press with the case on but that just means I want accidentally turn the screen off for sure.

Now the con's. This case has extremely small sharp edges all the way around it. The case goes off the screen as mate then turns angles and goes shiny then turns angles again and goes mate finished again over the buttons. It is at this second transition from shiny to mate where the molding is a lil off I guess and it makes a sharp edge all the way around the phone. Also if you, like I do, ever hold your phone in portrait mode and use our pinky finger to support the bottom where the charger port is you will find more unpleasant shapeness around the edges of the opening. The charger port edges just a sharp 90° angle and also a molding issue like with the perimeter of the phone cases bezzel.

Overall my phone feels safe from a buffalo stamped and from the explosion of a small thermonuclear detonation. The sharp edges aren't a deal breaker but for the price Supcase should be a little more stringent on tolerance in the molding of the case. Also there should be more attention to the beveling of the razor sharp edge at the charger port.

title: I really want to love this phone, but...
text:
When my G1 died, I upgraded to the Vibrant. The honeymoon was short, but breathtaking. Slim, light, big and brilliant AMOLED screen, fast, seven home screens, Bluetooth stereo, a virtual keypad that made me forget the G1's slider, and Swipe! I had doubts about Swipe, but I quickly got the hang of it. You gotta try this!

The Vibrant promises to be all that a smartphone can be wrapped in a stylish and comfortable package. Memory, both on-board and flashcard, is staggeringly huge. Running a lot of background apps doesn't seem to slow it down. Coverage where I live and travel is good, but the G1 seemed to have a better antenna.

Problems surfaced. Battery life running background apps is a disappointment. I installed System Panel and now monitor and kill some apps when working unplugged. I tried to use GPS without success. Several reviews noted the same thing, along with magnetic compass problems. There's a fix promised with the release of 2.2 next month. Mounting the phone via USB to my PC is a nightmare. It seems confused about whether it's connected to a computer when I plug in the charger, resulting in aberrant touch screen behavior and a constantly flashing message, "USB connected" whether the phone is plugged into anything. Turning off the screen sends it into a coma requiring roboot. I need to call customer service to work this one out.

The docking accessories announced by Samsung earlier this month are unavailable. Production problems? Last-minute bugs? Vaporware?

So the jury is still out. I hope I can revise this review up to what should be an unqualified 5 stars. All things considered, I really want to love this phone, and as the man says, "Love is patient..." Up to a point.

title: Great Screen Protector!! SPIGEN FOR THE WIN!!!
text:
I've become a super fan of Spigen products. I've used Spigen cases for several iPhones. I'm always impressed at how well they fit, how good they look great, and most of all, the level of protection they give my phone. I decided to try the Spigen glass screen protector. This glass screen protector is probably the easiest to install I've ever worked with. Putting the little flaps at each end of the glass made it REALLY EASY to position the sheet before installing it, making it easy to get a perfect cutout alignment on the first try.

It's really amazing to watch the sheet literally adhere itself to the phone screen. If you really cleaned the screen carefully before installing the sheet, you're literally done with the process once the sheet has adhered itself to the screen. Just give it a couple more wipes with the cleaning cloth and you're done. In fact, I didn't even have to open the supplied cleaning materials for picking up dust particles.

title: Not sure what more I could ask
text:
If I didn't know I'd replaced it, I wouldn't know I'd replaced it. I can't think of higher praise than that.

It's not a hard job, but there are bunches of youtube vids showing you how to do it - suggest watching a couple first.

Two tips:

There are little clips around the assembly. When you are putting the new one in, I found that I had to engage the left side with the upper screw first, then engage the right side clips. I pushed a little with the plastic tool that comes with this part to get one of the right-side clips to pop in.

Also - there is a little square gasket on the underside of the lens cover. It's slightly sticky, so the part that will go around the actual lens has a piece of clear plastic with a little tab that you must first pull off. When I pulled mine off, the gasket came WITH the clear plastic piece. Getting it aligned properly again was probably the hardest part of the job. So try to make the gasket stay with the replacement part when you pull off that clear plastic.

There is also plastic covering over the glass on the outside of the phone. This isn't super obvious, but make sure you get it off or your pictures aren't going to be so good.

Despite my couple of little hurdles, it took me almost exactly 10 minutes start to finish.

The case is thin and does not add any more thickness to the S5 than other 2-piece cases with screen covers.

title: Microphone holes fixed for Verizon, Great Case but a little Slippery!
text:
The Spigen Slim Armor at first glance appears to be a very nicely built case. The fit to the device (Galaxy Note 4) is excellent and I had no problem installing it. Much easier than the slightly finnicky install of the Neo Hybrid on my Galaxy Note 3. First point to make is that it appears Spigen has addressed the variance in mic position across US carriers, as my case received today has slots in place of the small holes for the bottom microphones. All other mic and sensor locations appear to be spot-on as well.

I like the flush-feeling buttons but they aren't easy to find in the dark or maybe I'm just not used to it yet. The buttons function very smoothly with no problems. I do like that the case has a continuous profile all the way around, it's a very clean look. My main concern and the only reason I rated 4 stars instead of 5 is that the hardshell portion of the case is quite slick. I am concerned that I may drop the phone and hope I'll get used to the slick feeling. Good news is that the TPU/rubber around the perimeter is quite thick at 3.0-3.2mm. It should handle edge falls relatively well. Down-side of this is that it does add a bit of bulk to the phone and brings the slightly slimmer (across the phone) Note 4 back to feeling about like a Note 3 with a standard TPU case when holding it in-hand for a call.

Some have complained that the heart sensor does not work well with this case. I find about a 75% success rate when using the heart rate sensor with a light touch or with my finger slightly sideways. Not as convenient as when case-less but still reasonable for me personally.

I look forward to putting this case to daily use and hope it holds up well. I would have preferred a black or matte black version but the only other dark alternative was slate. I chose the "Shimmery White" which is a somewhat iridescent white or pearl type color. It looks quite good with the black phone but if the function of the case and protection prove themselves, I may give another color a try. I would like to check out a Neo Hybrid for the Note 4 as it was a very slim and trim package on my Note 3.

title: P.O.S
text: I have good and bad review and you will know why I gave 2 stars (generous). I was looking to replace my two year old Pebble Steel which is starting to give some problems. The Pebble was great watch, but lasting only two years is not acceptable. It did everything I wanted from a smart watch. So after seeing many reviews of many different watches, this Zenwatch seemed to be getting good reviews and the cost was acceptable. Took me awhile to connect to my Iphone 6 and figure out how to operate the watch. The instruction was useless. My 10 year old quickly figure out the operation and taught me and connected to my Iphone. The most important feature I wanted was to receive in-calls, and text messages. I really careless about other features. I wanted to be able to receive vibration, especially when I am surrounded in a crowded and noisy place since I will not hear the call. The vibration on Pebble was great! You can really feel the vibration. The Zenwatch is just okay. You can feel better if the watch is somewhat loosely fit on your wrist. But not that great. The Pebble watch has many faces you can choose from. Mostly more conservative faces which I like. The Zenwatch does not have many choices and mostly colorful and too "flashy". Does not look elegant as you see in their advertisement. Very childish designs. And the band. NO choices at all. Comes in brown color or tan, I think. I got the brown one. I do not like leather, I get itchy when I wear it for a long time. I like rubbery or metal bands. The watch itself is very light and feels like a toy. The Pebble watch felt solid. During the daytime, you can barely see the screen. You need to get into shade to see, even at the highest light level. The Pebble had no problem. I could see it clearly in the daytime. So why not buying another Pebble watch? I read somewhere that Pebble is bought up by Fitbit and the support for Pebble watch is no longer available. So I researched for replacement and ended up with Zenwatch3. I was thinking about Zenwatch 2 because I like the square shape. NOW, the reason for 2 stars. I wore this watch for 3 days and the strap broke. They use a plastic piece which is attached to the strap to connect to the watch. Yes, a plastic piece. Ordinary watches do not have this. It is usually the leather band is attached to the watch with pin. The metal straps and rubber straps are same too. But strangely, Zenwatch has this small black plastic piece. I think they made this so nobody else can make a strap to fit to the Zenwatch. I do not know what happened but when I remove the strap to show the watch to a friend, the strap came off from the watch and I almost dropped the watch. I contacted Asus, the maker, for warranty replacement. I was told that this "repair" is not covered by warranty and would cost me $85. This does not include shipping costs. Seriously? Only to replace one strap which could have been defective would cost me $85+? All of the companies I dealt with warranty replacement  in the past never gave me this kind of treatment. I only asked to replace one strap, which broke from a watch I wore for 3 days. A simple replacement. This company does not stand on their product's quality. Giving me this type of treatment for a one strap? I just wanted to vent out my frustration. What if I dropped the watch and broke it due to faulty strap? Just unbelievable. I would not buy from a company who does not stand on their product and instead gives a customer a hard time.

Finally, a phone holder that works for me! I've tried the vent style mounts in the past, but either due to my vent slats and/or Jeep's bumpy ride, my phone would, more often than not, dislodge and spend more time on the floor than in sight. The phone holder itself has easy to adjust side brackets that hold my device securely and easily release by just tilting the plate downward.
I took some photos with an older, smaller phone to give you an idea of how it looks, but I'm using this holder with a much larger Samsung Note 10 plus and fit wasn't a problem even with a phone case. I should also mention that I drive a manual and this holder did not get in the way of my shifting. But as a suggestion check out the location of your vehicle's drink holders to make sure placement is safe and convenient for your use.
Bottom line, I recommend giving this holder a try especially, if like me, you've had issues with the vent mount models keeping your phone safely in place. Thank you for letting me share my thoughts with you and I hope that my experience, along with the photos, help a bit in deciding what's best for you. I think you'll enjoy it as much as I am!

text:
Bought the phone after looking closely at Wal-Mart, Target, Windows Store and AT&T Store.
I got an excellent price from Amazon -- $60 plus tax -- and then AT&T charged me $40 on top of that... presumably for the included mini-SIM card and the customer service to change my account over to the new phone.

The phone arrived from Amazon just two days after my order. I've had it now for about a month and I'm very impressed. This is the nicest phone I've owned and I've been an AT&T customer for over 15 years now.

The HD screen is excellent and the sound is amazing -- stunning really -- on phone calls and for music. But the best thing about this phone is the speed at which it does everything. Indeed, it's so fast that it takes time to get used to it. The camera is the fastest phone camera I've seen and takes really great shots, and I say this as a Galaxy owner who's taken award-winning pics with my phone. But this new phone is, in a word, AWESOME.

HTC's build quality is second to none. It's a big phone with a big screen and big sound, but nothing about it is too big. It's just about right on all fronts. The professional reviewers love this phone and I can see why. It feels great, it looks great, it performs better than all the other phones and there's a ton of accessories available.

Amazon has good prices on micro SD cards, so definitely take advantage of the fact that this phone's storage space can be greatly expanded so you'll NEVER run out of space for photos, music, apps, etc. Also, the battery appears to have excellent properties. It doesn't get hot. It lasts for at least 2 days with heavy use. It charges quickly and there's a turbo charger accessory available if you want that feature.

No matter how you use your phone, you'll love this One from HTC.

title: It's good but the packaging is misleading
text: These are good cheap screen protectors, but I seriously doubt they're actually a 9 on the Moh's Hardness scale. (Nowadays, most flagship phones are equipped with Gorilla Glass, which scratches at a level 6, with deeper scratches appearing at 7.) This screen protector is made with tempered glass. Tempered glass is produced by sandwitching sheets of glass and plastic together in order to form a toughened material that, instead of completely shattering, handles impact with long, straight lines, as opposed to tiny shards. If you want a basic screen protector to withstand scratches and maybe impact from say, dropping your phone waist-height, I would recommend this screen protector, but I would definitely pair it with a good case that absorbs shock and has a raised lip around the front bezels of the phone. However, the product packaging is definitely misleading. They're decent for the price you're paying, but just be aware that you're not getting a major steal on them. They're tempered glass screen protectors that will aid in preventing scratches and screen damage, but not serious impact or pressure. It's less durable than your phone's built-in screen, but any protection is better than no protection. Because the price is pretty good and the product is pretty solid, I will be repurchasing, but I would definitely be wary of any product that claims to be that high up on the Moh's scale, since 90% of the time it's just not true.

2. It has a hole for the speaker. This was something I didnt appreciate until I tried watching Netflix in the first case I had with a muffled sound. Also ring is louder and clearer now.
3. The color is a true pink and the case looks and feel rich.
4. Soft lining inside the cover so I don't have to worry about getting the screen scratched.
5. Earphone jack not covered when closed. (The charger jack is covered but i simply bend the case to the back when it's time to charge.

Overall, I like the case and will keep it. As I said, the model number might make the difference as to why the molded sides so not fold over enough that I would feel 100%
secured if it fell but the it works well for the day to day routine

text: This case fits my iPhone 6 with a Pong thin case and a glass screen protector perfectly. I mean it’s like military-grade strong, and my old case's plastic clip just broke off when I sat down in my car (not a very tough test, in my opinion).  Won’t be a problem with this one!  Also, the clip will rotate and can be removed if you rotate the case to the upside-down horizontal position (so it won’t just come off accidentally).  The nice thing, to me, is that the iPhone 6 with slim case and glass screen protector fits just right, not too tight, and there is a little finger hole at the bottom of the case that allows you to push up the phone after you open the case, so that you can retrieve it quickly and easily.  I really had to tug my phone from my old case, using two hands, and often missed calls while trying to retrieve it.  Yes, this case costs a little more, but it will last (and is upwardly compatible with newer iPhone models).  And it’s made in the USA.

title: I didn't expect it to work, but it does.
text: I am very surprised.  This phone holder actually works pretty well.  I have a Speck candy shell grip case so the magnet doesn't hold directly to the case, which reduces the strength a little, but as long as I'm not off-roading it still holds my iPhone 6+.  It came with two magnets (one with tape) and I threw the extra in my wife's phone case non-plus iPhone 6, and it holds well too.  Now we can suspend either phone.  I almost gave it 4 stars because it doesn't give a 100% hold on my big phone in a thick case, but it can't account for that and since the force of the magnetic attraction decreases by the square of the radius, thick cases or rubber grips on the outside of the case will dramatically reduce attractive force.  I wouldn't recommend this holder for anyone with a thick case, but it's surprisingly good for thin cases, even with heavy phones.

I had no trouble removing 4 links to adjust it to my skinny wrists, but I have some experience with this procedure. The included instructions are poor, but there are tons of instructions that can be easily found online that can be applied here.

The weak point of the bracelet appears to be the clasp. I don't know if I fully trust the clasp - it seems to open a little too easily with just the slightest pressure on the mechanism. But I haven't had any accidental releases yet.

I'm worried about the black finish and if I will hold up. So far, so good, and the finish looks great out of the box. I wouldn't mind if it wore off a little bit, but if the entire things starts turning silver, that wouldn't be good! Only time will tell.

The bracelet seems like an inexpensive way to make your Apple Watch stand out and also give it a more professional appearance. For now, I'm very happy with the purchase.

title: Mostly works. But there are some problems with it.
text:
After using it for about a week, here are my thoughts:

The Good:
- Seems to charge pretty fast.
- Battery lasts a decent amount of time.
- Easy to pair it to my iPad.

The Meh:
- Sound quality is acceptable, but not great. The higher tones seem to be a little bit more pronounced than the low tones, which can have a voice-shrill effect when listening to higher pitched voices.

The Bad:
- Whenever the device is connected-to or disconnected-from the charger, it will automatically turn on and attempt to connect to any paired device. This can inadvertently cause other BT headsets to be automatically disconnected from the device when the LEZII powers on by itself.
- If you "long-press" the device to turn it off, it will first do a "skip track" operation before the device turns off. This causes whatever you're watching to skip to the next program. This is very inconvenient. If I am turning off the LEZII to charge them and switch to a different headset, it causes me to have to manually go back and select the previous thing I had been listening to.

The Disgusting:
- Inside the packaging, there was a small note from the manufacturer, saying that they would send me a second device for free, if I were to make a "good review" of the product and link to it. I have more respect for myself than to falsely make a glowing-review in order to receive free product. Please keep this in mind as you read other reviews of this product -- they may be influenced by this offer.

All in all, it works, but had I known about the drawbacks ahead of time, I would have chosen a different brand.

title: Nicely built, not as ergonomically friendly
text:
I purchased this as a replacement case after the Bear Motion Premium Polio Case that I'd originally purchased began to fray and wear out.

First off, quality of materials is very nice and it is solidly built. Stitching looks nice, the interior contrast fabric is a nice surprise, and the wrist strap and accessories make this a really great deal.

I deducted two stars from my review because of a few flaws/issues I've found. First, the flap to keep the wallet shut folds into the back so I often find myself opening my phone case upside down (intuitively, I want this flap at the front of the phone).

Second, folding the front flap back on itself to hold the phone in one hand (but not book style) is difficult - I assume the leather will soften over time and this will become easier but I have had a couple instances where I lost grip when the cover wanted to flap closed.

Third, the credit card holders are deep (a problem I had with the Bear Motion as well) making it difficult to pull out your card as it tends to slip towards the bottom. The fabric has also stretched a little, so if the wallet isn't full, it's easy for things to slip out if you're not careful.

Overall, design, price, and accessories make this a steal, but there are still some design flaws that need to be worked out.

I draw/write at an angle, and more than half the time the iPad (and iPhone 5s, which I also tested it with) would not pick up the line at all. Nothing. The tip, albeit the side of the tip, was touching, but it would not read it. This, for me, is a fatal flaw and one I have never seen before in any stylus, even the cheap $1.99 ones.

I don't recommend you buy this.

title: Middle of the road as far as I'm concerned...
text:
As with an Aqua Mint Commuter case that I recently reviewed for use with Samsung Galaxy S8 plus phones, this particular case leaves me a bit disappointed. I'm growing less tolerant of the Otterbox premium price point. Otter products used to instill confidence and felt highly protective, though they were priced based on that confidence and protectiveness. This product doesn't feel bad, and actually feels fairly protective, but the plastic buttons don't necessarily line up as well as they should. A problem that I've had with an Otterbox case for my iPad mini that also has left me less enchanted with that case (like this one).

The Red (ROSSO CORSA (FLAME RED/RACE RED)) has a bit of a muddy appearance to it, making this less impressive on the looks side compared to the cooler mint colors and other choices among some of the other cases that I've seen in the market here. Perhaps the term should be "industrial". Either way, my thought is that this particular case doesn't sell itself well based primarily on the color scheme - people may buy it, but I don't think they're looking at this case and calling it "pretty".

For this one, I'm left with a rating of 3 middle of the road stars. It is OK, but nothing that makes me feel that attached or impressed. The price point also leaves me less enthusiastic as there are many choices out there that offer different advantages (and admittedly disadvantages).

title: Nice case, but not necessarily perfect
text:
Please note - I previously reviewed the same case, in a different color, so much of what you see here may repeat from that original review. Apologies if that occurs here as it is not my intent to bore anyone with reviews that only differ in regards to the color or aesthetics of an item.

In my original review, I had noted that my biggest complaint about this case would be the somewhat spendy price point. While the prices may vary for one color versus another, the prices aren't much different so that complaint remains. I've had similar complaints about products from the manufacturer's biggest competitor, but by the same token the cost of a case from either this manufacturer or that one is nothing compared to the cost of replacing the phone. Assuming this case provides a reasonable amount of protection, it should be worth the somewhat high price, but is that assumption a good one?

I would prefer to not have to find out just how protective this case is. Most frequently it is my family members that are no where near as careful with these expensive electronic items as they should be and inevitably it seems that these cases are needed to keep these devices safe. Thus far, the case that I had originally requested for review and have had in use has been working just fine, but we've not attempted any real stress test as we just don't want to take chances at damaging a phone that costs a few appendages when all is said and done.

The button extensions with this case were a concern with the first case but that concern was basically baseless. All of the buttons function as they should and don't require extra effort to make work for the user. If the buttons were not easy to use when necessary, it would have been incredibly frustrating and this case would have quickly been dropped in favor of something else that was less bothersome to use.

Previously mentioned (in the prior review), installing this without getting dust trapped under the screen protector is a bit of a chore. I've had that issue with numerous cases for various phones. I swear it makes me want to take these devices into a clean room before even thinking about installing them. I admit to being somewhat OCD about such things, but it does drive me crazy to see dirt and dust trapped below the screen protector. Oh, I should also throw in that the screen protector seems a bit glossy and that too can be a bit annoying for my tastes. I prefer not to have a shiny screen since it makes the phone screen difficult to read in bright light.

All told, this is a decent case. As before, this case isn't quite perfect, and to be clear, it probably is somewhat below 4 stars for me, but I've rounded up here and given the item 4 stars.

title: Good protection in a bulky and poorly designed package
text:
I will preface this review by saying I am generally disappointed by the quality of cases out there for the OPO and believe this case is a fine option for heavy-duty protection, perhaps even the best option available. That doesn't change my gripes with it, and I think my three star rating is accurate (though perhaps 3.5 or 7/10 would be closer to my feelings).

PROTECTION: 5/5
- This case protects almost every element of the phone. From the port covers to the built in screen protector, I wasn't worried about my phone in my purse or man-handling it in day to day use. That being said, the camera is not completely well protected and it has no military drop rating or seal rated to protect against water or dust. Still, it's more than ample protection for the average user, and I wasn't looking for those features.

LOOK AND FEEL: 2/5
- This case is bulky. Even for heavy duty protection it makes the phone feel huge, and adds a good amount of heft.
- The kickstand is an actual joke. Hard to pull out and very unstable.
- Included screen protector is atrocious. It's easy enough to remove, but I'm not sure why they included it in the first place (or didn't simply package a set of cheap screen protectors with the case). It has a visible gridline and reduced the responsiveness of my screen easily by a third. If you decide on this case, buy a tempered glass protector at the same time and take the cheap one out first.

USABILITY: 3/5
- While I usually have an issue with flaps that cover ports, there are well designed and close easily on their own without much encouragement. I was originally planning to cut them off, but they were good enough that I ended up keeping them.
- Very difficult to remove the phone from the case. Luckily you probably don't have to do this often, but I wanted to remove the screen protector and had a very difficult time simply getting the phone out
- Buttons become very hard to press. Trying to accomplish a double press for a screenshot or quick action was very challenging.
- When laying on a table face-up, there is a noticeable rock that makes it difficult to quickly write messages without picking up the phone. It's a small complaint, and probably more due to the OPO back than anything else.
- See issues with the built-in screen protector above

text:
When my wife and I got new S5 phones, it looked like this case was the logical choice since we wanted wireless charging and none of the other cases seem to work with Samsung's [[ASIN:B00ITI24EK Wireless Charging Cover]].

Even though we ended up sending them both back after a couple of days, here are the things we liked about them:

1) The wireless charging works great. It seems like a dumb thing, but it's really hard to go back to wires after you start using QI charging.

2) The S-View windows is pretty cool. It's nice having basic information available even while the cover is closed.

3) It preserves the water-resistant features of the phone - unlike some of the QI cards that cause the seal to break.

4) These offer pretty good protection for the phone.

Unfortunately, the cons outweighed the pros for us - even though these won't be very serious items for many people:

1) My biggest complaint was that the phone is just too thick with this case. I'm used to carrying my phone around in my pocket, and it was too noticeable with this case.

2) My second complaint is that it started hurting my ear when I talked with the case closed. This might just be me, but I get in long calls for work and this just wasn't comfortable for me.

3) Even after just a couple of days, it became obvious that keeping the window looking clean was going to be a big pain.

4) This is completely subjective, but we both didn't like the look. I guess I'm just used to a traditional case and had a hard time adjusting to this flip cover look; although, it does look more professional if that's what you're looking for (which is why I said this will be subjective)

Anyway, I would recommend this cover if you carry the case outside your pocket or are looking for a more 'corporate'/professional look. If you're just looking at this because of the wireless charging, I would recommend just getting a [[ASIN:B00F3J2KNI thin QI receiver]].

title: All-day battery life is amazing but orientation sensor quickly failed
text:
Good
- Battery: FINALLY a phone where the battery just lasts all day! You know, it's almost that nothing in the rest of this review even matters compared to this. It's such a HUGE relief that phone always has battery life left and I don't have to think about it, don't have to worry about it, etc. It's incredible.

- Everything else on the phone largely just works as you'd expect. The camera is fine though not exceptional, the speed of the phone is good but not exceptional, it goes on and on.
- Phone volume is good, speakerphone volume is good, call clarity is very good, and people seem to be able to hear me better vs previous phones (probably because they nicely put the microphones facing your mouth rather than facing downwards).

Not as good
- The one weird thing about sound quality on this phone is it's lacking in...bass? No matter what I use - the earpiece for calls, the speakerphone for calls, the speakerphone for youtube videos, the 3.5mm adapter for my stereo, bluetooth...bass always seems to be a bit lacking.

Bad
- Within the first month of owning the phone the orientation sensor died so tilting the phone sideways doesn't do anything any more. Amazon will not replace the phone, they insist you return it and order a new one, which is a problem for me because they applied some sort of credit in my purchase of the phone that they don't want to give back to me. I'm disappointed that the phone orientation sensor failed, and very disappointed that amazon will not directly replace the product.
- It's really annoying that they pointlessly removed the headphone jack.
- I periodically run into weird bugs that go away if I reboot the phone. Like maybe once a month.

Overall, if you're like me and your biggest issue is your battery lasting, this is a great phone and at the moment your only choice really for all day battery life.

title: Power supply is too small to charge through a case -- failed to charge Apple Watch after a month
text:
I like the appearance and styling of the charger. It has a small footprint which makes it easier to place on my dresser. I don't like the blue spotlight it paints on the bedroom ceiling. I know how to deal with that issue--black electrical tape. I don't like the fact that while charging starts normally on my iPhone 13 Pro, the charger LED begins to flash and the charger turns off. This makes the iPhone complain about the loss of charging power. Not cool and not conducive for a happy marriage. It did this all night. Every. Five. Minutes.

I had tested the charger in the den before taking it upstairs, but I had used a high-amperage USB charging adapter (a power strip with USB power ports) that can supply far more current than the tiny bricklet supplied with the charger. To test this upstairs, I replaced the supplied power bricklet with a higher-amperage model. It worked fine. Yes, I first tried to charge without a cover. Mine is hard to remove so I would not accept this as a solution and yes, the charger works when there is no cover. I'm considering returning this charger but with the high-amp bricklet, it is better than nothing. Now all I need to do is find some electrical tape.

I also discovered this "18 Watt" power bricklet is rated to provide 5 Amps at 5VDC--that's 15 watts, not 18. The reason I bought this charger is that it boasted a fast-charging 18W power supply.

What I don't understand is why people design devices that pollute the darkness of a bedroom to report "I'm doing what I'm supposed to do." SMH.

The company saw this review and immediately contacted me explaining that they were delayed (?) because of a hurricane--they spent two paragraphs describing the damage. They then gave me a very long description about how they had tested the charger with 20 different cases and they didn't always work but they fixed the problem. Apparently, mine didn't have the fix. They offered no other recourse. Of course, they begged me to withdraw the review. I'm debating on whether or not to return it as it does work with a high-current USB power supply, it's just that I don't have room on my dresser for another tech gadget... No word from the manufacturer in China if this is a safe alternative.

Update: After 45 days, the Apple Watch charger portion failed to work consistently. It would start to charge but when I got up in the morning something had happened and the watch was nearly dead. When it did this two night in a row I could no longer trust the charger. Waste of $$$.

Update: November. The watch charger has become even less reliable. I switched to the original Apple Watch charger and it charges twice as fast.

text:
I just got a Smartphone yesterday to replace my slide-open one (yes, I'm a late adopter. It's an iPhone 5.) I ordered this case (and a wallet-style one, so I could cover the front and carry other things right along with it) because I wanted something highly protective, but awesome-looking, since the phone itself is just solid black. Now it looks outstandingly snazzy! I loved the neon chartreuse color of this thing...that's kinda my signature shade...and its ruggedly rubbery, shock-absorbent-type appearance. It didn't look like the typical dinky little things. Plus, it had a kickstand--a necessity. Well, even my techno-expert brother was impressed with my choice, which made me pretty proud. The thing fits perfectly, leaving all needed spots guarded yet openly accessible for the headphones, charger, camera lens, and ring silencer--and the power and volume buttons remain pressable. The case makes the slippery little device much easier and more comfortable to hold, and isn't bulky or heavy. The phone's protected all around, and can be placed face-down without the screen contacting the surface. And the price?! Unbeatable!!

This is exactly the kind of case that's worth putting on your phone--one that will actually protect it from the inevitable falls and/or collisions.

The only way I'd make it even more perfect would be to have the kickstand's shape support the device standing vertically as well, if possible...and flip it so that the volume buttons and silencer are on "top" when you turn it sideways. However, I think another accessory I'll be getting just happens to include a vertical stand for it, anyway! Swell. The kickstand could also maybe lock super-securely into place, but that's being extremely nitpicky. It really is pretty dang great as is.

Highly recommended as particularly sweet-looking protection for your mobile investment. I've already got screen wipers/cloths and a stylus to try; now to wait on my packet of screen protectors and the plug-in keyboard I'm ordering next.

The arms of this holder strikes the perfect balance of being sturdy and also being flexible enough so that you do not have a workout of your arm when you are trying to flex the holder into a different position. Other products were the flex arm were either too weak or too hard to maneuver for me in the past, so I transitioned to straight bar mounts (RAM Mounts, Joy Factory mounts) that did the job, but were just a bit too hardcore and kind of an eyesore. My phone (Samsung Note S20 Ultra) has curved side screens, and the adhesive is not great along the sides, so that the protector wants to come loose.  And if you have lint or other stuff in your pockets, it will find its way under these "less stuck" sections of the protector, and thus reduces even more the adhesion to the sides.  There is a lifetime warranty on the protector, but be aware that you have to pay postage for a replacement (as I recently discovered on my old phone), which is about 1/3 the price of a new protector. title: BUY THIS. It's a lifesaver!
text:
I have a Google Pixel 4a (5g) with a pretty thick case. I needed to literally run it nonstop for videos one day--about 6 hours. It has TERRIBLE battery life now--I have to charge it multiple times a day during normal use!

I bought the two-pack of these, and my phone's battery stayed charged! I did need to go through both batteries (neither lost their entire charge, but I'm a worrier), but considering this was almost all videos, that's fantastic. The charge doesn't last as long afterward as it would if you had used the manufacturer's cord, but that's the case no matter what you use to charge your phone.

It stuck firmly into my phone, even through the thick case. They never fell out except for when I dropped my phone--oops--and that didn't cause any problems. Though you shouldn't drop your phone, just in case. Or in general. They even survived sticking on my phone while in my very full purse and being bumped around as I ran through airports.

The charge probably lasts 4+ hours, even if you're nonstop videoing.

They are a little heavy, so if you're planning on moving your phone a lot while you use it, you may want to take the charger out during that.

I also took these through airport security twice, and they didn't cause any issues. I mean, I can't promise anything because you never know with TSA, but I had no problems even after they had to search my bag for unrelated reasons. (I am quite dangerous with a multitool in my wallet!)

I'm planning on buying more, not because these will die soon but because I want to make sure I always have one on hand/in case I lose one, which I will.

This is likely the best tech purchase I've made in a while. If you're considering something like this, I assure you this is the product you need.

text:
Update #4: Posted a pic of my phone after having the protector on for 6+ months. You can see cracks in the screen protector from all the drops. At first I thought my screen was cracked but it's actually just the protector. Amazing. Also the edge on the left I cut with a little knife cause my case pushed up the edge of the protector. The right side... I didn't have a knife and was trying to make a straight cut with my finger nail....#fail. Bought a new protector to replace this old one. Super worth it. So durable and protects the screen. Original review below.

Update 3: 5 months later this thing is still going strong. I should add, I'm a nurse and wipe my phone almost daily with sanitizer (grey top) or alcohol wipes.

Update after a month or so: the edges came up pretty bad, so I cut the part that wasn't adhering and the rest is still stuck to my phone. It's pretty impressive. So basically where the edge stop being rounded is where I cut the screen cover (if that makes sense) I'll try to take a pic with my hobbies phone later.
Update after 6 days: I put my Spigen case on right after the screen protector, within 5 hours the edges were coming up slightly. I just squeegeed them down with the back of my finger nail when I noticed it and it was fine. 6 days later 3 corners are coming up slightly and wont go back down due to dust. It is something you can easily look past and still use the phone without noticing. I am not changing my rating because I feel this is the best screen I've come across. The actual screen part is unscratched and doing very well. It might do better with a different case as the Spigen edge sits right where the screen protector edge is. So really the screen is coming up from just picking up my phone and the case moving a little. That said. I still recommend it. I'm actually ordering another one and going to try to figure out a way to adhere those points. I can update again if I succeed!

Original review: I just put it on. I didn't follow the directions well. I missed something when I watched the video so I messed one up. I can't even tell it is on my screen. I feel if I drop my phone it will scuff easily because it is not slick, it's slightly rubbery, but it will definitely prevent my screen from getting scratched. I will update later if I feel it's horrible. I know! I hate when people review the first day of a product and not after they've had it a while. But for now this is it.

title: Remarkably solid for an inexpensive case, beware the durability of the tiny rubber 'ribs'.
text:
Use: I bought this to replace a damaged case on my iPhone XS Max.

Generally: The case is well made, fits my phone securely, and has outstanding grip and traction due to the myriad of tiny 'rubber' (probably silicone or TPU) 'ribs' or 'chevrons' that cover much of the case.

The good:

Provides ridiculously good hand-grip and 'dashboard traction', especially for the price.

Even though I'm not going to pitch it off a building to test, the case seems very solidly made and has soaked up a couple of drops from 4-5 foot onto carpet and linoleum, and once onto asphalt from off a car hood.

The dark 'olive drab' color is excellent, the color is consistent, and the black 'ribs' all look rather good.

The bad:

There isn't much to complain about, although the grippy 'ribs' pick up dog-hair and lint in a pocket pretty quickly.

There are reports that the 'ribs' will wear or pull away from the case over time, but I am not particularly gentle with my case, and this hasn't happened to me despite the somewhat rough handling.

title: Perfect for Entry Level VR Viewer and a GREAT Option as a Movie Viewer for Long Flights, Train trips, etc.
text:
I bought this as an 'entry level' VR headset while I wait for a free cardboard viewer.
My current phone is a Samsung Galaxy S3 and so there are issues regarding functionality
as noted by others who have purchased this item. I knew this ahead of time and so, with
that out of the way here are the PROs and CONs:

PRO:

1) Light weight, durable and well made
Padding around eyes is a major plus
2) Head harness fits snug and is adjustable
3) Lenses are clear- no bubbles, scratches etc.
4) Field of view is very wide and clear horizontally and vertically
5) The blank plastic to the right of TEEFAN logo is removable, allowing for
3D VR Camera capture using your smartphone

CON:

1) Additional foam pads required to insure firm placement/position of phone in caddy
2) No magnetic switch as provided in other viewers (including other TEEFAN VR set)
3) Field of view is more of a large screen as opposed to fully encompassing FOV that
provides an experience of full immersion into the material being viewed.

As mentioned, I already knew the limitations of my phone with ANY VR viewer currently available.
The field of view is acceptable for MY use and this headset will continue to be be useful for some
time and in the following manner:

I travel frequently and I often like to watch movies on my laptop or smartphone and so this provides
freedom from distractions by providing a movie theater type viewing experience. The addition of earbuds
increases my level of privacy as well as extending courtesy (to those seated to my left or right) by NOT
having the audio disturbing their flight, etc.

I have already used this at home to watch feature length films while lying on my bed-so far, no eye strain
or other discomfort. I also wore these to watch a series of animated short films in a local bar. This unit
(with my current phone) is a great combination as it provided the required 'isolation' from other patrons,
private viewing/listening and generated some buzz and interest for VR in general and TEEFAN specifically.

The cassette that holds the phone is pretty large. There is a spring loaded bracket to hold your phone in place
and this is easily removed with a small Phillips head screwdriver allowing use of a larger smartphone in the future.
A larger phone will made greater use of the wide field of view this particular model provides.

As mentioned, I am waiting for an actual (made of cardboard) viewer to experiment with in order to achieve the
same functionality of the magnetic switch and my current phone. THIS will form the basis of additional modification
to the TEEFAN headset with regard to correct placement of the switch in this headset.

"Cosmic Roller Coaster" (Google cardboard app) is sweet, fun and demonstrates the potential of properly done VR
production in CGI.

title: Really nice phone, S3 Alternative
text:
For some reason Amazon has this phone on backorder so I got it local from a VZW store on release day. My wife got the S3 a month back and I'm glad she did because I found I hate it. The biggest problem I have with it is the ridiculously shaped home button dead center of the bottom section of the phone. Why would you ruin a large touchscreen with a physical button?

So, I waited for release day for the RZR HD. There were 2 reasons that I wanted a RZR: The first is Smart Actions. It is basically a macro builder which allows you to automatically set the ringer off at certain times of day or based on location. Basically its a lot like the Outlook Rules for desktop email. The second item that had me eagerly waiting was the style. I simply like rugged looking phones. This one fits the bill. It is sleek but it is a nice shape for me. Some will call it boxy or square but I like the hard corners. The Kevlar back is a nice touch but if you get a case like I did you will never see it. Still, its a nice design choice and adds to the industrial/rugged look i mentioned earlier.

I didn't feel the need to go with the Maxx because a larger battery isn't worth $100 to me. If I traveled heavily or if I was on my phone constantly I would want the upgrade but I have been pleasantly surprised with the battery of the RZR HD. I used it on and off all day for normal stuff: Checking and sending emails, a few phone calls and my son spent 2 hours playing Plants vs. Zombies. I still have 60% of battery left and I took it off charge 17 hours ago.

The call quality is probably the best I have ever had on a cell phone. It is really clear for me and for the other party. I was extremely happy as I just assumed "ok" call quality was a fact of all cell phones.

I connect my phone via BT to my aftermarket car stereo and have no issues at all. Again, call quality is excellent.

I have not yet used the rear camera but I have put the front camera through its paces with the "Face Unlock" feature and I have no issues with the front camera.

The transitions from screen to screen are smooth. There is occasional choppiness but I have come to see that as standard depending on what else is running (I'm talking to you app addicts!) but it isn't a problem for me.

There is the standard suite of crap-ware courtesy of Verizon that you can't uninstall but at least ICS has the ability to choose favorite apps for the tray so you won't have to flip past "Verizon Navigator" and "Slacker Radio" every time you look for an app.

Overall I really like the phone. I highly recommend it.
