title: It is NOT tempered glass but it still works really well
text:
I'm not sure why it says that it is tempered glass in the description, but it is a flexible material. It feels a bit thick for non tempered glass plastic, but it feels like it'll be pretty strong. I haven't tested to see how scratch resistant it is, but I feel like it'll hold up in my normal usage.

The mold to hold the watch allows for a bit of play, but overall, should not have a noticeable effect on the placement of protector.

The protector is on a sticky sheet that gets fixed by a few studs coming off the mold in the corners. When you place it over the watch, it will not start to stick, so even if you took the plastic off the protector, there is no worry that it'll suddenly stick when you place it down initially. You have to press down on it for it to work.

With that being said, it is like a pretty normal plastic screen protector. If you get a piece of dust underneath, it'll create a small air bubble, no matter how much you squeeze and push on it. But if you just press down on it, and get stuck with a few bubbles, without any dust, it's pretty easy to remove, as if it were tempered glass. You should be able to push most, if not all, the bubbles out. You may need to lift a little, but that should be no problem in terms of dust, if it is already dust free.

As for lifting, there is a small lip that has no adhesive on it. Many other reviews have mentioned this lip, however, I noticed a lot mention how far it reaches over the watch. That is because its the 44mm cover on the 40mm watch. The watch cover will not overhang the watch, and its actually quite hard to notice. And maybe because it doesn't go in and out of a pocket like a phone, it doesn't collect much dust around the lip of the protector. Just take a quick wipe around it and that'll probably keep it looking okay for a long time.

Sensitivity also seems to be pretty unaffected. The face feels just as smooth with or without it. The touch bezel is also the exact same.

Overall, very satisfied. I would give this 5 stars if it didn't say that it was a tempered glass protector and cause confusion.

title: Nice robust and fast 30W charger with multiple port types
text: I've been using this wall adapter charger/power supply for a couple days now - so far very impressed. It not only charges or powers Apple devices with the supplied USB-C/USB-Lightning cable, but also any device with a USB-C connection or via any cable with a USB-A connector on one end. I've also simultaneously charged my Android phone with my own USB-A/USB-C cable and my coworker's iPhone with the supplied lightning cable. Both devices charged from about 30% to full in little under an hour - pretty good charge rate and the unit did not get very warm. I've also used it to charge a back up battery pack via USB-C faster than it would normally take with my other chargers. There is a warning on the outside of the box cautioning against using the USB-L and USB-C ports at the same time, but we used the USB-A/USB-C ports in this case which is okay. This appears to be a smart power supply with power delivery intelligence to manage the proper delivery of voltage and current based on load type. Currently I am using it to power a USB-A lamp but will charge my phone, tablet and other devices too when needed. Great value with the supplied cable.

text:
Final Update: I ended up ordering another Samsung Galaxy.. Why? Many items this phone will not blue tooth connect, the main thing being my car stereo and my Sony headphones. It also would not connect to my blue tooth speaker system at home, my mini speaker system, and other items. Also, the phone is missing the earphone jack. Finally, many carriers don't support SONY phones. I was going to change carriers and was going to have to buy another phone because they do not support Sony phones.

What will I miss about this phone? It charges fully in about an hour. The size is like a regular house phone. The phone is not fragile, many nights I lay on top of it while it is charging. It is just cool to have a phone not everybody has.

The 3* rating is because the phone will not Bluetooth connect to SONY products. My car stereo is Sony and my main headphones are Sony. It will not Bluetooth connect to these items. It does Bluetooth connect to Alltel. You can use regular headphones with the adapter to connect.

Do I recommend this phone? No, because tho sleek, it is a pain in the a.........s........s to own. Also, it will not Bluetooth connect to Sony products. How weird is that?

……..........
Original review below

was online getting ready to buy the latest Samsung ; an upgrade from the S7 when (coincidentally: wink, wink) Amazon asked me if I wanted to try out a phone. I really was hesitate. The last two phones I reviewed were knock offs of name brands and I was very upset that I had gotten rid of my good phone for the reviewed phone. FFd to the Xperia and it is actually a HIGH END phone. It is sleek (Pretty), as big as a house phone so you really feel like you are on your phone and not a calculator, and it comes LOADED. This phone retails for $949.00. I personally always buy my phones off e6ay so I can't say I would pay that, but for folks that buy the I9hone and other high end phones this is definitely worth it. Great pictures, clean and crisp, and quick. My prepaid data had slowed down and you could tell with the S7; it is not as noticeable with this phone.

Do I recommend? YES; if you are ANTI-apple like I am then consider this phone along with a Samsung. P.S., the phone came charged two weeks ago and when I went to the T-Mobile store for the transfer, it still had 13%. My S7 is always drained down to zero. The reviewed phone just comes with the charging cable; no headphones. You MUST have the charging cable; it is much bigger than the old Android charging cable. It is the C cord.

Cons:
The phone is too big to use one handed. The screen can be reduced to one handed use in the settings. Once I get a case I will try it out. Without a case, the phone is too long and slippery.
2. It is hard to fit in a small purse.
3. You probably will have to wait on running band holders and other special holders since it is so long.
4. Someone said it does not have a headphone jack. I will have to check on this. Because it is so slippery, I taped it in the carton it came in. Once the case arrives, I will be able to test out more features

Update 1:the Bluetooth will not connect to your car stereo. Bluetooth issues are common google search issues. I may have to go back to my s7. I listen to videos via Bluetooth everyday in my car and need Bluetooth.

2. The adapter for the earphone jack goes in the charging port. Basically, you can't use the phone jack and charge at the same time

3. My USB in the car just goes to ringtones. I can't get YouTube videos to play using USB with the phone

4. To stop the phone from vibrating with music, you press the volume button and dynamic vibration will appear

title: Great Product! Easy Install! Works Great!
text:
UPDATE TO REVIEW: After using this product for a couple of days, I found that my vehicle had difficulties with this OBD device, where the vehicle wouldn't start on the first key turn. I would have to turn off the ignition, try it again and usually repeat this process 3 or 4 times until the car would finally start. I called MotoSafety and they indicated that they have seen this on occasion and that there is no way to resolve the issue. Needless to say, I cannot use this device in this car if starting the car is compromised or delayed. Therefore, while I think the product is a great product, and the customer support is acceptable, I had to return this product. I may try the MasTrack product again (had problems with that device as well), but their customer support group had reached out to me and indicated that they might be able to modify the software on their side to allow compatibility between the OBD port and the device.

ORIGINAL REVIEW
I purchased this MotoSafety GPS tracker after a previous purchase of a competing product failed to work (see my other reviews for details). Unlike the big fail of the other device, the MotoSafety product was not only easy to install, but registration of the device was a snap! And, guess what? It worked right from the get-go.

Keep in mind that all of the real time GPS trackers require a supplemental service, which allows for real time vehicle tracking. The service with MotoSafety is $19,95/month, with a recurring charge to your credit card. This seems pretty typical and fair, as far as service cost.

(On a side-note, when you visit the website that they have listed in the packing documentation for activating your device, be sure to preface the website with the secure HTTPS:// notation. If you simply go to the website listed in the documentation, you will not be automatically directed to the secure checkout website for the recurring service credit card information, which could be a security issue as you enter your credit card into their site).

Now, back to the review of the product...As mentioned, the device installed very easily. I used a ribbon cable, also purchased here on Amazon, which allowed me to hide the tracker above the dash for aesthetic reasons. So, I got it installed and secured and took the car for a drive. (Be sure to load the MotoSafety app to your smartphone). The device immediately started reporting the vehicle position, as confirmed on my smartphone. When I got back home, I logged into the MotoSafety website (using the login credentials you provided at registration) and was able to view my trip history in a very nice mapping display. In addition, I like the fact it provides a "report card" of the driving habits during the trip. Heavy braking, acceleration etc. It also indicates top speed during each trip.

All and all, a very nice product. Easy install. And, most importantly, works as designed. Highly recommended!

title: Good Case
text:
I ordered the matte navy blue case for my iPhone 5S. Everything fits correctly including correct speaker and camera openings.
The case is a little darker than I expected since the picture shows the case as a lighter blue. The color of the case under daylight conditions is like that of a pair of dark blue jeans which makes it seem a little drab to me. This is the only reason it does not get a 5 star rating. Had I ordered the light blue or white case, this would receive a 5 star. The power button can be harder to access depending on your usage since it does tuck into the case to protect it.

Other than that, the case feels pretty sturdy in that it is not a Otterbox that will survive a 10 foot drop but it will protect against scratches and lower drops (repeated drops will likely reduce the protective ability of your case each time). The sides of the case is a hard plastic that feels like the back of the plastic iPhone 5C or the Samsung S3/4 which is quite nice for protecting side scratches. I actually prefer cases like this because it keeps the thin and light profile of my iPhone instead of turning it into a brick. I can also take the case off easily if I wanted too to clean dust off. I recommend if you get this case, also get a screen protector to protect all sides of your iPhone 5/5S.

text:
ORIGINAL REVIEW IS FOR NINTENDO SWITCH SCREEN PROTECTOR. For some reason, Amazon allows sellers to post different items on the same listing, so the following review is no longer applicable to this item, and I have removed all stars.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
I put off getting a screen protector for far too long and have a few light scratches that annoy me because of that. I am so glad this is the screen protector I chose. The installation was so easy, and the screen exceeds expectations.

The pictures are from after installing. The box is printed with simple instructions that confused me (there was nothing labeled "2"so that part threw me off). Inside were two screens and two sets of the cleaning wipes and guide stickers pictured.

The screen impressed me off the bat with how thick and rigid it is (pictured cantilevered). I wish I had taken a video when I applied it to my Switch, because it looked like magic. The adhesive set quickly and evenly, from the first corner that made contact, across the screen.

The touch screen still functions fine so far, and the screen itself is hardly noticeable. Overall, I'm quite pleased with the Oribox Glass screen protector!

title: It'll work until you find something better
text:
Automatically reading the description and seeing them say "if you're picky, don't buy or product" basically makes you think "what in the world am I buying?" Well I can assure you that even if you aren't picky and just want a quality product, you shouldn't buy this. If it is a stepping stone to a better screen protector, it could work for you temporarily. If you are buying this expecting it to be amazing though, you're not going to want to spend money on this protector.

The biggest issue I have with it is that as others have stated, the edges of the protector do NOT fully stick to the screen. You can see the lighter area around the entire phone where it is not sticking to the screen. That means dust and dirt are going to find their way in between the protector and the screen and basically make your phone look REALLY ugly after a while. This is MOST apparent, again mentioned in other reviews, at the bottom of the screen where it curves every so slightly. It curves enough to make the protector not adhere to the bottom of the screen at all.

I cleaned the screen with the provided wet cloth, dried it with the dry cloth. Screen was clear from all dirt/dust/particles and still having problems with the edges sticking. Luckily this protector was on sale for $4.99 from $11.99, though perhaps for a good reason.

ALSO! The "anti-fingerprint" coating is more like a fingerprint promoter. I had less fingerprints on my screen without the screen protector.

The company has been pretty responsive once you know to send an email with a picture of the problem and verify your address, but these screen protectors are far from "ballistic".  They chip easily and shatter on even the smallest drop. My wife and oldest child have NEVER had a phone issue, and baby their phones and even their screen protectors have shattered  more than once.  They were shattering so often I bought an extra to have a spare available since it takes over a week to receive a replacement, but now that's not even enough. The company has stood behind their product so far, but they have become increasingly easier to break... perhaps time to go with another product.

title: A well-thought out case that protects without ruing the aesthetics of the iPhone 6 - highly recommended
text:
The Alixo 6S iPhone 6 case is a sturdy yet slim protective case for the iPhone 6. It consists of two parts - the “inner” case, a hard shell with a screen protector which the iPhone slips into face-down, and the “outer” case, which is flexible and wraps around the inner case. The packaging includes two “inner” cases - one black and one white - so that you can choose the case that matches your iPhone color best.

The case comes pre-assembled and requires you to remove the inner case from the outer case before putting the case on your iPhone. Being paranoid, I was very careful removing the rigid inner case from the outer case - I was initially worried that, as it was thin and rigid, it might be fragile - but it came out easily with no signs of distress. After peeling away the almost excessive protective tape (which ensures that the screen protector is as clean as possible on both sides), I was able to put my iPhone inside of the inner case in seconds, without even referring to the instructions printed on the back of the packaging. After that it was a simple matter to “wrap” the flexible outer case around the inner case. It did take a few moments to make sure that the outer case was positioned “just right” - e.g. making sure there was a tight fit at all the edges, and pushing in the “stoppers” that protect the Lightning and Audio ports - but all in all applying this case to the iPhone was less work than any of the similar competing products I’ve used.

As for the case itself? It’s well thought out, with soft but sealed buttons covering the three physical side buttons (volume up, volume down, and the power button) of the iPhone 6, and an access port that allows you to reach the mute toggle (although you’ll want to make sure your finger nails are a bit longer than mine if you want to toggle the mute switch back and forth - I’m a consummate nail-biter and rarely have enough nails to do anything, let alone toggle the mute switch through this case). The Lightning and Audio ports, as mentioned above, have rubberized “stoppers” which are integral to the case - you can’t lose them, and it’s easy enough to pop them in and out. The only areas where the case isn’t completely sealed are the mute toggle (as described above), the rear-racing camera, which also has a cutout, the speaker (which has cutouts in the screen protector, described below) and the microphone area, which has a series of holes that don’t compromise the integrity of the case but clearly allow sound to get where it needs to go.

About that rear-facing camera cut-out? Love it. As you already know if you own an iPhone 6, the camera actually protrudes a bit from the aluminum casing of the iPhone. This case is just thick enough to make the camera recess a bit, protecting it from scratches and drops - actually amazing considering that the case doesn’t make the iPhone feel much thicker at all.

The screen protection of the inner case is what really impressed me. The face of the iPhone is almost completely protected with a scratch-resistant layer, with only two small holes in the protective layer above the speaker. I was very curious to see how well the TouchID sensor worked with the thin membrane that covers it in this case, and I was very pleasantly surprised. I kept expecting the TouchID sensor to fail to recognize my fingers, or at least to take longer to recognize them - but in the two days of testing, I’ve yet to experience any problems with fingerprint recognition.

While the case isn’t waterproof, there are actually very few places where water could get in - the speaker port, the microphone port, the mute toggle, and the camera opening - and most of those seem sufficiently tight that I’m less worried about my iPhone being subjected to the occasional splash or spill than I was before.

In conclusion, the Alixo 6S iPhone 6 case is a winner - without sacrificing any functionality and only a barely-noticeable increase in thickness, this case wraps and seals your iPhone 6, protecting all parts of the phone - case, camera, screen, and ports - from scratches and drops. While I was too cowardly to actually perform a drop-test, the outer shell feels “elastomeric” enough that I’m confident it will absorb significant levels of force from all angles. An impact directly to the screen area (e.g. if you drop a brick just right…) could still smash your screen, but this is true of even the thickest protective cases. It seems very unlikely that a typical sort of event like dropping the phone onto a flat surface will result in total catastrophe. This case is a really nice blend of safety, functionality, and aesthetics, protecting your precious iPhone 6 without locking it away inside of a case that removes all of the style and grace of the iPhone 6 itself.

title: Great phone, mediocre focusing/lowlight camera
text:
Well I struggled between a 3 and 4 star here. The device is great - but the photos and video are so blurry at times that it's almost a cause for alarm. But, if you take the time to let it get focus and calibrate properly, the photos aren't too bad. I'm just not used to having to manually focus EVERYTHING - life happens too fast and by the time the camera is ready, the photo op is gone. If it's a nice bright day then photos are great, I'm talking indoor shots, not always perfect lighting - and even worse darker rooms with a brighter subject. For example a lit Christmas tree in a dark room. I want to turn on the camera and take a shot - thats all I ask.

However, I still gave it 4 stars because you can't beat the price for everything else this phone gives you. The screen is sharp and responsive, the phone is fast, its thin and feels good in the hand, etc. If they could only get the camera/photo app working better, it would be an incredible phone for the price. But if you are ok with lots of ho-hum photos, then you should be good to go.

title: What would you rather see, a large box or a pile of cables?
text:
This is a LARGE box, please read the size description (16" x 6.2"). That means, this product is not for you if you don't want to see a large white box. This product IS for you if you'd rather see a large white box than a jumble of cables.

The sides are thin but sturdy enough. This is actually an advantage because your cable box probably won't endure a lot of abuse and you're getting the full size of the box, without any thick sides taking up your precious space. It's a very simple design, it's basically just a lidded box with two slits on either end and rounded edges, and if you're not going to stick this behind a desk, it won't look completely horrible (other than the size, it's pretty unobtrusive). Also, I bought the white so we can easily spray paint it to match our decor (or to stand out, if you want!). The lid does securely slide onto the box, but it does not 'snap' in.

An advantage of the simple design is that you could technically use this for whatever you need a box of this size for. For example, say your home has a second computer that you use this for but you later sell the computer and now have an extra cable management box. It could easily be used as storage for something else, in a craft room (ribbons?), garage, etc.

This is a simple product that simply does what it's supposed to do. Between this and my velcro cable ties (probably my best cable management purchase ever), our cords are looking better than ever. If you need a large cable management box, then I'd definitely recommend this.

I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest opinion. I make my recommendations as though a good friend or family member was to read my review. title: 4/5 Stars Overall
text:
My wife has a similar charger. Comparing to hers, this one has the same MaH and the same ports. However, this one seems to have 2 downfalls. First, as it sits in my bag, it loses charge. I have tested this for a long while before writing this review. Several times, if I leave the charger in my bag and come back to it in a week or two, the charger (which was charged to 100% and then not used), will show anywhere from 94-98%. So, I lose roughly 5% of charge just from it sitting in my bag.

Second, when it charges the phone, the % seems to drop quicker than my wife’s charger of a similar style. For example, if the phone has roughly a 60% charge on it, charging to a full 100%, her charger will drop from 100% to about 80-85%. From the same roughly 60% on the phone to a full 100% charge, this charger typically drops into the 60-70% range. I have not continued testing over and over to see how many charges I can get out of it, but I’m betting her charger would give close to 1 extra full charge over this one.

All of that being said, this is still a decent charger. It charges quickly itself, and does a pretty decent job of getting the phone charged up. I carry this with me in my shoulder bag everywhere I go, so I use it a lot. I would recommend it. Just be aware that it’s not the best charger on the market. But overall, for the money, it does what it’s supposed to do and has not let me down when I’ve needed it.

title: An honest review after a few weeks of use
text: The glass is very smooth and feels just like the actual touch screen on the iPhone 6. When I installed it I was happy with the fit considering the rounded edges of the iPhone 6 glass screen limit how far it can extend to the edge. Despite that it gives the most complete coverage any screen protector could considering the design of the phone. Reviews that condemn the product because it doesn't reach the edge don't understand how much more expensive it would be to actually make a screen protector that curved down on the sides to reach the edge. That's why it's just a flat piece of glass and it covers the flat portion of the iPhone screen perfectly. It took a while for all the bubbles to disappear, but eventually they did. Unfortunately for me I did get a few specks of dust caught under the screen but they are barely noticeable. Now after a few weeks of having the screen protector on the iPhone 6, I noticed that the bubbles are beginning to reappear and they don't seem to want to rub out. In all fairness to Spigen and their product, I did have to lift it once while aligning it and that may have compromised the adhesion. A screen protector like this needs to be perfectly aligned the first time for best results. Even still, the protection, smoothness and feel of the Glas.tR Slim is so much better than a film type protector that I will gladly take the trade-off. Nice product, but could be a little bit better.

text: Bought this for wireless charging since LG stupidly left this feature out of the phone. HEY LG!! WHAT'S UP WITH THAT?? Anyway, when I got this in the mail I was quite shocked to see it came a really sweet hard wooden case. It would take getting run over by the mail truck to damage this case! Once I was done ogling the case I put the cover on my phone. (The wooden box is perfect for storing your original back cover for safe keeping.) The color doesn't exactly match the AT&T blue shade but it comes close enough since most will use a phone case anyway. I actually like the color better as it's a little brighter. The case fits on the phone tighter than the original which makes me worry about repeatedly taking it off to swap batteries. It doesn't fit perfectly at the bottom but if you use a case you won't notice much. It also does not feel like the original case at all. The "rubberized" feel of the LG cover is gone as is the hand grip protection. This new case is quite slippery to hold and could be an issue if you are prone to dropping things. As for the wireless charging, It does work but causes my phone to rum warm while charging. It also charges a lot slower than the wire. I'm not sure if that is due to the cover or the actual wireless charging station I am using. As a bonus it also comes with a Tempered Glass screen protector which I haven't actually tried yet. It also came with a dry wipe cloth and a wet wipe cloth but no instructions on what they are for and which to use for what. I'm guessing they are for installing the glass screen but a small instruction sheet would be nice. Overall I guess you can read above and decide for yourself. Colorwise it is close enough to AT&T Blue but has some small functional/cosmetic issues as noted above.

title: Well designed and mostly sturdy
text: This product is really well designed and is a great alternative for those of us who want convenience but don't want to put one of those magnets on the back of our phones. In a nutshell, the "arms" of the product are wide open until you press the phone against the back of it, which will make the arms will snap inward and hold your phone tightly. In other words, you literally just press your phone against it and it will hold; takes less than half a second to get it in place, which is great when you're hopping in the car and leaving in a hurry. To release, you just press these other little arm things inward, which is also really easy. It's also very easy to install and mostly holds on well to the air vent. I will note though that it seems to hold better when attached to horizontal air vents, and not as well with vertical ones. I have an iPhone XS Max though, so it might just be a bit heavier (no case though), but it did start to slip a bit in the middle of a 4-hour road trip. I was able to stop and re-install it again though, and it lasted the rest of the way. I later switched it to a horizontal vent and it's been fine. Overall, really easy to put on and off, and I'm most comfortable recommending it for those with cars with horizontal air vents.

title: I've been looking for the perfect magnetic battery pack, and this isn't it
text:
I am primarily testing and using this pack with a Samsung Galaxy S22 Ultra with a magnetic case. I have also tested it on an Apple iPhone 14 Pro.

Design: This is a fairly large pack, especially to keep on your phone all of the time. If you put this on your phone and keep the phone in your pocket, you will notice that it is there. However, the added size and weight does come with added capacity, which is welcome, especially when there is loss associated with battery charging in general, and wireless charging specifically as quite inefficient. There is a metal flip out kickstand on the back of this pack which is sturdy, and much better than this pack's smaller cousin, the Anker 622. I feel comfortable using this kickstand to prop up my phone, and it is at a decent angle for viewing.

There is a USB C port on the side, and a USB A port on the bottom. The USB A port does not output as much power, but it would be good for charging a watch in an emergency. The two ports, and higher capacity, actually make this a decent small pack to carry around for emergency charging, even if you don't use the magnetic feature to stick it to your phone. The ability to do that and use it as a kickstand is an added bonus.

This pack will not trickle charge. That means, once your phone is at 100%, charging will stop, and the phone battery will begin to deplete. You an start charging again by pressing the button on the pack once. Additionally, if you are using this pack as a stand only and don't want it to charge, you can hold the button for a couple of seconds (the manuals says 2) and it will turn off and not charge. Unfortunately, the pack won't trickle charge like it's smaller cousin, the Anker 622 will.

This is a solid pack, and due to it's size, it has more room for heat dissipation. It will get a bit warm when charging a device, but not terribly hot. But do keep in mind that heat and charging are a sure fire way to shorten battery life. You should really try to use plug in chargers whenever possible and just rely on a pack like this for emergency situations.

This pack sticks to the back of your (Magsafe quipped phone) or back of your magnetic compatible case. It seems to stick fairly well, better than the Anker 622, but not as good as the Apple battery pack. This pack is made to swivel so that you can use the stand and place your phone in a landscape position. This means that the pack doesn't have all of the alignment magnets that the Apple pack has to keep it aligned perfectly. It is decent, but can be slid around on the back of the phone a bit. I do feel comfortable that it won't come off though, even in a pocket. It just bothers me a bit that it can be swiveled out of perfect alignment.

PROS:
Good build quality, feels solid
Two ports, USB C, and USB A, for charging devices with a cable
Nice kickstand, works well
Magnetic force is sufficient
Decent capacity for emergency situations and could also charge an additional small device

CONS:
Will not trickle charge your phone to keep it topped at 100%
A bit heavy to keep on your phone all the time, but can still throw it into a back pack if needed

If pressed between the Anker 622 (small cousin) or 633 (this item), I would choose this item for emergency use. If you need to keep it on your phone all the time, this might get a bit heavy and the 622 might be a better bet. I like the larger capacity, better build quality, two output ports, and nicker kickstand. This is a decent pack just to charge up and keep in your car's glove box for emergencies. But my best advice is to plug your devices in to charge whenever possible.

title: Nice little charging adapter
text:
These are great little adapters. They are very small so it is easy to throw one in your backpack, or in the car, or wherever. They are excellent for traveling (in North America, as they are North American plugs - 2 prong non-polarized). They deliver 20W of power and will fast charge your devices that support it. (My Android phones and tablets show "Fast Charging" when connected). The output connector is USB C, not USB A, which is ultimately a batter cable arrangement.

You can plug one of these into an outlet and it will not block the other outlet on the 2-outlet plate. You can plug one into each outlet without issue.

You get 2 in a package - very handy, and an excellent value. When I got the package I couldn't believe how small it was (for 1) and then when I opened the package and saw 2, I was amazed.

These are basic no-frills. There's no light or anything on them. This is great for use in a dark bedroom.

These are great to have on hand. Just get a package or two and leave one in each room of your house.

Note: They do not come with any cables. You will need a USB C to USB C cable to charge USB C devices, or a USB C to lightning to charge Apple devices.

PROS:
* Small
* 20W "Fast Charing"
* No lights to brighten a dark bedroom
* Great value
* USB C output jack

CONS:
* No light to let you know it is working

title: Several Problems, Disappointing
text:
There are several problems:

(1) Not all GPS navigation apps can display a mirror image. Unfortunately, there's no app to mirror everything on an Android phone. Sygic can, but I much prefer HereWeGo which does not. There are plenty of simple GPS speedometers that can do a mirror image.

(2) The ball-and-socket joint is too loose. It moves every time you hit a significant bump. It's worse when it gets hot.

(3) The smartphone overheats in less than an hour on the dash if it's sunny.

(4) The reflector is not just clear plastic. It's a half-silvered mirror, a.k.a. one-way or two-way glass. This allows it to reflect, especially in daylight, much better than the windshield. However, the reflector is tinted so dark that you can't see well enough through it to drive safely even in direct sunlight. It does make the phone's screen clearly visible.

(5) In certain positions the sun makes it unreadable. This happens about once an hour.

(6) The groove at the front meant to stand up the phone is useless. As soon as you accelerate, the phone tumbles out.

I might glue the joint into position with PVC cement and use it only at night and on overcast days.

title: Causing actual, physical pain.
text:
Received this device today as a freebie for purchasing a Galaxy S7 Edge. I loaded up my phone, installed all the apps and then proceeded to try using it. The main problem I have with this device is the extremely static OS design. The device is designed to lock the UI at exactly even with the ground. This means you cannot move the UI up even one inch to adjust for aspects such as sitting down while slightly leaning back to use the headset.

The result is that you MUST sit rigidly straight to use the device or the UI will be below your field of view. As a result, trying to use the headset while sitting in a relaxed position will mean leaning your head forward, putting pressure on your collarbone. Head movements are also extremely over-exaggerated, requiring large head turns to use menus. To access the apps menu on the store screen, it is necessary to turn my head 45 degrees to the left and 45 degrees down into a VERY uncomfortable position just to look at the menu option and select it.

It's been about 20 minutes since I took the headset off and my collarbone at the base of my neck is still painful after only 10 minutes of use. THe UI needs a huge overhaul to cause less neck strain.

In addition, the eyepads are a bit too large. When I put the headset on, the pads where squeezing in my nose. I ended up pulling the nose section of the padding loose and down just to take the pressure off my nose.

TL;DR, The UI isn't designed with neck comfort in mind and the eyepads are way too big near the nose. The neck pain from using it last long after the headset is taken off.

title: Proceed with caution
text:
This Spigen case (if it IS a Spigen case, more on that later) is nice looking and seems to offer great protection. The fit is great, and allows for the use of a screen protector as well. Pretty much what you want a case to do.

Two things prevent me from giving this a 5-star rating:

If you own an iPhone 6, you know that the new design is, well, easy to drop. The smoothness of the rounded sides make it easy to let slip. So, one of the things that I would expect from a case would be to mitigate this feel somewhat. This particular case doesn't do that. The sides are every bit as smooth as the phone itself. Would it really have been a major manufacturing issue to etch small "grip grooves" to the sides? Minus one-half star.

Secondly, and this is really the more concerning issue, is that Spigen does not warranty the item at all if it isn't purchased directly from them. Their warranty expressly states in the first line: "Spigen products purchased from distributors or resellers are not covered by the 2 year warranty." Although the Amazon product page shows, "Sold by Spigen, Fulfilled by Amazon," does that qualify for warranty or not? Who knows. More distressingly, the product I received would not authenticate on the Spigen website: the package contains a product code which you use at the Spigen site to determine if yours is a true Spigen and not a knock-off; mine would not validate. So, did I get a true Spigen product or not? Who knows. Minus one-and-one-half-star.

If it's a genuine Spigen, and if it's covered by warranty, it's a great product. If it's a knock-off and not covered by warranty, it's falsely advertised. Caveat emptor.

Feel: A bit slick but in a good way. If you were wearing cloth gloves or something you might slip but it feels great in the bare hand. Doesn’t slide on a surface at all.

I'm about to request a new nut from Charger City though I don't have much hope - this product does not seem to be listed on their website, or anyway searching and browsing for it didn't help. If Charger City won't help me I might try epoxy. Or an ugly pipe clamp.

But the fact is the design is poor and I think a lot of people are just putting up with sagging phones. I am not like that. I'm telling you don't buy this product. Too much time required to solve - if I'd known about the design flaw there's no way would have bought it. If Charger City comes up with a new nut or other solution I'll revise this review. title: Perfect-sized companion for travel, vlogs, anything!
text:
I wanted something to prop my new RX100 a little higher when making videos and thought about a GorillaPod since those were all the rage (and still is?). But the options were expensive and I had trouble deciding which one I wanted to get so then decided I'd look at alternatives. I've heard Manfrotto as a brand mentioned several times and have seen this product a few times in videos as well so thought I'd get it and try it out. Worst case, I'd just return it. Good news: I don't think I'll be returning this!

The box itself was easy to open even though it came in the packaging that everyone hates to open. When I first took this out, I was pleasantly surprised at all sturdy it was; so much heavier than I thought it would be and the finish is very nice. The legs feel sturdy and weighted and it just looked so smooth. The only con here is that when you push all the legs together and go to grip it, it is probably going to be more slippery than a GorillaPod with all those segmented pods on the legs. But this looks visually better and is cleaner. The ballhead could not be easier to operate. I'm a designer and this was wonderfully designed and delightful to use. I'm just wondering how the button will hold up after months/years of pressing over and over again and I wonder if it'll become loose. I'll update if that ever happens.

As stated, I'm using this for my Sony RX100 so there's no interchangeable lenses and it's always only going to be that large. As such, I've got no problems believing that my camera will be steady and won't fall off. It's great for compact cameras. I'm sure if I used the kit lens on my Sony a6000, it'd be fine as well. I'd be cautious trying to stick something like an 18-105mm lens on it though.

Overall, very happy with the cheap-ish purchase and I hope it holds up to months or years of use!

title: Very secure, worth the price, but likely have to use 2 hands!
text:
Toyota’s built in nav just really sucks and I switched to using a combo of Apple Maps, Google Maps and Waze. But now that I’ve started using my phone, I wanted to get a reliable phone mount. I’ve tried several - ones that stick to the windshield, ones that are essentially a platform, magnetic ones (that messed up my phone signal) and also other vent ones but none work as well as this one. I’ve used this with an iPhone 5s, 7, X and Xs and only had to replace this once since I lost it in another car (always bring it with me while using rental cars too). I’ve mainly used it in a 2003 Toyota Camry as well as a 2015 Toyota RAV4 and numerous rental cars from Jeeps to Chevys to Nissans.

When I use it, I always attach my phone to it first and then with the phone in it, press it hard into the air vents until it seems sufficiently lodged. Boston roads are notoriously full of potholes and I’ve never had it fall off once. The attachment to the air vents is very secure, in my opinion and the connection to the phone is very secure as well. When I take it off, I take the phone thing off and then the phone off. You don’t have to; that’s just how I like to do it. But this does mean that it’s not as easy to remove or put in your phone with one hand. I just personally find no issue with using 2 hands and with taking the whole thing off before attaching or removing my phone.

The size is great. Compared to other phone mounts, this is really small. It doesn’t block your view out the window, like most swivel head mounts do, which was a huge plus for me. It’s also just so easy to carry or bring with you. I took a weeklong trip to Cali and had a rental car and this was one thing I definitely did not want to forget so that I didn’t have to deal with holding my phone in my hand and also another car’s nav system. You do sacrifice a vent so just keep that in mind. Having it near the vent and not up further also makes charging your phone a bit easier. Just know that if you choose to use the vent to the left of the steering wheel, make sure your charger’s length is good and if too long, doesn’t become a safety issue.

The cost is a little rough but it’s worked really well and I’d gladly pay it again if i lost it again.

The rigid rubber around the edge makes it fairly easy to install while keeping it tight and sturdy. Entire case fits perfectly tight with zero room between case and phone. I usually by defender series otterboxes but after using this will probably stick with these int the future. Also kick stand is a little stiff to open but I'm sure will wear in over time. I locks both in the open and closed position with a very affirming and stiff clock so you know its in place and sturdy. This product has changed my mind about trying cheaper cases and would give this a 5 star review even if priced around a $40 range. title: Good case, protects your expensive investment - but traps lint
text:
I love my X, but they are fragile little things - I've broken two already. So I finally decided that I need to put the thing in a case (you know, since I've used up all my Apple Care replacements now). This case is awesome because it protects your phone physically, but also technically - you get one year of insurance for the cost of the case.

The case itself took some wrangling to get my phone into it and there is a whole process, but I like that it is clear and doesn't interfere at all with the phone usage. The camera is uncovered, the buttons are usable and the speakers are exposed. I like that it is clear so your phone still looks like an iPhone (just a slightly larger one).

There are a few problems with the case, however. The plastic traps dirt and lint, and that causes the face recognition to fail. I have to pull my phone out, clean it and re-install it (which is a pain) each time. That said, it protects the crap out of your phone - I dropped my phone from waist high onto the pavement and nary a scratch.

title: (Edited) The best thing I didn’t know I needed!! [But fragile]
text:
edit #1 — updated: use caution as it broke easily after a 6 months of use, but was easily repaired with duct tape

Edit #2 — broke again at 11 months, and not repairable this time. (The brackets shattered). I love the functionality of this product, and need to replace it, but I will be buy a different brand this time to hopefully find one more durable.

That said, for 11 months of daily use — it was decent and I really enjoyed the product. If you can be very very careful not to force it, you can probably get a few years before it breaks. I was careless in how I man handled it, and broke mine twice.

My original review:

I was very skeptical, but this turned out to be one of the best amazon purchases ever. I can sit or lay in any position to watch movies or use my phone. I can even walk or stand. Game changer. Highly recommend.

*CAUTION: the brackets cracked after 6 months of normal use. To repair it, I wrapped the broken piece in electrical tape, and continue to use it successfully. But I would caution new buyers to be very careful not pulling too hard or the plastic WILL crack. Specifically if you try to forced the arms apart for the purposes of lowering the screen, this is where there is a weakness in the design. To prevent this, do not force the unit, handle with care. And it might help to proactively wrap the brackets in electrical or duct tape.

Edit #2 the seller immediately offered to send a replacement so I am very happy with the service of this awesome product

Edit #3 although the seller offered to send a replacement, which seemed awesome, I never received anything or heard back from them and I have no way to contact them. So, not so great service after all.

title: Watch out for the latest operating system
text: Ive had this phone for over a year now and as far as a phone goes it's so so. Cuts out a lot. Hard to hear people talking. The worst thing is the new operating system. The OS5 sends your text messages via imessage if you are texting to another iPhone. This sucks your data plan fast. I called apple and told them my data plan was going fast it must have something to do with the new OS. They said no it isn't. Call AT&T.  I called AT&T and they told me first turn off imessage and walked me through a procedure that turns off all apps when you're not using them. It seems the new operating system constantly runs apps even when you're not using them. So if youre not near wifi your data plan is being used even if you arent using anything on your phone.  But the worst thing is the messaging. If you send a lot of text messages as I do I would highly recommend turning off iMessage. If you look on apples own website it even says in a little footnote "data rates may apply".  In other words Apple people don't know or won't admit this is a problem. If you have unlimited data plan no problem. But if you have a limited data plan watch out. Call your carrier and have them walk you through this or you will get a big surprise when your monthly bill comes.

title: Round-eartips do not fit well within the inner ear
text:
I purchased the Voyager 5200 mobile headset solely because it was the highest rated Bluetooth headset on New York Times WireCutter review site, which I highly trust. I was hoping for a device that can filter out wind and background noise so that I can use it on walks outside. So far I am happy with the sound quality and batter of the device. I need to test the noise cancellation out more, but expect it to be high because WireCutter tested this extensively.

I am disappointed with the Voyager 5200 eartips. I am used to iPhone/Bluetooth headsets that have a semi-pointed tip. The pointed tip allows eartips to fit snugly in the ear and not move around after inserted. In contrast, with the Voyager 5200 rounded shape, the eartip is constantly jostling around in my ear and coming out of my ear. I have tried all three sizes of the round eartips provided but none allow a secure placement in my ear.

I think that part of the problem is the weighting and shape of the over-the-ear part of the device. Since the weight rests on the top of the ear, the device swings in and out of your outer ear. That weighting issue, combined with the round eartips, means that when moving your head, you can feel the eartip moving around in your outer ear.

I have found a partial solution to the problem of the round eartips that were provided with the device. I have harvested the eartip-cover from my old mobile headset, which has a pointed-shape, and slid it over the round-Voyager-eartip. Now, using this Frankenstein-earbud, the eartip fits better inside of my ear and doesn't slide in and out when I move my head.

See review photo to view my solution to the eartip problem.

I think that Plantronics should provide pointed-eartips with the Voyager 5200 headset. For people paying $100 for the device, providing eartips that actually fit in the ears would be nice.

title: PROTECTIVE/BEAUTIFUL/MULTI-LAYER—100% Recommended
text:
I love everything about this case so far! It is beautiful, first off! This case was bought for an 11 year old girl who just got the white iPhone XR and wanted a protective case, but wanted to also show off the beauty of the phone without making it too too big. So I immediately showed her this one and she was sold. It looks so good on the white XR especially, but I’d imagine that this design may also look just as good with the black and coral color as well, maybe even the blue possibly. I doubt that the pink flowers would look very good with the yellow or red versions of the XR but who knows, possibly.

Because this case has a raised lip on the front and higher than the camera on the back, and a 3 piece construction that is sort of flexible so you don’t break it prying the front piece from the back, makes it super durable. The middle is a rubber soft cushion material that cradles your phone and the two front and back pieces snap together to complete the install. You’ll absolutely need to invest in a tempered glass screen protector as timhis case does not come with one but that is rather inexpensive and 100% imperative. It might be possible to get a full coverage tempered glass depending on how “full coverage” it is and as long as it fits, you will be completely protected with no gaps like a standard screen protector usually does. However, even with the standard screen protector, which is what I used, you should be fine using this case given the raised front bumper. With a standard tempered glass and this case, the possibility of breaking the screen is minimal unless by some freak accidental drop on a sharp rock or something just happens to hit on the very small areas left exposed between the tempered glass and the front bumper while dropping the phone face down. Though I have not seen or experienced personally any drops using this product yet, I’m confident that the average drop would not penetrate this case or damage the phone inside as long as it is paired with a tempered glass.

As with any case and tempered glass, use your better judgment and exercise safety precautions if you want to preserve the beauty, functionality, and life of your device. Use common sense obviously, and try to keep your $1000 investment (iphone) in mind as just that—an investment. Don’t go swimming with your phone—it is not waterproof contrary to what you may think!! And even LIFEPROOF cases if not installed properly or the slightest damage or pinhole renders it useless (ntm good luck trying to get that company to honor their warranty and fix your phone if it breaks while using their products). Always try and use tempered glass instead of the preinstalled flimsy film covers that some cases are made with. And, lastly, don’t try to talk on the phone while carrying bags of groceries and apply makeup at the same time. You’ll drop your phone every time. Don’t leave your phone on your lap in the car, or leave it in places that it can be damaged like under all the books and whatnot in your book bag. Train yourself to put your phone in places other than your back pocket—it’s never a good place considering over time it will bend the frame, or you will sit on it accidentally and no case will save it with that much pressure on a bend. Lastly, when using a clip and case, turn the phone face in when not in use. It’ll preserve the screen.

Albeit, I recommend this case 100% to anyone interested and considering it for their iPhone XR.

title: The Only Insurance Plan I'll Ever Need
text:
When you pay monthly insurance on a phone, you are paying for the comfort of knowing if a certain type of damage happens to your phone, you have paid to have it protected. Unfortunately, even with insurance, when my devices break I usually feel disappointed and then there is the inconvenience of having to have them fixed or replaced. That is why I like to protect and care for my devices myself instead of just being careless with them and having a bail out plan.

With the Body Glove and screen protectors (which you will have to purchase separately) I feel that nothing will go wrong with my device. One must also make a concerted effort to keep their phone out of water (that includes rain and steam). Follow these simple steps and you will have ease of mind regarding the safety of your device.

Of course there's always the possibility for hardware failure, but it is rare. Smart phones are well designed and unlikely to have components go bad. If they do, you have the one year manufacturer's warranty. If you make it past that then just one more year and you have your cell phone upgrade discount.

That's why I see no reason to pay for phone insurance which quickly adds up and goes towards nothing if you don't damage your phone.

The Body Glove and screen protectors are the only insurance I'll ever need.

While I recommend this case with mentioned caveats, I hope Torras can devise a sturdier version for portrait mode.

title: Good phone at a decent price, beware of other biased reviews.
text:
So I'm reading some reviews on the Treo 750 and it seems all the negative reviews are by people who are completely incompetent with technology and using Google. Let me first warn anyone who is technologically handicapped, do not buy this phone. You will get lost in all the OPTIONS, that are available within the phone.

On with my review:

Windows Mobile can do basically everything you want, just not in the prettiest manners. Upon receiving my Treo 750, it came with Windows Mobile 6. It worked well but had some slight bugs, so I upgraded to 6.1 which also has bugs but none that bother me. 6.1 is definitely snappier than the bundled version of windows mobile 6. You WILL NOT find the upgrade on Palm's Website, you'll need to Google this.

Call Quality: 8/10
Calls are crisp and clear. I have no problems hearing the other person in a busy street, and they have no problems hearing me. Although the speaker phone is slightly distorted at higher volume.

Battery Life: 8/10
Windows mobile devices and any other smart phone/pda (ie. Iphone, Blackberry) are known to have battery life that doesn't last. This is because of the processing power in these devices. The Treo has a 312mhz processor. My first Pentium II computer had a 300mhz processor. Seriously, what do you expect? My experience with the treo is that it will last me an entire day with heavy usage, but when I have it on standby (meaning not using it for anything) the battery last for at least 2 to 3 days.

Overall Design: 7/10
It's a little thick but this phone came out in Dec 2007, so it's not surprising. The curves on the side make it feel thinner than it really is and makes the phone feel very nice in your hand. The rubbery feel of the body is nice, and not slippery. The small keys take getting use to, but once you do, you type extremely fast. The screen is nice, bright, and big, but I wish it was at least 320x320 instead of 240x240.

Usability: 8/10
Windows Mobile is a powerful operating system, there are programs to do basically anything, but it isn't all in one place like you have it on the Android phones or Iphone. There are thousands of free programs and others are paid. I personally don't need any programs that you need to pay for.

Cons:
- Windows Media player will absolutely not goto the next song in the play list unless you have the ringer set to on instead of vibrate.

- In 6.1, the screen is still enabled when you press the power button to view the time while in locked mode.

-Interface isn't fun to look at.

-Lacks wi-fi

Conclusion:
I'm waiting for version 6.5 and 7 of windows mobile to come out which drastically changes the way Windows Mobile looks and also includes a app store. If you can get this phone for under $200, i would say do it. If you like to text message, the threaded sms is great. Few bugs in the OS but doesn't affect the overall usage. And the amount of software available for windows mobile is overwhelming.

title: Works as describes.
text: I was seeking for a band that would provide my watch a little more protection than normal Apple bands or more beautiful bands. When I received this band, it seemed firmer than any silicone band I'd ever used. It's similar to a traditional sports bracelet (think "Casio" sports watches). Although the material was firm, it was far more comfortable to wear than Apple's usual silicone strap. It fits perfectly on my wrist. It's also slightly longer than the regular band; my wrist measures 215mm, and most other bands are roughly the same length. There are also many adjustment holes. The band looks excellent with the carbon fiber insert. What I appreciate best about this band is that it provides a little more protection for the watch than other conventional bands. I adore Apple devices, but I always cover them with a protective case. This band has a slightly raised edge to protect the watch's face and provides full edge protection. This is significant to me because I frequently bump my arms while working around the house or in the yard. I've worn it on a variety of jobs without fear of it becoming damaged. I very recommend this band and hope that this review was helpful to you.

title: Great solid 4 port USB device!
text:
Shipping - The USB 4 port hub came in a orange manila envelope with bubble wrap lining, in addition to that the device was enclosed in a cardboard box with a cardboard wrap around liner on top of that. The shipping container ensures that your device will arrive in one piece.

Size - The device is the same size as a small stapler. It will easily fit in a laptop bag or laptop case pocket.

Construction - The device is very well constructed, it will last a long time. The USB connector pig tail is quite thick and solid. USB connector cable pig tail length is 1 foot (12 inches). It worked out great for me because it sits close to my computer and I can quickly add or remove devices easily and I don't have another long cord getting in the way.

Using the device - Plugging the device into the computer USB port was easy with a very solid insertion force; it wasn't going to come out easily. The same for the 4 USB ports on the device, inserting a USB thumb flash drive, USB memory drive or a USB device was solid they weren't going to come out easily. Very solid!

Data Transfer rates were very good (my computer does NOT have USB 3.0), but I was happy with the transfer rates. If you have a current computer with USB 3.0 you WILL have extremely fast data transfer rates.

I had to transfer some files from an 18gb USB hard drive that was starting to fail. The transfer went well. When removing a device you should always right click on the device listed and safely remove (if that won't work) or eject. Sometimes the computer will not let you do that, it will say device is being used. I had that problem with this setup. The last thing you want to do is just pull out the device. You should turn off the computer and disconnect the device. With this device you are given a 3rd option, just turn it off at the port with a switch. Awesome, how easy is that!

Final thoughts - Data Transfer activity LED lights always make me happy, I always like to have a visual confirmation of data transfer activity; sadly, the 4 port lights show only when the port switch has been turned on. I like that too. But I am giving this device 4 3/4 stars for not having data activity lights. I am being nit picky because the computer will always give you some kind of feedback on transferring data. Otherwise, this is a solid product that will increase the number of USB ports on your computer with the added ability to switch the port off when not in use. I recommend it!

I bought a Yootech and struggled with the installation and the end product looked terrible. Skinomi was the next choice. title: Looks, Value, Function, and 2 FREE front-glass screen protectors...for THIS price?  Wow!
text:
I buy a lot of things from Amazon, but don't write many reviews, nor even bother to rate most items, unless they really stand out either positive or negative. So that should tell you something.

I am making a positive exception in this case because I am so blown away with what I got for the bargain price I spent. I've only had the case installed for one day, so I won't be in a position to speak authoritatively about ''durability" until I've dropped it on concrete a half dozen times and likely owned it for a year.

That said, this was bought to replace a 2x as expensive "Spigen"-brand case which was built like a tank and, similarly, and had a similar back of the case "kickstand" for propping it up on a desk. The Spigen might provide a little better fall protection in the front, in an unusual fall angle, since it has ridges which extend further over the front edges of the phone. But, other than that, this appears to be of similarly strong construction, and it fits snug.

I figured I was overdue for a cosmetic replacement and -- in addition -- the underlying front face glass protector for my old case was broken in many areas, from many falls. Going from memory, I think I spent about $15 for the prior case, plus I independently spent about $10 for a pack of 3 front-face glass protectors. So $25 vs. $8?

What should I get? Well I loved my old case and might well have just bought the same case, same color again...only I didn't see it listed for sale. And I also needed a new front glass protector.

My eyes kept getting drawn to a picture of this bright red case for about $8. The red color might help me find it better when I misplaced it. I read more and noticed the case didn't just remind me of my older case in design, it also included a kickstand. And -- and this part I found hard to believe -- INCLUDED TWO GLASS PROTECTOR SHEETS I would otherwise have to buy independently, anyway.

A few of the one-star reviews (I always read one-star reviews first) for this case implied it wasn't, maybe, super well-built. But at the end of the day I decided to give it a try because it included the free front face glass protectors and I couldn't find anything near the price that seemed better. I figured: "I buy the two glass screen protectors and get the case free?" With that In mind I went for it.

Long story short: This is a wonderful deal -- especially if you don't already have spare front-glass protector sheets lying around. If you like the photo, I can say the case is even better... I'm very glad I got it. And I am pleased to take the time to recommend it -- and kudos to the manufacturer (I like seeing good products in a world where, increasingly, many businesses overpromise and under deliver.

It appears to be a very well-built case, which should supply better than normal protection, and an incredible value to boot. I hope my review sells a lot of extra cases for this company and makes a difference for skeptical shoppers.

title: PERFECT!!!
text:
Absolutely perfect mounting system for the Cobb Accessport V3. I didn't even bother using the mount they included, based on reviews of this system, and reviews of how poorly the included mount, from Cobb, performs (which were confirmed when I took a look at the flimsy mount provided in the Cobb kit).

This is so adaptable, with all the angles and adjustments available, and I have my AP exactly where I want it. This mounting system literally tilts and spins in almost any direction, so it provides a truly customizable mounting option.

Stays stuck like glue, holds the position that you set it in, and the Cobb AP pops easily in and out of the holder frame that Cobb provides, or, you can leave the Cobb unit in the holder frame, and the entire holder frame very easily slips off of this mounting system -- just lift and pull forward and it's off. So, lots of options here.

As stunningly amazing as the Cobb AP unit is (which it is!!!), it's too bad they did not provide a better mounting option, but this system has solved that problem, and no Cobb AP owner should be without this incredible solution!

LOVE IT.

I highly recommend!!!

title: Promotes slips and drops
text: This is a personal preference bias. The case itself is great quality, fits well and kickstand works smoothly, however, as a protective case it only promoted slips and drops because of the use of very slippery silicone for the inner shell, plus the use of a non-grip plastic outer shell, making the phone feel like it is coated in baby oil. Just like silicone products used in baking, the effect is non-stick, but in a phone case that doesn't serve well, for me. If they could have added some ridges or just used a different base material, or even used something more grippy for the outer shell, this case would be great, but, for me, when looking for something to protect my phone from drops, what I don't need is a case that slips through my hands far worse than just the phone itself would. I had a similar gripe with a Sedio case for my Nexus 7, but the silicone slip on that case was offset very effectively by a grippy outer shell and raised ridges along the exposed edges of the inner silicone shell as well. On this case, I also didn't like that the inner cover doesn't give much raised ridge protection for the screen in case of a face down fall, or at least not compared to the case I had. All that being said, if you like silicone cases, this one does have pretty excellent fit and finish. A slippery case just isn't for me.

title: Solid Case, Nice Looking Too
text:
I got this hard drive enclosure because we don’t get rid of hard drives around here. My husband has several that he needed to be able to safely store and so we decided to try this one out.

The hard drive case is a black plastic material that is really lightweight and has a soft silicone feel to the outside of the case. It looks really nice actually. It is really durable. The slides to open/close it are really well made so it doesn’t feel like you are going to wear it out with changing out the hard drive frequently. You can install your hard drive to the case without any tools required. It comes with the USB cord, just plug and play. The cord is a good quality cord. We did not have to download any drivers to get it to work. The case is actually really solid and provides excellent protection for the hard drive.

This hard drive case supports standard notebook 2.5” SATA hard drives with a thickness of 9.5mm and 7mm. We tried two different drives in it and both fit. It is compatible with Windows 2000, Windows XP, Windows Vista, Windows 7, and Windows 8. It also appears to be compatible with Windows 10 as that is the current operating system we are using and it worked fine.

It has a standard USB 3.0 interface, but it is reverse compatible with USB 2.0 as well.

We didn’t notice any heat at all when we had it on, so it does provide excellent heat dissipation.

The data transfer rate is limited by the device you place inside it, however even with an older hard drive in it, I am getting excellent transfer rates. The transfer speeds are proving to be better than a brand new jump drive. We’re not hitting 5 GB/s but we’re using an old hard drive at this moment. So I can see where you would get higher speeds with a newer drive.

I would recommend this if you have hard drives that you need to protect and be able to have access to.

I purchased this hard drive enclosure at a reduced price in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. My thoughts and experiences with this product are my own and are not influenced by the price I paid for this product.

title: YOU CAN RECHARGE WHILE USING (TX or RX)
text:
Love this device. Battery life using this to stream from my non-BT MP3 player to my BT headset (TX mode) is over 8 hours. Recharge is 2-3 hours. I really love that THIS DEVICE CAN BE RECHARGED WHILE TRANSMITTING OR RECEIVING, although it's undocumented, see procedure below. Not crazy about using 1 back-lit button to do everything and to know what it's doing, but it works. Beware it can take a few seconds after BT pairing before you hear the audio stream. Be patient.

How To Recharge (TX/RX)
The simplest way to get this working is to make sure you are already paired and streaming before you connect power. In most cases the only thing that happens is the back light around multifunction button turns RED, but streaming is uninterrupted. If the MPOW is off and you have already connected recharge power it will take pressing and holding the multifunction button (MFB) for 6 -8.9 seconds. You may have to repeat this procedure a few times before it works. Pressing and holding the MFB for 9+ seconds causes MPOW to enter discovery mode. If you must recharge while TX or RX-ing, do yourself a favor and get BT streaming working FIRST and then add power, easy-peasy.

Included directions are sparse.You must chose to TX or RX (switch on side) before your turn it on.
ON - press and hold Multifunction button (MFB) for 6 seconds. Blue light will flash about once per second
OFF - press and hold MFB for 4 seconds, red light will come on and then go out.
PAIRING- press and hold MFB for 9 seconds, blue light will flash quickly. Once paired blue light will flash at 1 second rate.
Power CONNECTED - light around MFB will be red during recharge and red light will go out once recharged. Blue light will not light.

title: Phone Completely Broke
text:
I've had this screen protector for over half a year, I got it right after I got my phone. It seemed to protect my phone, it wasn't scratched or cracked for around a month but I also didn't drop my phone at all really. As the time went on, it got some cracks but they were smaller than they had been on previous phones and I wasn't worried about them because I was confident they would go away whenever I replaced my screen protector. Everything seemed to be going well.
For what seems like no reason, my screen started glitching today. My touches wouldn't really register and it would be flashing. As soon as I got home I removed the screen protector and assumed that would fix the issue because my phone wasn't cracked it was just the screen protector right? Wrong. The cracks were somehow under my screen protector and on my phone screen even though it was supposedly protected. My phone kept glitching and now it's hard to do anything on it. I trusted this screen protector and now I probably need my entire screen to be replaced which could cost a lot of money. Don't buy this screen protector unless you want your screen to eventually completely break down.
